title: Bengals News: Joe Burrow’s evolution
summary: The 2026 NFL season kicks off Wednesday evening as we will be treated to a rematch of Super Bowl LX a day earlier than typical—and we still get a Thursday night game! This also means the Cincinnati Bengals will take the field in just a few short days at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Bengals are contenders, and much of that is because they have one of the best quarterbacks in the business, Joe Burrow. Burrow, who will be 30 in December, recently sat down with Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson, and we got to see a little glimpse into the quarterback’s evolving locker room role. “I’ve been pushed to do that in the past,” he said about being the loud voice in the locker room. “Not necessarily here, but just in my football life. I’ve tried it before, and it’s not really for me. But as I’ve grown and matured, I just think you have to be able to do it at some points, and you can’t be so bad at it when you have to do it.” Hopefully his presence as a leader is one of the things that helps push the Bengals into another deep playoff run. Here’s what else is going on: Zac Taylor has message about Bengals’ history of slow starts “Our guys are ready to go,” Taylor said. “Now we’ll spend the last five days here ironing it out … so they can go and help us be 1-0 to start the season.” The Bengals have never lost a game in which they played with their orange jerseys and white pants combos . We knew they were going to “open in orange,” but they’ve ditched the orange pants in favor of white ones. Is it superstitious? Considering the Bengals got beat by the Patriots in their home owner in 2024, and that Patriots team went on to win just two more games, I’m willing to accept some superstitious behavior. Cody Ford worked out for the Buffalo Bills on Tuesday . Ford was cut by the Bengals earlier in August after a disastrous second preseason game with the Bengals. He was originally selected in the second round by the Bills in the 2019 NFL Draft, and he spent the last three seasons playing pretty much every position on the line, other than center, over the last three seasons. title: Joe Burrow silences any doubts about staying with the Bengals
summary: Ever since it was clear that Joe Burrow was going to be the first overall pick by the Cincinnati Bengals in the 2020 NFL Draft, it has been the mission of so many national media members to make it sound like Burrow shouldn’t be there. Some called for him to pull an Eli Manning and […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) looks on during the AFC Championship trophy celebration after the AFC championship NFL football game, Sunday, Jan. 30, 2022, at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo. Cincinnati Bengals defeated Kansas City Chiefs 27-24. Cincinnati Bengals At Kansas City Chiefs Jan 30 Afc Championship 106 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Ever since it was clear that Joe Burrow was going to be the first overall pick by the Cincinnati Bengals in the 2020 NFL Draft, it has been the mission of so many national media members to make it sound like Burrow shouldn’t be there. Some called for him to pull an Eli Manning and refuse to play for Cincinnati. When he got injured in the 2020 season, many said the team was insane for drafting wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase instead of offensive line help (that resulted in a Super Bowl appearance). Then it was that the team wouldn’t be able to pay Burrow. They signed him to a market-setting deal. Then they said they wouldn’t be able to keep Chase and/or Tee Higgins, but they signed both. Even after an offseason where Cincinnati did almost everything in their power to address the defensive struggles that derailed two straight seasons, there were people saying Burrow was giving an ultimatum prior to the season that they needed to win or he was gone. Well, you can hear it from the man himself. “I’m efficient with my words, and when I’m efficient with my words, that leaves some room for interpretation,” Burrow told Geoff Hobson from Bengals.com . “But I mean what I say. I’m here for the long haul. I’m not going anywhere. I’m just trying to bring a now-or-never mentality to the day-by-day process. If you’re not, what are you doing? Attack the day with a championship mindset. The rest will take care of itself.” And there it is. Maybe some people can move on to quarterbacks who actually may be closer to leaving their teams becoming the target for five First Round picks. Burrow didn’t want to leave any doubt, though. “I’m just really proud to be quarterback of the Bengals,” Burrow says. “I’m happy to be here. I’m proud to represent the city of Cincinnati, state of Ohio, the Brown family. I’m just proud and I want to make everybody else proud, too.” Now we can get back to talking about how good Burrow is going to be this year!

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: It begins with Pirates
summary: The 2026 NFL season is here. The wait is over. The Cincinnati Bengals will take the field Sunday at Paycor Stadium against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a game that actually matters. And it does matter. Unlike the MLB or the NBA, which both have absurdly long regular seasons, the NFL (for now) plays only 17 games. That […]
full_text: Dec 18, 2022; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers linebacker Lavonte David (54) sacks Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement-USA TODAY Sports The 2026 NFL season is here. The wait is over. The Cincinnati Bengals will take the field Sunday at Paycor Stadium against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a game that actually matters. And it does matter. Unlike the MLB or the NBA, which both have absurdly long regular seasons, the NFL (for now) plays only 17 games. That means every game—from the first to the last—is important. The Bengals are contenders, and if they want the road to the AFC Championship to go through Cincinnati, they can’t afford to take games off. Cincy has an easy schedule this year. While I don’t think the Bucs are one of the best teams in the league, I do think they’re a top-five team the Bengals will face. I also think the Bengals are better than the Buccaneers, especially on offense. There aren’t many defenses in the league that can consistently keep up with Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and the ridiculous number of weapons at Burrow’s disposal. And I think the Bengals’ much-improved defense will make at least a stop or two. Having said all that, I don’t expect the Bengals’ offense to be in midseason form right out of the gate. Any supercar needs a couple of laps to warm up. I was also wrong about Baker Mayfield. When he was drafted, I thought he was a clown. And, from the outside looking in, pretty much anything happening in Cleveland resembles a burning dumpster. But once Mayfield got out of there, my opinion started to change. He’s since revitalized his career, and he’s become a pretty hard guy not to root for. Except for this week. He’ll be able to move the ball against the Bengals, and Tampa Bay has enough offensive firepower to make Cincinnati pay for mistakes. The unsung hero for the Bengals could be Chase Brown. If I’m a defensive coordinator facing the Burrow-Chase-Higgins trifecta, I’m focusing the vast majority of my attention on them. Chase has to be doubled almost all the time, and Higgins can’t consistently be left one-on-one either. Then there’s a third receiver, Mike Gesicki, Erick All Jr., or somebody else waiting to take advantage. The fact is, if the offensive line gives Burrow time to throw, someone is going to get open. That leaves Tampa Bay with two basic options: put as many defensive backs on the field as possible, or pin their ears back and try to get to Burrow before one of his weapons gets open. That’s where Brown could come in. If the Buccaneers load up on defensive backs, Brown could take advantage of a lighter box. And one of the best ways to slow down an aggressive pass rush is to make it pay with an effective running game. I don’t think the Bengals need to “establish the run” to set up the pass, but it’d certainly be nice to see them punish defenses for selling out to stop Burrow. They’ve spent a lot of time working with Burrow under center and adding more play action into the offense. If they can pull that off effectively, it could buy Burrow the extra second he needs to find one of his many weapons downfield. The guy the Bengals’ offense needs to keep an eye on is Rueben Bain Jr. Had the Bengals not traded the No. 10 overall pick to the Giants for Dexter Lawrence II, Bain is the guy I would have wanted Cincinnati to select. As it turns out, they’ll face him in Week 1. There hasn’t been a Buccaneers defender with double-digit sacks since the 2021 season, and they’re hoping Bain can help snap that streak. The Bengals would probably prefer he starts his push in Week 2. For Cincinnati’s defense, all eyes are on the defensive line. Last year, the starters were B.J. Hill and T.J. Slaton. Now, Hill and Slaton are the backups, while Lawrence and Jonathan Allen are starting. Throw in Kris Jenkins and rookie Landon Robinson, and suddenly the Bengals have a deep and talented defensive interior—something they’ve desperately lacked over the last few seasons. That group could make all the difference Sunday. If the Bengals can get consistent pressure from Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy while Lawrence, Allen and company collapse the pocket from the interior, Mayfield could be forced to get rid of the ball early or throw off-platform. That creates opportunities for Cincinnati’s linebackers and defensive backs to make plays. So, whose defense steps up the most? Vegas lists the Bengals as 3.5-point favorites, which is basically home-field advantage plus another half-point. I’ll take those odds. I see a close game that is somewhat frustrating at times. It’s Week 1. There will probably be some rust, some missed opportunities, and at least one moment that makes Bengals fans collectively wonder why they allow this team to do this to them every year. But I think Cincinnati wins. Bengals 27, Buccaneers 20. It might not be pretty, but being 1-0 is all that matters. Who do you think wins? Sound off! Who Dey, and welcome to what we will hopefully look back on as the first game of the greatest season in Bengals franchise history! title: Al Golden’s confidence in Cashius Howell says a lot about the Bengals’ promising rookie
summary: There is no shortage of excitement surrounding Cincinnati Bengals rookie defensive end Cashius Howell. And if defensive coordinator Al Golden’s assessment of his new pass rusher is any indication, the Bengals may have landed a player who can make an impact much sooner than some might expect. When Cincinnati selected Howell with the 41st overall pick in […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cashius Howell (55) recovers a Lions fumble during the game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There is no shortage of excitement surrounding Cincinnati Bengals rookie defensive end Cashius Howell. And if defensive coordinator Al Golden’s assessment of his new pass rusher is any indication, the Bengals may have landed a player who can make an impact much sooner than some might expect. When Cincinnati selected Howell with the 41st overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, the reaction was largely centered around one obvious trait: production. Howell recorded 11.5 sacks and 14 tackles for loss during his final season at Texas A&M, earning SEC Defensive Player of the Year honors and first-team All-America recognition. He finished his college career with 27 sacks and 35.5 tackles for loss. But Golden sees more than just a player who knows how to get to the quarterback. “Dynamic pass rusher, great production — not average production, great production,” Golden said after the Bengals selected Howell. That distinction is important. The Bengals didn’t simply draft Howell because he put up impressive numbers at Texas A&M. They believe those numbers are the product of a skill set that can translate to Cincinnati’s defense. Golden specifically pointed to Howell’s versatility. He can rush from a traditional edge position. He can line up as an outside linebacker. He can play in different fronts. He has shown that he can drop into coverage. And, perhaps most importantly for a Bengals defense looking to create more pressure, he gives Golden another option when it comes time to attack opposing quarterbacks. “He can play 4-2 edge, can play outside backer if you go to bigger people,” Golden said. “Showed proficiency with the ability to drop. Can help us on special teams. So, this is a multifaceted athlete and a really twitched-up guy.” That’s a strong endorsement. And it helps explain why Cincinnati reportedly viewed Howell so highly on its draft board. The Bengals had to wait until the second round to make their first selection, yet Howell was still sitting there at No. 41. Cincinnati’s decision-makers didn’t appear to view that as a problem. They viewed it as an opportunity. Assistant general manager Mike Potts called Howell’s ability to win quickly as a pass rusher “really dynamic.” At the same time, the Bengals’ draft team reportedly had Howell as the highest player remaining on its board. Following a recent practice, Golden continued to heap praise on Howell, noting that his intelligence has really helped the rookie transition to the pro level. “Hitting on Cashius, I can’t underscore how important that is because he’s come through for us in terms of his intellect, his work ethic, his ability to process, and his learning curve,” Golden told Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic . Golden’s comments reinforce the idea that Cincinnati wasn’t simply drafting for depth. The Bengals were adding another weapon. A Different Kind of Edge Rusher One of the more intriguing aspects of Howell’s fit in Cincinnati is his physical profile. At roughly 6-foot-2 and 253 pounds, Howell isn’t the prototypical long, towering defensive end. His arms measured just over 30 inches at the combine, something that became a major talking point during the pre-draft process. But the Bengals clearly weren’t overly concerned. They saw the burst, the bend, and the pass-rush arsenal. And they saw a player who consistently found ways to get home. Howell’s game is built around his ability to get off the ball and attack. That’s precisely the kind of skill set Golden can move around the formation and utilize in different situations. That versatility becomes even more interesting when you consider the rest of Cincinnati’s defensive line. The Bengals now have Howell alongside players such as Shemar Stewart, Myles Murphy, Boye Mafe, and Dexter Lawrence II. That’s a very different-looking group than the one Cincinnati had a year ago. And Howell doesn’t necessarily have to be the centerpiece of it. He can be the chess piece. Golden specifically compared Howell’s body type to Mafe’s and talked about the variety the two can provide on early downs and in obvious passing situations. That could be where Howell becomes particularly dangerous. The Production Is Already There There’s always going to be a learning curve for a rookie defensive lineman entering the NFL. But Howell isn’t coming to Cincinnati as some developmental project with theoretical upside. He already has a production track record. His 11.5 sacks in 2025 weren’t simply the result of playing a few favorable matchups. He became one of the most disruptive defenders in the SEC and earned the conference’s top defensive player award. That matters. The Bengals have spent years looking for ways to generate more consistent pressure without relying exclusively on one player to win his matchup. Howell gives them another legitimate pass-rush threat. And Golden seems to believe he can do considerably more than just rush the passer. That’s what makes the rookie so intriguing. Golden’s Confidence Should Get Bengals Fans Excited There is a difference between a coach saying nice things about a rookie and a coach describing exactly how that rookie can help his defense. Golden’s comments fall into the second category. He’s already talking about Howell’s ability to play different positions, rush from different alignments, drop into coverage, and contribute on special teams. That’s not the description of a player the Bengals intend to keep in a limited package. It’s the description of a player they believe can become part of the defensive identity. Howell himself has described his projected role as a hybrid edge rusher — playing defensive end on base downs, occasionally dropping into coverage, and being used in various blitz packages. That sounds an awful lot like the type of player Golden wants to have at his disposal. And perhaps that’s the biggest reason to pay attention to the growing buzz around Howell in Cincinnati. The hype isn’t simply coming from draft analysts or fans watching his college tape. It’s coming from the guy who designed the Bengals’ defense. Al Golden clearly believes Cashius Howell can be a difference-maker. Now Bengals fans get to find out just how quickly that belief becomes reality.

title: New former Browns TE Dae’Quan Wright news could lead to an NFL return
summary: Never in my wildest dreams did I think we would ever have the kind of whirlwind story about a practice-squad-level, developmental tight end as we have with Dae’Quan Wright. If you haven’t been following up on this potential “history” making process, let’s get you caught up real quick: The seemingly final update on Wright’s journey […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Dae'Quan Wright #88 of the Cleveland Browns warms up prior to a preseason game against the Buffalo Bills at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Never in my wildest dreams did I think we would ever have the kind of whirlwind story about a practice-squad-level, developmental tight end as we have with Dae’Quan Wright . If you haven’t been following up on this potential “history” making process , let’s get you caught up real quick: The Cleveland Browns added Wright in mid-August after the Philadelphia Eagles waived him One of our loyal DBN readers was very excited about the Wright addition and shared about it in The Feed: Wright was mostly away from the Browns for the first week he was on the roster, then came news that he was part of a lawsuit attempting to return to college Cleveland then waived Wright , which opened up his chance to return to college Given his plan to return to school, no other NFL team claimed Wright Lawsuits went back and forth , including the SEC making it a rule that schools would face punishment if they rostered players who had declared for and/or signed a professional contract. Another lawsuit said that wasn’t acceptable. Then most of us got lost in the legalese of it all Wright and Zxavian Harris were not placed on LSU’s roster for their game against Clemson , despite reportedly enrolling and practicing The seemingly final update on Wright’s journey with LSU is that he will not have a journey with LSU: NEWS: LSU football is adding two players to the school’s roster, which will complete it at 105 players, per ESPN sources. This will lock LSU’s roster for the rest of the year, which will eliminate the program’s ability to add Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. pic.twitter.com/gLJj7AyvPw — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) September 9, 2026 So, Wright now has two options: Find another school with a scholarship and/or NIL money or seek to return to the NFL, likely on a practice squad. Wright is currently an NFL free agent after clearing waivers, free to sign with any team if they so desired. According to a lawyer (unsurprisingly given all the legal moves involved here) the two would-be LSU players are thinking about their legal options: In response to the news tonight of LSU finalizing its roster without Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, Louisiana plaintiffs attorney Ryan Downton says "players are reviewing legal options." https://t.co/d0Honkz0tb — Ross Dellenger (@RossDellenger) September 9, 2026 Given the Browns flexibility with Wright as he went through his process, including allowing him to be away from the team despite being on the roster, it is at least possible that GM Andrew Berry would look to bring the former Ole Miss tight end back into the fold. We know Berry isn’t afraid of making a few extra roster moves. Cleveland fans, on the other hand, may just be sick of hearing about a player who went undrafted and whose best statistical season included 39 receptions, 635 yards, and five touchdowns. Then again, an athletic 6’4”, 255-pound tight end is always an enticing option. What do you think of the whole Wright story, and would you want the Browns to bring him back on the practice squad? title: Browns make 4 roster moves, including adding WR, DE, before Week 1 practice starts
summary: The wait is almost over; the Cleveland Browns 2026 regular season is almost upon us, with the team starting their normal practice schedule on Wednesday. With the week off after the initial 53-man roster, Labor Day on Monday, and the first official 2026 regular season game on Wednesday, nothing about the start of the season […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 15: Bub Means #16 of the New Orleans Saints catches a pass in the second quarter during an NFL preseason game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Caesars Superdome on August 15, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The wait is almost over; the Cleveland Browns 2026 regular season is almost upon us, with the team starting their normal practice schedule on Wednesday. With the week off after the initial 53-man roster , Labor Day on Monday, and the first official 2026 regular season game on Wednesday, nothing about the start of the season has felt normal. What is normal is the constant changing of the roster by Browns GM Andrew Berry. On September 3rd, we presented Cleveland’s combined roster, with their 53-man and practice squads combined . At that point, Berry had already made changes to the initial rosters. On Monday, the Browns switched out defensive linemen on the practice squad , and now, after working out nine during Monday’s practice, Berry is back to making moves: Signed WR Bub Means : There was a report that the team was going to bring in Means to the initial practice squad; instead, the 6’2” receiver joins that squad over a week later. Signed DE Nadame Tucker : Among Monday’s workouts, Tucker is a 26-year-old rookie. Tucker had a productive preseason with the Los Angeles Chargers but didn’t make their initial 53-man roster and was just released from their practice squad and now joins Cleveland’s version. Released WR Bryce Oliver : Signed to the practice squad six days ago, Oliver is a 6’1″, 215-pound receiver who went to Youngstown State. He has played in 13 games with seven receptions and, as noted below, played a lot of special teams. His ’25 season was cut short due to injury. Released P Wes Pahl : Competition for Corey Bojorquez; Pahl’s time on the roster seemed unlikely to last given how most teams use their practice squad. As always, DBN will keep you updated with all the moves, here and in The Feed. full_text: BEREA, OHIO - MAY 08: KC Concepcion #17 and Denzel Boston #12 of the Cleveland Browns run a drill during a rookie minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on May 08, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The start of the 2026 NFL regular season is on Wednesday. Yes, Wednesday, with a Thursday game in Australia. Heading into Week 1 versus the Jacksonville Jaguars, the overall sense about the Cleveland Browns is negative for now and excited for the future . The Browns young roster has been given high accolades after two very good draft classes by GM Andrew Berry. There is still much to be proven on the field, but Cleveland’s decision to draft two receivers early in the 2026 NFL draft has fans excited about the offense being explosive for the first time in a long time. KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have done little to calm the excitement around them, as training camp and preseason has seen both making big plays. Boston in particular has gotten a lot of attention as a second-round receiver with good size, speed, and great hands. Tuesday, The Athletic’s “NFL Future Hits List” included the Washington Huskies pass catcher at the top: AFC scout: “The definition of an NFL X receiver. A perfect complement with KC Concepcion.” NFC executive: “Huge, talented, and makes it look easy when clean. Preseason best play certainly flashed of a better player than (only) a rebounder.” Adding the two young receivers to a group that saw RB Quinshon Judkins and TE Harold Fannin Jr. have great rookie seasons last year only adds to the hype and excitement about what could be in the future for the orange and brown. Now, Browns quarterbacks need to get Boston and Concepcion the ball and HC Todd Monken has to put everyone in position to be successful. summary: It is Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, and that means it’s time to kick start a lot of our weekly features again, including where the Cleveland Browns stand in the eyes of the national media. With the quarterback situation the way it is and the departure of Myles Garrett, it’s understandable that the […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Denzel Boston #12 of the Cleveland Browns hands a flag to a fan as the team is introduced prior to a preseason game against the Buffalo Bills at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images It is Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, and that means it’s time to kick start a lot of our weekly features again, including where the Cleveland Browns stand in the eyes of the national media. With the quarterback situation the way it is and the departure of Myles Garrett , it’s understandable that the Browns have an average ranking of 30.6 heading into the season. Rightfully so, the Browns need to prove themselves before getting any form of respect in these rankings. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 31 They have talent on their roster. They just don’t have a quarterback. The good news is the college draft will be loaded with them next year. ESPN – No. 31 Milestone to watch: The Browns’ defense breaking the record for consecutive games without allowing a 300-yard passer. The Browns have gone 45 straight games without allowing a quarterback to throw for 300 yards, the longest streak in the NFL since the Colts went 52 games from 2005 to 2008. Cleveland could break the record in Week 8, a road matchup against the Steelers. The defense, though, will have to achieve the milestone without reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and with a new coordinator in Mike Rutenberg. NFL.com – No. 30 The Browns found a way to unite their fans in disgust by naming Deshaun Watson the starter two days after he was lustily booed during a ghastly performance on his home field. I expect a change under center by Week 3, which should tell you how I think Cleveland will fare in the first two contests of 2026 (road games at Jacksonville and Tampa Bay). Sporting News – No. 32 The Browns lost Garrett and are hoping they can find some return pop in Jared Verse, but the defense is bound to be weakened overall without the tone-setting leader, which isn’t good news for a toggling-QB offense. Yahoo Sports – No. 30 Everything has been said about Deshaun Watson starting at quarterback. It’s a weird, bad decision. That detracts from the exciting young talent on the rest of the team. Keep a close eye on rookie receiver KC Concepcion, a first-round draft pick who will contribute a lot right away. Bleacher Report – No. 30 Our experts all seem to agree that the Cleveland Browns are a bottom-tier team, and that probably says more about their quarterback situation than anything else. The Browns have some talented young players on their roster and the bones of a defense that ranked fourth overall last season—with Jared Verse trying to replace the departed Myles Garrett. Even with Garrett leading the defense, though, Cleveland couldn’t notch more than five wins, in large part because of bad quarterback play. The return of Deshaun Watson doesn’t really improve the Browns’ QB situation, and the looming 2027 quarterback class could eventually leave Cleveland searching for fewer wins than it got a year ago. USA Today – No. 30 Maybe the best way to get into position for a premium quarterback in the 2027 draft is to trade DE Myles Garrett … and start QB Deshaun Watson behind an offensive line that only retained one (spot) starter from 2026. Genius. title: Browns Week 1: A look at changes to Jaguars roster this year
summary: During the 2025 regular season, Cleveland Browns fans were also on “Jaguars Watch” because they had the Jacksonville Jaguars’ first-round pick from the Travis Hunter trade. Browns fans are on “Rams Watch” this season due to the Myles Garrett trade, but still have the Jaguars on their mind heading into Week 1 of the 2026 […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - JANUARY 11: Travis Etienne Jr. #1 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs with the ball during the AFC Wildcard Playoff game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Buffalo Bills on January 11, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images During the 2025 regular season, Cleveland Browns fans were also on “ Jaguars Watch ” because they had the Jacksonville Jaguars’ first-round pick from the Travis Hunter trade . Browns fans are on “ Rams Watch ” this season due to the Myles Garrett trade , but still have the Jaguars on their mind heading into Week 1 of the 2026 season. Cleveland and Jacksonville seemed on a collision course for overlap during the 2026 offseason, with Grant Udinski interviewing for the Browns head coaching position . At times, the young Udinski seemed like the favorite for the job that ended up going to HC Todd Monken . The Hunter trade ended up amounting to the cornerback/wide receiver for DT Mason Graham, RB Quinshon Judkins , and WR KC Concepcion , as well as a few Day 3 picks. Preparing to face the Jaguars on the road, the visitors have had a lot more changes than the home team, starting with the coaching staff. The Jacksonville roster has also seen some changes, as is usual in the NFL these days: Jaguars Roster Departures LB Devin Lloyd RB Travis Etienne DE Emmanuel Ogbah DE Dawuane Smoot DT Austin Johnson S Andrew Wingard TE Hunter Long WR Dyami Brown TE Johnny Mundt DT Maason Smith LB Yasir Abudllah CB Greg Newsome II WR Tim Patrick Jaguars Roster Additions DT Ruke Orhorhoro RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. QB Quinn Ewers RB Ameer Abdullah OL Sam Mustipher OL Daniel Faalele LB Jahlani Tavai Jaguars 2026 NFL draft class 2nd round: TE Nate Boerkircher 3rd round: DT Albert Regis, OL Emmanuel Pregnon, DB Jalen Huskey 4th round: DE Wesley Williams 5th round: TE Tanner Koziol 6th round: WR Josh Cameron, WR CJ Williams 7th round: DE Zach Durfee, LB Parker Hughes Based on expectations, only one starter from this year’s draft class (Pregnon). Much like the coaching staff, Jacksonville’s roster has a lot of continuity from last year. The current expected depth chart shows only one new starter who wasn’t with the team last year: Pregnon. The other 24 starters across the three units were with the Jaguars last season.

title: Browns vs Jaguars Week 1: Key matchups
summary: There is a lot of uncertainty about what the Cleveland Browns will look like this season, especially in their Week 1 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Deshaun Watson will make his first regular-season start since 2024, giving Todd Monken his first opportunity to showcase what the offense can look like with the team’s new, young […]
full_text: There is a lot of uncertainty about what the Cleveland Browns will look like this season, especially in their Week 1 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Deshaun Watson will make his first regular-season start since 2024, giving Todd Monken his first opportunity to showcase what the offense can look like with the team’s new, young talent. It will be particularly interesting to see how the Jaguars secondary fares against the Browns pass catchers, especially KC Concepcion . Concepcion is known for his route running and separation, and this game will be a good opportunity to see if this skill set continues to show up at NFL game speed. Josh Hines-Allen has had a fantastic career thus far and is likely to continue on this route in 2026. With the shakeup on Cleveland’s offensive line and the uncertainty of how Watson will look under center, Hines-Allen has the chance to really leave his mark on this game. This will be a big “Welcome to the NFL” moment for Spencer Fano as he tries to prove he is ready for his role on the offensive line. Mason Graham enters his second season with 17 games of experience under his belt, which should give him greater confidence heading into the new year. This game will be a big test for him as an interior defensive lineman going up against Trevor Lawrence . If the Browns want to have success in this matchup, it will be important to see how much pressure he can generate on Lawrence early in the game. Let me know what you think in the comments – What is the most important matchup in Browns vs. Jaguars?

summary: A few days ago we were all caught by surprise when the Dallas Cowboys announced that Tyler Smith would miss somewhere between 4-6 weeks with a thumb injury that requires surgery. full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Nick Leverett #51 of the Dallas Cowboys walks off the field after the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images A few days ago we were all caught by surprise when the Dallas Cowboys announced that Tyler Smith would miss somewhere between 4-6 weeks with a thumb injury that requires surgery. It was a matter of time until the Cowboys formally placed Smith on injured reserve and brought in someone to fill that spot on the roster. That happened on Wednesday morning when it was reported that the team is elevating Nick Leverett from the practice squad. The Cowboys are signing OL Nick Leverett to the active roster from the practice squad, per source. With Tyler Smith (thumb) out 4-6 weeks, Leverett can serve as the backup interior lineman on gameday. — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) September 9, 2026 This was always the most logical next step for the Cowboys as it gives them the most depth relative to the players they currently have in tow. T.J. Bass is going to slot in at Smith’s actual spot while he is out, but you have to have bodies as evidenced by this whole story. The Cowboys do now have an open spot on their practice squad so we will see what they do with that.

title: What you need to know about the Giants, Cowboys Week 1 opponent
summary: Week 1 is finally upon us, and with that comes the resurrection of professional football for the 2026 season. This year the Cowboys don’t have to wait long to renew one of their oldest rivalries. Dallas opens the 2026 season Sunday night against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium, and while plenty about this […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh looks on during the second half of a pre season game at Hard Rock Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 1 is finally upon us, and with that comes the resurrection of professional football for the 2026 season. This year the Cowboys don’t have to wait long to renew one of their oldest rivalries. Dallas opens the 2026 season Sunday night against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium, and while plenty about this matchup will look familiar, the team the Cowboys face isn’t quite the same one that went 4-13 a year ago. The Giants spent the offseason remaking their coaching staff and loading up on young talent. Now they get to see whether all that change can translate into wins. So, before the Cowboys and Giants kick off Sunday night, here’s a quick look at what has been happening in New York. The Giants added plenty of new faces The Giants overhauled their coaching staff. John Harbaugh takes over the team, giving the franchise a former Super Bowl winner with a large reputation in the NFL. Harbaugh’s teams are physical, and they will run the football. His presence is the big headline change in New York for the 2026 season. New York was also busy in free agency, bringing in several players with ties to Harbaugh’s former team in Baltimore while also addressing some obvious roster weaknesses. Among the notable additions were linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, cornerback Greg Newsome II, defensive tackle DJ Reader, tight end Isaiah Likely, fullback Patrick Ricard and punter Jordan Stout. The Giants also added receiver Darnell Mooney and safety Jevon Holland to finish a furious free agency period for the G-men. Then came the draft. The Giants had two picks in the top 10 and used them on Ohio State linebacker Arvell Reese at No. 5 and Miami offensive lineman Francis Mauigoa at No. 10. They added Tennessee cornerback Colton Hood in the second round and Notre Dame receiver Malachi Fields in the third, rounding out what could be a nice mix of young and veteran talent on the roster. Reese could stand out as one of the best players out of the 2026 draft. At Ohio State, he totaled 69 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2025. Harbaugh has said the plan is to move Reese around, allowing him to line up inside, attack gaps and rush off the edge alongside Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux, making them, on paper, one of the most athletic defensive lines in the NFL. . @BaldyNFL takes a look at the defense and Arvell Reese's instant impact pic.twitter.com/dXQ7Ggmegh — New York Giants (@Giants) September 3, 2026 This is Jaxson Dart’s team The Giants also enter 2026 with a second-year quarterback taking over the offense. Jaxson Dart is the starter, with veteran Jameis Winston serving as his backup. Dart’s development is arguably the biggest variable in determining how much better New York can be this season, but with the reins firmly in his grasp this year and a full offseason program behind him, the next step could be a big one for the second-year pro. Last year Dart threw for 2,272 yards on 216 completions (63%) with 15 touchdowns and five interceptions. Dart also showed he was a capable, dangerous scrambler. Adding 86 carries for 487 yards and nine touchdowns, and with all the offensive additions and the return of Cam Skattebo, Dart will have plenty of help around him in 2026. JAXSON DART CROSS BODY TO MALACHI FIELD FOR THE HEAD TAP TD pic.twitter.com/Q0QshxF2qg — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) August 15, 2026 Despite injury recovery, Malik Nabers should still be an offensive centerpiece If there is one Giants offensive player Cowboys fans don’t need an introduction to, it’s Malik Nabers. After torching Dallas last year in week two for 167 yards on nine catches and two touchdowns, Nabers is looking to continue his dominance against his divisional foes. However, the second-year receiver is returning from the ACL injury that ended his 2025 season, and his availability and effectiveness will be one of the biggest storylines Sunday night. New York released longtime receiver Darius Slayton just days before the season, leaving a receiver group built around Nabers, Mooney, Beckham and rookie Malachi Fields. That makes Nabers even more important. The Giants also have some interesting options in the backfield. As mentioned earlier, Cam Skattebo is back from his scary ankle/leg injury that derailed his rookie season, while Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary give New York plenty of options depending on the situation in the run game. The defense could be the biggest problem The Giants’ defense was a major weakness last season, particularly against the run, coughing up 145.3 rushing yards a game, good for 31st in the NFL, but there is considerably more talent on that side of the ball now. Burns and Thibodeaux are veterans, while Abdul Carter enters his second season and Reese gives New York another versatile weapon. Edmunds adds experience inside, while the secondary received a significant facelift with the additions of Newsome and Holland. And there is an interesting Cowboys connection here. Chauncey Golston, who spent the first five seasons of his career in Dallas, is now with the Giants and is listed as a starting defensive end on New York’s Week 1 depth chart. The Giants are also expecting a bounce-back from cornerback Deonte Banks, who has won a starting spot opposite Greg Newsome heading into Week 1. This isn’t the same defense Dallas saw last year. Like the Cowboys unit that struggled last year, this defense should and could improve a lot. So, how did the Giants look in the preseason? Pretty good. New York went 2-1, losing its preseason opener to Minnesota 13-10 before bouncing back with a 26-3 win over Miami and a 23-6 victory over the Jets. The finale against the Jets was particularly clean. The Giants held New York scoreless after its opening drive, while rookie kicker Dominic Zvada made three field goals, including a 53-yarder. Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Xavier Gipson also scored touchdowns. Of course, preseason results don’t tell us much about what a team will actually be in September. But for a first-year coaching staff, going 2-1 while establishing the physical identity Harbaugh has talked about is at least a decent starting point. The Cowboys have plenty of history on their side, however Dallas has dominated this rivalry historically, holding a 78-48-2 regular-season record against New York and winning 16 of the last 18 meetings. The Cowboys are also 11-1 against the Giants when the two teams have met in Week 1. Even if the most recent meeting didn’t go Dallas’ way, the Giants are facing some daunting and one-sided historical numbers against Big D. While this is still the Giants, it isn’t exactly the same Giants the Cowboys have beaten up on over the last decade. New coach. New defensive pieces. A different offensive philosophy. A second-year quarterback. And a roster that looks considerably more like the kind of team Harbaugh wants to build. For the Cowboys, Week 1 is the first chance to find out whether all of that change actually made New York better. And that’s really the question entering Sunday night: How much of the new Giants will show up when the games finally count? Will it be enough to beat history?

title: Predicting Dallas Cowboys win/loss record in 2026
summary: The first week of the 2026 NFL season has finally arrived! The Dallas Cowboys are expected to be one of the better teams in the entire league this year, but just how good remains to be seen. With the optimism around Cowboys Nation at all-time recent high, we believe they’ll win a lot more games […]
full_text: The first week of the 2026 NFL season has finally arrived! The Dallas Cowboys are expected to be one of the better teams in the entire league this year, but just how good remains to be seen. With the optimism around Cowboys Nation at all-time recent high, we believe they’ll win a lot more games than they lose this year and predict the outcome of each game below. Week 1 – at New York Giants The Giants will be a better team under John Harbaugh, but they’re not ready to compete on the Cowboys level yet. This is a good opportunity for Dallas to knock off a little rust against an inferior team in preparation for tougher opponents to come. Cowboys win: 1-0 Week 2 – Washington Commanders Back-to-back wins against divisional opponents? You bet! The Cowboys should be amped up in their first home game of the season, especially against division rival. They should dominate in all three phases of the game against a less talented Commanders team. Cowboys win: 2-0 Week 3 – Baltimore Ravens (Brazil) We could see this game going either way, but playing so far from home in Rio de Janeiro against the best dual-threat QB in the league, Lamar Jackson, is a lot to ask from Christian Parker’s new-look defense in the third game of the season. Tough to call, but we’ll get the Ravens the slight edge. Cowboys lose: 2-1 Week 4 – at Houston Texans Could it be the league’s best offense against the league’s best defense? This interstate matchup will likely be determined by who gets the better of their opponent, Dallas’ offense or Houston’s defense. With Brandon Aubrey as their ace in the hole, we predict the Cowboys coming out on top. Cowboys win: 3-1 Week 5 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Buccaneers attempted to revamp their defense this offseson, but it won’t be enough to neutralize Dak Prescott and Company. And without Mike Evans, the Cowboys new-look defense will be able to keep Baker Mayfield and Tampa Bay’s offense in check. Cowboys win: 4-1 Week 6 – at Green Bay Packers Micah Parsons is hoping to make his season debut in Week 6, but even if he does we believe Dallas is still favored in this matchup. This isn’t the same team the Packers faced last season. The Cowboys are much improved and should earn a tough road victory in a hostile environment. Cowboys win: 5-1 Week 7 – at Philadelphia Eagles Back-to-back road games against two of the best teams in the NFC may be asking too much of the Cowboys coming off what we predict to be a emotionally/physically draining victory over the Packers. It will be close, but will give the Eagles the slight edge with home field advantage. Cowboys lose: 5-2 Week 8 – Arizona Cardinals This is a game and team that has constantly given the Cowboys trouble, but not this year. The Cardinals are rebuilding and could be competing for the No. 1 draft pick in 2027. As such, should be one of the most winnable games on Dallas’ schedule this year. Cowboys win: 6-2 Week 9 – at Indianapolis Colts Other than RB Jonathan Taylor, there’s nothing all that concerning about the Colts, either offensively or defensively. With Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark the Cowboys should be able contain Taylor and easily secure another “W” at the midway point of the 2026 season. Cowboys win: 7-2 Week 10 – San Francisco 49ers The 49ers have been a nightmare matchup for the Cowboys in recent memory and have won the last four games in a row when these two teams of played. With the home field advantage and a much-improved defense, we predict Dallas puts an end to the win streak. Cowboys win: 8-2 Week 11 – Tennessee Titans The Titans or another rebuilding team with a young QB, Cam Ward, who is still trying to find his way in the NFL. This is another team the Cowboys should easily dominate in all three phases the game as long as they continue to remain focused/disciplined. Cowboys win: 9-2 Week 12 – Philadelphia Eagles (Thanksgiving) Thanksgiving against the Eagles will be the Cowboys third consecutive game at home. The winner could decide who the NFC champ will be and we believe Dallas will be extra motivated to secure the “W”. Cowboys win: 10-2 Week 13 – at Seattle Seahawks After a three-game homestretch, the Cowboys have somewhat of a mini-bye before they hit the road to take on the defending Super Bowl champs. They have all the pieces in place to come out of this game victorious, but the Seahawks home field advantage may be too tough to overcome. Cowboys lose: 10-3 Week 14 – Bye Rest. Recuperate. Repeat. Week 15 – at Los Angeles Rams This Week 15 matchup with the Rams could be a potential preview to the NFC championship game. Unfortunately, we don’t predict this game to go the Cowboys way. With home field advantage and the All-Pro defensive pairing of Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, it’s just too much for Dallas. Cowboys lose: 10-4 Week 16 – Jacksonville Jaguars The Cowboys have to be careful with the Jaguars. They are coming off a strong 2025 season and are an underrated contender in the AFC. This matchup could come down to who performs better, Dak Prescott or Trevor Lawrence? With the weapons he has surrounding him, No. 4 has the advantage. Cowboys win: 11-4 Week 17 – New York Giants This Week 17 matchup with the Giants feels like a “W” no matter how you look at it for the Cowboys. With playoff seeding on the line, Dallas simply has more to play for at this point in the season then the G-men do. Plus, they probably want to finish out the regular-season strong at home. Cowboys win: 12-4 Week 18 – at Washington Commanders We don’t know if this game will mean anything or not with any kind of certainty right now, however, it’s more than likely to be a meaningless game. The majority of the Cowboys starters could sit out in order to get them some rest before the playoffs get underway. Cowboys lose: 12-5

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 5
summary: It is Day 5 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: TEMPE, AZ - JANUARY 28: Emmitt Smith #22 of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates holding up the Lombardi Trophy after they defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XXX on January 28, 1996 at Sun Devil Stadium in Tempe, Arizona. The Cowboys won the Super Bowl 27-17. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) *** Local Caption ***Emmitt Smith | Getty Images It is Day 5 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’re down the final five here on our 100-day countdown to kickoff. This time we revisit the night Dallas captured its fifth Lombardi Trophy and completed the final championship run of the 1990s dynasty. The Cowboys built an early lead, survived a determined Pittsburgh comeback and relied on two huge Larry Brown interceptions to secure a 27-17 victory in Super Bowl XXX. Sunday, January 28, 1996 Sun Devil Stadium, Tempe, Arizona Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Pittsburgh Steelers 17 This was the third Super Bowl meeting between Dallas and Pittsburgh. The Steelers had beaten the Cowboys in Super Bowls X and XIII, both by four points, so Dallas finally had an opportunity to turn the tables. The Cowboys were also chasing their third championship in four seasons after winning following the 1992 and 1993 campaigns. Dallas started quickly. Chris Boniol opened the scoring with a 42-yard field goal before Deion Sanders provided one of the game’s most memorable early plays. Lining up on offense, Sanders caught a 47-yard pass from Troy Aikman that helped move Dallas into scoring position. Aikman soon found Jay Novacek for a three-yard touchdown, putting the Cowboys ahead 10-0. This would be the final touchdown Novacek would ever score for Dallas. Boniol added a 35-yard field goal during the second quarter, giving Dallas a 13-0 advantage. Pittsburgh finally answered just before halftime when Neil O’Donnell found Yancey Thigpen for a six-yard touchdown. Instead of taking complete control into the break, Dallas carried a much tighter 13-7 lead into halftime. The game’s biggest figure emerged during the third quarter. O’Donnell attempted a pass toward the sideline, but Larry Brown read the play and intercepted it at the Dallas 38-yard line. He returned the ball 44 yards to the Pittsburgh 18. Aikman then hit Michael Irvin for 17 yards before Emmitt Smith scored from one yard out, extending the Cowboys’ lead to 20-7. Pittsburgh refused to go away. Norm Johnson kicked a 46-yard field goal to make it 20-10, then Bill Cowher surprised Dallas with an onside kick that the Steelers recovered. Pittsburgh took advantage when Bam Morris scored from one yard out. Suddenly, with 6:36 remaining, a game Dallas had once led 13-0 had become a 20-17 thriller. The Steelers defense forced a Dallas punt and gave O’Donnell possession at his own 32 with just over four minutes remaining. Pittsburgh now had a chance to tie the game or take the lead. Brown made sure it never happened. On second down, he stepped in front of another O’Donnell pass and returned his second interception 33 yards to the Pittsburgh six-yard line. Two plays later, Smith powered into the end zone from four yards out. The touchdown restored a 27-17 lead with 3:43 remaining and finally gave Dallas enough breathing room to finish the job. Pittsburgh could not mount another serious comeback, and the Cowboys had their fifth Super Bowl championship. This game belongs near the very top of the countdown because it completed one of the greatest championship runs in NFL history. Dallas had now won three Super Bowls in four seasons under two different head coaches, Jimmy Johnson and Barry Switzer, with Aikman, Smith and Irvin remaining at the center of it all. The victory also gave the Cowboys their long-awaited Super Bowl revenge over Pittsburgh. #Cowboys vs #Steelers 1996 Super Bowl XXX Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 27, Pittsburgh Steelers 17 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/3syEGRUYto — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 8, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Brown became the first cornerback to win Super Bowl MVP. title: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Opponent Preview: Tennessee Titans
summary: For the first time since a 2018 Monday Night Football game in week nine, the Tennessee Titans come to AT&T Stadium in Week 11. This will be the final test for the Cowboys prior to a game that’s been circled on everyone’s calendar since it was announced, Thanksgiving Day against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Titans […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 8: Running back Tony Pollard #20 of the Tennessee Titans runs with the ball during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 8, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time since a 2018 Monday Night Football game in week nine, the Tennessee Titans come to AT&T Stadium in Week 11. This will be the final test for the Cowboys prior to a game that’s been circled on everyone’s calendar since it was announced, Thanksgiving Day against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Titans defense actually has a chance to be a good measuring stick for this Cowboys offense, going into 2026 with new head coach Robert Saleh. The former New York Jets head coach resurrected his career with the job he did with the San Francisco 49ers defense a year ago, getting another shot at a head job and bringing with him the former head coach he used to share a stadium with as offensive coordinator, former Giants HC Brian Daboll. The Saleh-Daboll dynamic has drawn a lot of attention this offseason, but it will be up to the development of second-year quarterback and 2025 number one overall pick Cam Ward to really determine how far this Titans team can go. Let’s take a look at what they’ve done to support Ward and rebuild the defense under Saleh this offseason, including adding for Cowboy Solomon Thomas through trade. Titans Key Free Agent Signings/Departures *SIGNED IN FREE AGENCY WR K.J. Osborn QB Hendon Hooker RB Michael Carter LB Mohamoud Diabate RB Julius Chestnut (Re-signed) SAF Tony Adams SAF Jerrick Reed (Re-signed) WR Wan’Dale Robinson DE Jacob Martin TE Daniel Bellinger CB Cor’Dale Flott DL John Franklin-Myers C Austin Schlottmann CB Alonte Taylor * DEPARTED IN FREE AGENCY CB L’Jarius Sneed CB Demon Hall SAF Xavier Woods WR Van Jefferson CB Kaiir Elam DE Arden Key The Titans started 0-4 a year ago, which took any spotlight for fans just interested in watching how Ward would play as a rookie away very quickly. They did go on to play one-score games against the Chargers, Texans, and Seahawks after beating the Arizona Cardinals in most improbable fashion, 22-21, in week five. Still, winning just three games with the top pick at QB and seeing the offense lack a dynamic element under Brian Callahan led to the coaching change this offseason in Nashville. Tight end Chig Okonkwo led the team in catches last season, but signed with the Washington Commanders in free agency. Their most targeted receiver in Elic Ayomanor is back, along with Chimere Dike and TE Gunnar Helm, as well as Calvin Ridley. Former Giant Wan’Dale Robinson who played for Daboll is new, as is fourth overall draft pick Carnell Tate out of Ohio State. As expected, having Brian Callahan (and Bill Callahan on staff) gave the Titans steady production from former Cowboy Tony Pollard out of the backfield a year ago, his second with the Titans, and he returns as the starter for 2026. The Titans seeing Ward get more comfortable as a passer and better as a team in the quick passing game could see Pollard be even more productive, creating the type of dual-threat offense that Daboll has curated before. On defense, the Titans brought in a host of former Jets and 49ers that have played for Saleh. Within their division, the Jaguars lost a lot of production from 2025 on offense and the Colts are still searching for answers at quarterback, making the Texans the favorite – mainly because of their super impressive defense. It’s not unimaginable to think that with another Saleh coaching masterclass on this side of the ball, the Titans defense can nudge close enough to the Texans to make this a two team race in the AFC South. Saleh will have to prove he can do so while handling the total responsibilities as a head coach, something he struggled to do in the New York market with the Jets. Titans 2026 Draft Class Round 1, Pick 4: WR Carnell Tate Round 1, Pick 31: EDGE Keldric Faulk Round 2, Pick 28 (60 Overall): LB Anthony Hill Jr. Round 5, Pick 2 (142 Overall): G Fernando Carmona Round 5, Pick 25 (165 Overall): RB Nicholas Singleton Round 6, Pick 3 (184 Overall): DT Jackie Marshall Round 6, Pick 13 (194 Overall): C Pat Coogan Round 7, Pick 9 (225 Overall): TE Jaren Kanak The Titans made quite the splash within the first five picks of the draft, by passing on Arvell Reese and drafting WR Carnell Tate. This pick also served as the first insight into how that all-important Saleh-Daboll dynamic was going for Tennessee, as Daboll got his new toy before the head coach did. The Titans used a second first-round pick on Auburn edge Keldric Faulk. Faulk feels like a perfect Saleh-type defender with his length off the edge, and pairing a similar type rusher in Jermaine Johnson could give the Titans a formidable duo on the outside, with Solomon Thomas, John Franklin-Myers, and Jeffery Simmons remaking the defensive interior. Behind this defensive front, the Titans also drafted an athletic freak in Anthony Hill Jr. out of Texas as a high-value pick in the second round. The Titans found Dike, Helm, and Ayomanor as pass catchers for their rookie quarterback in the same draft last year, and circled back to grab their potential star of this group in Tate this April. They then got to work bolstering the defense. If these picks hit yet again, this will be a team that has a chance to build on some late season improvement last year and truly find out who their core to build around for years to come can be in 2026. Titans 2026 Coaching Staff * New to staff this season: Head Coach Robert Saleh Offensive Coordinator Brian Daboll Offensive Line Carmen Bricillo Wide Receivers Greg Lewis Quarterbacks Shea Tierney Defensive Coordinator Gus Bradley Linebackers Dave Borgonzi Defensive Backs (Nickel) Dalton Hilliard Safeties Marquand Manuel Defensive Line Aaron Whitecotton With so much talk about what Saleh and Daboll will bring to the Titans this season in year one for both coaches, it’s no surprise to see a list of other new coaches this season riddled with ties to the previous stops both these former HCs have made. Carmen Bricillo was the Giants offensive line coach from 2024 to 2025, and new QB coach Shea Tierney was their pass game coordinator and QB coach during this time as well. Gus Bradley was the 49ers assistant head coach last year alongside Saleh, and while Aaron Whitecotton was with the Cowboys last year, he was a valued member of Saleh’s staff going back to the Jets tenure. Dave Borgonzi was with the Cowboys as linebackers coach last year as well, so this will be a prove-it game for the rebuilt Dallas defense to show they’ve put 2025’s failure behind them and give their team an advantage against an offense that will start 2026 as an unknown. By Week 11, this Titans offense could be a real threat, and for Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys offense, calling plays against Saleh’s defense will be something to follow closely as well. The Cowboys need to avoid this being a letdown game going into Thanksgiving, looking for their first home win against the Titans since 2002. full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Tyler Guyton #60 and George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys react to a successful two-point conversion during the second half of the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have spent a lot of time over the last few months thinking about what the Dallas Cowboys are building for the 2026 NFL season. Really, we started back in March when free agency opened up, and haven’t stopped through the draft, OTAs, training camp, preseason, and now we sit on the very precipice of the 2026 season. So how have the Cowboys done? We turn to some statistical models and expert input from ESPN to consider some answers. Of course we need context for this, and a team’s recent accomplishments or failings lean into a lot of what is predicted. For instance, the Cowboys are coming off two straight years of missing the playoffs. That will cool down any hot predictions for playoff success. They are also revamping a historically bad defense. It requires a leap of faith to believe they’ll settle that in one offseason. So enough preamble, let’s see some of what ESPN has to say about the Cowboys upcoming season. The headline gave away some of the game. The Cowboys have a 51.9% chance of making the playoffs. Does that sound right to you? Probably not based on the optimism that has invaded the fanbase’s thinking this offseason. Question 1: What percentage chance would you give the Cowboys to make the playoffs this year? ESPN gives Dallas a 33.9% chance of winning the division, behind the Eagles who are at 46.3% chance. (Good luck Washington and New York). They have the Cowboys with a projected win total of 9.2 wins. We’ll round that off to 9-8 record. The Cowboys went 7-9-1 last year in a poor season. Only two more wins on the year feels somewhat low. Does it to you? Question 2: What record would you give the Cowboys for the end of the year? ESPN projects a top-end/low-end spread of a 12-5 record down to 7-10. One item playing into that is the Cowboys schedule which is ranked as fourth-hardest in the NFL. Finally, they asked respected Cowboys observer Todd Archer to weigh in with what should be considered a success for the season. Archer said a return to the playoffs. Is that your benchmark? Do you feel like they need to do more to be a success? Or is it more about success being a fixed defense and a balanced team for the future? Question 3: What would you consider success for the Cowboys in 2026? Hit the comments and let us know how you feel about these data points.

title: The quiet shift reshaping the Cowboys
summary: The Cowboys may have quietly changed what they’re looking for in a football player. Not necessarily bigger. Not necessarily faster. Not necessarily more talented. Just more serious. Call them “Serious Dudes“, with a hat tip to Voch Lombardi for the moniker. It’s not a scientific category, and it’s certainly not a requirement that every player […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: The Dallas Cowboys huddle during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Minnesota Vikings on December 14, 2025 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cowboys may have quietly changed what they’re looking for in a football player. Not necessarily bigger. Not necessarily faster. Not necessarily more talented. Just more serious. Call them “ Serious Dudes “, with a hat tip to Voch Lombardi for the moniker . It’s not a scientific category, and it’s certainly not a requirement that every player walk around the facility looking like he’s preparing for a tax audit. It’s more about how a player approaches the job: preparation, accountability, doing his assignment, competing through the whistle, and not needing every moment to become a personal statement. The Cowboys have always had players like that. Every successful team does. What’s interesting is how many of them now seem to be showing up on this roster. And that makes me wonder whether Brian Schottenheimer has quietly started putting more emphasis on a quality that doesn’t show up particularly well on a draft board or salary-cap spreadsheet: professionalism. The new generation of Cowboys Start with Tyler Booker: The second-year guard was identified as a natural leader before he had even played his first NFL season, then followed that up with more than 1,000 snaps and 14 starts as a rookie. Now, just one year into his career, Booker is already part of the Cowboys’ 11-man Leadership Council . That’s not necessarily because he’s the loudest player in the room. It’s because the organization appears to trust him to help set the standard. Then there’s Caleb Downs. Downs is an even more interesting case because the expectations attached to him go well beyond simply playing good football. Dallas traded up to select Downs 11th overall, and the conversation around him quickly became about influence as much as ability. Mel Kiper called him a “ culture changer ,” while NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein described him as a “ culture piece ” for a Dallas defense that badly needed one. But perhaps the most telling assessment came from inside the Cowboys’ locker room. When DeMarvion Overshown was asked about Downs, he didn’t talk about giving a rookie time to adjust to the NFL. He said the Cowboys weren’t even looking at Downs as a rookie. They were looking at him as someone who could “change this defense around” and “change the culture.” That’s a remarkable expectation to place on a player who hasn’t yet played an NFL snap. And it tells us something about what the Cowboys think they drafted. Downs isn’t simply expected to be a good safety. He’s expected to be an influence. Of course, Downs hasn’t yet established himself as a locker-room leader. But the Cowboys expected that potential to be part of his value when they traded up to get him. And then there is the rest of the next generation. Jaishawn Barham might be the clearest example of the type. The rookie linebacker was one of the more talked-about players in training camp, and the description coming from the Cowboys themselves was almost tailor-made for this post: “ all business. ” Schottenheimer also highlighted Barham’s physicality, his ability to get off blocks, and his versatility. Malachi Lawrence is a quieter example. The first-round pick hasn’t attracted anything like the attention surrounding Downs, but his early approach has been refreshingly straightforward: learn from the veterans, understand what it means to be a professional, and work on the technical details of his game. That doesn’t prove Lawrence will become a leader in Dallas. It doesn’t even tell us what kind of personality he’ll have five years from now. But it is another example of the type of player the Cowboys appear to be bringing into the building. Donovan Ezeiruaku is a slightly different case. There is plenty of evidence of the work ethic and football intelligence Dallas likes, and the second-year edge rusher has talked about the importance of standards and learning from veterans . The Cowboys’ training-camp coverage has also highlighted his knowledge and experience. But Ezeiruaku also plays with an edge. His involvement in several training-camp fights was a reminder that taking football seriously doesn’t necessarily mean being emotionless. A Serious Dude doesn’t have to be boring. He can be intense. He can be emotional. He can be loud. The distinction is what happens when the helmet comes off. The veterans who changed the locker room The pattern becomes more visible when you look at the veterans Dallas added. Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark are probably the two strongest examples. Neither needed the Cowboys to teach them how to be professionals. They came with established reputations, extensive NFL experience, and Pro Bowl credentials. Yet both quickly became central figures in the locker room. Williams arrived in the middle of last season, when the Cowboys’ defense was already in trouble. Nine months later, he has been elected one of only four team captains by his teammates . Clark was also voted a captain. The other two are Dak Prescott and Brandon Aubrey. That’s worth noting because the Cowboys have made a distinction this year between their Leadership Council and their team captains. The four captains were chosen entirely by player vote, with Prescott, Williams, Clark, and Aubrey receiving the most votes. Williams has also been unusually open about what he sees changing. After spending the final seven games of 2025 in a defense that was struggling badly, Williams recently described the defense’s progress as “ night and day. ” He credited the coaching, the talent, the daily competition, and the overall change in the way the unit approaches its work. That’s exactly the sort of thing that makes the Serious Dude theory interesting. It’s not just about individual personalities. It’s about what happens when you put enough of the right people together. Kenny Clark fits the same mold. Williams has talked about Clark as someone who holds people accountable and does things the right way, both on and off the field. Jalen Thompson provides another piece of the puzzle. The veteran safety was brought in to stabilize a secondary that badly needed it and was subsequently included in the Leadership Council. Rashan Gary adds another veteran presence to the defensive front, while Cobie Durant brings experience, versatility, and toughness to the secondary. Jonathan Bullard and Otito Ogbonnia are less obvious examples of the personality argument, but they matter in another way: they are experienced defensive linemen who add depth around Williams and Clark. And that’s an important distinction. Not every new player has to be a Serious Dude in the same sense. Some are simply evidence of a roster being built around more experience, physicality, versatility, and professionalism. The pattern emerges from the combination. Meet the Leadership Council Perhaps the most tangible evidence that this is about more than individual impressions is the Cowboys’ Leadership Council. The 11-player group consists of: Dak Prescott CeeDee Lamb Tyler Smith Tyler Booker Jake Ferguson Javonte Williams Quinnen Williams Kenny Clark Rashan Gary Jalen Thompson Bryan Anger That’s an interesting collection of players. It’s also interesting because Schottenheimer has made clear that this isn’t just a ceremonial group. He has said that the council could have included as many as 15 players, but he deliberately kept it smaller. More importantly, he described it as “ their council, it’s not mine. ” The players are expected to bring issues from the locker room to the coaching staff and help solve problems before they become bigger problems. That’s a very different concept from simply naming a few captains for the coin toss. And it tells us something about what the Cowboys value in their leaders. You don’t need to be the…
