title: Cowboys news: All eyes on T.J. Bass stepping in for Tyler Smith at LG
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are going to be without all-world left guard Tyler Smith for at least the first four weeks of the season, something head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced on Monday. Coach Schotty also confirmed it will be T.J. Bass starting in Smith’s spot. The biggest phase of the game the Cowboys will miss Smith […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 21: T.J. Bass #66 of the Dallas Cowboys lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at AT&T Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are going to be without all-world left guard Tyler Smith for at least the first four weeks of the season, something head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced on Monday. Coach Schotty also confirmed it will be T.J. Bass starting in Smith’s spot. The biggest phase of the game the Cowboys will miss Smith in is his run blocking, with the Cowboys also counting on a repeat performance by Javonte Williams at running back, and sorting out the pecking order behind with Malik Davis and Emari Demercado. Cowboys LG Tyler Smith to undergo thumb surgery, miss 4-6 weeks – Nick Shook, NFL.com A huge blow to the Cowboys offensive line just ahead of two divisional games to start the season. The three-time Pro Bowl guard and cornerstone of Dallas’ interior offensive line was not seen at Monday’s practice, leading to questions regarding his status. With the entire regular season ahead and the thumb injury limiting Smith, the guard felt now was the best time to have the issue fixed, per Schottenheimer. “Just at the end of the day, he felt like he couldn’t do the things he had to do at a high level,” the coach said Monday. “We know this is a long season. It’s unfortunate but that’s why we coveted T.J. Bass and having T.J. Bass back. I think he’s played a lot of really good football for us, and we expect that he’ll continue to do so.” Cowboys have a ‘ton of confidence’ in T.J. Bass filling in for Tyler Smith – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com T.J. Bass has been called on and played well before, and the Cowboys will need more of it as he starts the season at left guard. During training camp, Bass would often times get work with the first-team offensive line in team drills when Schottenheimer and the Cowboys staff would give Smith less snaps in order to manage his workload as a veteran. Schottenheimer hopes those reps will pay off in a game setting. “Offensive line play is tied together,” Schottenheimer said. “We’ve gone into games with four new starters on the offensive line. I’m very, very confident that this group will play well against a really good front. I have great confidence in T.J. Bass. He’s extremely bright, very physical, great athlete. He’ll do a marvelous job for us, I’m sure, stepping in.” What T.J. Bass’ stats tell us about replacing Tyler Smith – Brandon Loree, Blogging The Boys Bass is a player the team can trust to not allow quarterback Dak Prescott to take unnecessary hits. Despite average overall stats for his position, the Cowboys could hang their hat on how efficient Bass was in limited reps. He started in games against the Green Bay Packers, New York Jets, Carolina Panthers, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders. He allowed zero sacks last year (T-1st among all 82 guards), had four pressures allowed (second best), and a 99.0 pass-blocking efficiency grade (first). A small sample size to be sure, but he acquitted himself very well. Brian Schottenheimer raises important question about Cowboys offense by answering another – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports Not having Tyler Smith at left guard will put a bigger magnifying glass on Tyler Guyton at left tackle, who the Cowboys will need to stay healthy to avoid going into the further depths of their OL backups. This is a big mystery for a Cowboys offense preparing to start a left tackle who has dealt with injuries in his first couple of NFL seasons. It’s a significant question, and Dallas does not have a firm answer right now. When push comes to shove, I think the Cowboys would end up giving Jones a shot at left tackle. But right now it doesn’t sound like they’re giving him swing tackle treatment. Emari Demercado may be more than just the Cowboys’ third RB – Jess Haynie, The Landry Hat It will be fun to see how RB Emari Demercado’s role develops as the season goes on. When Dallas added Demercado, his profile immediately sounds like a prototypical backup for Javonte Williams . He’s a patient runner with good vision, not adverse to contact while also having breakaway speed . He’s also a proficient receiver and pass blocker, both especially valuable for whoever spells Williams on third-down plays. Demercado is also noted as a “four-core” special teams player, meaning he can play on every unit. This is also a positive point on Davis’ resume, further showing their similarity. Giants cut Darius Slayton – Michael David Smith, Pro Football Talk A roster move for Dallas’ week one opponent ahead of Sunday night. The move comes as a surprise if only because of Slayton’s contract: Just last year, he signed a three-year, $36 million contract, and he is guaranteed $9.75 million this year. Cutting him only saves the Giants $2.5 million, but apparently they’re down enough on him that they thought that savings was worth sending him packing. The Giants presumably tried to trade Slayton before cutting him and found that no one wanted to trade for that contract. Daily discussion question: Which player on the Giants concerns you the most?
author: Sean Martin

title: Broncos at Chiefs preview: Denver aims for fast start
summary: The wait is over. This is true on multiple levels. The Denver Broncos will open the season. And quarterback Bo Nix is set to return to the field after an ankle injury ended his and the Broncos’ season. But there is something different about this season opener. Denver is coming off its best season in […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball for a touchdown against the Kansas City Chiefs during the third quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The wait is over. This is true on multiple levels. The Denver Broncos will open the season. And quarterback Bo Nix is set to return to the field after an ankle injury ended his and the Broncos’ season. But there is something different about this season opener. Denver is coming off its best season in a decade, having hosted and played in the AFC Championship Game, claimed the No. 1 seed in the AFC, won the AFC West, and beaten Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in one of the best wins in franchise history. Now, can Nix and the Broncos build off that incredible season and take the next step to the Super Bowl? The first test comes on Monday Night Football against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. FanDuel Sportsbook currently has Denver as the slight road underdog to its division rivals. The Broncos are +2.5-point underdogs to host Kansas City. The total sits at 43.5 points, with a lean toward the under at -112. Offensive Rankings (2025) Denver : Tenth in total offense (352.1 yards per game), 18th in rushing offense (118.3 YPG), eighth in passing offense (233.9 YPG), 13th in scoring offense (24.1 points per game). Kansas City : Thirteenth in total offense (342.9 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (109.7 YPG), ninth in passing offense (233.2 YPG), 20th in scoring offense (22.5 points per game). Defensive Rankings (2025) Denver : Fourth in total defense (291.6 yards per game), second in rushing defense (90.2 YPG), 10th in passing defense (201.4 YPG), fifth in scoring defense (19.7 points per game). Kansas City : Tenth in total defense (307.9 yards per game), ninth in rushing defense (103.4 YPG), 12th in passing defense (204.5 YPG), fourth in scoring defense (19.6 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Monday night’s game. Start fast This applies to Monday’s game and the season. One of the reasons Nix and the Broncos had so many comeback wins last season is that the offense started slow. The best way to ensure you don’t have so many come-from-behind, one-score wins in 2026 is to have the offense consistently start games faster. There’s no better time for that than Monday Night Football in Kansas City to open the season. And why not do so in Davis Webb’s first game as the offensive playcaller? Send a message to the rest of the NFL. On the first play from scrimmage, dial up a deep shot to Jaylen Waddle and test that Chiefs secondary. Coming away with an opening-drive touchdown on offense puts Denver in a great position to start the season with a big road win. — Ian St. Clair Stop the run Make the Chiefs one-dimensional. Force Patrick Mahomes to prove he can carry his team with a surgically repaired knee. — Adam Malnati Close the deal on third downs Whether on offense or defense, the Broncos will win if they beat the Chiefs on third down. — Tim Lynch Score more points than KC This will be a tough opening week matchup, but the key to the game remains the same. Score more points than the other team. According to advanced metrics, the Broncos are undefeated when they score more points than their opponents. So, if they do that on Monday Night, they will defeat their division rivals and start the year 1-0. — Scotty Payne Win the turnover battle Creating more turnovers has been a focal point of the team’s defense all season long. In order to win on the road at Arrowhead, the Broncos have to be on the right side with respect to turnover margin. Whether it’s a key interception, a strip sack, or a force fumble elsewhere, the Broncos’ defense has to make a few big plays to come out of Kansas City with a victory in Week 1. — Christopher Hart Test Chiefs secondary Push matchups hard against the Chiefs’ reconstructed secondary. That unit is debuting three new starters and trying to replace a whopping 2,415 defensive snaps vacated by McDuffie, Watson, & Cook. With 29-year-old L’Jarius Sneed bracketed by two young CBs, that secondary should present some big-play opportunities with the talent matchups the Broncos’ WR group and receiving RBs bring to the table. Let’s see Waddle & Sutton debut a Thomas & Sanders style lightning & thunder WR duo in strong fashion. — Taylor Kothe Force second- & third-&-long The Broncos defense allowed a league-best 4.0 yards per play on first down in 2025 and only 15% of first downs on first down — also league-best. They need to continue that against the Chiefs on Monday night. Get them off schedule and force them into second, third, and long counts. The Broncos need to take advantage of the weak KC offensive tackles and bring pressure with four, which will force Mahomes to make throws into tight windows, leading to incompletions and turnovers. — Joe Mahoney What are your keys to Monday’s game?
author: Ian St. Clair

title: NFL picks and predictions: Broncos vs. Chiefs and the rest of Week 1
summary: Finally, the 2026 NFL season is upon us. With that, it’s the return of my weekly straight-up picks for every game. My 2024 NFL regular season picks record was 190-72. Last season, I regressed and finished with a 178-94 record. Let’s see if I can start this year off on a high note with my […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 21: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos looks on before a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Tyler Schank/Clarkson Creative/Getty Images) | Getty Images Finally, the 2026 NFL season is upon us. With that, it’s the return of my weekly straight-up picks for every game. My 2024 NFL regular season picks record was 190-72. Last season, I regressed and finished with a 178-94 record. Let’s see if I can start this year off on a high note with my slate of Week 1 picks. New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks — Wednesday Night Football What a game to start the season. A rematch of last year’s Super Bowl. Can Drake Maye elevate his play in Year 3 against top defenses? Can the Seahawks running game, now led by rookie Jadarian Price, be consistent enough to replace the lost production of Kenneth Walker III? Only time will tell. But for this game, I’m taking the defending champs at home. Winner: Seahawks San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams — Thursday Night Football Thursday Night Football kicks off this year with a bang in an NFC West matchup. I’m interested in seeing how the revamped wide receiver corps of the 49ers performs. For the Rams, I’m intrigued with the various upgrades they made to bolster their defense. I expect this to be a close division rivalry game, but am giving the nod to the Rams. Winner: Rams Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals — Sunday (Early Game) I think this will be one of the more fun early games to watch on Sunday. I anticipate this game is going to be a high scoring affair. I’m giving the edge to the Bengals here. The Buccaneers have five new starters on defense, three of them being rookies, and it may be a while before they are firing on all cylinders. Winner: Bengals New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions — Sunday (Early Game) The Lions are coming off a disappointing 9-win season despite having a Top 5 offense in the NFL in ’25. In my opinion, they have a good shot at reclaiming their spot as kings of the NFC North. I believe the Lions will earn a decisive victory over the Saints for the first game of the season. Winner: Lions Baltimore Ravens at Indianapolis Colts — Sunday (Early Game) This is an intriguing matchup. Both of these teams faltered last year and missed out in a tough AFC race for the playoffs. In my opinion, this game will come down to who wins in the trenches. Baltimore’s revamped offensive line or the Colts’ rising defensive front seven? I’ll push my chips in for the Ravens—making them my first road team victor of Week 1. Winner: Ravens Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers — Sunday (Early Game) I don’t have much to say about this game. Long story short, I think the Falcons won’t be good this year and will be in the running for a Top 5 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. I’ll take the Steelers at home. Winner: Steelers Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers — Sunday (Early Game) This NFC matchup features two division winners from last season. I don’t think the Panthers are poised to repeat as NFC South champions. However, the Bears certainly have the talent to challenge for a second consecutive NFC North title. I’ll be taking Chicago on the road in this one. Winner: Chicago Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars — Sunday (Early Game) I really like what the Browns were able to cook up in the draft this past April. I’m just not confident an offense with seven new starters led by Deshaun Watson will be that competitive this season. I think the Jaguars will win this one quite handily. Winner: Jaguars Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans — Sunday (Early Game) This is one of my favorite matchups of the weekend. Two AFC playoffs teams last year trying to start off the season with a big victory. The Texans have one of the best defenses in the NFL, but Josh Allen is arguably the best offensive player in NFL. I think this will be a close one but have Allen and the Bills finding a way to win on the road. Winner: Bills New York Jets at Tennessee Titans — Sunday (Early Game) I honestly have a hard time getting a read on this one. Both teams had some drastic offseason changes and will be starting at least eight new players on their rosters for the upcoming season. I’ll just go with my gut and say Cam Ward will have a big day against a Jets defense that was one of the worst in the NFL a season ago. I’m taking the home team here. Winner: Titans Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders — Sunday (Afternoon Game) Easily one of the most boring games all weekend long. Two bad teams going head-to-head isn’t much fun to write about. Truth be told, the Dolphins could very well wind up being the worst team in football this year. I’ll be going with the Raiders at home. Winners: Raiders Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings — Sunday (Afternoon Game) A classic NFC North rivalry matchup is a great way for Packers and Vikings fans to begin their ‘26 gridiron campaigns. Quite frankly, I’m worry about both team’s running games. I think that could be an issue for both of them this season. For this matchup, I’m banking on Kyler Murray having a big debut for the Vikings in front of a sellout crowd in Minneapolis to earn them the ‘W’. Winner: Vikings Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Commanders reversed their record last season (5-12) compared to an impressive 12-5 outing in 2025. I expect them to be more competitive this season, but going up against the Eagles in an NFC East rivalry matchup to start the season is a tough draw. I think the Eagles come up with a big divisional win on Sunday. Winner: Eagles Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) I’m not sure that the Cardinals have what it takes on offense to take down the Chargers on the road. I think their rushing attack with Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier will be formidable. But will Jacoby Brissett be able to dial up the heat against a quality Chargers defense? I’m not so sure about that. I’m taking Los Angeles in this one. Winner: Chargers Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants — Sunday Night Football Sunday Night Football is a classic NFC East rivalry matchup. I think the Giants will be a lot better than last year with their additions and John Harbaugh coaching them, but I think Dak Prescott and the Cowboys offense will come out hot and put up some points in primetime against the Giants defense. Winner: Cowboys Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs — Monday Night Football This is a tremendous matchup to end the Week 1 slate of games. Can Bo Nix make a big jump in Year 3? Will Patrick Mahomes be able to revert to pre-ACL injury form? Those are two big questions that loom large for me for both teams this year. My gut tells me this is going to be a nailbiter, but I’m confident Denver can do enough to come out of Arrowhead with a big win against their AFC West nemesis. Winner: Broncos

summary: The hardest part about doing NFL power rankings for Week 1 is that no one really has any freaking clue where these teams should be. full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - FEBRUARY 11: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks raises the Lombardi Trophy during the Seattle Seahawks Super Bowl LX victory celebration and parade at Lumen Field on February 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The hardest part about doing NFL power rankings for Week 1 is that no one really has any freaking clue where these teams should be. We’re just projecting based on last season’s performance and the changes made over the offseason, but reality will be a completely new outcome. I decided to give the Super Bowl champions a break. They are the best until they prove otherwise. However, I did not give the benefit of doubt to some teams. I’m not a believer in the New England Patriots at all and totally believe last season was a fluke. We’ll see how that plays out for me. I actually believe any team in the Top 21 here are potential playoff contenders. That is how tight I think the 11-21 spots are. title: 2026 NFL predictions: Detroit Lions breakout player of the year
summary: Because the Detroit Lions didn’t make a ton of offseason adds, in order to improve in 2026, they’ll need several players to take the next step. The good news is there are plenty of candidates to have a breakout season this year. Our 2026 Detroit Lions season predictions series continues today with our staff picks […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Tyleik Williams (91) practices during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Because the Detroit Lions didn’t make a ton of offseason adds, in order to improve in 2026, they’ll need several players to take the next step. The good news is there are plenty of candidates to have a breakout season this year. Our 2026 Detroit Lions season predictions series continues today with our staff picks for 2026 Detroit Lions Breakout Player of the Year. And don’t forget you have the opportunity to cast your own vote at the bottom of the story. Previously: Offensive MVP predictions Defensive MVP predictions Who will be the Lions’ breakout player of the 2026 season? Al Karsten: Tate Ratledge, Tyleik Williams I’m going to keep it in the trenches, where the Lions’ first two draft choices of 2025, Tate Ratledge and Tyleik Williams, will transform their games by becoming more consistent overall while emerging as difference-makers on the interior of their respective sides of the ball. In the process, they’ll prove to be the next wave of young, homegrown pillars on this roster. With both players approaching the idealized versions of themselves already in Year 2, they’ll also be complemented by a trio of breakout rookies turning heads in the trenches: Blake Miller, Derrick Moore, and Skyler Gill-Howard. All three should provide dynamic flashes alongside an above-average level of play throughout the season as they steamroll past minimal early-season rookie bumps in the road. Together, that young group will help restore the identity of Dan Campbell’s gritty, tough, physical sons of guns—the type of team opponents don’t want to play because of the physical toll they’ll feel long after the final whistle. Erik Schlitt: Tyleik Williams The Lions’ defensive line showed a lot of improvement in training camp, and the play of second-year defensive lineman Tyleik Williams was a big part of that. Williams showed steady growth throughout his rookie season, but he looks like he’s capable of a huge sophomore jump in production this season. John Whiticar: Tate Ratledge There are a few returning players (Isaac Teslaa, Tyleik Williams) and a few rookies (Miller, Moore, Abney) that could stand out this year. However, I give the nod to Ratledge. I think this year, he could jump into the top-10 guards in the league and prove that he was not merely benefitting from playing next to Penei Sewell last season. Ryan Mathews: DJ Wonnum DJ Wonnum will be the Lions’ breakout player of 2026. Even though he just arrived in Detroit, Wonnum finds himself in one of the most coveted spots on a defensive line in the NFL, playing alongside Tyleik Williams, Alim McNeill, and Aidan Hutchinson. Anthony Balaj: Sione Vaki Vaki, the best pick of the 2024 draft class, earns a Pro Bowl nod as a special teamer, but also scores multiple offensive touchdowns. Brandon Knapp: Isaac TeSlaa, Nick Whiteside TeSlaa gets bumped up to the WR3 spot and with a rocky preseason, I think he can overcome those struggles and grow as a player. With LaPorta back, there should be less pressure from TeSlaa to excel, and less eyes focused on him. Defenses will overlook him still and I think he could have a solid contribution to the offense in 2026. Whiteside starts the year on the practice squad, but I don’t think that stay is long-term. He had an excellent preseason and deserves to be on the 53-man roster, arguably as the team’s CB3. I believe Whiteside will be given chances to play and excel with the chances he’s given. Morgan Cannon: Tyleik Williams I am going with defensive tackle Tyleik Williams. In terms of statistical production, the rookie out of Ohio State didn’t make massive waves during his 2025 rookie year. Still, there were plenty of flashes for Williams. Especially when you turn on the all-22 and watch how he takes on double teams and is able to help the interior defensive line collapse the pocket around opposing quarterbacks. If fellow defensive tackle Alim McNeill can return to pre-injury form and Williams takes the next step or two in his development, the Lions’ defensive front could be fun to watch. Jeremy Reisman: DJ Reed I feel we were robbed of seeing what DJ Reed is truly capable of due to his early hamstring injury in 2025. Thus far in camp, it looks like he has his explosiveness back. Plus, with—hopefully—an improved pass rush, it can take some pressure off of Reed and force some errant throws. I wouldn’t be surprised if he tallied a few interceptions this year while remaining a strong presence in the run game.

title: Detroit Lions scouting report: Are the Saints a sleeper in 2026?
summary: In what was the longest offseason since the end of the 2022 season, your Detroit Lions are back to playing meaningful football! Training camp and preseason are over, the rosters are finalized (for the most part), and the regular season has arrived. The Lions kick off at home in Ford Field to play the New […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints participates in warmups prior to an NFL Preseason 2026 game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what was the longest offseason since the end of the 2022 season, your Detroit Lions are back to playing meaningful football! Training camp and preseason are over, the rosters are finalized (for the most part), and the regular season has arrived. The Lions kick off at home in Ford Field to play the New Orleans Saints on Sunday in Week 1. The Saints are aiming to snag the NFC South divisional crown for the first time since 2020 and have higher expectations than last season. While most don’t believe this team can win it all, some think they can compete in what is known as the NFL’s easiest division. They have a young roster, but also veterans who can help them improve on last year. An up-and-coming team like the Saints could make a statement with a win on the road against the Lions. Detroit, on the other hand, could use a win to start the season after how 2025 went for them. Let’s dive in on the Saints and how much they’ve improved ahead of Week 1. New Orleans Saints 2025 Season 6-11 record (4th in NFC South) 28th in points for, 16th in point allowed Overall DVOA: 28 (27th on offense, 13th on defense) 2025 was a slight improvement for the Saints over their 2024 campaign, with one more win. Expectations were low heading into last year, with question marks at quarterback and a new head coach in Kellen Moore. With a young roster, it was going to be a difficult season, but in the end, they came away with clearer answers and a vision for the future. At quarterback, former starter Derrick Carr retired in May 2025 for health reasons, leaving the Saints with 2024 fifth-round pick Spencer Rattler and 2025 second-round pick Tyler Shough to battle for the starting job. Rattler won the job, but not for the entire season. After going 1-7, he was benched and replaced by Shough, who finished the year with 2,384 yards, 10 touchdowns, and six interceptions—and a 5-4 record. Shough also found the end zone three times on the ground for 186 yards. The biggest issue for the Saints offensively, despite the early quarterback play, was the rushing attack. Starting running back Alvin Kamara finished last year with 471 yards and one touchdown (career lows), missing six games due to an MCL sprain, and the depth behind him was nowhere to be found. Devin Neal had 206 yards and two touchdowns, with other running backs like Audric Estime and Kendre Miller getting a combined 391 yards and two touchdowns. The leading scorer on the ground was Shough, which says a lot about the running back room. When it came to passing the ball, the Saints found a lot more success, especially with wide receiver Chris Olave, who had the best season of his career. Olave finished with 100 catches for 1,163 yards and nine touchdowns. Another contributor was Rashid Shaheed, who had 499 yards and two touchdowns, but he was traded to the Seattle Seahawks midseason. Tight end Juwan Johnson had a career season as well, finishing with 889 yards and three touchdowns on 77 catches. On defense, the defensive line shone brightest. EDGE Cameron Jordan led the team in sacks with 10.5 and forced two fumbles, but right behind him was EDGE Chase Young, who had 10 sacks and also forced two fumbles. The secondary was led by second-year cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry, who paced the team with three interceptions and 17 pass deflections. The Saints’ run defense is what held them in a few games, allowing just 4.0 yards per carry, which ranked seventh in the NFL. 2026 offseason Key additions: G David Edwards, RB Travis Etienne, RB Ty Chandler, LB Kaden Elliss, TE Noah Fant, EDGE Tyree Wilson (trade), K Daniel Carlson Key losses: CB Alontae Taylor, LB Demario Davis, TE Foster Moreau 2026 NFL Draft picks Round 1: WR Jordyn Tyson Round 2: DT Christen Miller Round 3: TE Oscar Delp Round 4: G Jeremiah Wright Round 4: WR Bryce Lance Round 5: S Lorenzo Styles Jr. Round 6: WR Barion Brown Round 7: CB TJ Hall Overall, the Saints have more talent coming in than leaving, a good sign that this team is headed in the right direction. Their biggest free-agent move was keeping Jordan around after he tested free agency for his final season. When it comes to new incoming talent, though, the biggest add was guard David Edwards. This should help both the pass and the run, with a veteran guard strengthening the front. The team also made a trade for Las Vegas Raiders EDGE Tyree Wilson, giving up a 2026 fifth-round pick to acquire him and a 2026 seventh-round pick, giving them a potential suitor to replace Jordan after he retires. Running back Travis Etienne should see ample playing time with Kamara currently dealing with an MCL sprain. Linebacker Kaden Elliss gives them a younger linebacker core as Demario Davis left. Another replacement is tight end Noah Fant, who takes the spot of Foster Moreau and gives the Saints another viable threat in the passing game. The addition of kicker Daniel Carlson gives the Saints a big upgrade at the position, as their previous kickers, Blake Grupe and Charlie Smith, combined for a 71 percent field goal percentage. The biggest loss, though, was cornerback Alonte Taylor, and the secondary could be tested early, with few moves to bolster it. The rookie class did add some much-needed depth. Getting three wide receivers, led by first-round pick Jordyn Tyson out of Arizona State. Tyson will miss at least the first four games of the season after being placed on IR with a hamstring injury. The Saints also got help on the interior defensive line with defensive tackle Christen Miller, and more depth at tight end with Oscar Delp. The offensive line has a potential future starter in guard Jeremiah Wright, and the secondary got a few late-round picks in safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. and cornerback TJ Hall. 2026 season outlook New Orleans has a bit higher expectations in 2026. They are still an underdog to win the NFC South (second in odds behind the Buccaneers), but this could be a year for them to finally be on top again. They have their quarterback in Shough, and he’s been given some upgraded weapons—though his biggest one is on the sidelines for the moment in Tyson. The team must improve its running game, and it made moves to address that, but with Kamara already dealing with an injury, the depth might be tested sooner than expected. On defense, it should be a slight improvement as the team got younger on that side of the ball, but lost key starters in Taylor and Davis. If the young guys can show out and fill the roles of the vets who came before them, there should be ample improvement. Moore will now be in his second year as a head coach, and that should give him a leg up on the year before, when everything was new and different. The NFC South is anybody’s game this season. The Carolina Panthers won the title last year at 8-9, and they aren’t the favorites to win the division again. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are currently the favorites, but they still have questions at wide receiver and on defense. The Atlanta Falcons could be uncertain at quarterback and just signed their star running back, Bijan Robinson, to a new contract. No team in the division is standing out as a clear-cut favorite, which could be the perfect time for the Saints to swoop in and get back in the playoffs. Injury notes Key players ruled out : DT Bryan Bresee (IR), RB Ty Chandler (IR), WR Jordyn Tyson (IR) Key players to monitor : RB Alvin Kamara (MCL), EDGE Cameron Jordan (hamstring), LB Pete Werner (groin), CB Quincy Riley (groin) Injuries have struck the Saints early this season at key spots. First, losing defensive tackle Bryan Bresee to a torn ACL back in July hurt the interior defensive line. Then losing Tyson for at least four games hurts the offense’s ability to move the ball through…

title: NFL Week 1 power rankings: National media mixed on Detroit Lions returning to form
summary: The Detroit Lions open the 2026 season with high expectations and feel good about how they’ve prepared for the regular season, but it appears most of the National media is going to need some convincing, as we can clearly see in our NFL Week 1 Power Rankings roundup. Let’s take a look at where the […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JULY 29: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions speaks during a press conference during Detroit Lions Training Camp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on July 29, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions open the 2026 season with high expectations and feel good about how they’ve prepared for the regular season, but it appears most of the National media is going to need some convincing, as we can clearly see in our NFL Week 1 Power Rankings roundup. Let’s take a look at where the national media believe the Lions stand entering the 2026 season in this week’s power rankings. ESPN: 8 (Previous rank: 15) From ESPN Staff, excerpt from Eric Woodyard : This season is a success if … the Lions return to the postseason. Detroit missed the playoffs for the first time since 2022 last season. The organization has committed over $1 billion in contracts and extensions over the past two years and is seeking a return on its investment. Sports Illustrated: 8 ( Previous rank: 18) From Connor Orr : Easy schedule + upgraded play-caller + a little bit more health and stability across the front seven = a nine win team from 2025 winning double-digit games in 2026. Certainly the secondary is a concern, but the way Detroit can deploy itself schematically, I’m less worried about the team getting gouged in the passing game. At the very least, the Lions can score enough to keep pace. The Athletic: 9 (Previous rank: 17) From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall : Mock’s projected win total: 10.3 After missing the playoffs last season, the Lions will benefit from one of this year’s easiest schedules. The division will be tough, but they have a new offensive coordinator in Drew Petzing and more depth on the defensive line. Still, the secondary could have some struggles early due to injuries to Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, each of whom begins the season on the PUP list. Yahoo Sports: 9 (Previous rank: 17) From Frank Schwab : The Lions traded David Montgomery and might regret it. Isiah Pacheco is on injured reserve with general manager Brad Holmes saying he is “hopeful” Pacheco returns this season. The current backups are Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki. They have a combined nine carries for 29 yards in the NFL. The Lions desperately need Jahmyr Gibbs to stay healthy. They are also very thin in the secondary to start the season. USA Today: 11 (Previous rank: 18) From Nate Davis : If you subscribe to the theory that good teams are strong up the middle … then this one could be in trouble with C Cade Mays and starting safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph all at least a month away from playing. At least the Lions can lean on RB Jahmyr Gibbs, though there’s zero safety net behind a bona fide star who’s played fewer than 60% of this offense’s snaps through the first three seasons of his career. NFL.com: 15 (Previous rank: 14) From Nick Shook : The sidelining of center Cade Mays (wrist) has me feeling uneasy about this offense as Detroit embarks on a new campaign. Tight end Sam LaPorta followed up back surgery with a hip injury in August, which isn’t great, but I think the Lions still have the edge over the Saints in Week 1. Sporting News: 15 (Previous rank: 16) From Vinnie Iyer : The Lions are facing their first real adversity in the Dan Campbell revival era, having missed the playoffs at 9-8 last season. The defense remains a work in progress behind Aidan Hutchinson. The offense is headed toward being more pass-reliant with Jared Goff. The Ringer: 16 (Previous rank: 16) From Diante Lee : This might be the most banged-up team in football entering Week 1. Safeties Brian Branch (torn Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (bone bruise) still haven’t returned to practice after season-ending injuries last year. Cornerback Terrion Arnold was waived earlier in the offseason as a result of his arrest on eight felony charges, including armed robbery and kidnapping, in Florida. Backup running back Isiah Pacheco is dealing with a back injury that landed him on IR, and the Lions don’t have enough quality running back depth behind Jahmyr Gibbs for me to feel good. The Lions have been marred by injury issues like these the past few seasons, but I refuse to rank them lower than 16th because their championship potential is still evident. They could have the best offense in football. Receiver Jameson Williams is the Detroit offensive player I’m most excited to watch this season. If he lights up defenses deep downfield to start the season, the attention opponents will have to devote to him will open up the offense for everyone else. CBS Sports: 19 (Previous rank: 18) From Pete Prisco : They will again score a lot of points on offense, but there are issues on defense. The secondary is a mess.

title: 6 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ associate/assistant head coaches Week 1 pressers
summary: The Detroit Lions have a pretty unique power structure amongst their coaching staff this year. Scottie Montgomery, previously the assistant head coach and running backs coach, is now the associate head coach and wide receivers coach. That left the assistant head coach job vacant, which was then tacked on to safeties coach Jim O’Neil’s official […]
full_text: Detroit Lions assistant head coach and running backs coach Scottie Montgomery speaks during OTA at Detroit Lions headquarters and training facility in Allen Park on Thursday, May 30, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions have a pretty unique power structure amongst their coaching staff this year. Scottie Montgomery, previously the assistant head coach and running backs coach, is now the associate head coach and wide receivers coach. That left the assistant head coach job vacant, which was then tacked on to safeties coach Jim O’Neil’s official title. On Tuesday, both assistants were available to the media and offered a lot of insight into the Lions’ 2026 season and Week 1 vs. the New Orleans Saints. Here are my biggest takeaways from their media sessions: The Lions just completed one of their best training camps All offseason, the Lions preached that they were going to treat this offseason differently, with an emphasis on getting back to the basics and increasing competition within their own ranks. With no joint practices and 19 training camp sessions—including three scrimmage-style practices—both Montgomery and O’Neil spoke about how much progress they made in the past month. “This was a tough training camp,” Montgomery said. “[…] I thought Coach (Campbell) was just exceptional. He told you he was going to challenge the players; he told us he was going to challenge the coaches. Nobody coming into camp to practice against in camp made it even more competitive. We’re right where we need to be, in my opinion, at this point in time with physicality, with our scheme, our quarterback, our defensive quarterback Jack Campbell.” “This was as hard of a camp as I’ve been around,” O’Neil said. “We got after it, and I think that everybody got better. Offensively, defensively. We’re going against, for four weeks, you’re going against Jamo, and Jah, and Saint, LaPorta, Jared, and Penei; you can’t help but get better. And I think that the guys did a great job making everybody better. It was a hard camp. We got after it. You guys were out there, so I think we’re ready. I think guys are ready to hit somebody else.” Lions confident in starting safeties Chuck Clark, Avonte Maddox The Lions would obviously be better off if their starting safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph were healthy and at their best, but the Lions spent their offseason preparing for them to miss some time. Since the beginning of training camp, veterans Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox have held down the starting positions, and O’Neil showed a lot of faith in both on Tuesday. Particularly, he’s been impressed with how Maddox has grown into the position after entering last season as an option at nickel. After spending most of the 2025 regular season learning—and playing—the position, Detroit believes the veteran defender has grown into a legitimate safety. “Now he’s a pretty damn good safety,” O’Neill said. “I think him and Chuck, both, their ability to process information pre-snap and then put themselves or their teammates in position to make plays is what really stands out to me as their superpower.” “It’s pretty cool what’s going on right now in the middle of our defense with Jack Campbell, Avonte Maddox, and Chuck—when the three of them are out there together,” O’Neill continued. “Because they can handle a lot of scheme, checking, and they do a great job communicating with the guys on the outside.” Those communication skills are going to be huge in Week 1, when the home Ford Field crowd is expected to be extremely loud when the defense is on the field. But Detroit will be plenty prepared on Sunday “There’s no excuses,” O’Neil said. “You’ve got to get the whole call. And if the call calls for us to check, then it’s your job to communicate to the people around you to make sure that everybody in the back seven or on the entire defense gets the check.” Don’t forget about Thomas Harper When O’Neil was asked about the starting safeties, he started by noting that Thomas Harper needs to be included in that conversation. “Yeah, and I would throw Thomas Harper into that group, too,” O’Neil said. “He’s come on, unbelievably, as a young safety.” Harper is only entering his third NFL season after going undrafted in 2024. A waiver claim just before the 2025 season starter, Harper really started to come on toward the middle of this year’s training camp. “Before he rolled his ankle and missed the last couple weeks of practice, I thought he had his best week—that third week of training camp,” O’Neill said. “He’s the safety that is really good in space when it comes to tackling. He can go get the ball in the deep part of the field, which is a rare characteristic.” Those are exactly the traits the Lions had in Kerby Joseph, so it wouldn’t be surprising to see Harper make it on the field this year. In fact, O’Neil hinted that they may end up using all three of their top safeties. “I think all three are really different. I think that they all are going to help us,” O’Neil said. “I think that Shep’s doing an awesome job of putting those three guys and putting packages in where they can be at their best and do what they do best.“ How Tay Martin wowed the coaching staff Martin was one of the most unexpected stories for training camp, and his placement on the 53-man roster is a testament to how he went from tryout player during the spring to a standout amongst a very deep receiver room. Montgomery explained how Martin impressed the coaching staff every step of the way, from his tryout during OTAs all the way through the end of camp: “This kid, from Day 1, we worked him out. I had the ability to work him out, of course, and his movement skills were fantastic. So that’s what gets the eye of a lot of people, the movement skills. But you still don’t see any kind of physical demeanor outside of tape until you put the pads on. What made him stand out is his physical demeanor in the run game. There is a stamp that we want that we’re known by here: our grit, our physicality in what we do. And we saw him in 1-on-1 situations in the hole, in the c-gap, on the perimeter, and he just continued to win those battles. And then when we transitioned into special teams, those battles showed up again. So, now, if I see the physicaltiy in the run game, I see you doing exactly what you’re supposed to be doing on special teams, mentally, as a coach, I’m going to start working and try to find out is there a way that we can see what you can do with the football. So then when we gave him opportunities to catch the football, he did a pretty good job. He came up to me a couple days in and told me he knew multiple positions. That caught my eye once again. So then I tested him at multiple positions, and he did a really good job of it. Then when we put him in in games, he made plays when he had the opportunity to make plays.“ Kelvin Sheppard has a ton of respect within the coaching staff “I think Shep is just a brilliant, brilliant mind,” Montgomery said unprompted in his opening statement. The two did their fair share of jawing during training camp, but it came out of both of their competitive nature and their mutual respect for each other. This offseason, Montgomery got to spend more time with Sheppard, and he learned to appreciate just how hard he works. “The biggest thing that I think you see with Shep is the mind is continually growing,” Montgomery said. “The research that he did this offseason—every time that I was in the building, I feel like he was in the building. […] I come in, he’s here, he’s researching. There’s people in places that he’s researched, whether that be professional, collegiate, the things we’ve done in the past here.” O’Neil respects the way Sheppard has communicated the standard and the scheme in Detroit over the past two offseasons. “He’s done an unbelievable job not only stamping (the defense) with what we believe in as far as how we’re going to play—what’s our defensive identity, what we want to put…

title: Lions injury update: Detroit enters Week 1 with clean bill of health
summary: The Detroit Lions had their first practice of Week 1 on Tuesday, and they started the day with about as good a health situation as you could hope for. Of the 52 players on their active roster and 16 players on the practice squad, every single one of them was on the field during Tuesday’s […]
full_text: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (14), center right, practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions had their first practice of Week 1 on Tuesday, and they started the day with about as good a health situation as you could hope for. Of the 52 players on their active roster and 16 players on the practice squad, every single one of them was on the field during Tuesday’s practice. Only practice squad offensive tackle Devin Cochran was not participating in individual drills, as he was working with a trainer during that portion of practice. Media is not privy to any other part of practice now that the team is in regular season mode. And the Lions won’t submit an official injury report until Wednesday. So we won’t know participation levels until that drops, typically around 4 p.m. ET. But everyone being out there for practice is fantastic news for the Lions. For one, it provides some reassurance that Detroit’s safety position is getting closer to full health. Christian Izien and Thomas Harper had missed some time at the end of training camp, but both had returned. Obviously, Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch remain on the Physically Unable to Perform list and won’t be able to play for at least the first four games. Although, a new NFL rule will allow both players to start practicing after two games, if either are ready. On Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Joseph was back in the building after leaving for personal reasons during training camp. Campbell’s update on his health was brief. “He’s here, he’s doing good, he’s ramping up,” Campbell said. Also notable was the return to practice of rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder. The Lions’ fourth-round pick had missed the last month of practice after suffering a leg injury early in camp, but he’s back. It’ll be interesting to see whether Rolder will play early in the season or if Detroit will need to see him ramp up and get some reps before trusting him with a gameday role. In the meantime, the Lions have six other rostered linebackers, including veteran Joe Bachie, who recently re-signed to the 53-man roster . While everyone on the Lions’ roster practiced on Tuesday, it’s important to also point out that there are still a handful of players who are not technically on the active roster, but remain part of the team on an injury list. That includes: Season-ending IR LB Damone Clark WR Kendrick Law EDGE Payton Turner IR, with possibility of a return C Cade Mays RB Isiah Pacheco Other lists: OT Giovanni Manu — Reserve/Non-Football Injury S Brian Branch — Reserve/PUP S Kerby Joseph — Reserve/PUP G/C Mason Miller — Practice Squad/IR
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit Lions considering left guard rotation for Week 1
summary: During training camp, the Detroit Lions were hoping to have a full-on competition between Christian Mahogany and Ben Bartch (also, Juice Scruggs) for the starting left guard job. Unfortunately, Bartch missed a good chunk of training camp with an injury, and Scruggs had to slide to center to replace the injured Cade Mays. That left […]
full_text: Detroit Lions offensive lineman Ben Bartch (78), left, offensive line coach Hank Fraley after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co During training camp, the Detroit Lions were hoping to have a full-on competition between Christian Mahogany and Ben Bartch (also, Juice Scruggs) for the starting left guard job. Unfortunately, Bartch missed a good chunk of training camp with an injury, and Scruggs had to slide to center to replace the injured Cade Mays. That left the job Mahogany’s to lose, and he never lost it. But on Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell revealed that the competition is very much ongoing this week between Mahogany and Bartch, who returned to camp for the last couple of weeks. The competition is so on that both players will be splitting first-team reps in practice this week. “This week is going to be—today, they’re going to split (reps),” Campbell said. “I see them splitting on Thursday. I see them splitting on Friday.” The battle is so close that Campbell is considering continuing that competition on Sunday by playing both players against the New Orleans Saints in Week 1. “If nothing has been decided by then, then maybe they both play,” Campbell said. Immediately, that will draw a negative reaction from Lions fans, who are still haunted by when former Lions coach Matt Patricia opted to run a guard rotation with Graham Glasgow, Kenny Wiggins, and Joe Dahl. But there is certainly a bit of a difference here. Detroit is still in the midst of determining their starter, thanks to the training camp injuries that delayed the competition. There’s enough reason to believe that eventually they will land on a starter, but that decision may not be made until we’re a few weeks into the season. Mahogany, the team’s sixth-round pick in 2024, has the advantage of being in the offense for now his third year, and he has 12 starts under his belt, but he’s coming off a tough year. This is Bartch’s first year with the team, but he brings loads of experience (including 24 starts) and clear support from a Lions coaching staff that has hyped him up since they signed him in free agency. “Bartch hasn’t been out there as much, but when he was out there, he was good,” Lions general manager Brad Holmes said last week. “He performed well; he just wasn’t able to be out there as much. But I would say last week with the practices, the scrimmage, and that preseason game, he earned his spot.” Because we’re no longer in training camp, media will only be able to see warmups and not be privy to the guard competition happening behind the scenes. But we will see, come kickoff, which player has at least temporarily won the left guard competition.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: 2026 NFL predictions: Detroit Lions defensive MVP
summary: While the Detroit Lions’ offense is filled with proven talent, the defensive side of the ball has a few more questions than answers. That said, there is still some top-end talent. In total, five Lions defenders have earned All-Pro or Pro Bowl honors: Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Devin White, Brian Branch, and Kerby Joseph. That’s […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - DECEMBER 24: Aidan Hutchinson #97 and Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions look on against the Minnesota Vikings in the second half at U.S. Bank Stadium on December 24, 2023 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Lions defeated the Vikings 30-24. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Detroit Lions’ offense is filled with proven talent, the defensive side of the ball has a few more questions than answers. That said, there is still some top-end talent. In total, five Lions defenders have earned All-Pro or Pro Bowl honors: Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Devin White, Brian Branch, and Kerby Joseph. That’s actually the exact same number as the offense (Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, Penei Sewell). So, maybe there are more candidates for the 2026 Detroit Lions defensive MVP than you think. As we continue our 2026 NFL predictions, here are our picks for Lions 2026 defensive MVP. Don’t forget to cast your vote at the bottom of the page! Previously: Offensive MVP predictions Who will be the Lions’ defensive MVP in 2026? Morgan Cannon: Jack Campbell Obviously, there is an argument to be made for the monster on the edge that wears #97, but I am going with Campbell because I think by the end of the season, he will be the unquestioned heartbeat of the defense. From racking up tackles, forcing fumbles, and being a general game-wrecker against opposing teams’ running games, he is also a seasoned veteran in defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s defense. Being able to ensure everyone is where they need to be, while also being in control of pre-snap checks and shifts, is going to pay huge dividends for the Lions in 2026. Al Karsten: Alim McNeill It hasn’t exactly been a fairytale 20-plus months for Alim McNeill since tearing his ACL in Week 15 of 2024, just two months after signing his blockbuster contract extension. But for the hip-hop artist who goes by “Dream,” the nightmare appears to be over—and his dreams are very much at the forefront of reality after a remarkably strong bounceback during Lions training camp. While the expectation is for Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell to continue their All-Pro-level play, McNeill has an opportunity to completely shapeshift this defense if he can consistently maximize his talents. If the version of McNeill who flashed from 2022-24 returns for a career year, Detroit suddenly has the makings of a lethal defensive front capable of helping propel this unit into the top 10. Like his draft classmate Milton Williams did for the Patriots after joining them last offseason, McNeill could provide the type of uplifting impact that helps spearhead a defense on a run to the Super Bowl. A season with 7+ sacks, 20+ quarterback hits, and 10+ tackles for loss would make Detroit a force to be reckoned with come January and February. Erik Schlitt: Aidan Hutchinson The Lions’ defensive line looked great in training camp and could be a huge catalyst in their defensive success. Hutchinson is already one of the best defensive players in the NFL, but with a healthy Alim McNeill, improved Tyleik Williams, along with DJ Wonnum and Derrick Moore splitting time on the opposite edge, Hutchinson should see his opportunities increase and could be in for a monster season. Jeremy Reisman: Aidan Hutchinson I believe Hutchinson is in for a career year. While I think his supporting cast is better, I don’t think that will draw any attention away from Hutch. But with some of the things we’ve seen in training camp, I don’t believe defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is just going to let teams add an extra tight end or running back to Hutchinson’s side and make him fight off double and triple teams every play. No, the Lions are committed to keeping their pass rush creative this year, and Hutchinson is going to EAT. John Whiticar: Jack Campbell In the past, Aidan Hutchinson was the clear-cut MVP on defense, but Campbell has now become 1B to his 1A. However, I think the Lions have added a lot of good defenders to pair with Hutchinson (Wonnum, Moore, Gill-Howard), and with Alim McNeill back and healthy, Hutchinson will no longer be leaned on as the only reliable lineman on the roster. Campbell, meanwhile, is far and away the Lions’ best linebacker, a position that is vital to every part of the defense. Ryan Mathews: Aidan Hutchinson Aidan Hutchinson will be the Lions’ defensive MVP in 2026. This is as talented and deep the defensive line has been in Detroit since Hutchinson arrived in 2022. And while Hutchinson will be a key part of game planning for any opposing offensive coordinator, there’s going to be plenty of chances for Hutchinson to make impact plays. Anthony Balaj: Brian Branch While Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson will likely be tapped with the All-Pro accolades, Branch will be the player that unlocks Kelvin Sheppard’s ability to dynamically disguise the defensive scheme (and likely land Sheppard a head coaching job in 2027). Brandon Knapp: Aidan Hutchinson While he was looking to be on a career season in 2024, that injury didn’t appear to slow him down as much in 2025. Now that he’s had a full year under his belt post-injury, and more help added to the opposite EDGE position and the interior defensive line, I think Hutchinson makes a true case for DPOY in 2026. The help fans have pleaded for has arrived, and I think Hutchinson will benefit the most out of it.

title: Detroit Lions open 2026 as big favorites over New Orleans Saints in Week 1
summary: The Detroit Lions will open their 2026 regular season against the New Orleans Saints, hoping to rebound from a disappointing 2025 season. The Lions will get the advantage of hosting this game in Detroit, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -6.5 points. The Saints finished 2025 with a 6-11 […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 03: Jameson Williams #9 of the Detroit Lions dives to score a touchdown in the fourth quarter against the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome on December 03, 2023 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions will open their 2026 regular season against the New Orleans Saints, hoping to rebound from a disappointing 2025 season. The Lions will get the advantage of hosting this game in Detroit, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -6.5 points . The Saints finished 2025 with a 6-11 record under first-time head coach (and former Lions backup quarterback) Kellen Moore. While they certainly underwhelmed, they finished the season strong, with four of those wins coming in the final five games of the regular season. “This is a hungry opponent,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Monday. “It’s a lot of young, hungry players, talented players. You could see their progression as the season went on last year; they started playing pretty good football—minus Atlanta, in that last game.” This offseason, the Saints prioritized upgrading their offense and plugging holes on defense. One of the Saints’ biggest offseason moves was upgrading their guard positions. They signed starting left guard David Edwards in free agency, then added rookie Jeremiah Wright (a fourth-round pick) to the mix to challenge Cesar Ruiz, who is entering his seventh year as a starter (mainly at right guard) for the Saints. They invested in youth at their skill positions, signing running back Travis Etienne to complement Alvin Kamara, but Kamara is dealing with an MCL injury and is expected to miss the opener. The Saints also drafted three wide receivers—Jordyn Tyson (first round), Bryce Lance (fourth), and Barion Brown (sixth)—and a tight end—Oscar Delp (third)—and all four are expected to contribute as rookies. Unfortunately, the Saints will have to wait to see the eighth overall pick take the field as Tyson landed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and will miss the first four games of the season; Lance is expected to start in his place. Delp will open the season as TE3 and will challenge free-agent acquisition Noah Fant for TE2 reps. On defense, the Saints lost one of their best players in starting linebacker Demario Davis, but re-signed Kaden Ellis to fill his role. Along the defensive line, 2023 first-round pick Bryan Bresee is out for the season with a torn ACL and is expected to be replaced by 2025 third-round pick Vernon Broughton. The Saints are banking on 2025 picks corner Quincy Riley (second) and nickelback Jonas Sanker (third) to step into vacated roles in their secondary. The Lions and Saints will square off on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Ford Field in Detroit.

title: Packers vs. Vikings Week 1 TV broadcast map shows wide coverage
summary: When the Green Bay Packers open up the 2026 season against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, they will do so with the eyes of most of the pro football world upon them. Sunday’s kickoff will take place at 3:25 PM Central time, and the vast majority of the United States will get to see the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - DECEMBER 29: Carrington Valentine #24 of the Green Bay Packers intercepts a pass intended for T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on December 29, 2024 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Brace Hemmelgarn/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Green Bay Packers open up the 2026 season against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, they will do so with the eyes of most of the pro football world upon them. Sunday’s kickoff will take place at 3:25 PM Central time, and the vast majority of the United States will get to see the game on local CBS affiliates. Week one is a doubleheader week for both FOX and CBS, one of the few weeks when each network gets to show a game in both the early and late Sunday afternoon time slots. CBS stations will carry one of Packers-Vikings or Cardinals-Chargers in the late game, while FOX stations get their pick of Commanders-Eagles or Dolphins-Raiders. Here’s a look at the initial broadcast map from 506sports.com, with Packers-Vikings in red: The blue areas will instead see Cardinals-Chargers, which will go out to those two teams’ home markets plus those of the other AFC West teams (the Raiders, Broncos, and Chiefs). On the call for the Packers’ opening game is CBS’ top commentating team. This year, Jim Nantz will be joined by color commentator J.J. Watt, who is stepping up from the network’s #2 squad to take the place that fellow Wisconsin native Tony had Romo previously occupied. Romo was suspended from CBS programming this summer after being arrested in Milwaukee for OWI, a charge to which he later pleaded no contest, and the network is reportedly negotiating a buyout of Romo’s remaining contract . This is the first of four games that the Packers are currently scheduled to play in the late afternoon “Game of the Week” time slot this season, though all four of those come in the first nine weeks of the season. Most of the country should expect to see all of those games, except for areas on the west coast that have home teams or divisional opponents also playing in that late time slot.

title: Green Bay Packers drop Week 1 depth chart: 6 takeaways
summary: The Green Bay Packers updated their depth chart on Tuesday, the first time that they’ve done so going into the 2026 regular season. For the most part, it looks accurate, based on our charting of preseason and training camp rotations, but there were a few things that stood out to me — so I want […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-December21: tight end Jonnu Smith (81) of the Pittsburgh Steelers stands on the field ahead of an NFL football game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, December 21, 2025. (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers updated their depth chart on Tuesday , the first time that they’ve done so going into the 2026 regular season. For the most part, it looks accurate, based on our charting of preseason and training camp rotations , but there were a few things that stood out to me — so I want to talk about them today. Disclaimer: I’m aware that the Packers probably put little to no mental energy into posting a public “unofficial” depth chart. A few things turned my gears, though. Running Back First of all, Kaleb Johnson was listed as the Packers’ third-string running back, which may not be a surprise to some — because he just got here a week ago . Personally, I still believe that Johnson will be the number two ball-carrier in Green Bay while Josh Jacobs is out , as Chris Brooks, who was listed as a second-stringer, is more of a blocking back than a true ball-carrier. Jonnu Smith While Johnson just got to Green Bay and seems too low on the depth chart, tight end Jonnu Smith, who was signed by the Packers the same day that the team traded for Johnson, is listed as the team’s second-string tight end behind Tucker Kraft. Smith has played for head coach Matt LaFleur when they were together with the Tennessee Titans, but I thought Smith’s standing going into Week 1 would be more of a question mark, considering he wasn’t signed with anyone this offseason — unlike Johnson, who at least went through training camp with the Pittsburgh Steelers. It’s going to be tough for the Packers to keep four tight ends active on gamedays (they have to scratch a minimum of five players from their 53-man roster), and Smith and Josh Whyle both overlap as off-ball move tight ends who are primarily pass-catchers. If Smith is already ahead of Whyle, who has been in the program for two years now, then Whyle’s time on the 53-man roster might be long. Mark Redman, who is sharing the third-string role with Whyle on the Packers’ depth chart, is a blocking tight end, a role that is much more valuable than Whyle filling in as Smith’s potential backup. If I’m guessing today, Whyle is probably going to be inactive against the Minnesota Vikings. Offensive Line The Packers’ starting offensive line was listed as Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Zach Bako-Bewele (left to right). That’s not really the question right now. It’s whether or not Banks (tendinitis in his knee) and/or Bako-Bewele (coming off a partially torn Patellar tendon) will be able to play a full 60 minutes this week. Rookie fifth-round pick Jager Burton was listed as the backup center on the depth chart, but don’t make too much of that. If Banks can’t go, it’ll be Burton at left guard (and it’ll be Anthony Belton at right tackle if Bako-Bewele isn’t playing). Even if Banks can play, I wouldn’t be surprised if Burton rotates at left guard. Defensive Line We never got the opportunity to see the entire defensive line healthy and active this summer, either on the Family Night broadcast or for preseason games. Because of that, we’re not really sure how the pieces of this puzzle are supposed to fit together. Devonte Wyatt has been a three-technique (a 3-4 defensive end role in Green Bay’s new scheme) his entire career, so we can plug him in as a starter there. To the surprise of many, the Packers bubble-wrapped Karl Brooks in the preseason and treated him as a true starter, and he’s another 3-4 defensive end type, not a nose tackle body. On Green Bay’s depth chart, the team listed both Wyatt and Brooks as the starting ends, with free agent signing Javon Hargrave as the starting nose tackle, one slot ahead of Jonathan Ford. It will be interesting to see just how many snaps Hargrave actually plays at the nose this year, as he looked a little out of place filling in that role with the Vikings last season. For what it’s worth, Ford got the “starts” as a true head-up nose tackle this preseason. The lone third-stringer on the line is camp sensation Anthony Campbell, who will probably be inactive in Week 1, unless Warren Brinson can’t suit up for action due to his calf injury. Brandon Cisse Two days ago we reminded everyone that rookie Brandon Cisse hasn’t been named a starting cornerback by the team , but I guess the depth chart release means that that’s no longer true. Yes, Cisse was listed as the starter opposite Keisean Nixon. Nixon has been handling the bulk of the left cornerback snaps with the first-team offense this summer, while Cisse and Carrington Valentine rotated at right corner. Going into Week 1, I’m assuming that Nixon will play left cornerback full-time while Cisse will get the “start” on the right, even if Valentine rotates in some at the position. For what it’s worth, Cisse is the only rookie starter listed on the depth chart for either the offense or defense. Returner Options One of the most inaccurate parts of the depth chart every year is who they list as the team’s returners, but I think the choices they listed as the second-string options behind receiver Skyy Moore actually make sense this time around. On punts, slot receiver Jayden Reed was listed as the number two returner. On kicks, the second-stringer is receiver Bo Melton. Melton, who does a lot on special teams without needing the ball in his hands, is generally the “off-returner” for the team, a role where he’s deep in the backfield on kicks but really fills in more as a lead blocker than a true returner. My question is whether the Packers would keep Melton as the “off-returner” if Moore ever went down (or was scratched), or if they would have someone else (like a J. Michael Sturdivant) fill in as the off-returner. I’m also unsure if Moore will keep the kick return job when receiver Savion Williams is activated off the injured reserve, but we have a few weeks to figure that one out.

title: Every Former Packer the Team Will See in the 2026 Season
summary: Last offseason, I ranked the former Green Bay Packers the team would face in the upcoming season based on how much it was gonna hurt to play against them. I specifically ranked them based on pure emotion mixed with how much the Packers could use them at that time. This season, there are a handful […]
full_text: Nov 23, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams (17) acknowledges the crowd after scoring a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last offseason, I ranked the former Green Bay Packers the team would face in the upcoming season based on how much it was gonna hurt to play against them. I specifically ranked them based on pure emotion mixed with how much the Packers could use them at that time. This season, there are a handful more former Packers they’re facing, including some they faced last year and some they haven’t. So this time we’re side-stepping the emotional rankings and looking at every familiar face they’ll see on their schedule. Let’s get to it! Week 1: @ Minnesota Vikings RB Aaron Jones LB Eric Wilson Both of these guys were with the Vikings last year, so it’s nothing new to see them again. Eric Wilson initially signed with the Vikings as a UDFA in 2017, years prior to being one of the only positives on the Packers special teams unit. Aaron Jones was #1 in my ranking last year and would have been high on that list this year taking into account the current Josh Jacobs scenario . Jones will always be the epitome of what the perfect player is: a great player on and off the field. I wish nothing but the best for that man in every facet of his life (except against the Packers). Week 2: @ New York Jets EDGE Kingsley Enagbare C Josh Myers TE/FB Andrew Beck Kingsley Enagbare is a player the team will miss this week after only keeping 4 edge rushers on their final roster due to Micah Parsons and Collin Oliver both starting the season with PUP and IR designations, respectively. Not only are they very thin at the position, but they also have a lot of unproven talent (side-eyeing you , Lukas Van Ness) so it’s not the best timing to face Enagbare, who was a solid backup when injuries piled up. Josh Myers they don’t miss at center, but it’d be nice to have Sean Rhyan as a swing lineman with all the shuffling going on amongst the offensive line due to injuries. Andrew Beck, well, he played 32 snaps for the Packers and I had to Google who he was because I don’t even remember him, so no comment needed there. Week 3: Atlanta Falcons EDGE Za’Darius Smith Za’Darius Smith recently shared that his main reason for retiring so suddenly last season was to spend time with his mother who is battling Alzheimer’s before she passed away, which was shortly followed by the death of his father and grandmother. All of those things are gutting enough on their own, but all of them happening in such a short period of time is heartbreaking. Therefore, despite him consistently taking shots at the Packers, I will not be making fun of him (again) for the captains patch necklace and Lions Super Bowl ring . Thank you. Onto Week 4. Week 4: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles This will be the first week this season Green Bay won’t see a familiar face on the field . However, Bucs head coach Todd Bowles was a member of the team’s player personnel staff in the ‘95-‘96 season, when the Packers won Super Bowl XXXI, so shoutout to him. Week 5: Chicago Bears EDGE Jonathan Garvin (IR) Jonathan Garvin was placed on IR by the Bears in late August and hasn’t played a snap for them. The thing he’s most known for in Green Bay is being cut on his birthday . That’s all I got (plus this terrible meme I made and never got to use, featuring a scene from Role Models ). Week 6: Dallas Cowboys EDGE Rashan Gary DT Kenny Clark ALRIGHT NOW WE’RE TALKING. When I wrote this last season, it was months before the Micah Parsons trade that sent Kenny Clark to the Cowboys, so he wasn’t on that list. This is also the week Parsons is eyeing as his most “optimistic” return to the field, so there’s lots of reunions going on. The Packers faced Kenny Clark last season in their tie at AT&T Stadium, but this marks Clark’s first return to Lambeau as a Cowboy, along with Rashan Gary, who was traded to Dallas for a fourth-round pick earlier this season. If Parsons is back this week, he’ll surely be on a snap count. However, I fully expect him to still make a bigger impact against his former team in limited snaps than we’ll see from Gary, which is nothing new . Week 7: @ Detroit Lions No one, surprisingly! Week 8: Carolina Panthers RB AJ Dillon LT Rasheed Walker AJ Dillon, a fan favorite to some, has already faced the Packers as an opponent during his underwhelming stint with the Eagles last year. Dillon signed with the Panthers this offseason but, like last season, isn’t expected to see the field much unless injuries pile up in that room. Rasheed Walker, however, is facing the Packers for the first time after the team let him walk without a deal this offseason in favor of their former first round pick, Jordan Morgan. Walker signed a one-year, $4 million contract with the Panthers a few days into free agency. The contract, worth up to $10 million with incentives, is likely a lot less than he was expecting which should make Packers fans feel pretty good about the defense lining up against him. Week 9: @ New England Patriots WR Romeo Doubs OL Greg Van Roten (yes, he’s still in the league) First of all, Greg Van Roten is a month older than me so if any of you call him old I am calling the police. Second-of-ly , I wrote in last year’s article about how surprised I was that he was still in the league, then immediately forgot it, I guess because I had the same thought when writing this article. If you can’t tell, I’m stalling so I don’t have to talk about Romeo Doubs. But yeah, Van Roten, that one guy who played for the Packers all those years ago is still in the league at 36 years old (don’t you dare say “old”). He was with the Giants last year, and has been a “just fine” veteran over the last 15 years. PFF ranked him 35th out of 81 guards last season, so, you know, good for him. OKAY FINE! I’ll talk about Romeo Doubs! I hate seeing him for another team. I don’t expect the Packers to miss him on the field despite Doubs being their healthiest WR last season. However, I personally will miss his hilarious and goofy moments the last few years and seeing his comedically giant guardian cap helmet making the most incredible catch you’ve ever seen out of nowhere! Are you happy now?!? Week 10: Minnesota Vikings See Week 1 Week 11: Bye Week (so here’s some Packers free agents still available) C Lucas Patrick CB Corey Ballentine CB Trevon Diggs CB Robert Rochell DT Dean Lowry DT Mike Pennel (lol) EDGE Preston Smith K Brandon McManus TE/FB Josiah Deguara TE John Fitzpatrick TE/QB Taysom Hill (technically, I guess) TE Marcedes Lewis WR Malik Heath WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling Week 12: @ Los Angeles Rams WR Davante Adams WHEW this one’s gonna hurt. The Packers already faced Davante Adams in 2023, when he was in his second season with the Las Vegas Raiders, but this is different. Adams shined last season with a better team and offense than he’s had since being traded from Green Bay ahead of the 2022 season. Davante Adams clearly still cherishes his time with the Packers and even expressed being open to return to the team last offseason before ultimately signing with the Rams. The Rams are a favorite to win it all this year and if the Packers can’t get a ring this season, I hope Adams gets one. Week 13: @ New Orleans Saints DL Colby Wooden Wooden was the guy the Packers traded to the Indianapolis Colts for LB Zaire Franklin, who was recently named a captain by the team. The Colts released Wooden during final roster cutdowns at the end of August and the Saints claimed him on waivers the next day. So, looks like the Packers handled that trade pretty well so far. Week 14: Buffalo Bills None! But shoutout to Micah Hyde anyway. Week 15: Miami Dolphins aka Green Bay South General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan Head Coach Jeff Hafley QB Malik Willis QB Kyle McCord S Zayne Anderson S Jaylin Simpson…
