title: Predict the Green Bay Packers’ final win total in 2026
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Packers fans and fans across the country. Week 1 of the NFL season brings optimism and excitement for fan bases all across the league. (Well, except for the Browns, perhaps.) But how shall […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 21: Green Bay Packers fans cheer against the Denver Broncos during the second half of a preseason game at Empower Field At Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Packers fans and fans across the country. Week 1 of the NFL season brings optimism and excitement for fan bases all across the league. (Well, except for the Browns, perhaps.) But how shall we measure that excitement for fans of the Green Bay Packers fans heading into the team’s season opener this Sunday? With surveys and numbers, of course! Our highly scientific survey system will tell us exactly what the Packers’ fan base expects from this team heading into the season. Today, we want your feedback on how many games you think the Packers will win in 2026 and whether you’re confident in the team’s direction overall. How many games will the Packers win? title: The Packers’ Week 1 X-factor is the health of Zach Bako-Bewele
summary: The Green Bay Packers coaching staff has been non-committal about right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele’s availability for Sunday’s game for a couple of weeks now. Bako-Bewele himself was confident he’d be ready for Week 1, but you’ve definitely heard more convincing statements of confidence than this one: Offensive coordinator and former offensive line coach Adam Stenovich […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - DECEMBER 23: Guard Zach Tom #50 of the Green Bay Packers enters the field during player introductions prior to an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints, at Lambeau Field on December 23, 2024 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers coaching staff has been non-committal about right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele’s availability for Sunday’s game for a couple of weeks now. Bako-Bewele himself was confident he’d be ready for Week 1, but you’ve definitely heard more convincing statements of confidence than this one: I asked #Packers RT Zach Bako-Bewele if he feels ready for Week 1. This was his response: @fox11news pic.twitter.com/KMBDCAEDso — Michael Gross (@MichaelSGross) August 26, 2026 Offensive coordinator and former offensive line coach Adam Stenovich gave us an “ if ” he plays answer on Tuesday. Adam Stenavich says he expects to see an “elite” Zach Bako-Bewele on Sunday. “If” he’s out there, Stenavich adds. Sounds like the hope is he plays the entire game after offseason knee surgery to repair a partially torn patellar tendon. pic.twitter.com/x8MWFbtD79 — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) September 8, 2026 The entirety of the game may hinge on whether or not he does play. It’s no secret that Zach Bako-Bewele is quite good. That’s how he earned himself an $88M extension last summer. Despite this, I think he is somehow still underrated. ESPN’s win rate metrics have always been… kinda goofy… in comparison to some of the other more advanced metrics in the football space. They got a big rework over the off-season and generally look much more sensible now. In 2025, despite playing basically the entirety of the season with a back injury because of a cheap shot from Aidan Hutchison in the opening week, Bako-Bewele still ranked second in pass block win rate amongst all offensive tackles. ESPN tweaked how it calculates win rates for pass rushing and pass blocking. Under the new formula, Micah Parsons led all qualifying edge defenders in pass-rush win rate last season, and Zach Bako-Bewele finished second among qualifying offensive tackles in pass-block win rate. pic.twitter.com/cOuiLVNZb3 — Jason B. Hirschhorn (@by_JBH) August 23, 2026 If Bako-Bewele can’t go, the job will almost certainly be left to the 2025 second-round pick Anthony Belton. Belton, who went from tackle-only to starting right guard to tackle-only between the start of last year until training camp, has not impressed. Belton put up a collective PFF grade under 50 last season, albeit with many of those snaps at right guard. Playing just tackle, Belton posted a 62 grade against a bad Commanders front, but followed that up with grades under 45 at tackle against both Cleveland and Minnesota, the only other two games with material tackle snaps for him. In those latter two, Belton allowed pressures on a very porous 12.5% of dropbacks. The Cleveland game in particular was a horror show as he allowed pressures on 50% of Green Bay’s “true dropbacks” (i.e., not screens, RPO, play action). Rookies sometimes struggle, but his 2026 pre-season did not look much improved. A PFF pass blocking grade of 49 with pressure rates allowed of 15%, with snaps against some second-string defenders, is, if anything, only more concerning than what he put on tape last year. With Brian Flores’ defenses majoring in deception and attacking offensive line’s rules in the best of cases, this presents a potential nightmare scenario. Belton is already heavy-footed, and adding in hesitation, missed stunts, and passing assignments with a new partner at right guard in (likely) Jacob Monk, a high-powered Packers offense could be completely shut down by a right tackle who simply isn’t ready, and may never be ready. Add to this that both Vikings edge defenders Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel fall into the “more bendy than power” archetype, and that adds another problem for Belton, as his only real strength is, well, his strength. But if he can’t get his hands into his opponents’ chest, it won’t matter how strong he is. If Bako-Bewele plays, Green Bay should feel good about its ability to get the ball into its bevy of playmakers’ hands down the field, but if it is Belton starting at right tackle, expect a very frustrating offensive structure, as the Packers, in an effort to protect their franchise quarterback, will likely spend much of the game handing off to Marshawn Lloyd and manufacturing quick-game touches to the likes of Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed, which does not extenuate either of their skill sets. Just remember back in Cleveland last fall, when the right tackle was gone, and the Packers lost to an absolutely abysmal Browns team because they couldn’t protect Jordan Love. The 2026 Vikings are almost certainly better than that Browns team, even if the defense definitely isn’t. In order to win, Green Bay will need to score points, and if they can’t protect Jordan Love well enough, that will become difficult to do.

full_text: PHOENIX, AZ - DECEMBER 26: New Mexico Lobos running back Damon Bankston (1) signals first down during the Rate Bowl college football game between the New Mexico Lobos and the Minnesota Golden Gophers on December 26, 2025 at Chase Field in Phoenix, Arizona. Bankston was brought into Green Bay initially as a pre-draft visitor , but he ended up signing with the New York Giants as an undrafted free agent for $115,000 guaranteed, while the Packers opted to add Jaden Nixon — who was not kept on the practice squad after cuts — for $15,000 guaranteed. Damon Bankston is a RB prospect in the 2026 draft class. He scored a 8.13 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 425 out of 2268 RB from 1987 to 2026. https://t.co/YsK1v58Obp pic.twitter.com/6JChHWvpTv — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 2, 2026 The New Mexico product is an interesting prospect, as he posted a 4.43-second 40-yard dash during the pre-draft process but was overlooked by the major all-star games because he was a member of a committee backfield. At the college level, Bankston contributed not only as a one-cut runner, but also as a pass-catcher and a returner. Before transferring up to the FBS level, he was an all-conference player at Weber State in the FCS. It appears that the Packers are transitioning to an outside zone-based offense, similar to what head coach Matt LaFleur ran earlier in his tenure in Green Bay. For what it’s worth, Bankston is a very good fit for that scheme. Bankston had a workout with the Packers on Tuesday, and the following players were also brought in: QB Jack Plummer RB Phil Mafah RB Ian Wheeler TE Cody Hardy DB Sanoussi Kane DB Ambry Thomas It’s possible that Green Bay is still looking for answers to practice squad bodies at quarterback, where they signed Kedon Slovis from the Arizona Cardinals, and tight end, where the team retained Drake Dabney, but it also makes a lot of sense that they’re keeping an eye on defensive backs, too. The team only has 11 total defensive backs available between the 53-man roster and the practice squad, barely enough to make a two-deep at the position once you include nickel defenders. Eventually, the Packers will probably want to add numbers somewhere on the team in the secondary. title: The Colts’ defense is betting big on its cornerbacks staying healthy
summary: The Colts are going to need their cornerbacks to be one of the best position groups on the team this season. That is not really a preference as much as it is a requirement. This defense has talent, but it also has some obvious questions. The pass rush is nothing to write home about. Laiatu […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, IN - AUGUST 6: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward (7) runs through a drill during the Indianapolis Colts training camp practice on August 6, 2026 at the Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Colts are going to need their cornerbacks to be one of the best position groups on the team this season. That is not really a preference as much as it is a requirement. This defense has talent, but it also has some obvious questions. The pass rush is nothing to write home about. Laiatu Latu needs to take another step plus DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart are still high-level interior players, but this does not look like a unit that is going to consistently overwhelm opposing quarterbacks on its own. If the pass rush is closer to average than great, the coverage has to hold up. The corners have to make quarterbacks hesitate, shrink throwing windows and most importantly buy the front extra time. That puts a lot on Sauce Gardner, Charvarius Ward, Justin Walley and eventually Cam Taylor-Britt. On paper, the top of the group is strong. Gardner is the star and the player this defense should be built around. Ward gives the Colts a proven veteran outside corner opposite him. Walley is expected to handle a major role in the slot and Taylor-Britt will add another experienced body once he returns from his Week 1 suspension. Taylor-Britt also possesses the ability to play outside or inside, which is key. If all of those players are available and playing well, the Colts should feel good about what they have at cornerback. The problem is how much of that last sentence depends on “if.” Ward is a quality corner when he is on the field, but his concussion history makes his availability one of the biggest swing factors on the defense. They need him outside, handling quality players and letting Gardner stay in his role instead of forcing the rest of the secondary to shuffle around him. If Ward misses time, the cornerback room changes quickly. Walley brings talent and long-term upside, but he is also coming off a major injury. Asking him to step into a big role right away is already a lot. Asking him to do it while the team is thin around him adds another layer to the risk. The Colts may believe he is ready, and maybe he is, but corner is not a position where teams usually get a quiet, stress-free season from everyone involved. Even Gardner missed games last season. That does not make him injury-prone, and it does not change the fact that he is the best player in the group, but it is another reminder that cornerback depth usually gets tested. Cornerback is a very demanding position that requires constant cutting, change of direction and full on sprinting; it is the more athletically demanding position in the entire sport. Very few teams get through a season with their top corners completely untouched. That is why the Jaylon Jones move stands out. The Colts waived Jones while signing offensive tackle Luke Tenuta from the practice squad, which may be perfectly defensible on its own. Teams always have to balance the bottom of the roster, and offensive line depth is not something to treat lightly. Still, the move leaves the Colts light at cornerback going into Week 1, especially with Taylor-Britt suspended. Indianapolis did claim Kapena Gushiken, and there are some useful names on the practice squad, but relying on emergency elevations and new additions is not the same as having settled depth. Jones is not some irreplaceable piece, so this is not about making his release bigger than it is. The concern is the overall bet the Colts appear willing to make. They’re asking a group with several health questions to carry a defense that needs strong coverage to function at a high level. That is a lot of pressure for a room that already feels a little thin. The margin becomes even smaller because of what this defense is trying to cover up. If the pass rush does not consistently get home, the corners have to win longer. If the linebackers are young or slow to sort things out, the secondary has to clean up more mistakes underneath. If the safeties are still settling into new roles, communication on the back end becomes even more important. Good cornerback play can hide a lot of issues. Bad or injured cornerback play exposes everything fast. There have been many years with the Colts where the 3rd stringer is getting significant reps by the middle of the season. That is the part that makes the health of this group so important. Gardner can change a defense by himself, but he cannot cover every receiver. Ward can raise the ceiling of the secondary, but only if he is available. Walley can become an important piece, but the Colts need him healthy and comfortable quickly. Taylor-Britt helps once he returns, but he is not available for the opener and still has to earn a role when he gets back. The Colts are not wrong to bet on the top of their cornerback room. There is legitimate talent there, and if the group stays healthy, it should become the strength of the defense and maybe even the strength of the team. The issue is that the whole structure feels fragile. This is not a deep room loaded with proven backups. It is a talented room that needs its best players to stay on the field. For a defense that may not have a dominant pass rush, that is a risky place to be. If the group holds up, the defense has a chance to be much better than it was. If it does not, the Colts may find out quickly that the cornerback room was carrying more of the plan than anyone wanted to admit.

title: This time next week, what will be the Colts’ storyline?
summary: The season starts tonight, with the Colts following along at 1:00 on Sunday. We host the Ravens and Fan Duel has the Ravens favored by 3.5. The site also likes the Ravens in the big picture and has them at the 4th shortest odds to win the Super Bowl. They don’t hate the Colts, as […]
full_text: The season starts tonight, with the Colts following along at 1:00 on Sunday. We host the Ravens and Fan Duel has the Ravens favored by 3.5. The site also likes the Ravens in the big picture and has them at the 4th shortest odds to win the Super Bowl. They don’t hate the Colts, as 13 teams have longer odds to win the SB, but there is clearly not high expectations for the Colts. How ever you want to slice it, a Colts win on Sunday would be considered an upset. Win or lose, no one is going to drastically change their minds about how they think the Colts season will unfold. Those who see them as a conference competitor, will continue to think that way with a win. Those who do not have high hopes for the Colts will say that we caught the Ravens and their rookie coach, before they turned into the team that many will predict going to the Super Bowl. Or, they will say that anyone who they consider injury “prone”, will soon go down and seal the Colts fate as a lower tier team. Those of use who are basing our optimism on the offense being able to produce at or near last year’s early season level, will relish if the Colts put up 30 on the Ravens. We will say that it was against a good D, even though they were not all that good last year. We might also point out that the only piece that was really lost on offense was Pittman and he was easily replaced at a better price. Even if we give up 30 ourselves, all we need is for the defense to have been able to hold them to one point less than we scored and we will still have confidence, since it was against Jackson and Henry. Now if we look bad taking an L, there will be many “Told ya so’s”. The inability to compete with better teams will be the talk of the day and although the sentiment to axe our GM likely can’t get any greater, it undoubtedly will. The run biltz may still be effective against us and we’ll determine that it always will be. Or, the defensive could get gashed and the lack of pass rush is still the main culprit. Maybe the LBs still can’t cover? Those who are ready to pile on, would have plenty of ammo to do so. As the optimist, I expect to be happy with Sunday’s outcome. In my opinion, I think the Ravens are only being touted so high, because most think that Jackson will be healthy and return to MVP form. I simply think that it would take more than that for the Ravens to reinsert themselves into champions conversations. I think that they are flawed on the O-line as Luke shared yesterday. I mean, they were excited about Pinter? They will have a rookie starting at Guard, but it doesn’t always go as well as it did for the Colts. On D, they added the player that many of us wanted in Hendrickson, then drafted another Edge in the 2nd round. The Colts are certainly hoping that a infusion of a few pieces will raise our defensive level, but Ravens were 20th in the league in points allowed and I don’t think they made the kind of hay that will see anyone reminded of the Lewis-Suggs-Reed led teams. As it has also been pointed out, Steichen sort of shredded the Minter led Charger squad last year. Lastly, we’ve always played the Ravens well. I think their lofty ranking is as much about the fact that the AFC took a step back last year, as highlighted by the Pats representing the conference. I think we will fluster and turn Jackson over a couple of times, maybe more? My only concern is if Shane has instilled the confidence and killer instinct that it takes to win each week. I believe that we are the better team, but it plays a lot better if the team also believes that they are the better squad. So, what do you think we will be talking about a week from today?

title: Colts release unofficial depth chart for Week 1 opener versus Ravens—with a few takeaways
summary: On Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts announced their first unofficial depth chart of the regular season, and ahead of their Week 1 home opener against the Baltimore Ravens: Here are some of the key takeaways: OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - AUGUST 29: Indianapolis Colts linebacker Jaylon Carlies (57) during a NFL preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Indianapolis Colts on August 29, 2026 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts announced their first unofficial depth chart of the regular season, and ahead of their Week 1 home opener against the Baltimore Ravens: Our unofficial depth chart for #BALvsIND . — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) September 8, 2026 Here are some of the key takeaways: OFFENSE The transition project of Dalton Tucker to center has failed, and he has slid back over to backup left guard behind perennial All-Pro Quenton Nelson, which means Sedrick Van Pran-Granger is the primary backup center—as everyone already expected following his late acquisition. Rookie running back Seth McGowan has earned the 2nd-string running back job behind star workhorse Jonathan Taylor, which means 2nd-year back DJ Giddens has been relegated to third-string for now. Quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. is listed ahead of 2nd-year quarterback Riley Leonard as the primary backup behind starter Daniel Jones—as was already announced by head coach Shane Steichen last week. DEFENSE Former 2025 2nd round pick Jaylahn Tuimoloau is still ahead of rookies George Gumbs Jr. and Caden Curry on the defensive edge depth chart, despite a fairly underwhelming preseason showing—albeit against stronger opposing 2nd-string offensive lines. Veteran defensive tackle Jerry Tillery is the 2nd-string nose tackle behind run stopping stalwart Grover Stewart, which means Tim Smith has been currently relegated to third-string. Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies will be the starting linebackers in the opener, which means rookie linebacker CJ Allen, who had recently run with the first-team defense in preseason, but was limited a bit by a hamstring in training camp, will be 2nd-string to begin the 2026 campaign. That could eventually change as the season progresses, but for now, he’ll remain with fellow rookie Bryce Boettcher and the 2nd-team defense at linebacker. AJ Haulcy is still listed as the first-team starter at safety over Hunter Wohler, even with the lingering ankle injury, which could ultimately keep him out of making his Colts debut this Sunday. SPECIAL TEAMS Wideout Ashton Dulin and running back Seth McGowan are listed as the primary kick returners, which makes sense given Steichen’s explanation on Tuesday , but the punt return situation seems more fluid—especially if it comes down to starting slot Josh Downs. The Colts are still working through it , but it’s possible they could elect to promote special teams returner Anthony Gould ahead of Sunday’s game still yet for a more natural punt returner (and not to place Downs at greater injury risk).

title: Colts announce latest roster moves, which include waiving former starting defender
summary: On Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts announced that the team signed offensive tackle Luke Tenuta from their practice squad and waived former starting cornerback Jaylon Jones in a corresponding 53-man roster move: The promotion of Tenuta from their taxi-man team is not entirely unexpected, as the Colts had no natural backup offensive tackle behind their pair […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Jaylon Jones #40 of the Indianapolis Colts lines up during an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts announced that the team signed offensive tackle Luke Tenuta from their practice squad and waived former starting cornerback Jaylon Jones in a corresponding 53-man roster move: We have signed T Luke Tenuta to the 53-man roster from the practice squad and waived CB Jaylon Jones. We have also signed TE Kenny Fletcher Jr. to the practice squad. — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) September 8, 2026 The promotion of Tenuta from their taxi-man team is not entirely unexpected, as the Colts had no natural backup offensive tackle behind their pair of starters: Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis—although starting right guard Matt Goncalves could’ve theoretically slid over in a pinch (with perhaps rookie offensive guard Jalen Farmer playing there in further emergency, which would’ve been less than ideal). Clearly, the Colts were in need of another backup offensive tackle, as that prior tackle situation was precarious. It comes at the expense of former starting cornerback Jaylon Jones, who started in 29 games for the Colts over the past three seasons, and will now hit league waivers. The former 2023 7th round pick of the Colts had initially looked like a really good late round draft find by the Colts scouting regime, but he was miscast in veteran defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo’s coverage scheme since his arrival last season and could benefit from being deployed in a more zone heavy scheme going forward. Jones played reasonably well in preseason, even with the lack of natural coverage fit, but it was a telling sign that he was participating late in the second half of preseason games. It’s possible that the Colts were holding out hope for a potential trade partner, but it never materialized until they had to finally make a move regarding Tenuta. Without Jones anymore, the Colts look very thin and inexperienced at backup cornerback for Week 1 against the Baltimore Ravens, as Cam Taylor-Britt serves his one game suspension. They’ll either need to make another meaningful backup cornerback move or cross their fingers that the trio of Sauce Gardner, Charvarius Ward, and Justin Walley all stay healthy in the opener. Regarding tight end Kenny Fletcher Jr., who was added to the Colts practice squad, he is a 6,3”, 250 pound tight end out of Rutgers that was originally signed as an undrafted rookie free agent by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers earlier this late offseason. He was recently waived as part of their final 53-man roster cuts. The converted defensive lineman for the Scarlet Knights had 46 receptions for 373 total receiving yards (8.1 ypr. avg.) and 2 touchdown receptions during 17 games at the position over the past two seasons.

According to FanDuel Sportsbook, Liam Coen’s Jacksonville Jaguars are 8.5-point home favorites against Todd Monken’s Cleveland Browns. It’ll be the latter’s first game as an NFL […]
full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Jaguars fans and fans across the country. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Liam Coen’s Jacksonville Jaguars are 8.5-point home favorites against Todd Monken’s Cleveland Browns. It’ll be the latter’s first game as an NFL head coach, and his starting quarterback is a familiar foe for Jaguars faithful. Deshaun Watson, who was at one point the obvious successor to Andrew Luck as the king of the AFC South, has soured into one of the worst players in the National Football League. In 2024, he was the NFL’s least efficient passer through Week 7, when he ruptured his right Achilles tendon. Just a few months after he underwent surgery, he rolled his ankle and re-ruptured the same Achilles tendon. The nasty man turns 31 on Monday. Cleveland’s quarterback sucks. The bigger news is that, for the first time in a decade, reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett will not be wearing orange and brown. The Browns have significant questions across its roster. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see them forecasted for a top-three 2027 draft pick by the middle of the season. The Jaguars ought to take care of business and start the season 1-0. Do you trust Coen and company to get the job done? Is this a trap game? Are you confident in the Jaguars? title: Why the Chiefs are confident in the team’s young backup running backs
summary: After several battles in training camp and preseason to finalize the 53-man roster, the Kansas City Chiefs head into Week 1 of the regular season with three running backs on the active roster. Kenneth Walker, the team’s prize free-agent signing, heads the unit and will take on the majority of snaps this season, but rookie […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 28: Emmett Johnson #10 of the Kansas City Chiefs signals first down after a run in the first quarter of an NFL preseason game between the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs on Aug 28, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After several battles in training camp and preseason to finalize the 53-man roster, the Kansas City Chiefs head into Week 1 of the regular season with three running backs on the active roster. Kenneth Walker, the team’s prize free-agent signing, heads the unit and will take on the majority of snaps this season, but rookie Emmett Johnson and second-year back Brashard Smith both had impressive preseasons, instilling enough confidence in the team to part ways with veteran back Emari Demercado on cutdown day. Here’s what to know about the backups in the backfield: Emmett Johnson The Chiefs drafted Johnson in the fifth round of the 2026 Draft, but have wasted no time acclimating him to their system and giving him chances to show his abilities. The Nebraska product worked his way from the bottom of the depth chart to become the Chiefs’ second running back on the roster behind only Walker. In the preseason, Johnson flashed his natural blend of patience and explosion, which helped him find running lanes. Good balance by Johnson to stay on his feet and work through the initial contact to pick up extra yards. pic.twitter.com/iyZbLnK5AQ — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 2, 2026 With good hesitation moves and solid contact balance, Johnson used those tools, along with good vision, to break off decent runs and create plays even when the lane wasn’t there initially. On the snap, the Chiefs go left on a zone run, but there is not a hole for Johnson to hit initially. As Johnson approaches the line of scrimmage, He reads a small crease start to open up, and with a quick jump cut, hits the hole, and shakes off a tackle on his way to the second level. This wasn’t a home-run handoff, but it showed Johnson doesn’t need perfectly blocked looks to find yards. Good run by Johnson. Nygra and Caliendo good combo to the second level. One cut from Johnson and he hits the hole. Breaks a tackle. Might need to be careful spinning into traffic, but a solid run. pic.twitter.com/yvKHhor9Qd — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 29, 2026 Johnson’s quick slashing style and smooth jump cuts make him a natural fit for the Chiefs’ zone run game. The Chiefs run zone right, and on the snap, Johnson heads toward the line of scrimmage, but little opens up on the play side. Johnson recognizes this, and in one smooth motion, he quickly cuts back and finds a nice running lane. Johnson’s sense of timing and how to take advantage of defenses overflowing to hit cutback lanes is not something that can be taught in a classroom, but is a natural trait and ability that comes naturally to only a select few running backs. Brashard Smith Although Smith is seemingly behind Johnson on the depth chart, he still had a productive preseason and showed that he is worth the Chiefs continuing to develop. A seventh-round pick in last season’s NFL Draft, Smith played sparingly in 2025, but when he did find the field, he showed enough flash to make an impact. After playing only one season at running back in college, Smith’s career started slowly in 2025, but this preseason he looked more comfortable carrying the ball after being largely a pass catcher during his rookie season. Where Johnson operates better with quick jump cuts and working “north and south”, Smith uses his speed and quickness to try to create plays to the sideline and uses it to get around would-be tacklers. Smith takes the zone handoff and bounces it outside. The edge defender gets hands on, but Smith runs through the arm tackle and turns the corner for a nice gain. pic.twitter.com/WLoS9QjAt2 — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 2, 2026 On the snap, Smith takes a quick peek inside, but elects to bounce the run. The end-of-the-line defender does get a hand on him, but with his quickness, he can turn the corner and pick up a nice gain to the sideline. Like Johnson, Smith showed this preseason that he can find yards even when they aren’t there, and he can create big plays. KC goes Y counter, but nothing opens up on the front side. With good vision and patience, Smith allows the blocks to develop and takes the run to the backside, where he finds a crease. pic.twitter.com/IFXngCMIGZ — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) September 2, 2026 The Chiefs run counter, but not much opens up on the play side. Smith starts to head to the left to attempt to follow the blocks, but with little movement from the kickout block, there is no lane to run through. While the pullers don’t create much space, the play-side double team does create movement downfield, giving Smith an angle to work off of and helping him find a cutback lane. This play displays Smith’s overall development since his rookie season and that he has the vision needed to play running back in the NFL. The bottom line The Chiefs should plan to use Kenneth Walker as much as possible, especially given what he is being paid, but this preseason showed the team has capable backs behind him. Although Smith is the low man in the running back room, he will likely still find ways to help the team via special teams and other “gadget” looks due to his quickness and ability to run in the open field. Johnson appears poised to be Walker’s direct backup this season, and due to the physicality of the position, he should be poised to carry a decent workload for a rookie headed into the season. Most successful run games in the modern NFL operate with multiple running backs commanding close to equal touches, and while the Chiefs will certainly rely more on Walker, Johnson being able to step up and perform well as a rookie would add another layer to a team that will need to rely on the run game early. With depth issues at offensive tackle, quarterback Patrick Mahomes coming off of an ACL injury, and inconsistency from the pass catchers, the Chiefs will need to lean heavily on Walker, but to ensure that he is still in form for a late-season push, Johnson should look to help shoulder some of the load, especially when the grind fo the season kicks in. The Chiefs have not invested much in running back during the Mahomes era, but this offseason bucked the trend, and the team will be in a better spot if it uses its new talent and builds on its strengths.

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Why Sean Payton put Chiefs’ logo on Broncos’ practice field | Broncos Wire For the first time in the rivalry’s history, the Broncos will open their season at Arrowhead, with both teams looking to bounce back after losing their starting quarterbacks late in their 2025 campaigns. Patrick Mahomes expected to start Chiefs’ opener vs. Broncos on MNF | ESPN Patrick Mahomes is expected to start the Kansas City Chiefs’ season opener Monday against the Denver Broncos, according to coach Andy Reid. One reason to take them with a grain of salt: In Week 1 of the 2017 NFL preseason, Tyler Bray was listed ahead of Patrick Mahomes. That said, these aren’t entirely uninformed. They’re often based on what the PR staff observes in practice. Not just a sports mom. Randi Mahomes ‘reintroduces’ herself on social media | The Kansas City Star “Let me introduce myself. I’m Randi. Tampa Bay later announced the extension through the 2029 season. The news comes as a surprise after the two sides passed Mayfield’s self-imposed training camp deadline for a deal to get done, leading to the veteran QB to say he felt “disrespected” by the Bucs’ proposals. Roughly six weeks time, however, was enough to bridge whatever gap existed in contract talks, and Mayfield now will make $55 million per year on a new deal struck on the eve of the 2026 season. 49ers lose another key contributor to a season-ending injury | Niners Nation The San Francisco 49ers have another season-ending injury that happened before their season has even started. Defensive tackle Alfred Collins showed up on the injury report this week, and Kyle Shanahan later said it’s a torn patellar tendon suffered Monday . Collins will now be out for the season. This marks another season-ending injury before the season has even started. This certainly doesn’t bode well for the 49ers’ injury concerns and for Collins, who had flashes in 2025 but needed to get some consistency going in his second season as a pro. Rams’ Donald won’t travel to Australia; Garrett ‘ready to go’ | ESPN “He’s doing a great job,” McVay said. “I think he’ll be ready to go sooner rather than later, but we’re making a decision that we think is best for him and for our team. … He’s attacked this the right way, but it would have been a really quick turnaround.” McVay also said defensive end Myles Garrett, who has been dealing with swelling in his knee, will be “ready to go” in Week 1. Garrett, however, did not practice Tuesday, the team said on its official injury report. “He’s looked great,” McVay said. “We’ve been smart with Myles, like I’ve kind of told you guys, but his impact has been tremendous.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride The Chiefs’ offensive line will be ‘the five best guys’ in Week 1 But the bottom line is both options are first-year players, rookies. The rise of Benson as the potential right tackle has not inspired a lot of confidence about Moore, either. title: Andy Reid gives 4 more Chiefs injury updates
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have multiple key players returning from injury ahead of their season opener against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football.” At the top of most fan concerns is the status of left tackle Josh Simmons, who has been out of practice since midway through training camp with a back ailment. On […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Quarterback Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs warms up prior to the preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have multiple key players returning from injury ahead of their season opener against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football.” At the top of most fan concerns is the status of left tackle Josh Simmons, who has been out of practice since midway through training camp with a back ailment. On Tuesday, head coach Andy Reid conceded that there is a “good chance” the team plays without its starting blindside blocker . Other injury news is (mostly) encouraging. Reid all but confirmed the worst-kept secret in the NFL: Patrick Mahomes (barring an unexpected late setback) will be starting in Week 1 after suffering multiple torn ligaments in December. “There’s a pretty good chance Patrick will go ahead and start,” Reid predicted, “unless something were to come up in the next couple of days. Most likely, he’ll be the guy that’s out there.” Mahomes has met every threshold Reid hoped for in his recovery. “He’s shown everything, there.” Reid explained. “He hasn’t missed a day…Other than having a brace on his leg, everything looks normal. He’s running around the same way he’s always done and throwing the ball the way he’s always done. I think we’ll be fine there.” Also in Mahomes’ favor, Reid does not anticipate any limitations for his top wide receiver in Rashee Rice. Rice saw his offseason interrupted by a combination of a short jail sentence and a cleanup surgery from a 2024 knee injury. After being limited much of camp, Rice should be ready to go. “I liked the way he’s progressed coming off the knee,” observed Reid. “Every day, he’s gotten better and stronger. His endurance is better. He had a chance to play in the last game a few plays. I thought that was important. I think he’ll be fine going into this game.” Kansas City also navigated injuries at the safety position in the latter stages of camp. Chamarri Conner has been sidelined throughout the preseason with a knee issue. The Chiefs also scratched their other starter , veteran Alohi Gilman, just before the team’s second preseason game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with back pain. Reid’s update on the two was mixed. “Chamarri would be a stretch,” Reid noted. “Gilman was out there practicing and doing his thing. He’ll be ready to go, I think.” In his Tuesday remarks, Reid did not address the status of safety Ashton Gillotte, who reportedly ruptured his planter fascia in a camp practice. The team was reportedly hopeful that Gillotte could be recovered in time to face the Broncos. With the Monday night contest, the Chiefs and Broncos will issue official injury reports on Thursday, Friday and Saturday this week.

title: The Chiefs’ offensive line will be ‘the five best guys’ in Week 1
summary: Throughout the era of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the “next-man-up mentality” has applied to one position group more than any other on the way to three Super Bowl titles: the offensive line. Who could forget Mahomes’ de facto bodyguard, Cameron Erving, starting at left tackle for eight games during the 2019 season, filling […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 16: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Throughout the era of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the “next-man-up mentality” has applied to one position group more than any other on the way to three Super Bowl titles: the offensive line. Who could forget Mahomes’ de facto bodyguard, Cameron Erving, starting at left tackle for eight games during the 2019 season, filling in for Eric Fisher? Veteran Stefen Wisniewski filled in as the starting left guard for Andrew Wylie for all three playoff games that year, including Super Bowl LIV. Guard Nick Allegretti was a reliable backup during the 2022 regular season, starting three games and playing 262 snaps at right or left guard before returning to the bench, earning the ring that came with a win in Super Bowl LVII. Even Wanya Morris — whom the Chiefs traded away this offseason — started four games during the 2023 season at left tackle before handing the reins back to veteran Donovan Smith through Super Bowl LVIII. The point is: the Chiefs are familiar with working around injuries on the offensive line and still competing at the top of the NFL. However, the next man up usually has more experience than rookie offensive lineman Kahlil Benson, who was signed during rookie minicamp tryouts in May and has spent time at three different positions along the offensive line during his first NFL preseason: right tackle, right guard, and now left tackle. “I’m not telling you that,” Reid responded when pushed about Benson at left tackle. “But we’re comfortable with Kahlil on either side; he has been playing the left side, so I feel comfortable with that. We’ll end up playing the five best guys, and right now, he is one of them.” “If he has to be the left tackle, then he’s the left tackle,” Reid added. “And we roll with it. That’s just how it goes.” During head coach Andy Reid’s press conference on Tuesday, headlined by the reveal that there’s “a good chance” left tackle Josh Simmons does not play Week 1 , Reid all but said Benson is the next man up, citing that he has been on the blind side during recent practices. According to Pro Football Focus , Benson did not line up at left tackle for any collegiate snaps during his four seasons playing for the University of Indiana and the University of Colorado. 42 snaps at left guard 967 snaps at right guard 1,653 snaps at right tackle 2 snaps as an in-line tight end Reid was firm in his stance that Benson is one of the team’s five best offensive linemen (in the case that Simmons is unavailable), but does the team know how good he is at left tackle? It feels as if the coaching staff would know more about Benson as a right tackle, subsequently putting veteran Jaylon Moore at left tackle. So no swap may indicate the team’s confidence that Simmons will return soon and that they are unwilling to shake up two spots on the offensive line for a short-term issue. That’s pure speculation, but it’s logical, given that a more severe injury would have likely resulted in Simmons landing on the Reserve/Injured list at the beginning of the season. However, is that worth starting such an unknown on the blindside of Mahomes, who will be in his first live action since the devastating knee injury last December? As a reminder, the two-time MVP did not take any snaps in the preseason. Chiefs OL coach Andy Heck on Kahlil Benson: "It's a great story. Our scouts did a great job… Right away you could see he had dominant physical traits… We're doing our best to give him a chance to learn and grow in our system… He's doing a great job." — Charles Goldman (@goldmctNFL) August 19, 2026 It’s clear that Benson’s “dominant physical traits,” a quote from Chiefs’ offensive line coach Andy Heck during this preseason , enthralled the coaching staff enough to want him on the field. Those strengths seem to come as a run blocker, but there is evidence from preseason Week 2 — in which he played right tackle — that sound pass protection does not come as naturally. Those ugly reps against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers were excused by Reid, citing the lack of familiarity with the silent count, but the snaps came at a position Benson has been familiar with. In Week 1, Benson will potentially be lining up at left tackle, a position he hasn’t played since at least high school (if then), against one of the NFL’s best pass rushers. Denver Broncos ’ outside linebacker Nik Bonitto lined up on the right edge of the defensive formation for 86% of his defensive snaps last season, according to PFF . There were some games he exclusively aligned over the left tackle. An alternative to Benson would be Diego Pounds, a rookie left tackle the team acquired from the Baltimore Ravens during cutdown week. Over three years as a starting left tackle in college football, Pounds totaled 2,651 snaps on the left edge. This preseason, all 58 of Pounds’ snaps came on the blind side of the Ravens’ quarterbacks. That experience compared to Benson’s doesn’t seem to move the needle for Reid, who told local media on Wednesday that Pounds needs more time under his belt. But the bottom line is both options are first-year players, rookies. The rise of Benson as the potential right tackle has not inspired a lot of confidence about Moore, either. There was a lot of conversation this offseason about the Chiefs potentially needing to bolster the offensive tackle position. General manager Brett Veach and the front office did not add to that group in free agency, the draft, or the wave of undrafted free agents to close out draft weekend. Benson, signed after tryouts in rookie minicamp, is one of the Chiefs’ “best five guys” right now after one injury. It remains to be seen if that makes the front office look smart or foolish.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chiefs’ Andy Reid says there’s a good chance Josh Simmons misses Week 1
summary: With the Kansas City Chiefs starting the 2026 season on “Monday Night Football,” head coach Andy Reid’s weekly Monday press conference shifted to Tuesday ahead of the team’s first practice of the week on Thursday. That also delayed the unfortunate update Reid provided about starting left tackle Josh Simmons (Back), who has missed weeks of […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Josh Simmons #71 walks to the field during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the Kansas City Chief s starting the 2026 season on “Monday Night Football,” head coach Andy Reid’s weekly Monday press conference shifted to Tuesday ahead of the team’s first practice of the week on Thursday. That also delayed the unfortunate update Reid provided about starting left tackle Josh Simmons (Back), who has missed weeks of practice trying to recover from the preseason injury. After answering a few questions about the situation from local media, Reid got straight to the point about Simmons’ status. “There’s a good chance Josh doesn’t play this week; that’s where we’re at,” Reid told 810 Sports ’ Soren Petro during the press conference. “So we have that in our mind. He has an issue there that he is working through. I’m not putting any time restraint on when he comes back or when he can practice and how many practices he needs. I just want to make sure he’s healthy and okay to go.” Andy Reid on Kahlil Benson: "We're comfortable playing Kahlil on the left side. … There's a good chance Josh [Simmons] doesn't play this week." — Nate Taylor (@ByNateTaylor) September 8, 2026 Before he reiterated the doubtful state of Simmons’ injury, he shared his thoughts on what the offensive line would look like without Simmons. “If [Simmons is] not able to go, then we’ll be in with Kahlil [Benson] at that spot, and we’ll roll from there.” “We try to play the five best guys,” Reid added. “So we make that decision on that.” As the Arrowhead Pride staff has speculated during the preseason , rookie offensive lineman Kahlil Benson’s tools have impressed Kansas City enough to be considered one of the team’s top linemen, regardless of position. That’s why Reid sounds so firm on Benson filling in for Simmons, but he was not ready to confirm that Benson would be the direct substitute on the blindside. The rookie played only right tackle and guard in college. “I’m not telling you that,” Reid responded when pushed about Benson at left tackle. “But we’re comfortable with Kahlil on either side; he has been playing the left side, so I feel comfortable with that. We’ll end up playing the five best guys, and right now, he is one of them.” “If he has to be the left tackle, then he’s the left tackle,” Reid added. “And we roll with it. That’s just how it goes.” While Benson’s preseason wasn’t impressive on the surface, Reid sees a positive trait in the potential fill-in starter. “He normally doesn’t make the same mistake twice, which I’ve mentioned before,” Reid said. “That’s an important quality to have. He’s tough, so it’s just that he doesn’t have a whole lot of reps under his belt at this level as a rookie, but he’s very willing, and if he has to step in there and play — which it looks like he probably will — we feel comfortable with that.” While we await an official practice designation for Simmons once practice begins this week, Reid emphasized that the second-year player is doing what it takes to return to the field. “Josh is rehabbing; he’s working his tail off,” Reid shared. “This isn’t anything other than having an issue with his back; it’s just a matter of time here, but he continues to work hard with Rick and do his part there.” Reid also shared that rookie left tackle Diego Pounds, whom the team traded for a couple of weeks ago, is “getting used to what we do offensively.” Reid remarked on Pounds’ talent and willingness to work hard, but “it’s just a matter of him getting a little time under his belt.” Patrick Mahomes should be ready to roll Before Reid got into Simmons’ status, he said everything but confirmed that starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes will take the field in Week 1. “There’s a pretty good chance Patrick will go ahead and start, unless something were to come up here in the next couple of days,” Reid said. “Most likely, he will be the guy that’s out there.” “He has shown everything there,” Reid continued. “He hasn’t missed a day… other than having a brace on his leg; everything looks normal. He’s running around the same way he has always done and throwing the ball like he has always done. I think we’ll be fine there.” The Chiefs are scheduled to begin their three-day practice routine on Thursday, leading up to the AFC West battle on Monday evening.

full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 14: Travis Kelce #87 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs onto the field prior to the NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. There’s also the new-look secondary, which hasn’t been tested yet, leaving plenty of questions for the Chiefs to answer when they welcome the AFC West rival Broncos to Arrowhead Stadium on Monday night. — Nick Shook ESPN : 13 Entering this season, Kelce has 13,002 receiving yards. All he needs is 45 yards to surpass Jason Witten for the second most by a tight end in NFL history. Fans can expect Kelce to reach this next accomplishment in the Chiefs’ season opener against the Broncos, a rival he has tormented throughout his Hall of Fame-worthy career. Mahomes, who is expected to be ready for Week 1 after knee surgery, has always made Kelce his go-to pass catcher on third down. It’s possible Kelce passes Witten on a third down before the “Monday Night Football” halftime show. — Nate Taylor The Athletic : 14 Last ranking: 18 First game: vs. Broncos, Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET Mock’s projected win total: 9.6 Our last power rankings assumed Patrick Mahomes would probably miss the start of the season. Astoundingly, even though he suffered an ACL tear in mid-December, it looks like he will be the Chiefs’ starting quarterback out of the gate. There is still plenty that ailed the Chiefs a year ago (and could again this year), but it’d be wise not to bet against Mahomes. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk : 13 When it’s time to call the plays, will they truly commit to the run? — Mike Florio CBSSports.com : 12 Don’t go sleeping on the Chiefs. As long as Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid are together, they will be in the playoff mix and more. — Pete Prisco Yahoo! Sports : 12 Patrick Mahomes is likely going to start in Week 1 coming off an ACL surgery, but it will be a bit of an unusual Week 1 for him. Mahomes and the rest of the Chiefs’ starters usually log some time in the preseason. Mahomes didn’t play at all this preseason as the Chiefs played it safe with him. However, in 2020, when there were no preseason games due to the pandemic, Mahomes had 11 touchdowns and no interceptions in his first four games. We’ll see if he looks rusty early this season. — Frank Schwab USA Today : 13 While focus is justifiably trained on the Super Bowl MVP backfield of QB Patrick Mahomes and RB Kenneth Walker III, plenty should be devoted to a revamped defense − the secondary especially − that was quietly one of the league’s stingiest in K.C.’s lost 2025 campaign. — Nate Davis FOX Sports : 15 Patrick Mahomes may be on track to start the season opener, but will he be the same old superstar? The Chiefs have the chance to rise or fall quickly in these rankings based on the early answer to that. — Ralph Vacchiano

title: Chiefs begin week as favorites over the Broncos in Week 1
summary: To cap off Week 1 of the NFL season, on Monday evening, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Denver Broncos for a “Monday Night Football” bout at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:15 p.m. The game will be broadcast nationally on ABC and ESPN. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, Kansas […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Chris Jones #95 of the Kansas City Chiefs rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images To cap off Week 1 of the NFL season, on Monday evening, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Denver Broncos for a “Monday Night Football” bout at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:15 p.m. The game will be broadcast nationally on ABC and ESPN . According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Kansas City begins the week as a 2.5-point favorite. The last time these two franchises faced off was Christmas Day at Arrowhead; Denver closed as a 13.5-point favorite against the Chiefs without quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City covered, but the Broncos pulled away from a tie game in the fourth quarter to win 20-13 . Of course, Denver’s victory sealed the clean sweep of the Chiefs in 2025: in Week 11, the Chiefs were four-point favorites on the road against the Broncos, but lost 22-19 . In the 2026 preseason, the Chiefs were defeated by the Los Angeles Rams and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before tying with the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos beat the Atlanta Falcons and Minnesota Vikings , but lost to the Green Bay Packers .

That night, he looked a whole lot like the future for the Chiefs. The deal includes $102 million guaranteed, sources said. That’s his focus, and I think he’s told you guys that. He’s gonna focus on trying to get better every single day.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Will Chiefs’ offense or defense rank higher in 2026? It’s a tough question. title: Chargers receiving little respect ahead of 2026 NFL season opener
summary: NFL.com’s Nick Shook just dropped the first rendition of his 2026 NFL power rankings and while I didn’t have much for expectations going into it, I somehow walked away feeling very conflicted at what I was seeing. The first half of his power rankings held all the teams you would have expected, but in a […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 27: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) looks to throw the ball during the NFL preseason game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the Los Angeles Rams on August 27, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images NFL.com’s Nick Shook just dropped the first rendition of his 2026 NFL power rankings and while I didn’t have much for expectations going into it, I somehow walked away feeling very conflicted at what I was seeing. The first half of his power rankings held all the teams you would have expected, but in a very unexpected order. Here’s Shook’s top 16 before we go further: Rams Broncos Seahawks Bills Eagles Ravens Bengals Cowboys Jaguars Texans Bears Packers Patriots Chiefs Lions Chargers Yes, you’re seeing that right. The Chargers — who are winners of 11 games in back-to-back seasons — are ranked right in the middle of the NFL at No. 16. Shook has SIX (6) teams who won nine or less games in 2025 ahead of the Chargers. The Chiefs and Bengals won six games a year ago. The Cowboys won seven and the Ravens won eight. That means four of them also finished with sub-.500 record. And then here are the Chargers, who weathered one hell of a storm up front offensively to win 11 games and make the postseason, sitting behind all of them despite becoming an objectively better football team across the board based on the group that went 11-6. I just don’t get it. Far, far too many teams are poised for a rebound and that’s overall fine! But the Chargers no longer get the benefit of the doubt (at least during the regular season) to finally be consistent and go for 10+ wins a third year in a row? Looking at this list, the Bengals did not do enough to get that benefit of the doubt. Burrow is crazy good when he is able to stay healthy, but he has played a single season of 17 games. He missed nine games last year. History says he won’t be healthy the entire year and the team will suffer. The Cowboys? Top 10? Why? Recent history says the same thing. After back-to-back seven-in seasons, chances are they aren’t much better than that while sitting behind the Eagles in the NFC East. Obvious these are not super-detailed and analytical reasons I’m using here, but there just seems like something is missing. When you spend long enough in this industry, you start to see how the media likes to give the benefit of the doubt to certain teams over and over. And then when it comes to teams who actually have earned that benefit in recent years, they’re still hard-pressed to do the same. That’s how I see this in regards to the Chargers. Maybe all it will take is the first playoff win of Justin Herbert’s career. Maybe that’s truly it. But I think they’ve done enough, as a whole, to warrant more respect out of the gate this year.

title: Justin Herbert receives MVP votes in 2026 NFL award predictions
summary: From the moment offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was hired by the Chargers, the hype began to soar for Justin Herbert in 2026. After two years of Greg Roman and an offense that seemed to lean too much into the run at times on top of an anemic passing attack, the hope is that McDaniel will […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 20: Quarterback Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers prior to a NFL preseason football game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the San Francisco 49ers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Thursday, August 20, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images From the moment offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was hired by the Chargers, the hype began to soar for Justin Herbert in 2026. After two years of Greg Roman and an offense that seemed to lean too much into the run at times on top of an anemic passing attack, the hope is that McDaniel will get Herbert back to launching moonshots at a much higher clip. And this time, the expectation is that on the receiving end will be a wideo pen and singular player, not two receivers who were — for some odd reason — running to the same spot. If Herbert’s 65-yard touchdown strike to Quentin Johnston in the preseason finale against the Rams is any indicator of what to expect this season, then there will be fireworks aplenty all year long. It’s with that mindset that some even have Herbert in the preseason MVP conversation alongside the likes of Joe Burrow and Josh Allen. In ESPN’s predictions for the annual awards where they surveyed anonymous NFL coaches and executives, it was Burrow who ultimately was predicted to win the award while Herbert and Allen were in the “received votes” category. Here are some thoughts from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler along with an anonymous quote from a NFC executive: “ As for Herbert, people inside the league value his work much more highly than some factions of the internet do. ‘Don’t think he got enough credit for everything he did last year when the OL got decimated by injuries,‘ an NFC exec said. ‘They get healthy and a proven, creative playcaller that can make his life easier and [offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel] hasn’t had a QB this gifted.’” Justin Herbert for NFL MVP?! 🤯 Sony Michel thinks the Chargers QB has a strong chance at taking home the award at the end of the season. Do you agree? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/MXzDXYsnv2 — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 1, 2026 Herbert averaged well over 4,000 yards passing in each of his first three seasons. Then, following the 2022 season, he missed four games with an injury and finished with just 3,134 yards and 20 touchdowns. That was far short of his previous high of 4,336 yards (2020) and 22 scores (2023) and that all came in the worst and final season of the Brandon Staley era. In the years since, Herbert has pushed for 4,000 yards in the past two seasons under Roman but still fell short. They’ve become a defensive team under Jim Harbaugh and that’s what has kept the team afloat outside of Herbert’s arm. That’s great and all that they haven’t needed Herbert to toss 30+ scores, but it’s been really frustrating to watch this team flip-flop which unit is elite instead of just combining an elite defense with an elite offense. That’s what the 2026 season could be for the Chargers. If Chris O’Leary keeps things up to the status quo from their past two seasons, then how good can this team really be? The schedule is NOT great. But what if this elite cocktail really comes to fruition? What if the Chargers offense pops off for 28+ per game while the defense remains one of the stingier units in the league? If MVP tends to only go to quarterbacks on the best overall teams, then how wouldn’t this make Herbert one of the front-runners? Let me know all of your thoughts on this in the comments below. Why are you, or why aren’t you, very high on Herbert’s MVP chances this season?

title: Super Bowl LXI will be between…
summary: The 2026 NFL season is finally here, and the race to Super Bowl LXI is wide open. While several teams have legitimate championship aspirations, 10 stand out as the strongest contenders in their respective conferences. Here are the top five teams in the AFC and NFC — and why each could make a run to […]
full_text: The 2026 NFL season is finally here, and the race to Super Bowl LXI is wide open. While several teams have legitimate championship aspirations, 10 stand out as the strongest contenders in their respective conferences. Here are the top five teams in the AFC and NFC — and why each could make a run to Los Angeles for Super Bowl LXI. AFC 1. Buffalo Bills The Buffalo Bills remain one of the AFC’s safest championship bets because of Josh Allen. Buffalo has consistently been in the postseason conversation, and Allen gives the Bills the type of elite quarterback play needed to survive the AFC playoff gauntlet. With a roster built to compete on both sides of the football, Buffalo has a strong foundation entering the 2026 season. The biggest question is whether the Bills can finally turn their regular-season success into a Super Bowl appearance. 2. Los Angeles Chargers Justin Herbert enters his age 28 season with sky high expectations. He has Mike McDaniel as his offensive coordinator and Jim Harbaugh as a quarterback whisperer. But will Los Angeles have the defense to get deep into January and February? 3. Cincinnati Bengals Whenever Joe Burrow is healthy, the Bengals have to be considered a championship threat. Cincinnati possesses one of the league’s most dangerous passing attacks, giving the team the ability to win high-scoring games against virtually anyone. The question will be whether the Bengals can consistently complement that offense with enough defense. 4. Baltimore Ravens The Ravens are built for January football. Lamar Jackson gives Baltimore an incredibly difficult quarterback to defend, while the team’s physical identity and ability to control games on the ground make them a dangerous postseason opponent. Baltimore also has plenty of experience playing in meaningful games. If the Ravens can put everything together under their new-look coaching staff, they have the talent to represent the AFC. 5. Jacksonville Jaguars The Jaguars have a budding quarterback in Trevor Lawrence who started to make “MVP rumblings” at the end of the 2025 season if it were not for Matthew Stafford. Travis Hunter enters year 2 as the defense’s main chess piece. NFC 1. Los Angeles Rams The Los Angeles Rams enter the season with the strongest Super Bowl odds in the entire NFL. Matthew Stafford returns to lead Sean McVay’s offense, while the addition of Myles Garrett and the return of Aaron Donald give the defense an extraordinary collection of talent. The Rams are currently among the league’s clear Super Bowl favorites. With Puka Nacua and an offense capable of producing explosive plays, Los Angeles has the balance necessary for a championship run. 2. Seattle Seahawks The defending Super Bowl champions cannot be ignored. Seattle returns with the confidence of having already climbed the mountain, and its defense remains the foundation of the team. The Seahawks also have a balanced roster and an established identity under Mike Macdonald. Repeating is incredibly difficult, but Seattle has earned its place among the NFC favorites. 3. Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles remain one of the NFC’s most talented rosters. Philadelphia has the physicality, offensive weapons and defensive talent necessary to compete with anyone. Saquon Barkley remains a major offensive weapon, while the health of the offensive line could be one of the biggest factors in determining the Eagles’ ceiling. 4. San Francisco 49ers The 49ers have too much talent to overlook. Kyle Shanahan’s offense remains one of the NFL’s most creative systems, and San Francisco has playmakers at virtually every important position. If the 49ers can stay healthy and get consistent quarterback play, they have the roster to make another deep postseason run. 5. Dallas Cowboys The Cowboys enter the season with plenty of pressure but also plenty of talent. Dak Prescott remains capable of leading an explosive offense, while Dallas has the star power necessary to compete in the NFC. The biggest question is whether the Cowboys can finally translate their regular-season potential into postseason success. If they do, they could become a legitimate threat to reach Super Bowl LXI. Pick: Ravens vs. Rams The Super Bowl logo theory tells me to go with the Jaguars. Maybe it’s the thought of general managers James Gladstone and Les Snead bringing their franchises to the title game. Or previous coaches Liam Coen and Sean McVay dialing up their offenses against one another. Jacksonville took the league by surprise last year and nearly advanced to the divisional round after a back and forth with the Buffalo Bills. But the emergence of Baltimore makes too much sense with two-time MVP Lamar Jackson recouping his form while leaning on Derrick Henry. First year head coach Jesse Minter retools the defense to handle quality offenses like the Bills, Chargers, Broncos, and Jaguars. Meanwhile, the Rams have had eyes set on Super Bowl LXI since its loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship this past January. They know its within their grasp again… Score: Baltimore Ravens 23, Los Angeles Rams 29 Super Bowl LXI Champion: Los Angeles Rams. The Rams have been among the most widely backed teams entering the season, and this prediction ultimately comes down to believing their combination of Stafford, McVay, Garrett, Donald and Nacua is too much to overcome when the biggest games arrive.

title: Rams defense gets chance to shine without Aaron Donald
summary: Aaron Donald will not be suiting up in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers and on one hand, that’s disappointing for fans of the Los Angeles Rams. On the other hand, if the Rams can excel or win without Donald, then that bodes even better for his eventual return to the lineup. It’s only […]
full_text: Aaron Donald will not be suiting up in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers and on one hand, that’s disappointing for fans of the Los Angeles Rams. On the other hand, if the Rams can excel or win without Donald, then that bodes even better for his eventual return to the lineup. It’s only one game, but it’s a massive opportunity for L.A. to get a divisional win in an international game and set the stage and show this team has what it takes to compete out of the gate. It’s assumed that this defense should be good with AD, but he won’t be there Thursday so what will this defense be without him? You can bet AD will be watching. What Aaron Donald’s Week 1 Absence Means for the Rams Defense (si.com) “While the Rams will be disappointed to not have Donald available, they are playing the long game and want to ensure he is in game shape before he takes the field. The Rams have been preparing without Donald throughout much of the summer, which won’t change how they approach Thursday’s game against the 49ers. This is also a team that’s uniquely built to manage without Donald. I think what’s cool is you have such confidence in the group that we do have with Kobie, with Fiske, with Poona Ford, with Tyler Davis,” said McVay. “It’ll add value when he’s ready to go, but being two years off retirement, he’s attacked this the right way.” The Rams do have the depth to manage without Donald against the 49ers. Donald would have certainly added a boost, but the Rams had been preparing all offseason to be without him. It wasn’t until they traded for Myles Garrett that Donald’s return became a possibility. Even then, Donald didn’t make it official until two weeks ago.“ Aaron Donald won’t travel with the L.A. Rams to Australia for Week 1 (ktla.com) “Defensive tackle Aaron Donald will not travel to Melbourne, Australia , to play in the Los Angeles Rams’ season opener against the San Francisco 49ers. Donald, who initially retired in March 2024, came out of retirement on Aug. 30 . He signed a one-year deal with the team. While Rams fans will have to wait a bit longer to see Donald back in a Rams uniform, McVay did say that defensive end Myles Garrett, who has been dealing with swelling in his knee, will be “ready to go” in Week 1, according to ESPN. Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year who has the record for most sacks in a season (23), is also considered to be one of the best defensive players of his generation. “ Rams release first injury report of Week 1: 2 starters miss practice (ramswire) “With the Los Angeles Rams playing on Friday morning in Australia, they released their first official injury report of the 2026 season on Tuesday. They practiced in Los Angeles before flying out to Melbourne , and a handful of players were either held out due to injuries or rest. Myles Garrett, who will play against the 49ers in the opener, was listed as a non-participant due to his lingering knee injury. Grant Stuard was limited with a hamstring injury, while Jaylen Watson missed practice because of a toe issue. The severity of Watson’s injury is unclear, but there have been no indications that he’s in danger of missing the opener.“ Raheem Morris used to joke that Aaron Donald would ‘get fat when he retired’ (ramswire) “ ESPN’s Sarah Barshop spoke to Morris, asking if the champion coordinator was surprised by Donald’s return. “No,” said Morris. “I mean, he always stays ready. I used to joke with him and always tell him he’s going to get fat when he retired and he always told me there’s no chance. And he’s right.” Morris’ final game with the Rams was also Donald’s final contest. In their wild-card loss to the Detroit Lions , ending their 2023 season, Morris would go on to become the head coach of the Atlanta Falcons, while Donald opted to retire.“ Sean McVay and Myles Garrett talk Week 1 expectations ahead of Thursday’s matchup against the 49ers (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay and outside linebacker Myles Garrett addressed the media ahead of Thursday’s Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. They discuss expectations around the season opener, maximizing every opportunity & more.” Rams’ Chris Shula names 2nd-year DT who’s been a ‘pleasant surprise’ (ramswire) ““The guy that really stuck out to me was Ty Hamilton,” said Shula on Monday. “I thought he did an awesome job where in camp, it was like Giff (Smith), his position coach, really challenged him to play physical, play fast, play tough. As a rookie, we thought he was kind of thinking and hesitating a little bit too much, and you saw that show up on the tape. He was definitely a pleasant surprise for us, for sure.” Loaded Rams Carry Highest Ceiling, Highest Stakes in the NFL (sports.yahoo) “That talent cuts both ways. Health and chemistry will decide whether the Rams hit their ceiling or floor. Ceiling: 16-1 and Super Bowl Champions Injuries are the Rams’ biggest threat. They strike randomly and have doomed many Super Bowl contenders. Los Angeles does what it can to prevent that, managing practice schedules and giving rest when needed.“ NFL Power Rankings, Week 1: Cowboys rising after defensive makeover; Bears drop out of top 10 (nfl.com) “Am I worried about the statuses of Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua ? Mildly, although Garrett practiced Sunday , and Nacua appears to be on track to play against San Francisco in the opener in Australia. Oh, and Aaron Donald is back on the team now. No movement for the Rams here, but a big test awaits them Down Under.“ Patriots vs. Seahawks: Five must-know storylines for Wednesday’s 2026 NFL Kickoff Game (nfl.com) “Our national nightmare is over. After a 212-day break, the NFL officially returns on Wednesday night, with the New England Patriots visiting the Seattle Seahawks to kick off the 2026 season in an instant rematch of Super Bowl LX . This is the 12th regular-season game between teams that met in the previous Super Bowl, per NFL Research, and the reigning champs are 8-3 in the previous 11 such rematches. Last we saw these two squads on the same field, Seattle’s defense and running game dominated to the tune of a 29-13 victory. Can the Patriots pull off an upset, with marquee offseason acquisition A.J. Brown in tow this time around?“ 49ers catching early breaks — including avoiding Rams’ Aaron Donald (sports.yahoo) “ Kyle Shanahan went out of his way to avoid providing injury updates after the 49ers ‘ first practice in Australia, cleverly pointing out that they were a full day ahead of the Rams . On the flip side, when Aaron Donald was asked about his status after rejoining 11-on-11 practice for the first time this week, all he could muster was a big smile and that he was “feeling good.” Both sides dropped the act Tuesday. And the Niners clearly came out in the more favorable position once the dust of the NFC West rivals’ gamesmanship settled. They’ll have Nick Bosa and George Kittle — and will only have to worry about one future Hall of Famer ( Myles Garrett ) lining up opposite them.“ Comment of the Day: “2 things need to happen for Darnold to maintain his 2025 experience : The O-line needs to keep Darnold upright and clean to make his best reads/throws ( Jared Goff Syndrome) Seattle needs their running game to play to the same levels as 2025, Darnold alone on offense will have dl/dbs with their ears pinned back in mad dog attack ( see Rams/Vikings playoff game )“ -Watcher Of The Skies Fanpost of the Day:

While the emotional investment between the two fan bases always makes the matchup a “must watch ”, this year’s opener adds to the revelry by where it’s taking place, in Melbourne, Australia. It will be the NFL’s first foray down under and the Melbourne Cricket Ground will be the site for the September 10 tilt. Kickoff is set for 5:35 p.m. PDT. It was 1950 when the Rams and 49ers began their rivalry and the temperature has increased over the years. San Francisco leads the series by a slim margin 79-72-3 and has also put up more total points, 3481 to 3280. In the head-to-head battle between current coaches Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan, since both were hired in 2017, Lil’ Shanny and the ‘Niners lead 11-8. Over the last five meetings, L.A. is on a 4-1 run. The Rams, according to NFL.com, did not report any injuries for Week 1. Defensive end Myles Garrett and wide receiver Puka Nacua, who both missed large parts of training camp, are deemed ready to go. Defensive tackle Aaron Donald, getting up to speed after a two-season retirement, is not ready to play and won’t make the first trip. At least for now, L.A. appears to have dodged possible suspensions for Nacua and offensive tackle Alaric Jackson, both are in the fold for Week 1. Here’s how to follow the game!
