title: 49ers lose promising defensive lineman for the year
summary: San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Alfred Collins tore his patella tendon and will miss the entirety of the 2026 season. The injury occurred in Australia in the days leading up to Thursday night’s NFC West clash between the 49ers and Los Angeles Rams. Collins is a promising second-year defensive lineman. San Francisco embraced a defensive […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 28: Alfred Collins #95 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates a win against the Chicago Bears following the game at Levi's Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Alfred Collins tore his patella tendon and will miss the entirety of the 2026 season. The injury occurred in Australia in the days leading up to Thursday night’s NFC West clash between the 49ers and Los Angeles Rams. #49ers DT Alfred Collins tore his patella tendon in practice yesterday. He's out for the season. — Nick Wagoner (@nwagoner) September 9, 2026 Collins is a promising second-year defensive lineman. San Francisco embraced a defensive youth movement over the 2025 offseason and attempted to emulate the Rams’ 2023-2024 turnaround. Collins was a significant piece of that investment as a second-round pick. The 49ers are also missing their first round pick from the same draft class, Mykel Williams, who suffered a season-ending injury last year and remains on the NFL’s Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. Even more troubling is the history of recoveries from patellar injuries. This is a setback that not only threatens Collins’ 2026 season but the trajectory of his career. This is an injury that carries “ one of the highest risks of long-term performance decline ”, especially among heavier players like offensive and defensive linemen. Collins is a significant loss for the 49ers. There is no obvious replacement for him on the roster. CJ West was drafted two rounds after Collins in 2025. He will likely be the next man up, although he earned a lowly Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade of just 39.7 as a rookie. The other alternative is fourth-round rookie Gracen Halton from Oklahoma. If the 49ers were still in the United States, they could likely find a street free agent to be ready by Thursday night. It may be impossible to call in reinforcements to Australia on such short notice. Stay tuned for all updates for the Rams’ season opener on Thursday, and be sure to check out Turf Show Times’ gameday coverage.

title: Will Sam Darnold turn back into a pumpkin?
summary: The NFL season kicks off on Wednesday evening when the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch. It’s unlikely to expect both teams to reach the pinnacle of professional football again in 2026. The NFL stands for “not for long”. It’s a league of parity. Bottom feeders climb to the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - DECEMBER 18: Kobie Turner #91 of the Los Angeles Rams sacks Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on December 18, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL season kicks off on Wednesday evening when the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch. It’s unlikely to expect both teams to reach the pinnacle of professional football again in 2026. The NFL stands for “not for long”. It’s a league of parity. Bottom feeders climb to the top every year. Invisible forces pull contenders back towards average. Those same forces could bring an interesting twist in the storybook tale of Seahawks QB Sam Darnold’s career. Darnold was drafted by the hapless New York Jets. He attempted to rebound with the Carolina Panthers and cast Baker Mayfield out of town, still this stint did little to reinvent his career. Darnold had to pay his dues in a backup role with the San Francisco 49ers before finally scoring an opportunity to shine as a starter with the Minnesota Vikings. But even Minnesota wasn’t comfortable paying Darnold long-term following a crushing playoff loss to the Rams. He had to venture to Seattle in order to land the most significant payday of his career so far. Few thought the Seahawks would upgrade when they traded Geno Smith to the Raiders. Instead, Darnold led Seattle to a Super Bowl victory that most never saw coming. It’s a tale even Hollywood would be jealous of, and it’s fitting that the Seahawks had to take down the Los Angeles twice en route to their championship. How long will this run last for Darnold? Perhaps his downfall is even as difficult to foresee as his comeback. 2025 Leaders in FPts per Dropback on Deep Attempts *min. 20 deep att. Sam Darnold is a big regression candidate without Klint Kubiak. Darnold's last 2 full seasons w/o Kubiak or O'Connell as his playcaller: 2022: 0.74 FPts/db 2021: 0.40 FPts/db I'm sure it's not that bad… pic.twitter.com/WWNdh4c8b0 — Trav (Lunch Pail Stays Strapped) (@TSeel14) May 18, 2026 Why Darnold can turn back into a pumpkin Is Darnold a better quarterback than he was when he entered the league? Yes, but maybe marginally. We cannot ignore the fact he’s enjoyed strong supporting casts the last two years with the Vikings and Seahawks—and that cast is not set to erode much in 2026. But there are concerning signs. Darnold led the NFL in turnovers in the regular season a year ago with 20 (14 interceptions, six fumbles lost). His performance in the first two of three games against the Rams started off rocky. Many were quick to call him “Same Darnold”. In Week 11 Darnold threw 11 interceptions in a Week 11 loss. He tossed another two picks before turnaround his fortune and leading a Week 16 victory. It was a defying moment where he shed weight off his shoulders. He overcame the team that was holding his career back. Will we look back and say definitively that this was the game that changed Darnold’s trajectory? Or could time prove that this was just one moment in a long line that proved to be the exception to the rule? Before I fully buy in to Darnold as a long-term franchise quarterback I’ll need to see him succeed two years in a row. The turnovers are concerning. He enjoyed playing with one of the NFL’s best defenses. That won’t always be the case—and marginal regression could make a big impact in the win/loss columns. Just because Sam Darnold now has a ring on his finger does not mean he’s inevitable. He’s on shaky ground until he proves otherwise.

full_text: WOODLAND HILLS, CALIFORNIA - MAY 26: Jaylen Watson #35 of the Los Angeles Rams walks off the field after an OTA offseason workout at Rams Village at Warner Center on May 26, 2026 in Woodland Hills, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Rams have not expressed any concerns about Myles Garrett’s knee injury keeping him out of Week 1, despite the reigning Defensive Player of the Year missing so many practices already, but suddenly Jaylen Watson’s name is on the injury report just two days before L.A.‘s opening game against the San Francisco 49ers. Watson and Garrett are two of five Rams starters listed with a “Did Not Practice” on Tuesday, alongside Byron Young, A.J. Jackson, and Tyler Higbee. Here’s the first injury report of the week for the Rams and 49ers: CB Jaylen Watson did not practice with a toe injury. pic.twitter.com/1Z7hkWhwRR — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) September 8, 2026 Watson, one of L.A.’s major signings this offseason with a three-year, $51 million contract , is dealing with a toe injury. McVay: Myles Garrett (knee) will play Week 1. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) September 8, 2026 On the same note, there’s no indication that Young, Jackson, or Higbee will be held out of Week 1 either. author: Kenneth Arthur

title: 5Qs, 5As with Niners Nation: Mike Evans expected to be a ‘favorite target’ in SF
summary: The Los Angeles Rams kick off the season against a familiar foe in the San Francisco 49ers, this time in Australia. Both teams split the season series in 2025, with the Niners winning in overtime in Week 5, and the Rams returning the favor in a 42-26 beatdown in Week 10. Several players are new […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Mike Evans #5 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during training camp practice at SAP Performance Facility on July 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams kick off the season against a familiar foe in the San Francisco 49ers, this time in Australia. Both teams split the season series in 2025, with the Niners winning in overtime in Week 5, and the Rams returning the favor in a 42-26 beatdown in Week 10. Several players are new to the rivalry after joining the franchises this offseason. Most notably on the 49ers side is future Hall of Fame wide receiver Mike Evans, who swapped one bay for another after spending his first 12 seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Before we throw some extra shrimp (and hot wings) on the barbie for Thursday’s game, I spoke with Nicholas McGee from Niners Nation to get the inside scoop on Evans, the Niners’ injury concerns, the team’s travel plans and more. Q – Injuries have been a major concern for San Francisco for years under Kyle Shanahan, and it seems to be more of the same in a wild offseason for the Niners. Who are some key players battling the injury bug entering the season opener? A – The standout is Nick Bosa , who is dealing with knee tendonitis related to his ACL surgery. It seems like that’s an issue they’ll have to cope with all season, which is a significant problem given the distinct lack of difference-makers off the edge aside from him. Mykel Williams is on PUP and rookie edge Romello Height has dealt with an ankle issue. On offense, George Kittle’s Week 1 status was a question-mark following his Achilles tear in the playoffs last season, but it seems as if he will be ready to go almost eight months to the day of that injury. Q – We know about LA’s one-two punch at wide receiver, and the 49ers might have their own with free agent addition Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel back in the fold. How are you expecting that duo to fare in the offense this season? A – As long as he stays healthy, I anticipate Evans developing an excellent rapport with Brock Purdy and becoming the quarterback’s favorite target this season. With Samuel, I think his production is partially dependent on how the deep passing game fares. The 49ers brought in Evans and drafted De’Zhaun Stribling with a view to improving their downfield attack. Should that duo have success in winning deep, that will create more space underneath for Samuel, whose best work has always come in the short to intermediate areas. At this stage in his career, it’s hard to envisage Samuel being a huge part of the run game as he was for much of his first spell with the 49ers, and there are too many other options in the passing game to expect him to get close to a third season with over 1,000 scrimmage yards. San Francisco got 806 scrimmage yards and four scores from Samuel back in 2024. While they might hope for more in terms of touchdowns, I think they would see that kind of yardage as a success for Samuel. Q – Who have been some standout players in training camp and preseason that Rams fans should know? A – Stribling was the star of camp and preseason. His selection with the 33rd overall pick raised a lot of eyebrows, but there’s already evidence to suggest that pick will be justified. He’s excelled running timing routes that are a staple of the offense and has demonstrated impressive body control and strong hands while essentially cementing his spot as WR2. Stribling has the speed to be a true deep threat and do significant damage after the catch. I would expect him to be an integral part of the passing game this year. On defense, there are a couple of names. Rookie fourth-round pick Gracen Halton flashed in preseason and looks to be a player who, alongside Osa Odighizuwa, can provide a substantial boost to an interior pass rush that was too often ineffective last season. There’s also a great deal of excitement around rookie fifth-round linebacker Jaden Dugger. He’s a former safety who possesses an outstanding blend of size and speed and has shone with his speed to the ball in preseason. Though defensive coordinator Raheem Morris has urged patience with Dugger, he’ll likely see the field early as the SAM linebacker and could be key to slowing down the Rams when they get into those 13 personnel looks. Dugger has also been cross-training as a pass rusher and, with the 49ers light on numbers at edge rusher, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see San Francisco take advantage of that versatility right off the bat. Q – Much of the talk this offseason has been about the Rams and Seahawks, but the Niners are no slouch, as they’re coming off a 12-win campaign. How do you expect their season to play out in 2026? A – Unfortunately, I think it will be quite similar to last season, though hopefully with fewer injuries. I expect another double-digit win season, but I think the massive hole at left guard — where rookie fourth-rounder Carver Willis seems the most likely starter — and the lack of strength in depth on the defensive line place a cap on this team’s ceiling. I expect Kyle Shanahan to pick up his 10th career playoff win, but the 49ers are still a step below their division rivals for me. Right now it’s hard to view the Niners as anything more than a wild-card team that exits in the Divisional Round again. Q – San Francisco is a 3.5-point underdog at FanDuel Sportsbook ahead of their venture down under against LA. Much has been debated about both teams’ travel plans, so which do you think will pan out and why? A – Rams and 49ers games are always fun, and with the strength of the two offenses, I expect the first game in Australia to be very entertaining. I do think the Rams are taking a little bit of a gamble with their travel plans — though it worked for them last year in London — but when I look at the two rosters I see more avenues for Los Angeles to get defensive stops than I do with San Francisco. Three-and-a-half points is about right. It’ll be close, but I think the Rams win. Let’s go 34-30.

(Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The wait is nearly finally over. The 2026 NFL regular season is here, and Week 1 offers 16 games spread across four days. From a Super Bowl rematch to the league’s first regular-season game in Australia, there are plenty of intriguing matchups to consider before locking in your picks. New England Patriots @ Seattle Seahawks — Wed., 8:20 p.m. ET The NFL season begins with a Super Bowl LX rematch. The Seahawks return home looking to defend their championship, while the Patriots get an immediate opportunity to prove they can contend again in the AFC. Seattle will have to replace Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III, who is now with Kansas City, while New England will look to make life difficult for the Seahawks’ offense. The biggest questions involve how both teams have changed since their championship matchup and which team handles the pressure of opening the season under the national spotlight. My Pick: Seahawks 30-10 San Francisco 49ers @ Los Angeles Rams — Thurs., 8:35 p.m. ET The NFC West rivalry gets an unusual setting as the Rams and 49ers meet at Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia. This is the NFL’s first regular-season game in Australia, adding an additional layer to an already important divisional matchup. Travel, preparation and the unusual game environment could all become factors. Sean McVay’s Rams enter the season with major expectations, while Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers will try to establish themselves immediately in the division. The battle in the trenches and the ability of each offense to find a rhythm overseas will be worth watching. My Pick: Rams 27-20 Chicago Bears @ Carolina Panthers — Sunday, 1 p.m. ET Two former No. 1 overall picks headline this matchup as Caleb Williams and the Bears travel to face Bryce Young and the Panthers. Williams enters his second season looking to continue his development, while Young is attempting to build on the progress he showed last season. Chicago’s defense could create problems if it generates consistent pressure, while Carolina needs to find ways to keep its offense on schedule. The quarterback matchup naturally receives the most attention, but whichever team controls the line of scrimmage could have a significant advantage. Baltimore’s physical rushing attack and defensive pressure will immediately test the Colts. Indianapolis, meanwhile, will need to find ways to consistently move the football against one of the league’s most aggressive defenses. Turnovers could be especially important in a game featuring two teams that would like to establish their identity early. Both teams may want to lean on their bruising running backs..Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor to set a tone early. My Pick: Ravens 23-13 Atlanta Falcons @ Pittsburgh Steelers — Sunday, 1 p.m. ET This matchup features two teams with plenty of questions entering the season. Atlanta has undergone significant changes and could lean heavily on its rushing attack and defense, while Pittsburgh enters another season built around physical football. The Steelers’ pass rush will be a major factor, particularly if Atlanta struggles to protect its quarterback. Pittsburgh will also be looking for consistency offensively. With both teams having playoff aspirations, this could be an early test of which roster is better prepared to handle pressure situations. My Pick: Steelers 16-9 Cleveland Browns @ Jacksonville Jaguars — Sunday, 1 p.m. ET The Browns and Jaguars enter Week 1 with plenty to prove. On the other side, Tampa Bay’s ability to protect Mayfield against Cincinnati’s pass rush will be equally important. Tennessee also enters the season with second-year quarterback Cam Ward, giving the Titans a young centerpiece to build around. The Chargers’ ability to establish the run could be particularly important, as it would prevent the Cardinals from simply focusing on the passing game. Arizona’s ability to generate pressure and create turnovers could keep the game competitive. My Pick: Chargers 31-17 Green Bay Packers @ Minnesota Vikings — Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET An NFC North rivalry opens the season with Green Bay visiting Minnesota. The Vikings will have the advantage…

title: The Rams’ new long snapper is special
summary: Joe Cardone is the Rams’ long snapper for the next two years after being signed by LA this past offseason, and he’s good, very good. So good, in fact, that he’s now the third-highest-paid long snapper in the league. While a salary of $1.725 million doesn’t seem like a whole lot in a sport where […]
full_text: Football: New England Patriots long snapper Joe Cardona (49) in action, snaps the football vs Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Green Bay, WI 10/2/2022 CREDIT: David E. Klutho (Photo by David E. Klutho/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X164183 TK1) Joe Cardone is the Rams’ long snapper for the next two years after being signed by LA this past offseason, and he’s good, very good. So good, in fact, that he’s now the third-highest-paid long snapper in the league. While a salary of $1.725 million doesn’t seem like a whole lot in a sport where almost all players are making over a million dollars a year, it’s a raise of more than $300,000, or about 20%, and it will surely impact the Cardone family. The position of long snapper is about as glamorous in football terms as is the bass player in the house band at your local bar. Nobody notices them until they make a mistake. In fact, I’d be willing to bet 98% of all football fans couldn’t name two long snappers in the league, and probably 97% couldn’t name the one playing on their own team, but they’re important. CARDONE’S JOURNEY Joe Cardone’s father was a Navy man , and he instilled many Navy traits in the young man, such as discipline and the belief that being on time means arriving at least fifteen minutes early. Joe’s dad was also his junior football coach. They’d arrive at practices a half hour early, his dad teaching him the finer points, as he knew them, of kicking, punting, and long snapping because he wasn’t sure if his son would grow to be large enough for many other positions in the game. But even after a growth spurt, Joe decided to refine his LS skills. Says Joe: “I was very fortunate that my father had the foresight to teach me a specialty,” “I probably didn’t have the genetics to be in the NFL unless I learned something different. I probably didn’t have the genetics to be a college football player, to be honest. Fortunately, I got a good head start.” Following in his father’s footsteps, Joe attended the Naval Academy, where they encouraged him to focus on his LS game, and by the time he was ready to enter the draft, he’d bulked up to 240 pounds. At the Naval Academy, you don’t think there’s going to be this opportunity. You’re not planning on it. I was planning on being an officer and preparing for that. My thought process was, ‘Hey, if I can prepare to be the best Navy football player I can be and it turns into something bigger, then, that’s a win. At least I’m doing my job here.'” Bill Belichick and the New England Patriots selected Cardone in the 5th round of the 2015 draft, making Joe one of the few LS in history to be drafted. They liked him so much that they kept him on the team for 10 years. During that time, he played in four Super Bowls. When they released him, the Dolphins quickly signed him to a one-year deal. Perhaps they should have signed him to a longer deal, but the Rams are happy he didn’t. WHY THE RAMS NEEDED HIM As I said above, the only time you notice a LS is when they screw up. Sadly, that was the case with Alex Ward, who started last season as the Rams’ LS. I believe this was the turning point for Ward: By the time Ward lifts his head, the entire defensive line is behind him! If it weren’t the Rams, you’d have to laugh. Rams head coach Sean McVay wasn’t laughing, and Jake McQuaide was hired to finish out the year, and with his 39th birthday coming up, I’m not sure he was even being considered for this season. Aside from blocking well , Cardone also gets involved in coverage better than most long snappers. While most will average one tackle a year, usually assisted, Cardone has had 5 over the past two seasons and even forced a fumble. It’s that type of play that gets you noticed by the GOAT. Belichick was asked once if he’d consider removing the long snapper position altogether and just cross-training a player at another position on the team. Belichick’s response went 1,500 words. Not exactly the concise Belichick we know, he finished with: “I mean, it’s a great question,” Belichick ultimately concluded. “There would be so much value in a player that could do a couple of things and save a roster spot, but I would say there are so few of those players available … I’m not saying it’s impossible or unheard of, but it’s a lot to ask, and that’s why you don’t see it very much.” Belichick saw that a team absolutely needs the LS specialist; now Rams fans will get a chance to. I mean, if you notice him.

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks to pass against the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Heading into the Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, there’s been some discussion about whether Fernando Mendoza or Aidan O’Connell will be the backup quarterback behind starter Kirk Cousins while the other serves as the emergency/third QB. The Raiders released their first listed depth chart ahead of Week 1. pic.twitter.com/MzFENWqK6m — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) September 8, 2026 It’s important to note that this is unofficial, and the coaching staff could mix it up by game day. title: Michael Mayer, Jackson Powers-Johnson, 8 Las Vegas Raiders entering make-or-break season in 2026
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are entering year one of a rebuild, which means a heavy emphasis of the upcoming season is determining which players on the roster can be part of the team’s long-term plan. Within that, a handful of younger veterans, primarily guys entering the second-to-last or last year of their rookie contract, are […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 28: Michael Mayer #87 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs the ball against the New York Giants in the third quarter of their game at Allegiant Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are entering year one of a rebuild, which means a heavy emphasis of the upcoming season is determining which players on the roster can be part of the team’s long-term plan . Within that, a handful of younger veterans, primarily guys entering the second-to-last or last year of their rookie contract, are heading into a make-or-break season heading into the 2026 campaign. Michael Mayer Mayer has had an interesting tenure in Las Vegas. He was viewed as the long-term answer at tight end after being a second-round pick, but that only lasted a year after the Raiders took Brock Bowers in the first round during the following draft. On top of that, health issues have taken the Notre Dame product off the field, as he’s missed at least three games each season so far in his career. Also, Mayer is part of the group of players who are about to play for their fourth head coach in as many years and have had several offensive play callers in Vegas. So, there’s a handful of justifications for his lack of production to this point. However, with Klint Kubiak’s 12 personnel-heavy offense and the fact that he’s entering a contract year, it feels like it’s the “now or never” period for Mayer. Especially since the offense lacks talent at wide receiver and could use someone else to step up and pick up the slack. Jackson Powers-Johnson While Powers-Johnson started 21 games during his first two seasons, he’s left something to be desired. The 2024 second-round pick has had a handful of impressive outings, but the consistency in his play has been lacking. So much so that he was competing with second-year pro Caleb Rogers to remain with the first-string offense during training camp. At the time of writing, Kubiak hasn’t officially named a starting right guard, but all signs are pointing toward JPJ winning that battle. In other words, the third-year pro has another chance to prove himself as a formidable and consistent starter. But if he doesn’t, Rogers is lurking to take over the spot. JPJ also has to prove that he can stay healthy after missing 11 total games over the last two seasons combined. DJ Glaze It was surprising that the Silver and Black didn’t have a competition for the starting right tackle job during training camp. Glaze struggled last season to the point where it looked like he was going to have to at least fight to get his spot back in 2026. But, to his credit, the third-year pro had a good enough summer to ease some concerns and was really sharp in the two preseason games he played in. Now, Glaze needs to build on that momentum and continue to play well when the competition level rises. While there may not be an immediate replacement on the roster, right tackle will be a priority in the offseason if the 2024 third-round pick isn’t getting the job done, especially in pass protection. Tommy Eichenberg Defensively, Eichenberg’s hopes of becoming a significant contributor may be hanging on by a thread. It appears as if he’s entering the 2026 campaign as the fourth linebacker on the depth chart, behind starters Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker and backup Cody Lindenberg. So, the 2024 fifth-round pick’s chances of becoming a contributing backer are fading away. However, Dean and Walker have both missed several games over the last few years, adding extra significance to the Raiders’ linebacker depth. So, Eichenberg could have one more chance to show that he can impact the game beyond special teams. Dylan Laube Along the same line, Laube enters his third season as the third running back behind Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr., signaling the third-year pro will primarily be a special teamer again. However, Jeanty may not be 100 percent entering the year after suffering a sprained ankle at the end of training camp. That could lead to some third-down opportunities for Laube at the beginning of the season, which he’ll need to make the most of if he’s going to have a role in the offense moving forward. Laube did have a handful of impressive catches during the preseason, making defenders miss to pick up first downs, to build off of. Ball security also needs to be a point of emphasis for him after fumbling twice on just 11 touches during his first two seasons. Jonah Laulu Laulu is in a fairly similar situation as Powers-Johnson. The defensive tackle has recorded 22 starts over the last two seasons, including 15 last year. Additionally, he’s provided a handful of splash plays to show some promise but has struggled with consistency, forcing him to compete to remain in the starting lineup this summer. However, where Laulu and Powers-Johnson differ is that it appears as if the former is looking at having more of a rotational role behind Adam Butler and Tonka Hemingway this season. Fellow 2025 starter Thomas Booker IV may even be ahead of Laulu on the depth chart right now, while second-year pro JJ Pegues and veteran Foley Fatukasi are lurking in the shadows. So, the third-year pro is close to being expendable if he doesn’t step up this year. Isaiah Pola-Mao Pola-Mao is different than the six players previously discussed here since he’s entering year five in the NFL/with the Raiders. He was primarily a special teamer in years one and two, though, before becoming a regular starter at free safety over the last two seasons. However, his time as a starter might be coming to an end with rookie second-round pick Treydan Stukes factoring into the mix. Las Vegas hasn’t specified who the starting free safety is yet, but Stukes was seen getting reps with the first-team defense toward the end of training camp while Pola-Mao was just mixing in with the ones. Considering that the veteran is in a contract year, it certainly seems like his seat is getting warm in the desert. Malcolm Koonce Another guy who breaks the rookie contract mold, Koonce is a rare player to receive “prove-it” contracts in back-to-back offseasons. He signed another one-year, $11 million-and-change deal, with the hopes that he can get back to the eight-sack performance he put together in 2023. Being two years removed from a torn ACL should help the bounce-back effort, but that also means the excuse train is leaving the station. If Koonce doesn’t produce in 2026, Las Vegas has too much invested at edge defender between signing Kwity Paye and spending a third-round pick on Keyron Crawford this offseason—on top of Maxx Crosby still being in the building—to justify keeping him around any longer.

title: How Patrick Johnson made Las Vegas Raiders’ 53-man roster during preseason
summary: Arguably the biggest surprise from the Las Vegas Raiders’ preseason was the emergence of edge defender Patrick Johnson. The 28-year-old was signed the day before veterans reported to training camp but was arguably the team’s top performer during the preseason to earn a spot on the Raiders’ 53-man roster. According to Pro Football Focus, Johnson […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - AUGUST 20: Defensive end Patrick Johnson #93 of the Las Vegas Raiders readies for play during the NFL preseason game between the Houston Texans and the Las Vegas Raiders on August 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Arguably the biggest surprise from the Las Vegas Raiders’ preseason was the emergence of edge defender Patrick Johnson . The 28-year-old was signed the day before veterans reported to training camp but was arguably the team’s top performer during the preseason to earn a spot on the Raiders’ 53-man roster . According to Pro Football Focus , Johnson led Las Vegas with five pressures and tied for second among NFL edge defenders with a 90.2 defensive grade. The latter was the result of recording a pair of sacks (including a strip sack) and four ‘defensive stops’ against the run. Clearly, that was enough to catch the coaching staff’s attention, so let’s flip on the tape and see what he can bring to the team. Patrick Johnson's best rep of the preseason Wins with speed and a rip move to get the strip sack #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/BFpKNDBVOS — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 2, 2026 We’ll start with Johnson’s best rep of the preseason, and apologies for the Houston Texans being in preseason mode with their endzone camera. It’s third and five as the Texans leave their left tackle on an island with no tight end or running back on his side. That, combined with the Raiders putting three defensive linemen on the other side of the offensive line and having the middle linebacker present a blitz threat over the center pre-snap, sets up a one-on-one opportunity for the right edge defender. Johnson takes advantage by winning with speed and a rip move around the edge before ripping at the ball while the quarterback starts his throwing motion, creating the turnover that gives the Raiders the ball on the plus side of the field. This was something that stood out about the late free-agent signing’s performance, showing good speed around the edge on a handful of occasions. Patrick Johnson's 1st sack of the preseason Turns speed to power to get the RT off-balance and be in position to make the play when QB tries to leave the pocket #Raiders pic.twitter.com/kCN2qSK3xL — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 2, 2026 We’re working backward as this is Johnson’s first sack of the preseason, which shows off some pass-rush diversity. This time, the tackle he’s going against has some help with the in-line tight end chip blocking before releasing into a route. Notice how Johnson eyes the tight end off the line of scrimmage. He sees the chip is coming and beats the tight end to the punch by planting off his outside foot to turn speed to power into the right tackle. While he’s still going in the direction that the offense wants him to go, that allows the edge-rusher to stay in control of his pass-rush rather than getting knocked off-balance and reduced inside. That’s a smart decision because the offense’s formation/play call protects the edge, meaning it’s going to be very difficult to win with an outside move. Instead, Johnson gets the right tackle off-balance by maintaining his momentum and effectively turning speed to power. He also does a great job of using his hands before and after initial contact to keep the tackle off his body. So, when the quarterback tries to step up and escape the pocket, the pass-rusher is in position to come up with the sack. Cardinals chip Patrick Johnson to create a soft edge, but Johnson recovers and recognizes the QB leaving the pocket to force the grounding call #Raiders pic.twitter.com/yRRxtvD0hn — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 2, 2026 The Cardinals have a similar pass protection call here, where the tight end chip blocks Johnson. The difference is that the tight end is more aggressive this time and makes contact with Johnson before Johnson can turn speed to power or work an inside pass-rush move. That creates a soft edge for the defense, which the quarterback tries to take advantage of by scrambling out of the pocket. However, the veteran pass-rusher makes a heads-up play, recognizing the scramble and taking a good pursuit angle to meet the quarterback near the sideline. While Johnson can do a better job of breaking down in space to finish with a sack here, he doesn’t completely overpursue and is still in a position to force the ball out for an intentional grounding call. So net-net, the result is about the same as a sack. Patrick Johnson on the backside of a zone run, closes the gap with the man and squeezes to clean the play up with a TFL after Fatuaski gets penetration #Raiders pic.twitter.com/x0CtgFThNS — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 2, 2026 Shifting gears to run defense, Johnson is on the backside of a zone run here. The Texans have a receiver in a reduced split (in other words, close to the offensive line) to protect the backside of the play. Technically, the edge defender should stay inside of the receiver’s block to take away the D-gap between the tight end and wideout, while the cornerback (No. 28, Jermod McCoy) is responsible for containing the outside. However, Johnson still fulfills his responsibility by closing the gap with the man, pushing the receiver inside so that the receiver ends up hip-to-hip with the right tackle. That takes the C- and D-gaps away from the running back and puts Johnson in a perfect position to get involved in the TFL after a great rep by Foley Fatuaksi, where Fatuaksi gets immediate penetration in the backfield. For a breakdown of this play from the defensive tackle’s perspective, see the related article below. Something that stood out about Patrick Johnson's run defense is that he refuses to get blocked by TEs Sets the edge and wins across the TE's face to make the tackle here #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/wdSLDoSbYY — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 2, 2026 Finally, what stood out the most about the six-year pro’s run defense was that he refused to get blocked by tight ends. He’s on the playside/strong side of Houston’s halfback dive call. Fatukasi pops up again by taking away both A-gaps and forcing the running back to bounce outside. The back tries to take advantage of the open lane in the C-gap. However, Johnson wins at the point of attack against the Texans’ tight end to set the edge and beat the tight end across the tight end’s face to make the tackle for a short gain. That effectively takes away two rushing lanes because the edge defender was also in perfect position to make the play had the running back bounced outside even further. It remains to be seen how much playing time Johnson will get and how impactful he will be when the competition level rises during the regular season. But there’s no denying that the veteran earned the job as the Raiders’ fourth edge defender with his performance this summer.

title: How the Las Vegas Raiders are going to win season opener against Miami Dolphins
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders open the 2026 season at home at Allegiant Stadium against the Miami Dolphins. With the preseason now behind us, we have had three games to try to decipher what this team is all about. Let’s take a stab at how the Raiders are going to beat the Dolphins. First things first, […]
full_text: The Las Vegas Raiders open the 2026 season at home at Allegiant Stadium against the Miami Dolphins. With the preseason now behind us, we have had three games to try to decipher what this team is all about. Let’s take a stab at how the Raiders are going to beat the Dolphins. First things first, we must acknowledge that the Dolphins parted ways with former head coach Mike McDaniel and began the tear down stage of a rebuild. Currently, the Dolphins feature a quarterback making his first NFL season-opener starting as the guy, an explosive running back, no more Tyreek Hill or Jaylen Waddle or Darren Waller and an offensive line with question marks. The defense is filled with guys yet to prove themselves and a new coordinator and coaching staff. Win the line of scrimmage on offense and defense Games are won and lost in the trenches. It’s no surprise that a run-dominant team such as the Raiders would want to impose its will. Controlling the line of scrimmage and pushing defenders back will be the optimal first day out for the starting offensive line. Defensively, this is a taller order. The return of Maxx Crosby will give the Raiders an elite presence at the edge. The interior is a different story altogether. Through the preseason, Folorunso Fatukasi has provided the most amount of push up the middle. Will he be a rotational piece, or will he be the starting nose tackle, remains to be seen. Miami’s primary weapon on offense is going to be its running back. Contain Devon Achane Achane is fast and explosive. If he has lanes to run through with blockers in front of him, it could make for a long day on defense. In the past, he was utilized primarily as an outside zone, stretch and counter runner. In new offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik’s scheme, we should expect him to do more of the same. If the Raiders can not control the line of scrimmage, they will be in a very bad way. Achane is the type of back who can and will put up career numbers in a hurry. More importantly, if he gets going, then he takes a ton of pressure off of his quarterback. Don’t sleep on Malik Willis Willis desperately needed a change of scenery after Jordan Love entrenched himself as the Packers quarterback of the future. In his last three starts, he went 2-1. Throwing for 972 yards, six touchdowns and no interceptions, while completing 78.7% of his passes. The Raiders have young defensive backs; if the running game is leaving them on an island, eventually the play-action pass is going to cook them. If the Raiders pass rush outside of Crosby is unable to corral Willis and allow him to break contain and run around, things could get ugly. Willis is a talented dual-threat quarterback looking to establish himself and the Raiders should tread carefully. Keep Kirk protected Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins is a good quarterback capable of winning games in the NFL. Having a football player of the caliber of Brock Bowers will allow him to have success for as long as he has time to throw. The Raiders may be a run-first team, but Kubiak designed an offense in Seattle that made Sam Darnold the first USC quarterback ever to win a Super Bowl. If the offensive line can do its job and keep defenders off of Cousins, he can stand in the pocket and do his thing. He will find the open receiver, get him the football in rhythm and place it where they can do something with it after the catch. Cousins will manage the Raiders to a win if kept upright.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Raiders News: ESPN gives Las Vegas slim playoff odds in Klint Kubiak’s 1st season
summary: In the span of about two months during the offseason, new Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak went from winning the Super Bowl to making the first pick of the NFL Draft. In other words, Kubiak went from being a part of the best team in the NFL to taking over the worst team […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Head coach Klint Kubiak of the Las Vegas Raiders walks on the field during warmups before a preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 18-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the span of about two months during the offseason, new Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak went from winning the Super Bowl to making the first pick of the NFL Draft. In other words, Kubiak went from being a part of the best team in the NFL to taking over the worst team in the league. The Raiders are also entering year one of a rebuild after reconstructing the roster during the spring. As a result, not much is expected of the former Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator during his first season as the head man in Las Vegas. A good example of that comes from a recent season preview and predictions column from ESPN , where the Silver and Black were given just a five percent chance to make the playoffs. The article also gives Kubiak’s crew a 1.3 percent chance to win the competitive AFC West, a projected 5.7 wins with a “best-case scenario” of an 8-9 record and matching last year’s 3-14 mark as the worst case. That begs the question: With such low expectations heading into the campaign, how do the Raiders measure success in 2026? “[Fernando] Mendoza shows the signs of a franchise quarterback,” ESPN’s Ryan McFadden said in response to the question above. “The Raiders are a young team that requires patience, so it’s not worth placing postseason expectations on them. But whenever Las Vegas decides to start Mendoza, it will be important for him to show flashes that he can guide this offense for the foreseeable future. Given the team’s recent history at quarterback, having stability at the position is essential for turning the organization around. Building on McFadden’s take, the youth movement in Las Vegas likely won’t yield immediate results in terms of the win/loss column. Instead, the organization’s biggest priority should be developing the young roster so that the team can grow together and become a legitimate and consistent contender in 2027 and beyond. Obviously, Mendoza is the biggest factor in that. But that could mean taking some bumps and bruises during the upcoming season, which starts on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins. In Other Raiders’ Links: More practice squad moves: The Raiders announced that they added defensive/nose tackle Tim Keenan III and tight end/fullback Patrick Gurd to the practice squad , releasing defensive/nose tackle Gary Smith III and safety Devin Lafayette in corresponding moves. Raiders land edge rusher in early mock draft: “The Las Vegas Raiders were this close to trading Maxx Crosby this offseason. With or without Crosby next year, the lineup could still use another pass-rush threat to improve the entire defensive front. Texas’ Colin Simmons is super-productive and difficult to handle working off the edge,” via Bleacher Report’s Scouting Department . title: 10 bold predictions for Dolphins 2026 season
summary: Every other city we go; every other video; no matter where I go, I see the same… NFL power rankings for the Miami Dolphins.  Pick a site… any site… and I guarantee you that you’ll see the Miami Dolphins ranked 32nd.  That negative 3-star restaurant that gave you expired sushi and cold pizza rolls?  They […]
full_text: Every other city we go; every other video; no matter where I go, I see the same… NFL power rankings for the Miami Dolphins. Pick a site… any site… and I guarantee you that you’ll see the Miami Dolphins ranked 32nd. That negative 3-star restaurant that gave you expired sushi and cold pizza rolls? They have a higher ranking than the Dolphins and they aren’t even an NFL team. Expectations are THAT low for the Dolphins. Everyone expects this team to be the Keystone Cops of the league, being a day off for any opponent to play them. Even the most optimistic media source out there predicts a high total of 5 wins. Five. One, two, three, four, FIIIIIFFFFTH! Well don’t let the eternal optimist within you listen to the negativity. The 2026 Miami Dolphins are here to spit in the wind face of all the doubters. Even if they don’t, they will be a tougher out than people are expecting and maybe even fun to watch. Ol’ Earl’s here with some bold predictions that will show you how. 1. MALIK WILLIS PROVES TO BE A FRANCHISE QUARTERBACK I was firmly on board the “Sign Malik Willis” train in March and was incredibly excited when I saw the news he was going to be a Dolphin. Losing receiver Jaylen Waddle put a dent into the expectations for the signal caller, but the rookie class has stepped up and may give some electricity to the pass catching units. But they are rookies and rookies have growing pains and lessons to learn and all the other 90s sitcoms tropes . But that won’t stop me from making this prediction. I highlighted what I think will be baseline expectations for Willis on Substack . Now, I’m predicting he will exceed them. I believe he will pass all the “eye test” criteria. I also think he will exceed the statistical baseline. I’m going to go with a 66% CP, 7.7 YPA, 5.7% TD%, and 1.8% INT%. Using my same dropbacks and attempts totals (595 dropbacks; 476 attempts), that gives him a stat line of 314-476, 3665 yards, 27 TDs, and 9 INTs. That would yield a passer rating of 100.17. Looking at 2025 stats, that would put 12th in yards (a grand total of 3 yards behind what Josh Allen threw for), 16th in completion percentage (just under, but in line with Burrow, Herbert, and Love), tied for 6th in TDs thrown, 7th in TD%, and 10th in passer rating. Those aren’t All-Pro numbers, MVP numbers, or numbers that necessarily stand out. But given the overall situation, these numbers mean that Miami has found their QB for now and the future. 2. TIGHT END GREG DULCICH ECLIPSES 1000 RECEIVING YARDS Dulcich was an afterthought to most fans during the 2025 offseason. The Dolphins added him to the practice squad in late August, then elevated him in late October. He played in 10 games, with 3 starts. He didn’t play until week 8. He didn’t receive a target until week 9. He managed to get 33 targets, 26 catches, 335 yards, and 1 TD. His 33 targets in those 9 games works out to 3.7 or so per game. In 2026, he does not have any target hogs in front of him. There is no more Tyreek Hill, Jaylen Waddle, or Darren Waller. The rookie class looks promising, but they need to prove it. While that loss of proven talent hurts overall, this gives Dulcich a big opportunity step into a prominent role. He has already developed some chemistry with Malik Willis and he was making plays in OTAs. He was quiet in preseason, but the starters didn’t get much playing time. Can he really get to 1000 yards though? Last season, his yards per reception average was 12.9. He had couple of games below 10, but he was mostly above 11. For the sake of argument, let’s say he averages 12 even. To get to 1000 yards, he would need 84 receptions. Based on his catch percentage, he’d need about 108 targets. On a per game basis, that’s 6.4 targets. Are you telling me that the Dolphins and all the questions regarding their pass catchers, can’t find 3 more targets per game to Dulcich? Yes, I know the Dolphins want to be more run oriented. But last season saw the Dolphins throw the least of any season under McDaniel. There were still targets to go around. It can be done. 3. THE OFFENSIVE LINE RANKS TOP 10 FOR THE SEASON Ah yes… the dreaded profootballfocus talk. They posted their 2026 OL rankings and surprisingly, the Dolphins were not ranked in the low 40s. They weren’t even last! They were in the bottom quartile, however. But do not fear folks… for I predict that the Miami Dolphins offensive line will have fans turning those thumbs the right way up and that the OL will be a top-10 unit in the league. In what you ask? Pressures allowed. Pressures allowed per game. Per dropback. Pass Block Win Rate. Run Block Win Rate. Best dressed. Iron Chef rankings. I care not for what metric is to be used. Miami’s offensive line will be top 10 in ALL of them. Outside of QB, I can’t think of a position or position group more polarizing to Dolphins fans. It doesn’t matter who they sign, how much they spend, who they draft, or how many players they draft. The offensive line remains a sore spot. In 2026, the OL will shut the fans up. Well… most of them. Patrick Paul continues to develop into one of the best LTs in the league and was named captain. Kadyn Proctor locks down the LG spot and strikes fear into the hearts of interior DL. Aaron Brewer continues his All-Pro run. Jonah Savaiinaea proves that his rookie season was an aberration and locks down the RG spot. Either Austin Jackson plays all season and plays well, or Caedan Wallace steps in and fills in seamlessly. In either case, the OL goes from constant weakness to a source of strength in 2026. And that’s the bottom line … 4. ALL THREE ROOKIE RECEIVERS HAVE A MINIMUM OF 500 YARDS EACH The Dolphins knew they needed help in the receiver room and the cheap vets they signed weren’t going to be the answer. They added 3 rookies in the draft. But at the time, there were serious questions. The “consensus” board had Caleb Douglas – the 75th overall pick – as a late day three player and was considered a reach. Chris Bell was coming off an injury that would force him to redshirt his rookie season. Kevin Coleman Jr. was a slot specialist only and would be stuck behind Malik Washington. All that “help” was just half-truths and gorilla dust. Fast forward to now… the “reach” earned his spot in the starting lineup. Bell hasn’t just returned from injury; he has played real football in a Dolphins uniform. It was real. I seent it. Oh… and guess who is the other outside starter at receiver ? Coleman? Making plays in preseason. One could very easily argue that the rookies would have shown out more in preseason if the QB play hadn’t been buns. Well… except for Douglas. He only played the limited reps with the starters and was stashed for the regular season. Of course, preseason doesn’t mean anything. We’ve all seen players show out, then disappear. But I don’t think this rookie group will. They will be used and used heavily. Receiver is a position that generally transitions quickly from college to the pros. Yeah, learning curve and growing pains and all that. But this trio is going to be a force. To the point they each get at least 500 yards. Is that too bold? Following the previous predictions, I have Willis at 3665 yards. Dulcich is getting at least 1000 of those. If the rookie trio ( assignment for the class: create a nickname for the trio ) gets at least 1500 total, that leaves just over 1100 for everyone else. That’s Washington, Achane, and whomever else. So no, I don’t think it’s too bold. I would argue I’m underselling it. 5. CHOP ROBINSON GETS DOUBLE DIGIT SACKS AND MAKES A PRO BOWL The Dolphins traded Jaelen Phillips last season and released Bradley Chubb this offseason. That left the edge room bereft of talent. They didn’t have the financial resources to go out and sign players. They didn’t really address it in the draft, with the first edge player being a 4th round pick and he is more of a hybrid player. That put the onus to lead the pass rush group firmly on the shoulders of the former 1st round pick.…

I dont dislike the Pats or bill just the Jets and that is because I live on LI But in order for their to be a rivalry we need to start winning USMCFinPhreak is equal opportunity with his hate. The Dolphins jumped at the opportunity to sign Willis, provide him stability, and give him a chance to prove he is a capable starter in the league. Now named the Dolphins’ starter, Willis has battled to earn this opportunity. The Palm Beach Post’s Joe Schad took a look at the perseverance and belief that it took for Willis to get to this point in a one-on-one interview: Joe Schad: I think people appreciate perseverance. Some people feel like they were handed things and you have not been handed things. You have had to earn this. What qualities do you admire most in other people? Malik Willis: Probably that perseverance that you talk about. I think that’s an important quality as far as life goes because you just never know what happens. All the ups and downs of life, if you can, you can always work towards something better. Regardless if it goes better or not, you can work towards something better. And that’s the opportunity. title: Packers/Vikings Coverage Map: Border Battle To Be Shown (Almost) Nationwide
summary: The 130th regular season installment of the Border Battle between the Green Bay Packers and the Minnesota Vikings will take place in the late window of the first week of this NFL season, and as a result nearly everyone from coast to coast and border to border will be able to see this one on […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - JANUARY 04: Minnesota Vikings running back Jordan Mason (27) runs with the ball while Green Bay Packers safety Kitan Oladapo (27) during the second half of the NFL game between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings on January 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 130th regular season installment of the Border Battle between the Green Bay Packers and the Minnesota Vikings will take place in the late window of the first week of this NFL season, and as a result nearly everyone from coast to coast and border to border will be able to see this one on good, old fashioned over-the-air television, free of charge. The good folks from 506 Sports have released their first coverage maps of the 2026 season, and we’ve got the map of the late window on CBS below. The Packers/Vikings game is shown in red. If you are in the blue area, your game on CBS will be the Arizona Cardinals visiting the Los Angeles Chargers. (Hallmark doesn’t make cards for that, sorry.) You’ll still be able to find the game on YouTube TV Sunday Ticket if you have it. CBS seems to be going all out for this one, as their crew for their NFL Today pre-game show will be setting up shop in the Twin Cities for this one, and the game itself will be called by their #1 team in the booth, which now features Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt, who has replaced Tony Romo while Romo deals with his. . .issues. The Vikings will be on CBS for this one, and then they won’t be on CBS again until they come back from their bye week when they host the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 7. All of their games in Weeks 2 through 5 are slated to be on the FOX family of networks. So, when you’re getting ready to watch the game on Sunday afternoon, be sure to remember that the game starts at 3:25 PM Central time, not at noon, and that the game is on CBS. We’ll have an Open Thread over in the Feed for folks to talk about the early games that are happening on Sunday as a bit of a warm-up for the main event.

The Packers are coming into this one a bit short-handed, but the Vikings come into it with yet another new starter at quarterback. U.S. Bank Stadium should be rocking for the first real football game it’s seen since January, but will it be enough to get the purple off to a 1-0 start to the season? Also, with the new season upon us, we want to know how confident you are in what this team is capable of in 2026. It’s the fifth season of the Kevin O’Connell era in Minnesota, and if you ask the Really Smart Football People™ around the league, it doesn’t seem as though the expectations for this squad are terribly high. There are a lot of column inches being devoted to a couple of other teams in this division, but not a lot being devoted to the Vikings. Is this team being overlooked? Are there big things in store for the Vikings, or should we be keeping the expectations low? As always, we invite you to participate in our survey for this week by voting in both of our polls, whether you do so here or over in the Feed, and by sounding off in the comments as well. Go ahead and have at it, everybody! We’ll have the results of both of these polls posted for you before kickoff on Sunday afternoon. What will happen in Week 1? Are you confident in the Vikings? title: Week 1 Preview: Fast Start Needed
summary: Training camp is over, the preseason is in the rearview mirror, Kyle Van Noy is signed, and future Hall of Fame inductee Harrison Smith is returning for a 15th season. After eight long months, the Minnesota Vikings will finally play a regular-season game. SETTING THE STAGE The Green Bay Packers arrive at U.S. Bank Stadium […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - JANUARY 4: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings runs a route against Shemar Bartholomew #34 of the Green Bay Packers in the second quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Training camp is over, the preseason is in the rearview mirror, Kyle Van Noy is signed , and future Hall of Fame inductee Harrison Smith is returning for a 15th season. After eight long months, the Minnesota Vikings will finally play a regular-season game. SETTING THE STAGE The Green Bay Packers arrive at U.S. Bank Stadium in a strange situation. They’ve been the 7th seed in the NFC playoffs for three straight seasons. They’re in that 8- to 11-win “good, perennial playoff contender, but there’s a definite ceiling to the whole thing” zone under Matt LaFleur in the post-prime Aaron Rodgers era. I previously likened it to the 1992-97 Denny Green Vikings, and that’s a fair comparison. As I also noted, there is no Randy Moss on the horizon for the Packers. But more immediate problems are facing the Cheeseheads. It was already known that the 3-time First-team All-Pro Micah Parsons was out for this one, but now they’ll ( likely ) be without their star running back, Josh Jacobs. VIKINGS ON OFFENSE There are a lot of unknowns here as Kyler Murray takes over as the fourth opening-week starting quarterback in Kevin O’Connell’s five seasons as head coach. It is what it is. Will Murray end up being the elusive long-term answer at quarterback? Well, the answer to that question begins. Murray and the Vikings offense will face a Packers defense with many question marks. Aside from the enormous Parsons issue, it’s a unit that saw turnover in the offseason. EDGE Rashan Gary, LB Quay Walker, and CB Nate Hobbs are all gone, with DT Javon Hargrave, LB Zaire Franklin, and CB Benjamin St-Juste coming in as the primary reinforcements. The Packers also have a new defensive coordinator, Jonathan Gannon, for whom Kevin O’Connell has had some trouble as the Vikings’ head coach. After an initial impressive showing in his debut as the Vikings’ coach in 2022 against… drumroll… the Green Bay Packers, the following week in Philadelphia, against Gannon as the Eagles’ defensive coordinator, was ugly. The Vikings were held to a putrid 264 total yards and just 7 points. Kirk Cousins threw 3 interceptions, while Justin Jefferson was limited to 6 catches for 48 yards. They faced off again at U.S. Bank Stadium in 2024, this time with Gannon as the Arizona Cardinals’ head coach. The Vikings secured a 23-22 victory, but they were quite fortunate. I’d argue they were lucky. We trailed 19-6 late in the third quarter and 22–16 with 3:20 remaining. We were outgained 406-273 in total yards. The Cardinals also committed 10 penalties. The key for Gannon in 2026 will be generating pressure in Parsons’ absence. Despite going down in Week 15 last season, he still accounted for 12.5 of the Packers’ 36 total sacks. Their sack rate plummeted from 6.8% to 2.3% in the final three games of the season. Gannon is a big Cover 4 and Cover 3 guy who has historically been a low-to-moderate blitzer. The preference has been to get home with four by incorporating stunts and simulated pressure looks. This may have to change this season out of necessity, especially early on. The good news? With Parsons injured, Gannon will not have nearly the talent at his disposal that the stacked 2022 Eagles unit had. And KOC will have that 2024 game on film to make advantageous adjustments this time around. The bad news? He didn’t do much to improve the Vikings’ offensive output the first time around. Even against an average Cardinals defense, it was a slog. While I think Kyler Murray will have a strong season, it will be his first start in KOC’s system after playing only one preseason series. Expecting him to hit the ground running on all cylinders may be too much. One can be hopeful, I guess. VIKINGS ON DEFENSE Brian Flores had the Vikings rolling on defense at the end of the 2025 season, highlighted by an absolutely dominant Week 17 performance against the high-flying Detroit Lions, with everything on the line. Training camp performances, along with late roster additions, do not indicate a letup. Dallas Turner appears ready to take the next step, while the Kyle Van Noy signing and Harrison Smith’s return calm the nerves a bit. Concerns remain along the defensive line, but overall, this unit looks poised to stay elite. That doesn’t mean LaFleur and company haven’t had some success against Flores. Jordan Love has been largely feast-or-famine in his five outings, with two strong performances averaging 323 yards, 3.5 passing TDs to 1.5 INTs, and three weak ones, with a high of 229 yards passing (two under 200) and a combined 2 TDs and an INT. It’s also a good-news/bad-news scenario for the Packers offense. The good news is they’ll benefit from the return of tight end Tucker Kraft, who was on the verge of an All-Pro season before an ACL injury. Yeah, a lot is riding on Kraft not missing a beat after major knee surgery. The bad news is that they have to be at the top of the list for vacated target share in the NFL this season. They’ve put a lot of faith (and money) in Christian Watson taking the next steps toward the elite WR1 category, and whether Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden can replace the reliable Romeo Doubs and the departing Dontayvion Wicks remains to be seen. I’d expect Flores to try to get home early, using simulated pressures and stunts to exploit a shaky, uncertain Packers offensive line that has many questions after allowing one of the highest pressure rates in the NFL last season. A surely raucous crowd at U.S. Bank Stadium will undoubtedly assist in this effort. This, in turn, will make it easier to take Watson and Kraft out of the equation. Jacobs’ absence should also create more opportunities to focus on coverage. PREDICTION As much as I’d love a repeat of the comfortable 2022 season-opening win over the hated Packers, I see this one more like the 2024 games. In both, the Vikings came out strong, with leads of 28-0 and 20-3 (and 27-10), respectively, only to escape with two 2-point wins. We were especially fortunate at Lambeau, where it seemed we’d have taken a loss if there’d been a few more minutes on the clock. Hopefully it won’t be that much of a nail-biter. With the Packers missing their best defensive player, Parsons (and arguably the best in the NFL), along with their most dangerous offensive weapon, Jacobs, they should struggle to keep pace if the Vikings’ offense can reach the mid-20s (which it should). The importance of getting this win and a fast start to the season is clear. You have to beat the Packers at home when they’re this short-handed. Simple as that, folks. The next two weeks on the road at Chicago and Tampa Bay are tricky, and the middle stretch of the season (@Detroit, Buffalo, @Green Bay, @SF in Mexico) looks brutal. Entering that stretch at 5-1 or 4-2 may be necessary if we want to challenge for a playoff spot, let alone the division. It won’t be easy, and some aspects of the offense will need time to gel, but I believe the Vikings will take an important first step on Sunday. I can see a key turnover and a short field helping the good guys win. Minnesota Vikings: 24 Green Bay Packers: 20

title: Harrison Smith Returns — And the Cap Gets Complicated
summary: Harrison Smith is back — and Tyler Forness is not doing the fanboy version. On a Labor Day Real Forno Show, Forness and producer Dave Stefano unpack the Hitman’s one-year Vikings return, the cap squeeze it creates, and a CFL-inspired pitch for a real NFL Rivalry Weekend before Week 1 vs. Green Bay. The contract […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Harrison Smith #22 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during warmups before the game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Harrison Smith is back — and Tyler Forness is not doing the fanboy version. On a Labor Day Real Forno Show , Forness and producer Dave Stefano unpack the Hitman’s one-year Vikings return, the cap squeeze it creates, and a CFL-inspired pitch for a real NFL Rivalry Weekend before Week 1 vs. Green Bay. The contract is the headline. Smith’s deal is structured as roughly $8 million base value with $4 million in per-game roster bonuses and $4 million in playoff incentives that max near $16 million only if Minnesota wins the Super Bowl. Play all 17 and he lands around $12.25 million. Forness supports the player getting paid — “Harrison Smith got his money, and on a human level, good for him” — then flips to the team view. Minnesota had about $8.8 million in cap space before the signing. After bonus, per-game money, and the leftover dead cap from the spring release, operating room looks closer to $2 million. “That’s not enough to operate a season,” Forness said. “You have to have more than that.” The football case is layered. Forness will not pretend Smith is replaceable by a draft pick. “Harrison Smith’s brain cannot be found on the street. It cannot be drafted.” Bringing him back lets Josh Metellus stay in his own role instead of becoming a full Harrison clone. The worry is the other half of the job. Flores’ packaging still needs legs after the snap — the A-gap look that bails to single-high. “If he can’t do that anymore, then you can just absolutely destroy it. Jared Goff, Matthew Stafford, they’ll kill it.” Stefano pushed the conductor argument: “The Vikings are not paying for Smith’s legs, they’re paying for his pre-snap chaos.” Forness’s answer: chaos is worthless if quarterbacks can just throw at the 37-year-old. He also walked the ugly cap chess — Blake Cashman, T.J. Hockenson, Will Fries, Andrew Van Ginkel — where pushing money out only works if you actually want those players long term. They also spent the open on a CFL Labor Day Classic idea: lock one mid-October weekend as Rivalry Weekend, same divisional pairings every year, trophies, merch, promotion that actually sells the fight. “Everything is pro wrestling. It is what you make it.” Then they read fan bold predictions: Kyler Murray leading the team in rushing, Justin Jefferson chasing 2,000 yards and the Triple Crown, Dallas Turner leading the league in strip sacks, Will Reichard drilling 70 in Mexico City, Super Bowl 61 matching the franchise’s 1961 founding year. Key points: Smith return: one year, ~$12.25M if he plays 17, max via Super Bowl incentives Cap: thin operating space after Jefferson, Darrisaw, and Murphy already restructured On-field: brain and communication vs. possible athletic drop Metellus stays Metellus if Smith is the communicator Rivalry Weekend pitch: fixed October week, not Thanksgiving Fan spice: Murray rushing title, Jefferson records, Turner strip sacks Next on the network: Packers preview, Who Will Be King , Two Old Bloggers Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Watch the full Labor Day episode on Vikings 1st & SKOL / Bleav. Forness is not here to tell you the Hitman is automatically a win. He’s here to ask what $12.25 million costs in August flexibility — and whether Week 4 still looks like Week 1. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . What do you think? Is Smith the glue that holds Flores together, or the cap bill that shows up in November?
author: David Stefano

title: Patriots vs. Seahawks: Who has the edge in Week 1?
summary: Seven months ago, the New England Patriots struggled mightily in their Super Bowl loss against the Seattle Seahawks. They did compete fairly well defensively, but on offense simply did not do enough to prevent a relatively lopsided 29-13 defeat. With the 2026 season about to be kicked off by those very same teams, we will […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Mack Hollins #13 of the New England Patriots catches a touchdown reception against Riq Woolen #27 of the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Seven months ago, the New England Patriots struggled mightily in their Super Bowl loss against the Seattle Seahawks. They did compete fairly well defensively, but on offense simply did not do enough to prevent a relatively lopsided 29-13 defeat. With the 2026 season about to be kicked off by those very same teams, we will get an instant look at each’s development since the Super Bowl and a first point of reference for 2026. For the moment and considering all the information available, however, here is how we think they stack up heading into their meeting on Wednesday night. Passing game Patriots pass offense vs. Seahawks pass defense: Based on the Super Bowl, there would not be a question about who had the edge in this particular matchup; Seattle effectively shut down New England’s passing game all day due to a mix of relentless pressure and tight coverage — a combination the Patriots found no remedy against. However, the last seven months saw the AFC champions made some significant moves at wide receiver and along the offensive line to prevent a similar outcome from happening in 2026. The Seahawks themselves also suffered some personnel losses in the backend; you can see why Drake Maye and company should be better equipped to go up against the unit this time around. It will be for naught if the offensive line can’t hold up, but we are optimistic and therefore giving this head-to-head to the visitors by a small margin. | Edge: Patriots Patriots pass defense vs. Seahawks pass offense: Had the Christian Gonzalez contract situation not been resolved, we might have gone in a different direction here. With the star cornerback signing a four-year, $135 million pact earlier this week, however, this question has been answered. Others do remain such as the source of New England’s pass rush particularly off the edge, but on the whole we like this matchup for the visitors: the interior defensive line and Zak Kuhr’s aggressive pressure packages could create problems against Seattle’s O-line, while Gonzalez and company have the coverage prowess to limit Sam Darnold, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the rest of Seattle’s aerial attack. | Edge: Patriots Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Running game Patriots rushing offense vs. Seahawks run defense: One of the Patriots’ offensive goals this season is running the ball more effectively, and they should be better based on the personnel available compared to 2025; the additions of Alijah Vera-Tucker and Reggie Gilliam alone should make a positive difference. That said, one big part of the core personnel, TreVeyon Henderson, will not be playing on Wednesday, putting pressure on Rhamondre Stevenson and RB3 Corey Kiner. Add the fact that the Seahawks have one of the best front sevens in all of football, and you can see why New England — no pun intended — might be running into some trouble on the ground against the Seahawks. | Edge: Seahawks Patriots run defense vs. Seahawks rushing offense: Kenneth Walker, who had 135 rushing yards in the Super Bowl and took home MVP honors, left Seattle for Kansas City in this year’s free agency. Zach Charbonnet, the projected RB1 with Walker gone, will open the year on the physically unable to perform list. As a consequence, first-round draft pick Jadarian Price will be the top dog in the Seahawks’ backfield facing New England — a tall task for a rookie. That being said, he will be going up against a Patriots defense that had its issues versus the run this summer. Edge-setting in particular looked problematic throughout training camp and with Harold Landry on PUP as well remains a massive concern going into Lumen Field. | Edge: Seahawks Special teams Both the Patriots’ and the Seahawks’ are among the stoutest special teams units in the NFL. And yet, we are giving Seattle the edge for one particular reason: their kick return game as a whole looks more dangerous with Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton both capable of breaking big plays as punt and kickoff returner, respectively. Marcus Jones is as well, of course, but New England is missing that proven top-tier player to return kickoffs. Other factors such as Brenden Schooler’s absence and Andy Borregales’ accuracy also push this head-to-head toward the home team, at least on paper. | Edge: Seahawks Coaching The last time these two teams met, the Seahawks out-classed the Patriots every step of the way — including from a coaching perspective. The main actors in this battle, head coaches Mike Vrabel and Mike Macdonald, are still calling the shots for their respective teams. However, Wednesday’s game will be the first for new Seattle offensive coordinator Brian Fleury and his new-look staff. Any growing pains could help tip the scales in New England’s favor, which is why we are giving the slightest of advantages to Vrabel and a crew that is largely unchanged from a year ago. | Edge: Patriots Verdict The Patriots lost Super Bowl LX by 16 points and were unable to get out of their way particularly on offense for much of the day. That being said, their eventual deficit was inflated by untimely turnovers: early in the fourth quarter, the team was still down only 12 points and finally started to build some momentum. Obviously, that was undone by back-to-back series ending in interceptions, but the gap up until that point was not unbridgeable either. The question now becomes whether or not New England’s offseason investments and natural progression in Year 2 under Mike Vrabel will be enough to bridge the gap against an opponent who appears to have a few more uncertainties within its ranks nowadays. At the very least, the game should be more competitive for four quarters.
