title: 5 questions and answers about Patriots vs. Seahawks in NFL Week 1
summary: On paper, the Seattle Seahawks are a familiar opponent for the New England Patriots. They are, after all, the most recent team they game-planned against. Of course, that process is seven months away and the two teams — especially the Patriots — have changed a lot since the Super Bowl. So, order to find out […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 8: Head coach Mike Macdonald of the Seattle Seahawks looks on during the second half NFL Super Bowl LX football game against the New England Patriots at Levi Stadium on February 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images On paper, the Seattle Seahawks are a familiar opponent for the New England Patriots. They are, after all, the most recent team they game-planned against. Of course, that process is seven months away and the two teams — especially the Patriots — have changed a lot since the Super Bowl. So, order to find out more about the Patriots’ Week 1 opponent, we spoke with John Gilbert of Pats Pulpit’s sister site Field Gulls , the SB Nation community for all things Seahawks. Do you expect Mike Macdonald to copy and paste his Super Bowl game plan? Or could we see some tweaks on Wednesday? Macdonald is the type to always look for every little way to improve or do things better, so the overarching idea of what the Seahawks want to do will likely be the same, but there will undoubtedly be tweaks to the specific implementations. On defense, things are likely to be somewhat more vanilla than in the Super Bowl simply to prevent communications mishaps that could allow for a big play that alters the outcome. Over on the flip side, everyone is waiting to see how Brian Fleury calls a game, because there weren’t a lot of fans who were excited by the team putting just 32 points on the board over the course of the entire preseason. Of course, most of the starters didn’t play at all, and there’s not a lot to take from preseason results, even more so when it is second and third stringers on the field, so even Seattle fans are anxious to see what the Hawks will do differently on offense in Week 1 as opposed to what they did in the Super Bowl. Do you expect any significant offensive changes under new OC Brian Fleury? I expect the offense to be similar, but of course anytime there is a change at offensive coordinator there will be slight differences. Fleury will have full time play calling duties for the first time in his coaching career, so it wouldn’t be a surprise for there to be bumps along the way as he gains experience. The biggest difference for the offense might be in the ground game, as Klint Kubiak tweaked his historically wide-zone heavy tendencies when Kenneth Walker was on the field and called more gap runs for Walker than any other running back in his three seasons as an offensive coordinator between Minnesota, New Orleans and Seattle. With that in mind, Kubiak guided the Seahawks to an average of 28.4 points per game, and while the group certainly benefited from the performance of the defense, the offense performed at a high level and executed what was asked of them. It will be a tall task for Fleury to come in and immediately exceed or even match the results Kubiak was able to deliver in 2025, so a step back, even if small, would not come as a surprise. Do you see significant drop-off from last season at CB, RB, SAF, and ED3 with the losses of Riq Woolen, Kenneth Walker III, Coby Bryant, and Boye Mafe? The area where there is likely the potential for the biggest drop off after the free agent losses of the offseason is in the secondary, where the combination of the loss of Woolen and Bryant could lead to breakdowns that hurt. Specifically, players in their second season in Macdonald’s system have performed at a much higher level than in their first season in the system and replacing thirty percent of the snaps played in the secondary last season won’t be easy. Thus, it won’t be a surprise if there are some early-season communications breakdowns as the 2026 group learns to play together as a group. . On the other side of the ball, Walker’s departure to the Kansas City Chiefs brings the discussion How do you expect the CB rotation to look on game day? Especially if Nick Emmanwori isn’t healthy enough to man the slot in nickel? The Seahawks base is five defensive backs, with the situation dictating whether they have three cornerbacks or three safeties on the field, but this is something even Seattle fans will be watching closely. In addition to the departures of Woolen and Bryant in free agency, injuries hit the secondary hard during the preseason. Ty Okada started eleven games in 2025, stepping into the lineup at times for all three of Emmanwori, Bryant and Julian Love, but Okada has been ruled out due to a hamstring injury , which could make things interesting. On top of that, second round pick Bud Clark is on injured reserve and out for the year, while rookie third round cornerback Julian Neal missed much of training camp due to injury and likely hasn’t practiced enough to be a significant part of the rotation just yet. With all that in mind, it won’t be a surprise if the team dips into the secondary depth on the practice squad ahead of the opener Wednesday. Veteran D’Anthony Bell is primarily known for his special teams play, but he started a pair of games for the Seahawks in 2025, and 2021 All-Pro Trevon Diggs is looking to re-establish himself after several injury-plagued seasons the past few years. Has Sam Darnold taken another step in Seattle’s offense? Would you be comfortable if things came down to a shootout? Darnold has continued to improve in each recent season, but there will likely always be those who will doubters as long as he drops a stinker of a game like he did against the Los Angeles Rams in the 2024 postseason or the first matchup against the Rams in 2025. Fleury will mark the seventh different offensive coordinator Darnold has played under in the past seven seasons, and it bears watching whether Fleury can find as much success with Darnold under center as Klint Kubiak and Kevin O’Connell have the past couple of years.

title: Running back rooms in the spotlight ahead of Patriots vs. Seahawks season opener
summary: The New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks have seen changes to their offensive backfields in the offseason. The more drastic shift overall was Seattle’s, but the Patriots also have a situation with their second-year back that shouldn’t be ignored. Let’s dive in. The Seahawks’ big loss The Seahawks are entering the year coming off […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Rhamondre Stevenson #38 of the New England Patriots is tackled by Jarran Reed #90 of the Seattle Seahawks and Leonard Williams #99 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks have seen changes to their offensive backfields in the offseason. The more drastic shift overall was Seattle’s, but the Patriots also have a situation with their second-year back that shouldn’t be ignored. Let’s dive in. The Seahawks’ big loss The Seahawks are entering the year coming off a dominating Super Bowl win against the Patriots, in which Kenneth Walker III, the fourth-year rusher who started every game in 2025, was awarded Super Bowl MVP. Walker carried the ball 27 times, and picked up 135 yards on the ground. He also hauled in two receptions for 26 yards in the championship game. Last season, Walker rushed for 1,027 yards, which was the first time he had for over 1,000 yards since his rookie year back in 2022. After his eye-popping performance in the 29-13 win over the Patriots, the star back hit free agency. Walker ended up landing with the Kansas City Chiefs on a three-year deal, worth up to $45 million. The outlook on 2026 So, where does this leave the Seahawks now? They answered that question 45 days later on Day 1 of the NFL Draft, when they used the last pick of the first round to acquire Jadarian Price. Price was a four-star recruit out of high school, and became a member of the Fighting Irish in 2022. But after suffering a season-ending ruptured achilles tendon in the offseason of what would have been his true freshman year, he began his college football career in 2023. Throughout his college tenure, he racked up 1,692 yards, and found the end zone 21 times on the ground. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel praised Jadarian Price when asked about him. “Jadarian’s got great speed,” Vrabel said. “He’s a slasher. He’ll test edges. He’s got great patience. But, I watched him circle guys up in college fairly easily. So, the speed, I think, is real.” Price will now be the feature running back for the reigning champs in his rookie campaign, although this likely wouldn’t have been the case if it weren’t for an injury to Zach Charbonnet. Charbonnet tore his ACL in the 41-6 rout of the San Francisco 49ers in last year’s divisional round of the playoffs. The 25-year-old is coming off of a career high in carries and rushing yards, and he was also tied for sixth in all of the NFL with 12 touchdowns. All of which came in a secondary role behind Walker. So while Charbonnet looked as if this would have been his first year as the primary back, it will have to wait as the Seahawks look at what they have with Price. Entering Wednesday, it will be George Holani and Emanuel Wilson behind the first-round pick. The Patriots’ backfield this season As for the Patriots, the halfback room will look mostly the same. Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to take possession of the RB1 role, with Treveyon Henderson behind him. Stevenson, entering his sixth season with the Patriots, had his lead role pressured the most last season since Ezekiel Elliott back in 2023: Henderson ended up recording 911 rushing yards to Stevenson’s 603, and scoring nine touchdowns to seven for Stevenson. However, Stevenson provided a little bit more of steady option in backfield compared to Henderson, who’s numbers were inflated by long, explosive runs. Vrabel expressed that the running back room has a variety of skills sets, explaining that, “some guys have a little bit of different strengths than maybe the other guys. So, there’s a little bit of everything.” However, Henderson has now been ruled out for Week 1 with an ankle injury . The 2025 second-round draft pick has been dealing with this injury since aggravating it during practice on August 24. A trade that could become increasingly important With Henderson unavailable, Corey Kiner, the Patriots’ trade acquisition from the Arizona Cardinals, projects to play an elevated role. Kiner, like Henderson, is heading into his sophomore season in the NFL. An undrafted free agent signing by the 49ers, he suffered a high ankle sprain in his rookie preseason that led to his release. He then was signed to the Minnesota Vikings practice squad, and never touched the field while he was there. Lastly, Kiner was picked up by the Cardinals off the Vikings’ practice squad, which is where he appeared in his first professional game. While he only carried the ball 12 times for 58 yards last year, Vrabel and the Patriots saw something in him. “He was a player that we had looked at trying to get last year coming out,” conveyed Vrabel. “He’s a good young runner.” The hype around the Patriots versus Seahawks rematch is real, which was defined by the running game in the Super Bowl. The Patriots will look to match the production the Seahawks got out of that position last year, and kickoff the new season with a huge win in Seattle — but doing so without the big-play threat that is Henderson could prove to be a challenge.

title: Revenge not on Patriots’ minds for Super Bowl rematch with Seahawks
summary: When the New England Patriots come out of the tunnel at Seattle’s Lumen Field on Wednesday night, 214 days will have passed since their loss in the Super Bowl. In those 214 days, the Patriots turned the page in emphatic fashion, making major investments in hopes of turning themselves into a true championship-caliber team. However, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots is pressured by Boye Mafe #53 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the New England Patriots come out of the tunnel at Seattle’s Lumen Field on Wednesday night, 214 days will have passed since their loss in the Super Bowl. In those 214 days, the Patriots turned the page in emphatic fashion, making major investments in hopes of turning themselves into a true championship-caliber team. However, with the reigning champs right back on their schedule to open the 2026 season, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will be confronted with its recent past again. The stage therefore seems set for a revenge game against the Seahawks. Just don’t tell the Patriots. “You like to think it’s a new year,” said quarterback Drake Maye. “You like to think that, but at the same time, you could go against an opponent that you just lost a Super Bowl against. In the last game that I played and was out there, we lost to them in the biggest game. That’s what you play the game for. So there’s definitely, I would not say extra, just a little bit of, ‘Man, this is our chance to start the season off strong on a good foot and knowing the opponent that we have.’ “You get to say, you get a little bit of a revenge game, but I would not say revenge game. They won the big one, and we got to start the season off. You cannot get that game back that we lost, so we are onto something new.” After winning all three of their playoff games in the AFC in January, Maye and company qualified for Super Bowl LX. While they did manage to keep the contest against the the NFC’s top seed relatively close early on, the floodgates eventually opened late. Seattle ended up winning 29-13, with the Patriots’ offensive output in particular disappointing. The lack of consistency on that side of the ball also helped undo what was a mostly solid defensive effort led by newly-extended cornerback Christian Gonzalez . So, is the Patriots defense feeling any extra motivation heading into Week 1? “I wouldn’t say so,” said linebacker Christian Elliss. “They’re a good team. They’re coached well. For us, it’s just about playing to our identity, going out there, and having fun.”

title: Christian Gonzalez turns attention to Seahawks after Patriots contract extension
summary: A day before the New England Patriots kick off their season, they agreed to terms with star cornerback Christian Gonzalez on a record-breaking four-year, $135 million contract extension. Now, Gonzalez’s full attention turns to slowing down Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the opener. “[Jaxon’s] a great great receiver. Respect him completely,” Gonzalez said. “He can do it […]
full_text: Feb 8, 2026; Santa Clara, CA, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (0) breaks up a pass against Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (11) during Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A day before the New England Patriots kick off their season, they agreed to terms with star cornerback Christian Gonzalez on a record-breaking four-year, $135 million contract extension . Now, Gonzalez’s full attention turns to slowing down Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the opener. “[Jaxon’s] a great great receiver. Respect him completely,” Gonzalez said. “He can do it all. I mean, everybody saw the year he had last year.” Smith-Njigba led the league last season with 1,793 receiving yards last season, setting additional career-highs in receptions (119) and touchdowns (10). The performance led to him being named the NFL’s Offensive Player of the Year in addition to a first-team All-Pro. “Just the suddenness, route craft. He is smooth, he can play at different speeds, he plays inside, he runs a full route tree, he is strong at the catch point,” head coach Mike Vrabel said about the receiver. “But I just think that the savviness and the ability to get in and out of breaks is really impressive.” For all the success Smith-Njigba had last season, one of his quietest performances came in Super Bowl LX against Gonzalez and the Patriots. The Seahawks’ top offensive weapon was held to just four catches for 27 yards, with Gonzalez in coverage for just one reception to go along with a pass breakup in the end zone. But even with the relatively quiet performance, Gonzalez came away impressed by what makes the receiver so difficult to defend. “It kind of stood out just how smooth he is of an athlete. I mean, he’s doesn’t really look like he’s running, but he’s moving pretty fast. So, he’s just really smooth and makes everything look the same,” Gonzalez said. “That’s a skill set that a lot of receivers do to confuse the corners — is make everything look the same. And he does a very good job at that.” Both growing up in Texas, Gonzalez and Smith-Njigba are long familiar with each other and their games. The duo were each part of the 2023 NFL Draft and now have both inked $100-plus million extensions this offseason. A rematch Wednesday night to open the 2026 NFL season will now be the next part of their story. “Just being from the same area, it’s real cool to watch each other come up and then be able to play on the biggest stage and then just support each other and see each other do what we do. So, it’s fun,” Gonzalez said.

title: Instant grades for Christian Gonzalez contract extension with Patriots
summary: On Labor Day, the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez birthed a contract extension to make him the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL. According to reports, the months-long process culminated on Monday in an agreement that will pay the 24-year-old $135 million over four years. We don’t know the full structure of the deal yet, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - DECEMBER 1: Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots warms up prior to the game against the New York Giants at Gillette Stadium on December 1, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Labor Day, the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez birthed a contract extension to make him the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL. According to reports, the months-long process culminated on Monday in an agreement that will pay the 24-year-old $135 million over four years . We don’t know the full structure of the deal yet, but the fact that it got signed in the first place is telling. So, let’s put a grade it. Instant grades: Patriots sign CB Christian Gonzalez to 4-year, $135M extension Bernd Buchmasser: The signs always pointed toward Gonzalez and the Patriots ultimately reaching an agreement, but the timeline and eventual scope of the deal was where the uncertainty lied. It took a while for those questions to get resolved, but doing so before the start of the season is the best-case scenario even though it meant a massive investment on the team’s part. | Grade: A+ Andrew Guindon: This is a regime that’s emphasized retaining and rewarding its top talent, and that’s what the Patriots ultimately did with Gonzalez. Having a true premier shutdown cornerback on your roster, such as Gonzalez is a luxury in the NFL. Those are the types of players you pay while Drake Maye is still under his rookie contract. He showcased how impactful he can be in the biggest moments during last season’s Super Bowl, and now he’s under contract through 2031. | Grade: A+ Pat Lane: I don’t care how long it took, they locked up their CB1 and sent a message that they are going to reward guys for their play and commitment to the team. I don’t love the fact that Robert Kraft spoke about it to the media, because he opened the door on that, but the fact that they signed him, and had it just above Devon Witherspoon is fantastic. | Grade: A+ Matt St. Jean: There were some questions about how Christian Gonzalez might fit with Mike Vrabel’s scheme, but those were erased down to stretch as he embraced physicality and then showcased his premier coverage skills in the Super Bowl. Gonzalez is the kind of player who can take any opposing receiver out of the game and erase any chance for big plays in his area of the field. That’s highly valuable, and worth the price the Patriots paid. | Grade: A+ Dylan Klayman: Gonzalez as a top corner in the league deserved to be paid like it, especially after his standout performance throughout the playoffs. Locking him up before the season starts is huge, so it doesn’t create another distraction, and your CB1 can just go out there and play. Obviously, it would have been nice if there wasn’t a whole story in the media from Kraft about the contract, and Gonzalez’s camp getting mad about it. But at least it is in the rear view mirror now, and you have one of your best players signed for the foreseeable future. | Grade: A+ What do you think about the Gonzalez extension? Do you like it? title: A look back at the history between the Saints and Lions
summary: The New Orleans Saints will open the 2026 season on the road Sunday afternoon against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. The Saints and Lions first met on Nov. 24, 1968, at Tiger Stadium in Detroit, with the game ending in a 20-20 tie. Since then, the teams have met just 28 times, with New […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 03: Alvin Kamara #41 of the New Orleans Saints runs with the ball in the fourth quarter against the Detroit Lions at the Caesars Superdome on December 03, 2023 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints will open the 2026 season on the road Sunday afternoon against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. The Saints and Lions first met on Nov. 24, 1968, at Tiger Stadium in Detroit, with the game ending in a 20-20 tie. Since then, the teams have met just 28 times, with New Orleans holding a 14-13-1 advantage in the all-time series. The last time these teams faced one another, Detroit came away with a 33-28 victory in New Orleans in 2023, giving the Lions the edge in the most recent chapter of the series. The Saints enter the 2026 season looking to improve on their 6-11 record from a year ago. Following another losing season, New Orleans made several changes during the offseason in an effort to turn things around and return to playoff contention. With a new season comes renewed optimism, but that optimism will ultimately have to translate into wins. The Saints believe they have added enough talent to compete in the NFC South, and Sunday’s opener against Detroit provides their first opportunity to show they are ready to take the next step. The Lions enter the season with a similar goal after a disappointing 2025 campaign. Detroit finished 9-8 and missed the playoffs, a significant step backward after going 15-2 and earning the NFC’s No. 1 seed in 2024. Despite that disappointing finish, Detroit remained one of the NFL’s most productive offensive teams, averaging 28.3 points per game, which ranked fourth in the league. The Lions will look to carry that offensive firepower into 2026 while putting last season’s struggles behind them. For both teams, Sunday’s matchup represents a fresh start and an early opportunity to set the tone for the season. Kickoff is at 12:00 pm and the game will be broadcast on FOX with Kenny Albert (play-by-play), Jonathan Vilma (color analyst) and Megan Olivi (sideline)

summary: The New Orleans Saints have officially released their team captains ahead of the 2026 NFL season. The Saints named 9 players as captains. Your 2026 Captains ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/IX3jGZvbCf — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) September 8, 2026 New Orleans named quarterback Tyler Shough, center Erik McCoy, Guard David Edwards, EDGE Cameron Jordan, EDGE Chase Young, linebacker Chris Rumph II, linebacker Kaden Ellis, safety Justin Reid, and long snapper Zach Wood as this season’s captains. There are quite a few interesting takeaways from the Black and Gold’s captain list for 2026, but the most notable is Shough earning the captain badge in his first season as the starter. The second-year passer has been a major voice for the team since their 2025 campaign ended, and even took over pre-game speeches. The Saints labeled five defensive players as captains. Jordan is a no-brainer, and Young has certainly earned his spot, but Rumph is the standout. He’s had a strong camp, and the chatter around the team has been that players and coaching staff love him, and that was certainly proven after he earned the captain honor. Notably left off the list for New Orleans is running back Alvin Kamara. The veteran back served as a team captain in 2022, 2024, and 2025. While he may no longer be RB1, he still remains a leader on the team, and his commitment to getting his extension during the offseason was an interesting development. The Saints have four recurring team captains, with McCoy, Reid, Jordan, and Wood all reclaiming their roles as captain. Of New Orleans six captains from 2025, only those players remain on the roster. Two captains from last season, Brandin Cooks and Blake Grupe, were released midseason.

title: Are the Saints for real if they beat the Lions on the road to open the season?
summary: The New Orleans Saints couldn’t ask for a much better opportunity to make an early statement as they open the season on the road against the Detroit Lions, and a win would immediately give fans a reason to believe this team could be different in 2026. But would it be enough to say the Saints […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 03: Jameson Williams #9 of the Detroit Lions dives to score a touchdown in the fourth quarter against the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome on December 03, 2023 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints couldn’t ask for a much better opportunity to make an early statement as they open the season on the road against the Detroit Lions, and a win would immediately give fans a reason to believe this team could be different in 2026. But would it be enough to say the Saints are for real? That might still be an overreaction. The Saints are 4-1 in their last five season openers, with last year’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals being the only exception. Starting fast clearly hasn’t been a problem for New Orleans, but maintaining that success throughout an entire season has been a different story. Detroit also won’t be at full strength. The Lions will be without key players including Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph, Isiah Pacheco and Cade Mays. That gives New Orleans some opportunities to take advantage of, particularly against a Detroit secondary missing two important pieces. At the same time, the Lions still have plenty of firepower. Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta give Detroit several ways to create problems for the Saints, while Aidan Hutchinson remains one of the league’s most dangerous defenders. That’s what would make a Saints victory so intriguing. If New Orleans can go into Detroit start the season strong with a win, it would be hard to not be optimistic. It would show that the Saints are capable of competing with a team that has legitimate expectations entering the season. So, would the Saints be for real if they win in Detroit? Maybe not yet. But it would certainly be time to start believing they could be.

title: State of the NFC South: Week 1 preview
summary: We are finally here. The 2026 NFL season begins this year, and with that, it’s time to look at a regular season preview for each team in the NFC South. Tampa Bay Buccaneers To open up the season, the Buccaneers have a tough battle ahead of them. In week 1, the Bucs will face off […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 26: A detailed view of a New Orleans Saints helmet on the field after a practice at Yulman Stadium on August 26, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are finally here. The 2026 NFL season begins this year, and with that, it’s time to look at a regular season preview for each team in the NFC South. Tampa Bay Buccaneers To open up the season, the Buccaneers have a tough battle ahead of them. In week 1, the Bucs will face off against the Cincinnati Bengals, and that is usually the worst time to face off against Joe Burrow and the roster. The Bengals have been extremely unlucky with injuries in recent years, and they usually happen after week 1. So, Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and the other dynamic players should be ready right away, but it is important to note that Chase and Higgins are questionable for the game, so that may change. Where the Bucs are likely going to win this game is on offense. Baker Mayfield had a really great start to last year, and it fell apart the more the season went on. This game is a chance for him to start well again, and although the Bengals made some massive additions (such as Dexter Lawrence), the defense is still very unproven and could be exposed. Carolina Panthers Speaking of difficult opening games of the season, the Panthers are playing the Chicago Bears. For the division champions, this is going to be a massive test to start the season. We can see right away if the moves the team made this preseason will improve the team, and if QB Bryce Young can take yet another step forward. Don’t forget, these two teams were the ones involved in the trade that got Carolina Young and Chicago Caleb Williams. The main focus will be on both QBs in this game, and if last season told us anything, Williams is ahead of Young, which is not great for Carolina. Young is also trying to prove to the team that they should sign him to a contract extension. Atlanta Falcons In one of the more shocking moments this offseason, Tua Tagovailoa will be the starter. The reason for this was that Michael Penix is not ready to play yet due to his season-ending injury from last season. If both players were healthy, the job would likely go to Penix, but Tagovailoa will have a big opportunity in front of him on Sunday. The only issue is the Falcons are going up against T.J. Watt and the Pittsburgh Steelers. That type of pressure off the edge is a scary sight for any QB, especially Tagovailoa. But the Steelers are probably the easiest opponent a team in the NFC South faces this week. Pittsburgh is not the complete team they have been, and with Mike Tomlin no longer at HC and Aaron Rodgers nowhere near what he used to be, things could get ugly for them. New Orleans Saints And now we have the Saints, and they will be going up against one of the scariest offenses in the league. Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and Sam LaPorta will be a massive test for the Saints, and that’s worrying with how much of a priority the offense was this past offseason. Still, with a coach like Brandon Staley leading the defense, there’s a chance that the Saints can do enough to get the win. On offense, this is going to be a great oppurtunity for Tyler Shough and Kellen Moore to start off on the right foot. The Lions’ defense is dealing with major injuries, and although that defensive line is still extremely worrying, the Saints can still have a great offensive game.

title: If the Saints win/lose vs. Lions
summary: The regular season is finally upon us, and the New Orleans Saints are set to open their 2026 campaign on the road against the Detroit Lions. Here’s a preview of what either result could mean for the black and gold on Sunday. If the Saints win: Should the Saints go into Detroit on Sunday afternoon […]
full_text: The regular season is finally upon us, and the New Orleans Saints are set to open their 2026 campaign on the road against the Detroit Lions. Here’s a preview of what either result could mean for the black and gold on Sunday. If the Saints win: Should the Saints go into Detroit on Sunday afternoon and win the game, it would likely be in contention as one of the biggest surprises of the week across the NFL. It would amplify the hype that’s been building all offseason since the Saints finished last year on such a strong note, and make for a real statement of intent for the campaign ahead. With a trip to Baltimore on the horizon next week, a victory would do wonders for New Orleans with such a tough pair of games to open the season. Such an outcome would require the team to make big plays on both sides of the ball, forcing turnovers while limiting their own. It’s the sort of win that instantly raises the expectations of outside observers and would set the tone in emphatic fashion. If the Saints lose: A loss in Detroit shouldn’t cause any panic or despondency. Of course, the manner in which the defeat arrives can have a huge bearing on the conclusions one might draw; the Saints shouldn’t get blown out here. But a defeat on the road against a team with aspirations of a deep playoff run is indeed the likelier outcome. Regardless, Kellen Moore will want to see signs that his team is trending in the right direction, and that can be the case even in defeat. Can the Saints pull off the upset to start the season 1-0? How high are your expectations for the year? Let us know in the comments!

title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 1 preview – Start/sit and more
summary: Welcome to the 2026 NFL season! It’s my third season writing fantasy content for Big Blue View and I can’t wait to get after it. I’m also excited to fire up my own fantasy lineups for the first time in many months. I might even take my own advice this season. As in prior years, […]
full_text: Drake Maye | Getty Images Welcome to the 2026 NFL season! It’s my third season writing fantasy content for Big Blue View and I can’t wait to get after it. I’m also excited to fire up my own fantasy lineups for the first time in many months. I might even take my own advice this season. As in prior years, the schedule is this column on Thursdays, and a waiver wire column on Mondays. I’ll also have a Giants’ best bets column up a day or two ahead of each Big Blue game. Check back often. Week 1 is tricky for fantasy. On the plus side, most managers have their entire roster at their disposal. You’re going to sit points this week. Don’t sweat it — just accept it. On the flip side, Week 1 is hard to handicap because we don’t have a perfect picture of player usage, or how certain offenses are going to look due to personnel and coaching changes. More than half of the NFL’s 32 teams have a new offensive play caller in 2026. Complicating matters further is that we don’t know how good or bad certain defenses and defensive position groups are, so we have to rely a lot on last season. A reminder: Week 1 overreactions in fantasy, which can lead to catastrophic waiver drops and trades, are the stuff of legend. In Week 1 last year, Ja’Marr Chase had two catches for 26 yards, and Jahmyr Gibbs had nine carries for 19 yards (he did have ten catches, but those gained just 31 yards). Neither player scored. Meanwhile, Quentin Johnston and Keon Coleman were the WR2/4 for the week, with both topping 20 points. After a terrific September, Johnston was the WR47 from Week 5 on, while Coleman finished outside the Top-60 WRs. See where I’m going? It’s a long season. Stats of the Week : Across the last three seasons, the Bengals scored 30 points, TOTAL, in Week 1. After losing his first two career starts against the Giants in 2016, Dak Prescott won his next 14, before losing his most recent one in Week 18 last season – but Dallas pulled its starters, including Dak, early in that contest. Dallas opens its season at New York on Sunday night. Tua Tagovailoa is slated to start for the Falcons on Sunday, and that makes six straight seasons with a different opening day QB for the Dirty Birds. OK, Week 1, here we go! Bye Weeks: NONE Week 1 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start Puka Nacua . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade ,and Sleeper of the Week . The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. ***NOTE: Because there’s a Wednesday game in Week 1, this column is posting early. Be sure to check the latest player news before setting your lineups. *** Ride of the Week: Chris Olave (@DET). This game should have fireworks, with two fast-paced offenses squared off against two suspect defenses. The 49.5 game total is the second highest on the board. Detroit is banged up in the secondary and especially at the safety spot, and it’s not like they were already good against the pass – they allowed the fifth most fantasy points per game (FPPG) to opposing wide receivers last season. With first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson out, the Saints have limited options at receiver, and Olave should see a massive target share. A Top-5 wide receiver finish from him in Week 1 is on the table. Fade of the Week: Drake Maye (@SEA). Look, I’m a big Drake Maye fan, and if you drafted Maye (the QB2 last season), you spent real draft capital and you aren’t considering sitting him. I get that. He struggled mightily against the league’s top defenses in his final three games last season, and that includes the Super Bowl, where he was stymied by Seattle until very late in the contest. Now he’s got to face them again, on the night their banner goes up, in one of the NFL’s loudest and most hostile stadiums. Maybe he was more banged up than we knew, maybe Will Campbell was so injured he shouldn’t have played, and A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs are massive upgrades. Seattle’s secondary is also not at 100% at the moment. I get all that. I also know what Mike McDonald’s defense can do to good offenses. I see this being a pretty low-scoring game (the total is 44.5). I think Maye’s numbers will be OK, but pedestrian for a player of his caliber. Sleeper of the Week: Mike Washington, Jr. (vs. MIA). Sleepers are a little silly in Week 1, since few fantasy managers need to start players ranked outside the overall Top-100. My pick is Washington, making his NFL debut after a stellar preseason. I have no idea if Ashton Jeanty is going to play Sunday, but even if he does, I think Washington will get plenty of work against what might be the NFL’s worst defense. It’s certainly the most inexperienced. Miami allowed the seventh most FPPG to opposing backs last season, and there’s no reason to think they’ll improve on that. If the Raiders are comfortably ahead, expect to see Washington, and not the recovering Jeanty, eating the clock in the second half. If you need a reach in Week 1, he’s a good option. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow, Justin Herbert, and Dak Prescott; the analysis starts below them. Rides: QB is loaded this season, and there are lots of good choices in Week 1. Quarterbacks ranked inside the Top-15 for the week who I think could beat their weekly rankings are Jaxson Dart (vs. DAL), Jared Goff (vs. NO), and Baker Mayfield (@CIN) . All have favorable matchups for fantasy, in games with shootout potential. Sleepers: If you need a second QB in a Superflex, there are nice options, including Tyler Shough (@DET), who finished last season on a tear, and Malik Willis (@LV). Willis is risky but the rushing upside is tantalizing. In a pinch? I think you can also go with Bryce Young (vs. CHI), and believe it or not, Geno Smith ( @TEN) and Kirk Cousins (vs. MIA), who have tasty matchups against defenses that were Bottom-8 in FPPG allowed to opposing quarterbacks last season. The 1972 undefeated Dolphins had the legendary “no-name defense”, which didn’t allow a point in Super Bowl VII. The 2026 fish actually ha v e a no-name defense. Fades: Brock Purdy (@LAR, Australia). I don’t like this matchup, halfway around the world, and with the 49ers’ offense (and Head Coach) coming off one of the most bizarre and injury-plagued summers you’ll ever see. Oh, and they’re facing the first defense in league history featuring two guys with 100 career sacks and a 20-sack season on the resume. I’ll also fade Patrick Mahomes (vs. DEN) in his first game back off a torn ACL, against a stingy defense that allowed just 18 TD passes last season. Others : Lower-ranked quarterbacks that you might be considering, but who I’d try to avoid in Superflex this week include Jordan Love (@MIN, fewest FPPG allowed to opposing quarterbacks last season), Daniel Jones (vs. BAL), and Jacoby Brissett (@LAC). Running back: Elite options this week – Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson, Jonathan Taylor, and Christian McCaffrey ; the analysis starts below them. Rides: Give me Javonte Williams (@NYG), coming off by far his best season, against a Giants’ defense that ranked 31 st against the run last season and traded away Dexter Lawrence. I also like Travis Etienne, Jr. (@DET) and D’ Andre Swift (@CAR), as both could be…

title: NY Giants’ depth chart: Deonte Banks wins starting CB job, and other surprises
summary: The New York Giants released their unofficial depth chart ahead of their Week 1 showdown against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. While some things are to be expected — like Jaxson Dart being QB1 while Brian Burns and Abdul Carter are listed as the starting outside linebackers — there are also a few […]
full_text: New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants released their unofficial depth chart ahead of their Week 1 showdown against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football . While some things are to be expected — like Jaxson Dart being QB1 while Brian Burns and Abdul Carter are listed as the starting outside linebackers — there are also a few things we need to note. Deonte Banks takes advantage of his clean slate Most observers left Banks’ career — or at least his career with the Giants — for dead after the 2025 season. He had been completely unseated by Cor’Dale Flott and it was widely assumed that Banks would just be a kick-off returner while Greg Newsome II and Paulson Adebo started at corner. Instead, Banks has knocked off Adebo and will be starting next to Newsome. He has clawed his way up the depth chart with a renewed attitude and determination. He consistently played well when he got the opportunity and was sticky in coverage in preseason games. There was doubt among some in the media whether the Giants would commit to playing Banks against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1, but John Harbaugh’s staff seems to be confident in Banks after his work this summer. Chauncey Golston jumps Darius Alexander We’ll likely see an active rotation on the defensive line, but Golston is listed as the starting defensive end in base defense. We’ll likely see quite a bit of 2-4-5 nickel looks with just two down linemen, and it’s interesting that Darius Alexander is listed as the primary backup to both Golston and Shelby Harris. That suggests that we’ll be seeing plenty of him as the Giants shift alignments and subpackages. The Giants also list Kayvon Thibodeaux as the backup to both Brian Burns and Abdul Carter. The Giants will get all three of their edges on the field plenty, both to keep them all fresh and to overwhelm opponents with waves of rushers. Dealer’s choice at running back It isn’t a surprise that Cam Skattebo is the Giants’ starting running back. However, it’s definitely interesting that Tyrone Tracy, Najee Harris, and Devin Singletary are all listed as the second string running back. That could be the Giants’ way of saying that while Skattebo will take the first snap, their running game will be varied. We could see them tailor their running back usage to their opponents and not favor any runner in particular. No slot receiver Calvin Austin III was set to be the Giants’ primary slot receiver when he was lost for the season with a torn ACL. We immediately began to ask who would replace him as the Giants’ primary slot receiver. The answer? Nobody, apparently. At least not on the unofficial depth chart. In reality, we’ll likely see a combination of TE Isaiah Likely , WR Malik Nabers , WR Odell Beckham Jr. , WR Darnell Mooney , and RB Tyrone Tracy will all line up or motion into the slot. We’ll also likely see far more 21 (two back), 12 (two tight end), and 13 (three tight end) personnel sets than we have in recent years. The Ravens frequently used non-receiver options as pass catchers, and we could see that with the Giants this year. It’s also somewhat jarring to see a modern NFL depth chart with just four wide receivers on it. We’ll likely see one of the Giants’ three return specialists elevated off the practice squad each week. title: NFL power rankings, Week 1: NY Giants haven’t convinced the voters, yet

full_text: The New York Giants are not quite looked at as a bottom-feeder in NFL Week 1 Power Rankings. They are not, though, given a whole of respect, either. In 12 Week 1 power rankings aggregated below, the Giants come out with a ranking 23.5. Consider that 23rd if you are a glass half-full person, 24th if you are a glass half-empty person. Either way, it shows that while the NFL at large is curious about John Harbaugh’s Giants, no one is yet convinced that great things will happen for New York in 2026. The Ringer | No. 24 We will find out nearly instantly whether head coach John Harbaugh has one more late-career surge in him—or whether he’s this year’s version of Pete Carroll in Las Vegas. The Giants play the Cowboys and Rams in prime time in back-to-back weeks, which will put his entirely new staff and young quarterback, Jaxson Dart, under national scrutiny from the jump. Harbaugh and Dart aren’t the only ones in the pressure cooker to start the year, either. Rookie linebacker Arvell Reese will be going up against quarterbacks Dak Prescott and Matthew Stafford, and rookie guard Francis Mauigoa will be matched up against defensive tackles Quinnen Williams and Aaron Donald. By the next edition of our power rankings, we will have an idea of whether these guys were ready for the brightest lights to start their careers. ESPN | No. 23 Chances to make the playoffs: 19.7% Chances to win division: 10.3% Projected wins: 7.5 Strength of schedule: Eighth hardest 2025 record: 4-13 Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 10-7 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 5-12 Windy City Gridiron | No. 24 2026 Question To Answer: Will John Harbaugh be the difference maker with a promising young core of players who need to take big Year 2 steps? In many ways, landing the eldest Harbaugh brother felt like the biggest win for the Giants in recent history. Although the Brian Daboll era got off to a promising start, it quickly became the same old Giants. Without flashes from last year’s rookie class, the future wouldn’t feel quite as bright, but Abdul Carter, Jaxson Dart, and Cam Skattebo all showed plenty of promise in Year 1. Now it’s up to Harbaugh and his staff to maximize their ceilings. If they can do that, the Giants could see a big jump in 2026. Bleacher Report | No. 24 The New York Giants should be instantly more competitive with John Harbaugh taking over as head coach. He knows what it takes to build a contender and to sustain success, and fans should expect to see glimpses of that in 2026. However, we’re probably still a year away from seeing New York make a real run in the NFC East. Despite having several promising young players, the Giants still have a lot of unknowns. Much will hinge on Jaxson Dart’s ability to stay healthy and make a significant second-year jump. NFL Media (Shook) | No. 26 The John Harbaugh era begins with a major showdown against the Cowboys in prime time on Sunday night. I expect high energy at MetLife Stadium, but I’m not as sure about whether the Giants will match it defensively. FOX Sports (Vacchiano) | No. 23 Odell Beckham is back, but a fourth WR doesn’t move the needle much. I’m still waiting to see how back WR Malik Nabers and RB Cam Skattebo really are. They could make the Giants a surprise team, especially with a defense that could end up in the top 10. Pro Football Talk | No. 20 John Harbaugh may have them on the brink of a quick turnaround. SB Nation | No. 25 No explanation given. The Athletic | No. 25 Optimism reigns thanks to the hiring of John Harbaugh and what should be a great pass rush. But the team lost Calvin Austin to a season-ending ACL tear, and second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart’s weapons behind Malik Nabers aren’t great. Pro Football Focus | No. 23 Odds to make playoffs: 24% Odds to win Super Bowl: 1% John Harbaugh takes over a Giants team looking to make its second playoff appearance in the last 10 seasons. New York boasts an impressive young nucleus in Abdul Carter, Brian Burns, Malik Nabers and Andrew Thomas, which added a pair of top-10 picks in Arvell Reese and Francis Mauigoa. Whether or not Jaxson Dart can improve upon his 64.2 PFF passing grade — as well as the play of the team’s secondary — will decide how much noise Harbaugh’s group can make in a crowded NFC field. USA Today | No. 23 Amid injuries and ongoing turnover at the position, including the recent release of Darius Slayton, rookie WR Malachi Fields quietly projects as one of Big Blue’s most important players entering the opener. CBS Sports (Prisco) | No. 22 John Harbaugh’s No. 1 goal is to get quarterback Jaxson Dart to take the next step. If he does, they can push for a playoff spot.

title: Darius Slayton cut is a gamble the NY Giants might regret
summary: John Harbaugh is running a meritocracy, and Darius Slayton’s play this summer did not warrant him being ahead of any other wide receiver on the New York Giants’ roster. That is the biggest reason Slayton is an ex-Giant today. Slayton missed the entire spring after double sports hernia surgery. He had a quiet summer, admitting […]
full_text: Darius Slayton | Getty Images John Harbaugh is running a meritocracy, and Darius Slayton’s play this summer did not warrant him being ahead of any other wide receiver on the New York Giants’ roster. That is the biggest reason Slayton is an ex-Giant today. Slayton missed the entire spring after double sports hernia surgery. He had a quiet summer, admitting not long ago that he still was not running at 100%, though he felt “pretty good.” Malik Nabers is the Giants’ No. 1 wide receiver. Malachi Fields, Odell Beckham Jr., and Darnell Mooney were all better than Slayton this summer. For that matter, practice squad receivers Braxton Berrios and Dalen Cambre were also better. Slayton was ticketed for the game-day inactive list when Sunday’s season-opening game against the Dallas Cowboys rolled around. None of that means that cutting Slayton isn’t a massive gamble by the Giants. The Giants have already lost one wide receiver they were going to count on heavily, Calvin Austin, to a season-ending injury. Depth at the position is now, to use an informal word, sketchy. Yes, moving on from Slayton is likely a sign that the Giants feel good about the possibility that Nabers will play Sunday against the Cowboys. Even if he plays, though, Nabers will probably play a limited number of snaps in his return from last season’s torn ACL. Fields is a rookie third-round pick. He had an impressive summer, but there is no guarantee he can carry that performance into real games. We have seen impressive summers fizzle before when fall arrived. Beckham earned his spot, no doubt. Still, he is a 33-year-old who did not play in 2025 and has not played a full NFL season since 2019 — yes, 2019. How much can he play? How long before his body breaks down and he misses time? How productive can he be when he does play? Darnell Mooney has a 1,000-yard and a 900-yard receiving season on his resume over six NFL seasons. He is coming off a down year with the Atlanta Falcons, though, where he caught just 32 passes for 443 yards. Are the Giants going to get a version of Mooney that deserves consistent playing time? What about the practice squad guys? Berrios has six receptions in 10 games over the past two seasons. Cambre was impressive this summer, but he has played 16 NFL offensive snaps and does not have a catch. Jalin Hyatt? Thirteen receptions over the past two seasons. Charlie Jones has eight catches in 33 career games, only one of which came in the last two seasons. Can any of them produce at an acceptable level if the Giants need them to play extended snaps at wide receiver? That is debatable. Slayton hate is unwarranted The subhead says exactly what it is meant to say. Slayton has been a better player than many Giants fans, needing someone or something to blame for the struggles of recent seasons, are willing to admit. Yes, his career drop rate of 6.3% is too high. No, he was never able to be what the Giants needed in the pre-Nabers days — a bona fide No. 1 receiver. Let’s be real, though. Slayton was a fifth-round pick, 171st overall, out of Auburn in the 2019 NFL Draft. He has not been an All-Pro like 2023 fifth-round pick Puka Nacua, but Slayton has vastly outplayed his draft position. Slayton led the Giants in receiving yards four times in seven seasons, with 700+ receiving yards in each of those seasons. He has a 15.0 yards-per-catch average. He is four catches shy of 300 for his career, and his 4,435 receiving yards are 565 short of 5,000. Slayton is 14th on the team’s all-time receptions list. His career average is 42 receptions per season. If he accomplished that in 2026, he would have moved all the way to ninth. Slayton is 12th on the team’s all-time list in receiving yards. His average 633-yard receiving season would have skyrocketed him to fifth, behind only Amani Toomer, Odell Beckham Jr., Frank Gifford, and Tiki Barber. Slayton has been a good player for the Giants. Instead of ripping him for his shortcomings and pointing a finger at him as part of the reason the team has been mostly awful during his time in New York, fans should be thanking him for being an overachiever, a good player, and an excellent representative of the franchise during his time with it. We have seen Slayton outplay expectations before. There might come a time this season when the Giants wish they still had him around to try and do it again.

title: Aaron Glenn takes on the hardest job in sports: Professionalizing Woody Johnson’s New York Jets
summary: Timing is funny. I have been working on this article for a while, and today Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic dropped a long feature on Jets owner Woody Johnson. The article portrays Johnson as an owner who is changing for the better. The sources for this belief that Woody Johnson is becoming a better owner? […]
full_text: FLORHAM PARK, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 27: (L to R) New York Jets co-owner Woody Johnson, general manager Darren Mougey, head coach Aaron Glenn and co-owner Christopher Johnson pose after the press conference announcing the hirings of Mougey and Glenn at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center on January 27, 2025 in Florham Park, New Jersey. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Timing is funny. I have been working on this article for a while, and today Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic dropped a long feature on Jets owner Woody Johnson. The article portrays Johnson as an owner who is changing for the better. The sources for this belief that Woody Johnson is becoming a better owner? Woody Johnson and people close to Woody Johnson. Call me cynical. Call me jaded. Call me whatever you want. I feel like we’ve heard this all before. Maybe the owner is turning over a new leaf. The proof will be in the results. Let’s talk about the challenges the Jets face from this owner and what head coach Aaron Glenn needs to do to turn this team around. I would argue that it is the toughest job in professional sports. At the start of training camp this year, I saw social media posts saying some version of the following over and over. 3 years ago #Jets fans were in Training Camp Heaven pic.twitter.com/YrkWEKD5Jj — uSTADIUM (@uSTADIUM) July 29, 2026 This post and many like it expressed nostalgia for Jets training camp in 2023. The Jets were emerging from an offseason full of hype and heading into a training camp…well…full of hype. The team was featured on HBO’s Hard Knocks . They were one of the top storylines in the national media on a daily basis. They were a trendy Super Bowl pick in the national media. The galvanizing force behind all of this was the trade for future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers. During training camp in 2023, no team in professional football had more buzz than the New York Jets. Unfortunately, what followed were two catastrophic years for the Jets. Rodgers suffered a season-ending injury four plays into his first Jets season, and the team stumbled to a 7-9 record without him. In year two the Jets managed to win fewer games with Rodgers than they won the year before without him. The team’s final record in 2024 was 5-12. Looking back it comes off as kind of ludicrous that the Jets fanbase looks back at a training camp as the glory days. Fans of franchises like the Eagles and Chiefs look back on Super Bowl wins as the pinnacle of their fandom. Our recent peak is a period of offseason hype. This offseason hype preceded perhaps the most disappointing stretch of play in franchise history after the games actually started. In other ways, however, few things sum up the experience of the Woody Johnson Jets better than the team’s peak being a period of massive offseason hype. At the end of the 2024 season, Johnson responded defensively when asked to summarize what had happened in an interview with the New York Post’s Brian Costello. “At the beginning of the season, I said this is from a talent standpoint this is one of the best teams I’ve ever had,” Johnson said. “Obviously, the networks and everybody agreed with that.” On the surface that seems like an innocuous comment, but I think it actually is a window into what Woody Johnson prioritizes building his team. For the great franchises in the NFL, the focus is on field stability. For Woody Johnson, the Holy Grail is positive media buzz. That has directed all aspects of the Jets franchise in recent years. Indeed, many members of the national media did predict big things from the Jets in the Rodgers era. ESPN’s Mike Clay declared that the team had the NFL’s best roster in 2024 and predicted they would win the Super Bowl. Pro Football Focus also suggested the Jets had a top five roster. Peter Schrager, then of NFL Network, predicted the Jets would finish the regular season with the top seed in the conference. This is a small sampling of the preseason buzz around the Jets in the Rodgers era. All of this must have been the sweetest music to Johnson’s ears imaginable. To be clear, I don’t think Woody Johnson is indifferent to whether his team wins or loses. I believe he genuinely wants to win. Where he runs into trouble is that he believes the things that get a team media hype are the same sort of things that lead to victory on the field. It just isn’t the case. Football is singular in this way. Follow any other sport, and the formula to build a winning team is simple. Get a couple of high impact players, and you’re a contender. Landing a big name star generally can transform your franchise. The NFL doesn’t work that way. There are eleven starters on each side of the ball. Then you have numerous role players who play small yet significant roles on subpackages and special teams. Simply put, a big name star in football moves the needle less than a big name star in any other sport. Additionally, the NFL has the franchise tag lingering for any big name who might want to test the market in free agency. The tag provides a player with a lucrative one year contract, but it limits long term earnings. With the nature of football meaning that a career altering injury is potentially lurking around every turn, true star players are incentivized to stay with their own team. Generally speaking, when a true superstar changes teams it is at the end of his career at a point he is declining. Some of the players who hit free agency are big names, but their name is bigger than their actual impact. Don’t get me wrong. You absolutely need stars to win the NFL, particularly at quarterback. The best teams have the best players. It’s just you need more good players to win in professional football than in any other sport, and one great player only means so much. Our current sports media landscape isn’t set up to appreciate this, however. Across sports, offseasons have become as interesting as the seasons themselves with widespread player movement. Make splashy moves, and you win the offseason. In other leagues, pundits are accurate enough when they claim a splashy offseason has genuinely made a difference. In the NFL, a few big name signings typically aren’t enough to change a team’s fortune. There are too many pieces a winning team needs to have, and the guys available are a lower caliber than in other leagues. Of course, a great team can make a timely veteran addition in free agency that makes a genuine difference. But it’s important to do the under the radar things in the NFL, more than in any other league. Great teams are also developing midround Draft picks at a high level. A top heavy roster cannot be carried alone by big name players in a sport where gameday responsibilities are so spread out. That brings us to the fateful decision the Jets made in 2023 to pursue four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers, a move influenced in no small way by the team’s owner. Now I want to be clear. If you were excited when the Jets traded for Rodgers and optimistic before his two seasons with the team, I am not criticizing you. I’m a fan too. Our job is to be fired up when our team makes a trade for a legendary player and to be hopeful for the year ahead. I had skepticism about the deal on many levels we will discuss, but I was hoping for the best. I’ll admit I did not think the Jets would only win five games with Rodgers as their quarterback. What I’m going to explain is how there were clear red flags in the moment that the Jets should have seen. They ignored them I believe because of the owner’s view that headlines triumph over all. Because of the way the national media works in the NFL, the trade for Aaron Rodgers was treated as a masterstroke by the Jets. They had just gone 7-10 in 2022. Their biggest problem was quarterback. They had what was widely considered a top five defense. Drop in a big name like Aaron Rodgers, and presto changeo. You have a Super Bowl team. Looking a bit further under the hood, the Jets and the national…

title: Eagles News: ESPN picks Philadelphia to return to the Super Bowl against the Chiefs
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! ESPN’s Bill Barnwell is apparently big on the Birds this year. Losing another Super Bowl to the Chiefs by three points sure wouldn’t be fun. I do think it would be cool to see a rubber match between these two teams. […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - FEBRUARY 09: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles talks with Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) after Super Bowl LIX at Caesars Superdome on February 9, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! ESPN’s Bill Barnwell is apparently big on the Birds this year. Losing another Super Bowl to the Chiefs by three points sure wouldn’t be fun. I do think it would be cool to see a rubber match between these two teams. Same goes for a potential Super Bowl matchup against the Patriots. Especially cool if the Eagles actually go out and win the game. Predicting the 2026 NFL playoff field, plus Super Bowl pick – ESPN On the NFC side, I’ll pick the Eagles. I really believe in their defense as potentially being the league’s most complete unit, with difference-makers at all three levels and one of the best defensive coaches in Vic Fangio. There’s understandable skepticism about the offense after the Eagles made coaching changes and moved on from legendary offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland, but when Lane Johnson has been on the field, the Eagles have been successful. The star right tackle should be in the lineup more often in 2026, and the Eagles will have more success running the ball than they did a year ago. They’re one of the few teams that can compete with the Rams along the line of scrimmage and hold up in coverage against their playmakers. […] That leaves us with a Super Bowl rubber match. And as you can probably guess, if I believed enough in the Chiefs to pick them to win the AFC, I’ll ride with them to gain a measure of revenge and beat the Eagles in Super Bowl LXI. The added rushing element with Walker will give the Eagles issues they didn’t face when these two teams met in Super Bowl LIX, when the Chiefs basically abandoned the run altogether after the Eagles took an early lead. Without the ability to pin their ears back and strictly go after Mahomes as a passer, the Eagles might not be quite as dominant on defense this time around. Jalen Hurts has been spectacular in the Super Bowl matchups against Mahomes, but his one fumble in Super Bowl LVII helped swing seven points back to the Chiefs in a 38-35 victory. This one wouldn’t be quite as high-scoring, but let’s say that the Chiefs let Kelce (and potentially other members of the organization) ride off into the sunset. My pick: Chiefs 27, Eagles 24. Eagles Film Preview: Commanders could struggle to stop Philadelphia’s rushing attack – BGN Overall, I still favor the Eagles. Washington is installing a complicated new defensive system with a number of new starters, while the Eagles have far more continuity within the roster even if the offensive structure has changed. The obvious concern is that Jones’ entire defensive philosophy is built around making quarterbacks and offensive lines second-guess what they are seeing. That is probably not ideal for an offense playing its first meaningful game under a new coordinator. However, Washington also has to execute all of that complexity, and I’m not convinced the defensive personnel is good enough right now. Every NFL team ranked by their 2027 Super Bowl chances entering Week 1 – SB Nation Tier 1: Super Bowl Contenders. Nobody in our top five should really surprise anyone. These are the teams that are the elite of the elite, the cream of the crop, the organizations that either have everything together they need to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, or have issues so minor they won’t play a major role in their success. These are the teams that would stun us if they missed the playoffs, or got eliminated early. The Rams speak for themselves in this tier. The big question comes at the back end with the Ravens, who perennially get ranked high because they should have all the tools to make it, but end up with a fatal flaw in the playoffs. This year we see new head coach Jesse Minter having the capability to get them over that hump. No. 1: Los Angeles Rams, No. 2: Seattle Seahawks, No. 3: Buffalo Bills, No. 4: Philadelphia Eagles, No. 5: Baltimore Ravens. Season Predictions w/BLG | OTSP #157 – Eagles Pin-Pull Network Shane and Jonny are joined by Brandon Lee Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation to make predictions for the Eagles’ season. Know Your Enemy – Jayden Daniels – Iggles Blitz Daniels having to open the season against a loaded Eagles defense isn’t ideal for Washington, especially behind a questionable OL. The one advantage is that the Eagles won’t have good game tape to study. Washington limited their playbook in the preseason. The Eagles faced the Lions offense last year so they know the basic system, but they don’t know about Blough as a play-caller or how the offense will look with Daniels running it. I think it is fair to say he’s just a tad different from Jared Goff. Why Jalen Hurts will flourish in Sean Mannion’s offense – NBCSP And I don’t see any reason Hurts won’t flourish in this system. For starters, he’s flourished in every system so I can’t come up with a reason this would be any different. But Mannion really seems to have tailored the offense to what Hurts likes to do within the heavy play-action, under-center tenets the scheme is built on. This is a system that is quarterback friendly because the QB doesn’t have to read the whole field, most passes are high-percentage low-risk throws and there’s a heavy emphasis on running the ball and disguising plays pre-snap to keep defenses off balance. If the offensive line can stay healthy – and so far so good – and Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Makai Lemon can help make up for the loss of good ol’ What’s His Name in New England, and Saquon Barkley can run the ball consistently and productively, there’s nothing that can hold this offense back. Will it take a few weeks before it all comes together? Probably. The starting offense hasn’t played one snap of real football with Mannion calling plays, and that’s a little scary. They’ll go into Sunday’s opener vs. Washington without a dry run. But ultimately, this season is going to end the same way as 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. With the Eagles in the playoffs and Hurts as one of the biggest reasons why. Why Eagles OC Sean Mannion’s ‘beautiful mind’ matters more than new scheme – The Athletic The Eagles did not game plan specifically for preseason games, so his first time planning and sequencing the calls comes Sunday against the Washington Commanders. Early feedback on the operation was favorable. Quarterbacks appreciated how quickly they heard the play call. The call sheet appeared organized. Communication remained sound. Substitutions were clean. Mystery still exists. The scheme, which the Eagles consider a competitive advantage, will evolve as Mannion sees how it fits the personnel. But Mannion’s success will depend on more than the binder he put together. It hinges on how he puts those ideas to work. “As the year goes on,” Mailata said, “we get to display what’s in the beautiful mind of his.” ‘It’s his time:’ DeVonta Smith enters 2026 primed to prove the Eagles — and himself — right as the new WR1 – PHLY Eagles Dating back to the spring, there has been palpable internal enthusiasm for what Smith can become in new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s scheme. The 27-year-old has yet to surpass the 100-catch mark in his career mostly spent as the “1B” to Brown’s “1A.” How productive can he be if he starts getting thrown the ball more often? According to TruMedia, Smith ranked 12th in target share last year at 24.4%, while Brown finished 10th at 26.1%. But what if that number were closer to the 30% mark Jaxon Smith-Njigba surpassed last season (35.8%) and Puka Nacua approached (28.5%) in similar schemes geared around a play-action passing game that funnels targets to versatile pass catchers. Those close to Smith believe he’s ready for that workload. Actually, those close to…
