title: Eagles Film Preview: Commanders could struggle to stop Philadelphia’s rushing attack
summary: Hello! I’m back this year with BGN, as always, and I’ll have two review articles and two preview articles every week. Last year was the first year I’ve ever previewed games. There are a lot of statistical previews out there, but this one will always be film-based. I think my previews improved as the year […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball and scores a touchdown during an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello! I’m back this year with BGN, as always, and I’ll have two review articles and two preview articles every week. Last year was the first year I’ve ever previewed games. There are a lot of statistical previews out there, but this one will always be film-based. I think my previews improved as the year went on, and it was cool to see stuff on Sunday that I had seen during the week. Hopefully we can hit the ground running this season. However, Week 1 makes this article a little different from the usual preview. Let me know what you think of the position breakdowns. Normally, I can watch around three recent games and get a pretty clear idea of what the Eagles will face. That isn’t really possible here. Washington has a new defensive coordinator in Daronte Jones and has kept plenty hidden throughout the preseason, while the Eagles are also entering the season with a completely new offense under Sean Mannion. So this is less a traditional matchup preview and more an attempt to understand what Washington is building, which players matter, and what the Eagles are likely to see. Overall, I still favor the Eagles. Washington is installing a complicated new defensive system with a number of new starters, while the Eagles have far more continuity within the roster even if the offensive structure has changed. The obvious concern is that Jones’ entire defensive philosophy is built around making quarterbacks and offensive lines second-guess what they are seeing. That is probably not ideal for an offense playing its first meaningful game under a new coordinator. However, Washington also has to execute all of that complexity, and I’m not convinced the defensive personnel is good enough right now. Daronte Jones and the new scheme Jones is a fascinating hire as DC because his background includes many different influences. He has coached defensive backs for much of his career, was LSU’s defensive coordinator in 2021, and has worked under coaches including Mike Zimmer, Vance Joseph, Lou Anarumo and, most recently, Brian Flores in Minnesota. I wouldn’t simply describe this as the Flores defense moving to Washington, but the Minnesota influence is clearly the most relevant when projecting what we are likely to see. 3) I mean… look at the rotation here. It's just absurd. I would be terrified of throwing hot routes against this defense because you have to be sure you aren't passing straight into the arms of a linebacker pretending to blitz and then dropping into coverage (like here). This… pic.twitter.com/fxRY1ZV4lN — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 15, 2025 The Vikings’ defense under Flores was one of my favorite units to study last season because the pre-snap picture often meant nothing. They would crowd the line of scrimmage with six or seven potential rushers, threaten Cover 0, then rush four and drop several linebackers into coverage. On the next snap, they might present almost the same look and actually send the blitz. The whole structure was designed to slow the quarterback down. Jones has spoken about disguising coverage, using multiple fronts and building the scheme around his players, and Washington has clearly added defenders who fit that philosophy. 5) The rotation is awesome to watch. Flores must be an excellent teacher, because I didn't see many busts at all. We go from cover 0, to a cover 1 man look to cover 2 all in a few seconds. Poor Jake Browning didn't a clue what he was looking at, and by the he had processed what… pic.twitter.com/Ce4iJz0dz4 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 15, 2025 The biggest personnel change is speed. Washington’s defense looked old and slow at times last year, whereas this group has been rebuilt around athleticism and movement. Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson and Joshua Josephs give them explosive edge speed, while Frankie Luvu and Sonny Styles can line up in multiple spots at the second level. Jones wants to dictate to the offense rather than simply react to it, and this collection of athletes gives him a much better chance to do that. This could create some early problems for the Eagles because Mannion is installing a new offense. We know the Eagles want to use more motion, under center offense, and play action, but we don’t know how comfortable the whole operation will look right away. Hurts could turn his back to the defense on a play-action fake, then turn around to find two defenders have dropped and the coverage has completely rotated. That is a difficult picture for any quarterback, let alone one working within a new structure. Minnesota made this style work because the defense was incredibly well coached and rarely busted assignments despite all the movement. Washington has not earned that level of trust yet. Jones is installing a complicated system with a secondary that has plenty of uncertainty, so the Eagles should force the Commanders to prove they can communicate for four quarters rather than assuming every disguise will be executed perfectly. The Eagles should not play scared on offense. It is also worth noting that Jalen Hurts played exceptionally well vs the Vikings last year. He handled a lot of the disguised coverages well and looked as comfortable as anyone that I watched go up against the Vikings’ defense. 7) I thought Hurts processed things really well and efficiently in this game. This defense does an extremely good job confusing quarterbacks, but Hurts did not seem phased at all. He was calm in the pocket and had a good understanding of where to go with the football. We saw a… pic.twitter.com/URZntk50eN — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 20, 2025 Defensive Front Daron Payne remains the best player in the group, while Javon Kinlaw, Tim Settle, and Charles Omenihu give Jones a number of different body types to move around. Johnny Newton’s injury is significant because it removes one of their most talented young interior defenders, but this is still a group with enough depth to rotate heavily. Minnesota frequently used three-man fronts and trusted its front to survive with two safeties deep, while the Commanders already had players such as Payne who could move around and align as heavier defensive ends. Washington also has several linebackers who can walk down onto the line, so I expect the distinction between defensive line and linebacker to become pretty blurry at times. The picture could change constantly even if the personnel does not. 7) Late safety rotation from single-high to Tampa 2, and dropping a defender into coverage while bringing a LB from the opposite side. It's beautiful. And must suck to play QB against. pic.twitter.com/cPUVmEa6yy — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 15, 2025 However, this is not a collection of edge defenders I would want playing endless snaps against heavy personnel and taking on Jordan Mailata and Lane Johnson in the run game. I watched Chaisson for the Scouting Academy this year, so I have an excellent read on him. He does not play hard vs the run. He wants to get up field and rush the QB, so I would get after him in the run game. This feels like a week where the Eagles should trust the offensive line. If Washington wants to keep both safeties deep, move linebackers around, and create uncertainty before the snap, the Eagles should be willing to run directly at those looks. Saquon Barkley doesn’t need endless schematic creativity if the box is light and the offensive line has favorable numbers. I want to see the Eagles establish the run early on. 9) Some good news though… I wasn't impressed with their run defense. I thought they were a little soft up front. I thought the safeties took bad angles coming downhill and the interior defensive line could get moved. They seemed to…

title: Eagles depth chart: Roster thoughts entering Week 1
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles’ first team-issued 2026 regular season depth chart is here ahead of Week 1! Since it’s compiled by the team’s media relations department, it’s not necessarily the most accurate representation of how the front office and coaching staff truly view the roster. But the media relations department certainly takes public perception into account. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to an NFL preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles’ first team-issued 2026 regular season depth chart is here ahead of Week 1! Since it’s compiled by the team’s media relations department, it’s not necessarily the most accurate representation of how the front office and coaching staff truly view the roster. But the media relations department certainly takes public perception into account. And, on that note, there are some interesting takeaways here. Depth chart first and then some thoughts to follow. OFFENSE QUARTERBACK — Jalen Hurts, Andy Dalton/Tanner McKee, Cole Payton RUNNING BACK — Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley WIDE RECEIVER — DeVonta Smith, Hollywood Brown WIDE RECEIVER — Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper WIDE RECEIVER — Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore TIGHT END — Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Eli Stowers, E.J. Jenkins LEFT TACKLE — Jordan Mailata, Markel Bell LEFT GUARD — Landon Dickerson, Willie Lampkin CENTER — Cam Jurgens, Drew Kendall RIGHT GUARD — Tyler Steen, Micah Morris RIGHT TACKLE — Lane Johnson, Fred Johnson DEFENSE EDGE RUSHER — Jalyx Hunt/Jonathan Greenard, Arnold Ebiketie EDGE RUSHER — Nolan Smith/Jonathan Greenard, A.J. Epenesa DEFENSIVE TACKLE — Jalen Carter, Byron Young DEFENSIVE TACKLE — Jordan Davis, Ty Robinson DEFENSIVE TACKLE — Moro Ojomo LINEBACKER — Zack Baun, Smael Mondon LINEBACKER — Jihaad Campbell, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. CORNERBACK — Quinyon Mitchell, Kelee Ringo CORNERBACK — Riq Woolen, Jonathan Jones NICKEL CORNERBACK — Cooper DeJean, Mac McWilliams SAFETY — Marcus Epps, Michael Carter II SAFETY — Andrew Mukuba SPECIAL TEAMS KICKER — Jake Elliott PUNTER — Braden Mann HOLDER — Braden Mann LONG SNAPPER — Rocco Underwood PUNT RETURNER — Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore KICK RETURNER — Will Shipley, Tank Bigsby THOUGHTS The Eagles are still refusing to reveal their backup quarterback. The Commanders won’t know what hit them if — God forbid — Jalen Hurts has to leave the game! Snark aside, it’ll be interesting to see how the Eagles handle this four quarterback situations. We know Hurts is starting. Guessing Dalton is the backup to begin the season with McKee dressing as the emergency third QB? And then Payton is inactive … unless he’s able to help out on special teams? We’ll get more clarity on this front soon. Not a surprise to see DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, and Makai Lemon listed as the starters at wide receiver. That was the top trio by the end of camp once both Smith and Lemon returned from hamstring injuries. With that said, it’ll be interesting to see what the snap counts looks like at receiver. One would think some combination of Hollywood Brown/Elijah Moore/Darius Cooper will rotate in to some extent. Especially with Lemon not exactly looking ready to handle all of the WR3 snaps with no questions asked from the jump. Cooper seems like a good bet to be active on game day due to his special teams contributions. Are both Brown and Moore going to be active or will one of them be scratched? Goedert is the starting tight end and Mundt is the primary backup. Stowers is listed third ahead of Jenkins … but the latter seems more likely to be active. If I’m projecting the Week 1 inactives, I think it might be Payton, Stowers, Micah Morris, Markel Bell (if still injured) or Willie Lampkin (if Bell is healthy), and Mac McWilliams. They’ll need one or two more inactives if they make any temporary practice squad elevations. Curious to learn more about the Eagles’ plan when it comes to offensive line depth. The read here is that Drew Kendall will be the top backup behind Landon Dickerson, Tyler Steen, and Cam Jurgens … not unlike how Brett Toth was the top interior depth option last year. At tackle, I think Markel Bell might be the swing option if he’s healthy (the rookie blocker finished camp with thumb/leg injuries). But maybe he’s just the backup on one side and Fred Johnson is the guy on the other? Maybe it’s nothing but I can’t help but notice how the Eagles usually list two players in the same spot, like they did here at QB2, in last name alphabetical order. But they didn’t do that with Jonathan Greenard, who is listed in starting contention with both Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith. It’s unclear when Greenard will be ready to play. But given what the Eagles traded to acquire him and then paid him in the form of a contract extension, one would think he’ll be starting at some point. Will be interesting to see how the Eagles distribute snaps at edge rusher. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. is clearly the top backup at both linebacker spots. I think Jonathan Jones might be the top backup at outside cornerback if there’s an injury to Quinyon Mitchell or Riq Woolen? He also has inexperience on the inside, though I’d think Michael Carter II would be the top backup to Cooper DeJean in the slot. Vic Fangio has insisted there’s an ongoing competition at safety but Marcus Epps didn’t play in the preseason games while Carter II did. And now Epps is clearly listed as a starter. The veteran defender could quickly lose that status and be replaced by MC2 if he falters. But, for now, Epps is starting next to Mukuba. Is Lemon really going to be the punt returner? I have my doubts. He only returned six punts in college (albeit for a productive 11.8 average) and then didn’t get many reps in that regard this summer. Not to mention it’s probably best to have him just focus on his offensive role, at least early on. The Eagles might opt to temporarily Britain Covey from the practice squad to handle punt returning. Or maybe they’ll actually get Moore in the mix?

title: Brandon Graham officially retires, again [UPDATE]
summary: Brandon Graham will not be returning to the Philadelphia Eagles to suit up for a 17th NFL season. The two-time Super Bowl champion reportedly stated as much during an event in Philly on Tuesday morning. UPDATE: Here’s Graham making the announcement. “I’m officially done. Y’all hearing it from me first. But let me tell you […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Brandon Graham #55 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after winning the game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Graham will not be returning to the Philadelphia Eagles to suit up for a 17th NFL season. The two-time Super Bowl champion reportedly stated as much during an event in Philly on Tuesday morning. Eagles news: Brandon Graham says he is officially retired. He made those comments during today’s “Breakfast with the Birds” pep rally at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital. #FlyEaglesFly — Chris Shepherd (@ChrisShepherd) September 8, 2026 UPDATE: Here’s Graham making the announcement. title: Eagles News: Jalen Hurts is “bought in and fighting hard through the learning curve”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! What are you expecting from Jalen Hurts this season? Yeah, he threw a lot of interceptions in training camp, but I don’t think any daily practice observer would describe his summer as a bad one. My feeling on him is that […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 2: Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on June 2, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! What are you expecting from Jalen Hurts this season? Yeah, he threw a lot of interceptions in training camp, but I don’t think any daily practice observer would describe his summer as a bad one. My feeling on him is that I’m not worried about Hurts. I’d be pretty surprised if he bottomed out because he offers a high floor. At the same time, I’m not expecting him to be MVP. Which is fine! He doesn’t need to be for the Eagles to have a successful season. I tend to think Hurts will have a good but not great season. What say you? Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … An Eagles Q&A: Is Hurts acclimating? Will Lemon contribute? – ESPN Passing game coordinator Josh Grizzard described a timing-based aerial attack which requires Hurts to have consistent footwork and trust in his pass catchers to be at the right place at the right time. “I think it’s the commitment from the whole group,” Grizzard said on what has impressed him most about the passing offense so far. “I think what you saw from the spring and where we’re at right now, with everybody’s understanding of the spacing of the field and the attention to fundamentals and details has really come a long way.” There’s going to be growing pains, no doubt. We witnessed some of that during the summer. Hurts threw double-digit interceptions during training camp — much more than we’re accustomed to seeing from him. Some of those fell on the receivers, some can be chalked up to a lack of synchronization in a new scheme, and some were on the QB. It’s worth noting Hurts is making more over-the-middle throws in this offense and he got burned a handful of times while doing so. The real test for Hurts’ commitment to this style of play will come during the regular season when the inevitable bumps in the road hit. The consensus to this point is he is bought in and fighting hard through the learning curve. NFL Week 1 odds: Eagles favored to beat Commanders – BGN Can you believe it? The first game of the 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season is just days away! And there’s reason to believe the Birds are going to begin this year’s campaign with a win. The Eagles are 5.5-point home favorites against the Washington Commanders. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 187: 2026 Season Predictions – NFC East Mixtape It is officially Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season and every team within the NFC East is playing another one. What does this season have in store for the NFC East? Last year saw a team win it in consecutive seasons for the first time in 20 years, so anything is on the table. RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton offer their 2026 predictions for the division in a way that only they can. You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! Eagles-Commanders preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice The Commanders allowed 141.5 rushing yards per game last season, third-worst in the NFL. So what did they do this offseason? They paid over $40 million in cash in 2026 to a couple of edge defenders in Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson who should really only be playing on obvious passing downs. They also did not bring back Bobby Wagner, which is understandable as he became a liability in coverage, but he was at least still a good run defender and he had a deep understanding of what opposing offenses were trying to do. Meanwhile, high-priced Javon Kinlaw gets pushed around in the run game, DaRon Payne is on the downside of his career, and fake tough Frankie Luvu is a situational pass rusher who has been masquerading as a three-down linebacker. (It seems the Commanders finally figured out that Luvu isn’t that guy, by the way, based on their acquisitions of Leo Chenal in free agency and Sonny Styles in the draft.) Meanwhile, I don’t think I’ve seen a worse tackling secondary than what the Commanders were last season. The success of the Eagles’ offense in 2026 is going to be dependent on their rushing attack. If they can’t get that going, it’s going to be a long, frustrating season on offense, like it was in 2025. This Commanders defense offers an outstanding opportunity to get the run game going right out of the gate. Another Journey – Iggles Blitz I don’t know how things will turn out this season, but I am confident that this season will be more fun than 2025. We’ll get to see a new offensive scheme. The O-line is healthy and that means we’ll see a more productive Saquon Barkley. He only had 3 games with 100 or more yards last season. I’ll be shocked if he doesn’t at least double that total this season. The defense could be the best in the league. There are special playmakers at each level of the defense. Make sure you enjoy the journey. That could be seeing a young player develop or an old player navigate his final season. Lane Johnson is an all-time great right tackle. We won’t see anyone like him in the future. Enjoy his greatness while you can. Nick Sirianni has led the Eagles to the postseason in each of his five years as the coach. I don’t expect that to change. He led the team to the Super Bowl in 2022 and 2024. That would seem to bode well for 2026. We’ll have to wait and see on that. The waiting is almost over. Football season is here. How Jalen Hurts is preparing for a season that could shape his Eagles future – The Athletic But it did raise two questions: “When should Hurts abandon his progressions and scramble? And how much will Mannion’s offense leverage Hurts as a runner? Hurts totaled a career-low 65 designed runs in 2025, apart from his 39 scrambles. Hurts totaled 92 designed runs in 2024, and 105 in 2023. Sirianni, Mannion and Hurts have all been cagey about any reason for the downward trend. Runs inherently carry risks, and Hurts, who did not suffer a long-term injury in 2025, had entered each of the playoffs of the previous four seasons managing some form of injury. Mannion vaguely acknowledged that Hurts’ rushing ability is a “special talent” the Eagles still intend to use — including in their continued usage of the Brotherly Shove. Fangio did note that Hurts is faster this season. Hurts demurred when asked if he’d changed his offseason approach at all to improve his speed. “He is a true weapon with his feet,” Grizzard said. title: Steelers Week 1 power rankings roundup: Does the national media have faith in Mike McCarthy?
summary: The NFL is back, and the Pittsburgh Steelers open up their 2026 regular season on Sunday afternoon at Acrisure Stadium when they take on the Atlanta Falcons. The game will mark an entirely new era of Steelers football, as Mike McCarthy is set to enter his first season as head coach of the franchise. McCarthy […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 21: Head coach Mike McCarthy of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the New York Jets at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is back, and the Pittsburgh Steelers open up their 2026 regular season on Sunday afternoon at Acrisure Stadium when they take on the Atlanta Falcons. The game will mark an entirely new era of Steelers football, as Mike McCarthy is set to enter his first season as head coach of the franchise. McCarthy is, of course, reunited with his former quarterback from his time with the Green Bay Packers, Aaron Rodgers. The legendary quarterback returns for his second season with the black and gold and is looking for a storybook ending to an already illustrious career. After going 10-7 and winning the AFC North last season, the Steelers are returning much of the talent that earned them a playoff spot. Is that enough to earn them some respect among the national media in the Week 1 power rankings? Let’s take a look at where the Steelers rank among the rest of the league in our weekly power rankings roundup. SB Nation: No.18 “Hitting Tier 4 we have the teams that have the pieces to make the playoffs, and that’s more or less their ceiling. There’s a mixture of lacking top-end talent, one side of the ball which is highly problematic, or simply being too young to really believe they can put a run together.” – James Dator and Mark Schofield The Athletic: No.18 “The Steelers haven’t had a losing season since 2003, so maybe it’s unwise to predict only eight wins. They boast the league’s highest-paid defense, but the big question is how good the offense can be with 42-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers reuniting with Mike McCarthy.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk: No. 18 “They need to get off to a fast start; there are plenty of tough games after the Week 9 bye.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.21 “While I expect the Steelers to prove their superiority against the Falcons in Week 1, I’m more interested in seeing how this offense operates under the direction of new head coach Mike McCarthy. The new-look receiving corps could produce some highlights to start the season and alter expectations quickly.” – Nick Shook USA Today: No.21 Another squad facing so many questions in 2027, particularly on the offensive side, probably should think long and hard before dumping more money into this defense” – Nate Davis ESPN: No. 21 “This season is a success if … the Steelers win a playoff game in coach Mike McCarthy’s first season. Yes, the organization sets its eyes on adding another Vince Lombardi Trophy to the case every season, but the first step is winning the team’s first playoff game in a decade.” – Brooke Pryor Seeing Pittsburgh placed in the middle of the pack was to be expected, but it is hilarious that, of the publications featured, all of them rank the Steelers either 18th or 21st. Given the fact that Week 1 is always undpredictable, it will be interesting to see how much we see the Steelers rise or fall in the power rankings after their date with Atlanta. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Steelers 2026 season predictions: Record, award winners, and more
summary: The NFL’s 2026 season gets underway tonight with a Super Bowl matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots. The Steelers season won’t be long behind, with Pittsburgh set to face off against the Falcons during the early slate of games this Sunday (1 p.m. EST). With anticipation mounting, we at BTSC decided […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 12: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up prior to an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Houston Texans at Acrisure Stadium on January 12, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s 2026 season gets underway tonight with a Super Bowl matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots. The Steelers season won’t be long behind, with Pittsburgh set to face off against the Falcons during the early slate of games this Sunday (1 p.m. EST). With anticipation mounting, we at BTSC decided to bring back our staff roundtable and discuss what we’ll be watching this season with the Steelers, and what else we’re thinking about the rest of the NFL. While we’re certain to be surprised by some outcomes of this season — this is why you play the games! — it’s always fun to look back at the end of the season on how we thought the season would go, and see where we were on the right track and where we were hilariously off base. After you’ve read our selections, be sure to sound off in our comments with your takes! We look forward to reading your thoughts about the upcoming seasons and talking ball with the BTSC community. Here we go Steelers! Which Steeler are you most excited to watch this season? Mike Nicastro: Call me crazy, but my choice is Aaron Rodgers. How often will we get the chance to watch a top-five quarterback of all time have his swan song with the team you root for? I’m excited about the additions to the offense, as well as reuniting with his former coach, Mike McCarthy. It will be entertaining – for better or for worse. Joey Bray: I am very much looking forward to seeing Nick Herbig in what should be an expanded role. Every season Herbig has been in the league, his sack total has increased. This season should be no exception, given the fact that Herbig signed a massive extension in the offseason. I would not be shocked if Herbig leads the Steelers in sacks this season. Ryland Bickley: Jaylen Warren. He’s long been one of the league’s most underrated running backs, in my eyes, and I’m excited to see what he can do in Mike McCarthy’s offense. Ryan Parish : I will echo this answer a little further on in this exercise, but the Steelers selected the exact two players I wanted them to in this year’s draft when they took Max Iheanachor and Germie Bernard with their first two picks. I think both will eventually take over important roles for the team during the season, and I will eagerly await their debuts. Jarrett Bailey: I look forward to Aaron Rodgers shutting up a lot of people again. Not projecting a top-10 quarterback season by any means, but he’s still a top-20 guy. What is the most interesting storyline for this year’s team? Ryland Bickley: It’s abstract, but can the new coaching staff finally give the Steelers the jolt the team has seemingly been missing the past several seasons? In more concrete terms, that’s innovation on both sides of the ball and maybe some rising stars on the coaching staff. It’s also the roster’s most highly-paid position groups actually living up to their potential. And most importantly, will the team look like it’s actually building towards eventual Super Bowl contention, not floating in a perpetual state of wild card losses? Ryan Parish : The Steelers are a team trying to straddle two different timelines. They want to “win now” for their older core (Rodgers, Heyward, Watt, Ramsey), but they’re also keeping 11 rookies and have several other young players we’d like to see make the leap this year: Derrick Harmon, Yahya Black, Troy Fautanu, Roman Wilson, Payton Wilson, Mason McCormick, Jack Sawyer, Carson Brueneer. Nick Herbig and Keeanu Benton just got large extensions — and Joey Porter Jr. will either get one just under the wire before Sunday or potentially be a franchise tag candidate next year — can they continue to get better and pay off those deals? While the Steelers may have the “ oldest roster ” on average in the NFL (27.1 years old), that list of players I reeled off is a significant chunk of the roster. How many of those players can take a major step forward in their development this year? The answer will tell us how viable this roster’s construction is as the team enters the post-Rodgers era in 2027. Jarrett Bailey: If the Steelers are a playoff team again, the best storyline will be how everyone who swore Mike Tomlin was the only thing good about the Steelers and the only reason they win games will have egg on their face. Defensively, they’ll be better. Offensively, they should be better. This is a team that has all the tools to make it to the postseason. Mike Nicastro: The Rodgers-McCarthy reunion is intriguing, of course, but I’ll go with the aging defense. When will Father Time find them? Cam Heyward and Jalen Ramsey will eventually hit a wall – and TJ Watt isn’t getting any younger. Do they have a stellar year left in them collectively? Joey Bray: How different does this team look under Mike McCarthy? While the Steelers return much of the same talent that won them the division last season, how differently will the team perform week-to-week and respond to adversity under a new head coach? I am very intrigued to see a new era of Steelers football under Mike McCarthy. Who will be the Steelers team MVP, Defensive Player of the Year, and Offensive Player of the Year? Jarrett Bailey: Team MVP: Aaron Rodgers DPOY: Nick Herbig OPOY: Jaylen Warren Ryland Bickley: Team MVP: Troy Fautanu DPOY: TJ Watt OPOY: Jaylen Warren Mike Nicastro: Team MVP: Aaron Rodgers DPOY: TJ Watt OPOY: DK Metcalf Joey Bray: Team MVP: Nick Herbig DPOY: Cam Heyward OPOY: Zach Frazier Ryan Parish: Team MVP: Zach Fraizer DPOY: Cam Heyward OPOY: Michael Pittman Jr. 11 rookies made the roster. Who is the Steelers Rookie of the Year? Ryan Parish : Anyone who followed my draft coverage knows I was a big fan of both the players the Steelers selected with their first two picks: Max Iheanachor and Germie Bernard. Iheanachor likely won’t start for the first part of the season, but I believe Bernard is already putting pressure on the coaching staff to play him with how he looked in the preseason. His ability to get open quickly underneath, as well as create yards after the catch, pairs well with the type of quarterback Aaron Rodgers is at this point in his career. That’s why I have Bernard eeking out this honor. Joey Bray: One of the biggest surprises of the 53-man roster was the Steelers keeping Eli Heidenreich as the team’s RB3. Not only will Heidenreich be the team’s third running back, but he will also be the personal protector on special teams. I would not be shocked to see Heidenreich get some runs as a return man this season as well. It’s pretty obvious that the Steelers coaching staff sees Heidenreich as someone who can play anywhere on the field, and it would be silly to keep him on the roster and not put the ball in his hands. Despite being a seventh-round pick, he has one of the clearest paths to immediate production of any Steelers rookie. I think he is an underrated pick for Steelers rookie of the year. Mike Nicastro: I think Max Iheanachor will take over the starting right tackle spot early and won’t let it go. Germie Bernard will come on late, but “IMax” will have the biggest impact. Ryland Bickley: It appears Max Iheanachor is on the fastest track to a starting gig this season of the team’s rookie class, and if he continues on what has been a promising trajectory this summer, he should quickly establish himself as the roster’s top right tackle. If the Steelers hit on the Iheanachor selection, it’s an easy pick for this award. Jarrett Bailey: Germie Bernard. He’ll get quality snaps very early on and be an important part of the passing game. title: Steelers’ secondary concerns and other storylines to follow in Week 1 vs. Falcons
summary: The 2026 NFL season is on the horizon. And after weeks of discussions, predictions and analysis, we’ll finally get to see some of the year’s biggest Steelers stories thus far finally play out on the football field as Pittsburgh hosts the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. With that in mind, here are some of the biggest […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker (3( participates in training camp drills at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2026 NFL season is on the horizon. And after weeks of discussions, predictions and analysis, we’ll finally get to see some of the year’s biggest Steelers stories thus far finally play out on the football field as Pittsburgh hosts the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. With that in mind, here are some of the biggest narratives Read & React will be monitoring this weekend: How will the new-look secondary perform? RB : There is a lot we still don’t know about the 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers, but the secondary might be where the most uncertainty lies. When I predicted which Steelers units would be most likely to finish in the NFL’s top 10 in the upcoming season, the pass defense was the hardest to get a read on. With a cornerback room made up of Joey Porter Jr., Jalen Ramsey, Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr., Brandin Echols and Daylen Everette, there’s a legitimate argument that this group could be elite. But at the same time, it isn’t difficult to imagine scenarios that result in the Steelers dropping closer to their 29th-in-the-NFL ranking in passing yards allowed per game in 2025. There’s a lot that can go wrong, especially early in the season. Starting with Porter, who is expected to be the top name in the secondary this year, there’s a chance he doesn’t even play if he doesn’t receive an extension by kickoff. But assuming he does suit up, it’s worth noting Porter missed the bulk of summer on the Physically Unable to Perform list with a reported back injury, and never took a rep in the preseason as a result. Rust could be a factor early-on in his game. Most of my concern regards the safety room, however, which will be especially undermanned early in the season with starter DeShon Elliott opening the year on injured reserve. Veteran Rayshawn Jenkins is expected to start alongside Jaquan Brisker, but I’d expect a short leash and Ramsey to rotate in at safety as well sometimes to give the group some needed extra range. We haven’t seen much of free agent signing Jamel Dean this offseason, who has flown under the radar a bit this offseason despite having the makings of a high-end CB2. He wasn’t far behind Porter in most metrics in 2025, allowing a 63.1 passer rating when targeted and a 49.2% completion percentage for Tampa Bay. Rewatching the tape from last night, and already impressed with #Steelers CB Jamel Dean GB got the ball out fast, but Dean had a number of strong man reps against Packers WR Matthew Golden, his primary opponent Showed off his physical press and mirrored well too pic.twitter.com/wrjlz8ilmU — Bradley Locker (@Bradley_Locker) August 14, 2026 Dean will turn 30 this season, meaning age is a concern but a Darius Slay-esque drop off in play isn’t expected this season. However, Dean’s availability is a minor question; he’s averaged four missed games per season in the last three years. But the arguable biggest piece of the puzzle is how that assortment of names will mesh with the scheme of new coordinator Patrick Graham. Graham is seen as a highly-adaptable defensive mind, but if the looks he did show in the preseason are any indicator, he isn’t afraid to use a number of coverage concepts in one game — or blitz. Graham sent a heavy dose of pressures in Pittsburgh’s slate of August games, putting the team’s secondary (that was missing names such as Porter, Ramsey and Brisker, to be fair) in tough spots where they didn’t always succeed. Now up to almost-full strength, we’ll get to see how Pittsburgh’s defensive backs mesh with Graham’s coaching in a real game. It’ll also be interesting to see how Porter’s speciality in press-man coverage fits into a more diverse scheme. The good news is that while the Falcons boast a talented group of offensive weapons, starting quarterback Tua Tagovailoa shouldn’t present a massive challenge for the defense in Week 1. But if things go poorly against Tagovailoa, who was benched by the Dolphins late last year, it could be time to worry a little bit. How soon can top rookies make an impact? RP : As Week 1 gets closer, the team is letting out more info about how head coach Mike McCarthey sees the roster at this early stage of the season. The team has put out its first depth chart of the season Tuesday, which came with some items to ponder. While it’s wise to remember a depth chart is ultimately just a list of names that a coaching staff can quickly pivot from on game day, it is also useful for setting initial expectations. It isn’t shocking that the Steelers top two rookies, first-round selection Max Iheanachor and second-rounder Germie Bernard, are absent from the list of starters. McCarthy and the Steelers’ brass have been telegraphing that for most of August, even with the two youngsters giving plenty of reason for optimism this summer. But how long can we expect either rookie to remain sidelined? We’ll start with Iheanachor, the team’s top pick. The Arizona State product was the talk of Steelers camp in the early days of training camp, and might have had a legitimate shot to start in Week 1 if he hadn’t suffered an untimely shoulder injury that sidelined him through the first two preseason games. With that amount of time missed, it was going to be next to impossible for him to earn a starting spot with a viable alternative at the Steelers disposal. The Steelers believe Dylan Cook is just that. “We feel really good about Dylan,” McCarthy told the media Monday, when he said that Cook was taking most of the reps at right tackle this week. I think it’s safe to pencil Cook in as the starter for Week 1, but I also think McCarthy’s comments are telling. Cook was taking the majority of the snaps, but not all. McCarthy also declined to outright name Cook the starter when he was asked. This, paired with other comments from the head coach, as well as from the team’s offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio , should make it clear that Iheanachor taking over this season is a matter of when and not if , as long as health allows. Mike McCarthy says Max Iheneachor has been 'impressive' but because he has missed so much time, it is tough to throw him into the starting role right away. Added the ability has been there when he's out there. "Make no mistake about it, he can play." — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) September 7, 2026 Projecting when Iheanachor might take over is trickier. He was healthy enough to play in the final preseason game, so I have to believe he is physically capable of going now. You wouldn’t want to see it go down this way, but like most NFL backups, he’s realistically just one injury away from entering the lineup. But barring that, I’m eyeing Week 5 and October 11 as a possible entry date. That would give him another month to ramp up, and the Colts have one of the least intimidating pass rushes in the NFL. If they feel like that start date is still too soon, then perhaps coming out of their bye week against the Bengals in Week 10 might be another alternative. McCarthy wasn’t just playing coy about the right tackle position, though. Instead, he said he wouldn’t discuss the starters, citing it as an attempt to keep the Falcons off balance heading into the matchup. While I ultimately don’t believe that will have much impact on the game one way or the other, it’s a long-held tactic by many football coaches I’ve met across all levels of football, so it shouldn’t be that surprising. Mike McCarthy said he doesn't want to give definitive declarations on who will start and what the rotations will be to keep the Falcons off balance for now. So, no sure fire answer on who will be WR3, starting RT, etc. — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) September 7, 2026 But unlike Iheanachor, I’m having a hard time believing the Steelers will keep Bernard sidelined for long. For one thing, Roman Wilson barely has any more…

title: Ian Rapoport tells Steelers fans not to give up hope on Joey Porter deal
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. is the lone cornerback remaining on contract extension island. The New England Patriots signed All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez to a four-year, $135 million extension early Tuesday. Gonzalez will receive $102 million guaranteed. full_text: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. is the lone cornerback remaining on contract extension island. The New England Patriots signed All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez to a four-year, $135 million extension early Tuesday. Gonzalez will receive $102 million guaranteed. Porter Jr. now stands as the last young corner still looking for a new deal before kickoff on Sunday afternoon. NFL Network/ESPN insider Ian Rapoport isn’t closing the door on a new deal being completed yet. “I would say, ‘the season has not started yet,’” Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show Tuesday . “Until the season starts, I will not give up hope that this could get done.” Play begins in five days and marks the unofficial official deadline for negotiations, as the Steelers don’t negotiate during the season due to a team policy established in the 1990s. A trade doesn’t seem likely, either. That means Porter would make just under $4 million on the last year of his rookie contract and stay with the Steelers. “There’s been a lot of trade rumors with Joey Porter Jr.,” Rapoport said. “I’m not sure at this point whether or not those are going to come to fruition.” NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo reported Tuesday that the Steelers made an offer to Porter, but extension talks remained far from close. “There’ve been some conversations, but (it) doesn’t seem like they are far along contract-wise,” Rapoport said. “You get Christian Gonzalez done; that’s come in as the highest-paid. The more information there is, the more the market is built, the easier it is to get deals done.” In 14 games last year, Porter recorded 52 tackles, 14 passes defended, one sack, and one interception. He didn’t allow a touchdown in man coverage and began following the opponent’s top receiver more often later in the season. The Steelers listed their starting cornerbacks as Joey Porter Jr. OR Asante Samuel Jr. in their updated depth chart on Tuesday, opposite Jamel Dean. It feels like a clear message to Porter Jr. to suit up and play against the Falcons and get the contract negotiations all sorted. Let us know what you think in the comments . Still a lot of work to be done in the coming days to reach a deal. pic.twitter.com/eU74bFtds6 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) September 8, 2026 “But, the Steelers have shown a willingness to engage,” Garafolo added. “Which means we got a couple of days for both sides to figure out what are the right numbers to get a deal done. There is a lot of work to be done from my understanding. I would not call it imminent. I would not call it close. But I will call it an actual negotiation now that the Steelers have made an offer.” Porter is now the last big-name cornerback still hoping for an extension this offseason, with the Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez agreeing to a record-setting four-year, $135 million deal early Tuesday morning. With Porter back in practice after spending most of the summer on the physically unable to perform list, it appears the two sides are starting to make some progress. However, Pittsburgh doesn’t negotiate once games start, and Porter hasn’t ruled out an in-season holdout, adding an extra sense of urgency to the negotiations. Steelers beat writers such as PennLive’s Nick Farabaugh have posted that the Steelers will probably not need to make Porter the league’s new highest-paid corner to get a deal done.

full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 21: Aaron Rodgers #8 watches Will Howard #18 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warm up prior to the game against the New York Jets at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers entered the preseason with one of the most talked-about quarterback rooms in the NFL. With Mason Rudolph as the veteran backup, second-year quarterback Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar were both looking to show that they could be the future of the team at the position throughout the summer. Many believed that Howard would take over for Rudolph as the No. 2 quarterback, as long as he played well enough in training camp and preseason to give Pittsburgh enough confidence to make that decision, while Allar would be the high-ceiling “project” quarterback for Mike McCarthy to try and mold into a potential starter. Rather than moving on from Rudolph and keeping both young signal callers, Pittsburgh kept all four – something Rodgers himself did not expect. “I did not expect four quarterbacks on the roster,” Rodgers said on Cam Heyward’s podcast, Not Just Football . “I’ve never been part of [a room that kept] four quarterbacks. There were many years where two were just active and one on the p-squad. I knew when Drew was picked that would definitely shake things up in that room…” Rodgers applauded Rudolph for his improvement during the offseason, as well as his play in the first preseason game agains the Green Bay Packers, saying he “closed the door” on the backup quarterback conversation. He also noted how proud he was of both Howard and Allar. “I was proud of both those guys,” Rodgers said. “I love Will. He’s been in my hip pocket for a year now… it was fun to see him go out there because he’s basically a rookie. He didn’t play last year in the preseason… and Drew’s been a sponge, as well. Quiet, as most rookies are. But it’s one of my all-time favorite rooms for sure.” Part II of Heyward and Rodgers’ conversation comes out later this week. Let us know what you think in the comments . summary: Every NFL season is important. The 2026 season, though, feels even more so for the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Year One of life after Mike Tomlin, and in Year Two of the Aaron Rodgers era, few expect Pittsburgh to be a playoff team again. In order for Pittsburgh to silence any critics, they’ll need big production […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 12: Dk Metcalf #4 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up before the game against the Houston Texans at Acrisure Stadium on January 12, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every NFL season is important. The 2026 season, though, feels even more so for the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Year One of life after Mike Tomlin, and in Year Two of the Aaron Rodgers era, few expect Pittsburgh to be a playoff team again. In order for Pittsburgh to silence any critics, they’ll need big production from all of their big stars, and that certainly includes wide receiver DK Metcalf. The Steelers acquired Metcalf last March in a trade with the Seattle Seahawks and then rewarded him with a four-year, $132 million extension. And while 2025 wasn’t an awful year for the two-time Pro Bowler, it didn’t live up to the expectations that come with a big contract, as he caught 59 passes for 850 yards and six touchdowns, while adding a rushing touchdown to give him seven on the year. The 1,000-yard mark is something everyone would like to see Metcalf hit in 2026, but it’s not something that the receiver himself is concerned about. “I mean, I’ve done it,” Metcalf told Jonathan Jones of The Athletic . “So me doing it again is proving what to anybody? I want to win the Super Bowl and I’ll let the rest speak for itself.” Steelers fans would love nothing more than to see the team bring a seventh Lombardi Trophy to Pittsburgh, especially in what will be the final season in the storied career of Aaron Rodgers. To go out on top like Peyton Manning in 2015 would be the ultimate exclamation point for the four-time MVP, but would also give several players like Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt Super Bowl rings – something that has eluded them thus far. While Metcalf may not be worried about putting up huge numbers, the only path the Steelers have to a Super Bowl in 2026 involves him having a big year. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Seahawks vs. Patriots, Week 1 preview: The key questions entering NFL Kickoff 2026
summary: Seven months after Super Bowl 60, the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots meet again. The rematch gives us an unusual Week 1 matchup. These teams know each other extremely well after facing off for the Lombardi Trophy, but both have also spent the offseason changing important pieces of their rosters. Seattle still has much […]
full_text: Seven months after Super Bowl 60, the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots meet again. The rematch gives us an unusual Week 1 matchup. These teams know each other extremely well after facing off for the Lombardi Trophy, but both have also spent the offseason changing important pieces of their rosters. Seattle still has much of the defense that dominated New England in February. The Patriots, meanwhile, added significant talent around Drake Maye and made changes to an offensive line that struggled in the Super Bowl. And then there is Seattle’s biggest unknown: what exactly will Brian Fleury’s offense look like when the games finally count? We saw plenty of concepts during the preseason. We still haven’t seen the real thing. Depth chart: What changed in Seattle? The good news for Seattle is that much of the defense that won the championship is still here. Leonard Williams returned on a new multi-year extension , while Devon Witherspoon also received a major extension this offseason and Derick Hall too . Byron Murphy II, Jarran Reed and DeMarcus Lawrence remain part of a defensive front that was one of the biggest reasons the Seahawks were able to control Super Bowl 60. But the secondary has undergone meaningful changes. Coby Bryant is gone, and Seattle decided to invest in the position by selecting TCU safety Bud Clark in the second round . Ty Okada was also expected to take on a bigger role after playing significant snaps last season. Clark, however, is out for the season. Okada is now dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play on Wednesday, while Nick Emmanwori is still working his way back from ankle surgery. Emmanwori’s situation is particularly unusual. He suffered the injury during Super Bowl week, played in the game, and underwent surgery later. He has returned to practice but remains uncertain for Week 1. If both Okada and Emmanwori are unavailable, Seattle could be forced to elevate two safeties from the practice squad, with D’Anthony Bell, AJ Finley and Rodney Thomas II among the most likely options. At cornerback, Seattle also has to replace Riq Woolen. The Seahawks are betting on Josh Jobe continuing to develop and hoping Nehemiah Pritchett can take another step. The late addition of Avery Smith — a player capable of working both inside at nickel and outside — was another indication that Seattle wanted more flexibility and depth at the position. Julian Neal, the team’s third-round pick, has also returned to full practice after missing much of the offseason with a quad injury. So while the championship defense remains largely intact, there are enough new pieces in the secondary for New England to test. The same is true at running back. Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP, is now in Kansas City. Seattle responded by selecting Notre Dame running back Jadarian Price with the No. 32 overall pick . Price didn’t play during the preseason, likely in part because the Seahawks wanted to preserve a player they expect to have a significant role this season. The question is whether Seattle’s defense can maintain the same level it reached last season despite the changes around it. What changed in New England? The Patriots spent the offseason making sure Drake Maye would have more help. The biggest additions came at wide receiver. Stefon Diggs is gone, but New England added A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Brown gives Maye a true No. 1 receiver who can dictate coverage, while Doubs provides a complementary option capable of attacking different areas of the field. The Patriots also reinforced the offensive line, signing Alijah Vera-Tucker and selecting Utah offensive tackle Caleb Lomu with the 28th overall pick. Will Campbell enters his second season, and the Patriots are hoping the additional experience and new pieces make the group much better than the one Seattle faced in the Super Bowl. This is a very different Patriots team from the one Seattle faced in February. Where will the Patriots attack? The first place to look is the Seattle secondary. New England now has more ways to stress a defense that relies on disguises, split-safety structures and four-man pressure. A.J. Brown can force Seattle to account for him on every snap, while Doubs and the rest of the receiving corps give Maye more options underneath and in the intermediate areas. But the Patriots may also try to attack Seattle on the ground. They couldn’t establish the run consistently in Super Bowl 60. That was a major problem because it allowed Seattle to play more freely against the pass and let its defensive front dictate the game. If New England can run the ball this time, the Seahawks won’t have the same luxury. And if the Patriots can keep Maye clean, the matchup changes completely. A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs can only make the difference if Maye has enough time to find them. That puts Seattle’s defensive front and the Patriots’ revamped offensive line at the center of this rematch. The Brian Fleury Test This is where Week 1 becomes particularly interesting for Seattle. We’ve seen more of Fleury’s running-game ideas than his passing game during the preseason. Seattle showed heavy personnel, motion, running back motion, outside runs and plenty of play action. Fleury also used the fullback frequently, sometimes essentially treating him as another tight end while moving him around the formation. That could create a bigger opportunity for Brady Russell. Russell is already a key piece of Seattle’s special-teams unit. The question now is whether Fleury’s offense can finally give him a chance to contribute consistently on offense as well. He can line up as a fullback, tight end or even split out as a receiver, giving Seattle another way to manipulate defensive looks and create mismatches. It could be an opportunity for Russell to finally make a bigger impact with the ball in his hands. Elijah Arroyo is another player worth watching. He brings a different skill set at tight end, with legitimate vertical-threat ability and the versatility to occasionally align as a wide receiver. Heavy personnel and play-action concepts should suit his strengths particularly well, potentially creating opportunities for him to attack defenses down the field. And that’s part of what we still don’t know about Fleury’s offense. We’ve seen enough to understand the philosophy. We haven’t seen enough to understand the full passing game. How much attention will defenses give Jaxon Smith-Njigba? Where will he consistently line up? How will Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed, Arroyo, Russell and the running game affect the way defenses can play JSN? And perhaps most importantly: how aggressively will Fleury attack vertically? The Seahawks barely played their starters during the preseason, so we saw the concepts without seeing the complete offense. Week 1 is where we finally start getting those answers. Christian Gonzalez changes the equation There is no longer any question about whether Christian Gonzalez will play. The Patriots agreed to a four-year, $135 million extension with Gonzalez , making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history and surpassing the contract Devon Witherspoon signed with Seattle only weeks earlier. That immediately creates an interesting question for Fleury. Does Seattle try to avoid Gonzalez? Does it attack him directly? Or does Fleury use motion and formations to manipulate where Gonzalez lines up and create favorable matchups elsewhere? New England has a good, disciplined defense, and Gonzalez gives them the ability to trust one side of the field more than they otherwise might. Fleury will need to have an answer. This is also where the vertical element becomes especially interesting. Seattle has shown more of its running-game identity than its passing-game depth, so Week 1 should give us our first real indication of how Fleury intends to create explosive plays against a defense capable of taking away easy answers. The Offensive Line gets its first real test Seattle brings back all five…

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 8: Julian Love #20 of the Seattle Seahawks returns an interception during the fourth quarter of the NFL Super Bowl LX football game against the New England Patriots, at Levi's Stadium on February 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to… Wednesday Night Football?! Featuring the Seattle Seahawks? Why yes, the Seahawks are opening the 2026 season on a Wednesday due to the NFL scheduling the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers for the following night in Melbourne, Australia. Is it really such a bad thing that Seahawks football is back in your life sooner than planned? The Super Bowl champions will unveil their latest banner in front of their new ownership group, then it’s all business for Mike Macdonald’s men. They conquered the New England Patriots to complete a dream 50th season, and indeed the final season under the ownership of the Allen Family. Now the Seahawks are owned by the Khoslas , who will surely be in attendance to watch their team (and maybe a ceremonial 12 Flag raise?). It’s year three under Mike Macdonald, year two of Sam Darnold at quarterback, and year one of Brian Fleury as offensive coordinator for the Seahawks. They might be second fiddle in terms of betting odds and publicity to the Los Angeles Rams, but they’re still among the favorites to at least make Super Bowl 61, and why not when the majority of the roster has been retained? Meanwhile, the Patriots had more turnover than realized , but that includes major upgrades at receiver with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, who should be outstanding targets for quarterback Drake Maye. Can New England pass protect well enough against Seattle’s monstrous defensive front in order for Maye to not be rattled like he was in the Super Bowl? We’ll find out very soon. title: Why Baker Mayfield’s contract extension is relevant to Seahawks, Sam Darnold
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have taken care of some major contract extensions over the past several months. They’ve extended Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Devon Witherspoon, Leonard Williams, and Derick Hall, all of whom were either in contract years or (in the case of JSN and Witherspoon) in their first extension-eligible year. As far as the next big contract […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 05: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers looks on after beating the Seattle Seahawks 38-35 at Lumen Field on October 05, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have taken care of some major contract extensions over the past several months. They’ve extended Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Devon Witherspoon, Leonard Williams, and Derick Hall, all of whom were either in contract years or (in the case of JSN and Witherspoon) in their first extension-eligible year. As far as the next big contract extension for John Schneider and company to deal with, that figures to be quarterback Sam Darnold, who’s entering the second of his three-year, $100 million contract . Tampa Bay Buccaneers just gave Baker Mayfield a three-year extension worth $165 million , including $110 million in new guaranteed money. This will put him in Josh Allen and Joe Burrow territory once the final details are revealed. Mayfield, who replaced Tom Brady in 2023 as a “buy low” free agent bargain, was set to have his current contract expire at the end of this season. Any thought of the Buccaneers immediately looking elsewhere at the quarterback position has been put to rest. Mayfield has, for the most part, had his best seasons in Tampa despite perennial offensive coordinator changes. He led the Buccaneers to the NFC Divisional Round in his first season, but the last two have ended in a Wild Card exit and a brutal collapse from 6-2 to 8-9 and out of the playoffs. Mayfield played through a shoulder injury toward the end of last season, which is not a first time occurrence for him in his NFL career. While the Seahawks are gearing up for another Super Bowl run, Darnold extension talks are inevitable and will be impacted by how this season unfolds. Mayfield represents a data point, if not a floor for a Darnold extension given Baker’s previous contract was worth pretty much the same money. Darnold, of course, has a Super Bowl ring and that might help his case to at least be a notch above Baker money. The reality for the Seahawks is that, unless Darnold suffers a major injury, plays very poorly, or is very willing to play at Daniel Jones money, the next contract Darnold signs is going to be comfortably north of $50 million/year . If he plays well and Seattle is anywhere near another Super Bowl, you might be looking at $60 million. Needless to say, the Seahawks have benefited greatly from above-average to elite quarterback play at discounted prices. Whether it’s Russell Wilson during his rookie contract, Geno Smith’s 2022 season on a one-year deal, or Darnold right now, John Schneider has done well to field playoff-caliber (and, at his best, Super Bowl-caliber) teams without paying the quarterback top dollar. Very soon, we’re about to find out whether or not Schneider is going to pay a quarterback top dollar again like he did with Russ back in 2019.

title: Seahawks-Patriots injury designations: Ty Okada ruled out, Nick Emmanwori questionable
summary: As if losing safety Bud Clark, wide receiver Jake Bobo, and offensive lineman Mason Richman for the season wasn’t enough, the Seattle Seahawks are set to be without a starting safety and possibly two more key contributors in Wednesday’s home opener against the New England Patriots. Seahawks injury designations Out: Questionable:  While it’s unknown when […]
full_text: As if losing safety Bud Clark, wide receiver Jake Bobo, and offensive lineman Mason Richman for the season wasn’t enough, the Seattle Seahawks are set to be without a starting safety and possibly two more key contributors in Wednesday’s home opener against the New England Patriots. Seahawks injury designations Out: S Ty Okada (hamstring) Questionable: S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) WR Tory Horton (hamstring) While it’s unknown when and how Okada suffered the hamstring injury, his absence from practice on both Sunday and Monday seemingly indicated he wasn’t trending toward suiting up in Week 1. Now knowing for certain he’ll be sidelined, there’s little doubt Seattle will turn to the practice squad for game day elevations. However, Emmanwori’s status is cetainly a surprise, and could prevent the Seahawks from having to elevate more than one safety come tomorrow. After undergoing ankle surgery in July, his status for Week 1 was up in the air. On August 30, ESPN’s Brady Henderson reported the second-year’s odds of returning for the start of the regular season were ‘iffy,’ but after practicing in full pads on Sunday, it appears he has a realistic chance of suiting up—at a much needed time. The team’s decision to keep just three safeties on the active roster (Julian Love, Nick Emmanwori and Ty Okada) was questionable at the time but even if Emmanwori is ultimately ruled out, they’ll have a big pool to choose from, with four waiting in the wings on the practice squad. After appearing in 14 games with Seattle last season where he served as a reliable depth piece, D’Anthony Bell, who signed on September 5, would be the obvious choice. The Seahawks also have Rodney Thomas II, Maxen Hook and AJ Finley to choose from. On the other side of the ball, it’s been difficult to know what to make of Horton, especially after head coach Mike Macdonald said he’d miss a “period of time” in his press conference on August 21. However, the second-year wideout practiced in a limited capacity all week and appears to be on track towards an early season return, if not on Wednesday. Should he be sidelined, look for Rashid Shaheed to see more targets downfield. As for the Patriots, center Ben Brown (knee) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) were ruled out, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson the opportunity to dominate carries against one of the best defenses in the NFL. Both teams will release their official inactives at 3:50 pm P.T. on Wednesday.

title: Should Brian Fleury call a run or pass for first play as Seahawks offensive coordinator?
summary: As we’re all mentally preparing ourselves for the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks to open the 2026 NFL season against the New England Patriots, one question sticks out in my mind. What play will first-time Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury call to open the game?  Maybe that seems like it’s not a huge deal […]
full_text: As we’re all mentally preparing ourselves for the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks to open the 2026 NFL season against the New England Patriots, one question sticks out in my mind. What play will first-time Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury call to open the game? Maybe that seems like it’s not a huge deal to you, but there’s a specific reason why it’s bouncing around my brain. You see, while waiting for Seattle’s opener, I actually have another one to prepare for on Tuesday night. This year, I’m coaching middle school football, calling offense for 7th grade and defense for 8th grade. While I’m coaching at an infinitesimal level compared to the NFL, I’m also wrestling with how I want to start off my first game as a play caller. That first play can be used to establish an identity. Fleury has said that Seattle is going to continue to play “Seahawks football.” Hell, that was the reason he was hired in the first place, the continuity that he brought with him from the same scheme as Klint Kubiak. With that in mind, a run play would seem to be the odds-on favorite. The Seahawks commitment to the run paid off in a big way down the stretch in 2025, catapulting them to the mountain top. Yet, there are significant changes in the backfield. Kenneth Walker III plays for the Kansas City Chiefs. Zach Charbonnet is on PUP. Jadarian Price hasn’t taken a handoff in an NFL game. Everyone is excited about Price’s potential, so giving him the ball off the bat could be the best way to go. Like Walker, Price can break a game open on one play with his explosiveness. Wouldn’t a long TD run be a fun way to start? But the Patriots know that the Seahawks want to establish the run. Their inability to stop it was a big part of their downfall in February. They understand it, and have likely been prepping for it all offseason. Fleury also knows that, so is it the time to zig when everyone thinks they’ll zag by calling a play-action pass and try to hit an explosive? Seattle has the reigning offensive player of the year in Jaxon Smith-Njigba and other weapons including Rashid Shaheed, Elijah Arroyo, Cooper Kupp, AJ Barner, and (hopefully) Tory Horton. That’s a lot of firepower for Sam Darnold to target through the air. With all the questions about the Seahawks running back corps right now, maybe Seattle should lean on their passing game? Obviously, I have an easier decision than Fleury since my first call comes with much less pressure. After two weeks of practice, my kids can run power, counter, pitch, and boot…not a ton of choice there. That likely makes my decision easier, and boils it down to a choice between which run play to call. Fleury’s first call will be a look into his offensive philosophy, and how it differs (or doesn’t) from Kubiak. Personally, I’m hoping Fleury gives the ball to Seattle’s new toy on a play with added motions that we didn’t see last season. That would be the right mesh to show that, yes, the Seahawks will still be running the heck out of the ball, albeit with some new wrinkles. Maybe I can even learn a thing or two for my own playcalling down the line…it’s hard to trust 7th graders to execute a pass play after all!

title: 49ers lose another key contributor to a season-ending injury
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have another season-ending injury that happened before their season has even started. Defensive tackle Alfred Collins showed up on the injury report this week, and Kyle Shanahan later said it’s a torn patellar tendon suffered Monday. Collins will now be out for the season. This marks another season-ending injury before the […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers have another season-ending injury that happened before their season has even started. Defensive tackle Alfred Collins showed up on the injury report this week, and Kyle Shanahan later said it’s a torn patellar tendon suffered Monday . Collins will now be out for the season. This marks another season-ending injury before the season has even started. This certainly doesn’t bode well for the 49ers’ injury concerns and for Collins, who had flashes in 2025 but needed to get some consistency going in his second season as a pro. Ricky Pearsall’s season ended in August after the team decided he needed surgery for his PCL . Mykel Williams is on the PUP list. Collins becomes the latest player on a rookie contract to miss significant time with a season-ending injury. The most recent example of an NFL player who weighs over 300 pounds missing time with a torn patellar tendon was Los Angeles Chargers offensive tackle Rashawn Slater. He missed the entire 2025 regular season after sustaining the injury in August 2025. His recovery time was 10 to 12 months. Slater returned to practice for the Chargers OTAs in June. If all goes well, Collins will be ready for training camp in 2026. Unfortunately, for Collins, things don’t usually go well when we’re talking about athletes returning from patellar tendon injuries. According to a recent study from 2025 , 85.7% of the athletes return but fail to start as many games as they did before the injury, while another 76.8% fail to return to their previous performance level. The 49ers have Osa Odighizuwa, but the spot next to him seems a bit ambiguous. CJ West, Gracen Halton, and James Thompson Jr. are on the depth chart, but Thompson hasn’t been practicing. According to Kyle Shanahan, Thompson Jr.’s availability will be determined by how Wednesday’s practice goes for the undrafted free agent. A practice squad call-up is probably in the cards with both injuries. The options include Sebastian Valdez and Kevin Givens. The 49ers are currently in Melbourne, Australia, preparing for the Los Angeles Rams. For Collins, this just sucks on a number of levels, especially days before his season gets started. Last year, when the 49ers were on the road against the Rams, Collins helped stop the Rams from scoring on the 49ers’ own goal line, one of many impact plays the 49ers made to win a game many did not see them winning. Seeing a repeat would have been nice, but it won’t be happening this year. Next man up, I guess.

title: Sean McVay provides updates on Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett against the 49ers
summary: When Aaron Donald signed with the Los Angeles Rams, the assumption was that the 35-year-old who hasn’t played since 2023 would travel across the world in a couple of weeks with little practice under his belt for Week 1. The odds of Donald playing Week 1 were slim once he sat out of training camp. […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - JANUARY 14: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL wild-card playoff football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on January 14, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Aaron Donald signed with the Los Angeles Rams, the assumption was that the 35-year-old who hasn’t played since 2023 would travel across the world in a couple of weeks with little practice under his belt for Week 1. The odds of Donald playing Week 1 were slim once he sat out of training camp. Last week, Sean McVay told reporters that Donald would make the trip with the Rams . That would’ve meant he had fewer than ten practices to play. That changed today after reality hit, as McVay said Donald won’t make the trip with the team. That means whoever is rotating at left guard for the San Francisco 49ers won’t face Donald when he’s at his freshest, still trying to prove to himself he made the correct decision to come out of retirement. That’s a good thing for Brock Purdy, too. Donald will need more time to ramp up before returning. The circumstances aren’t the same, but if George Kittle needed a longer ramp-up, it would’ve made complete sense. Week 1 is already taxing enough without the trip to Australia. The mental and physical toll after a long layoff would make the entire experience exhausting. Add in the recovery from that, and it’s understandable why the Rams elected to give Donald more time. As for Kittle, 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said, “He’s practicing full speed. He’s getting a ton of reps. So, I feel like we’re in good shape.” An extra week of practice might’ve been the difference in Kittle not needing a longer ramp-up period. That’s a good thing for Brock Purdy, too. McVay said Myles Garrett will be ready to go. So, as much of a break as the Niners are getting without Donald, there’s still the reigning Defensive Player of the Year fresh off a 23-sack season. Garrett didn’t do much for the Rams during training camp and the preseason as he dealt with swelling in his left knee. It makes you wonder if they were doing the same thing the 49ers did with Nick Bosa, given the player’s importance. Judging by the video where Garrett is working on hitting more violently , I’d say a lot of this is gamesmanship.
