(Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator told the media the team would “ease them into this thing and get them ready to go” when discussing rookie Romello Height. He acknowledged that it’s a different ball game, playing against the pros as opposed to college players: “Feeling really good where he was going, his growth, his development, but at the same time when you prepare for rookies, you prepare for those guys to be able to be in the lineup, be out of the lineup, what it’s like to play in the National Football League. We all know, and we expect these guys to know from having the experience in college, but it’s different. These are grown men doing grown men things, and we’ll ease them into this thing and get them ready to go.” Morris mentioned that he had a “very high confidence level” regarding Nick Bosa’s availability . It’ll be difficult to ease Bosa in with the current depth chart. Morris must manage Bosa’s playing shape while also not having another early-down defender now that Sam Okuayinonu broke his foot . Morris has a couple of familiar faces who will likely get elevated ahead of Week 1: Ogbo Okoronkwo and Khalid Kareem. Morris said he has a lot of confidence in that duo: “Well, fortunately, two guys that I have a lot of experience with, right? Kareem last year, the last couple of years in Atlanta, and then obviously Ogbo with L.A. Being able to watch those two guys go out there and compete this week and be at a high level, it’s going to be fun. Two guys that I’ve got a lot of confidence in. Two guys that I was fortunate enough to be able to have some say to be able to get here and try to help us. This personnel department does a great job of identifying people that we need when these things happen, so we’re fired up.” Kareem could help offset the loss of Okuayinonu with his 268-pound frame. Okoronkwo, listed at 250 pounds, might not hold up against the Rams’ heavier personnel packages — another reason why it’d be tempting to leave Bosa on the field. ESPN went through predictions for each team. For the 49ers’ biggest concern, unsurprisingly, it was their pass rush: The pass rush. In 2025, San Francisco finished last in the NFL in sacks (20). It brought in defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa , but it’s still fair to wonder if the 49ers have enough on the edge with Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams coming off ACL injuries and rookie Romello Height replacing Bryce Huff. If the pass rush isn’t markedly better, it could be another long season for the defense. There are two questions: Can the 49ers weather the storm until Mykel Williams returns from the PUP ? Once he does return, will he play up to his draft status? The 49ers are relying on two players coming off season-ending lower-body injuries to carry the edge-rushing group. We’ll see if Keion White is a better fit for Morris’s scheme, or how early Height can contribute. Ultimately, it’s about how effective Bosa and Williams will be. If Williams doesn’t look the part, a veteran like Leonard Floyd might be the next player to get a phone call. Floyd turned 34 on Tuesday, and probably shouldn’t be relied upon as an every-down player. He racked up a bunch of pressures last season, but we saw firsthand how empty those can be. If Mykel isn’t who the 49ers think he is, we’ll see a splash trade around the deadline. But if he looks like a first-rounder and can be disruptive, the Niners will hold onto their future draft assets.
author: Kyle Posey

title: The best and worst-case scenario outcomes for the 49ers this season
summary: After a long and controversy-filled offseason, the San Francisco 49ers finally kick off the 2026 season with a date on the other side of the world against the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday night (for us).  Entering Kyle Shanahan’s 10th season, we’ve seen a couple of best-case-scenario seasons (2019 and 2023) and some worst-case-scenario seasons […]
full_text: After a long and controversy-filled offseason, the San Francisco 49ers finally kick off the 2026 season with a date on the other side of the world against the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday night (for us). Entering Kyle Shanahan’s 10th season, we’ve seen a couple of best-case-scenario seasons (2019 and 2023) and some worst-case-scenario seasons (2020 and 2024). So where does 2026 fall on that spectrum? Here is what I see as the best-case and worst-case scenario for the 2026 49ers: Best-case scenario: Win the Super Bowl I mean, this one is pretty obvious. The 49ers are still very much Super Bowl contenders. Now, is the Super Bowl window as open as it was in, say, 2023? No, certainly not, but the door is definitely ajar. The core is largely the same, but some key pieces have changed. Brandon Aiyuk is now Mike Evans. Charvarius Ward is now Deommodore Lenoir. Jake Moody is Eddy Pineiro. Dre Greenlaw is now Dre Greenlaw, and Deebo Samuel is Deebo Samuel. The talent might not be as great as it was in 2023, especially on the defensive side as the ball, but it is a more experienced team and there’s still plenty of talent. The team as constructed is good enough to be a Super Bowl contender,, but what’s around them could prevent a February trip to SoFi Stadium. When the 49ers last went to the Super Bowl after the 2023 season, they won the NFC West with 12 wins. Last season, 12 wins was good enough for a third-place finish for San Francisco, and with how the Rams and Seahawks are looking, that could be the case again in 2026 in the division. The path to the playoffs will be much more daunting this season than it was in 2023. And even if the 49ers make the playoffs, the postseason path will be tough. Maybe the Seahawks or Rams will be on that road, but look around the NFC; there are plenty of good teams that could upend the 49ers’ Super Bowl hopes. But a Super Bowl championship isn’t out of the realm of possibilities for this 49ers team. There is talent in the NFC, and the path will be difficult like it always is, but the talent is there, and hoisting the Lombardi at the end of the season is realistic. Worst-case scenario: everything goes to plan but fall short of a Lombardi Trophy The easy worst-case scenario is everybody gets hurt, and the 49ers miss the playoffs. But we have seen that before in 2018, 2020, and 2024. Injuries create an excuse for struggles everybody would understand, even after a 2025 season when the 49ers overcame injuries and made a postseason run. A scenario where the 49ers can keep a healthy roster but not win a Super Bowl would create more questions than answers. The first set of questions would surround Kyle Shanahan and his ability to win “the big one.” Shanahan was already heavily criticized before signing on with the 49ers, becoming the first offensive coordinator to be blamed for his defense blowing a 25-point third-quarter lead. Since he’s taken over the 49ers, Shanahan has certainly steered the boat in the correct direction, but still hasn’t been able to get to the final destination, losing two NFC Championship Games and two Super Bowls. A third loss of either would put Shanahan in the “Andy Reid with the Eagles” territory. Now, his tenure is slightly shorter than Reid’s with the Eagles (2026 will be Shanahan’s 10th season with the 49ers; Reid was let go from the Eagles after his 14th season), and a playoff appearance without a Super Bowl win wouldn’t put Shanahan on the hot seat right away; the conversations about Shanahan being the “right guy” will only get louder. After four straight years without winning a playoff game, Reid was let go by the Eagles before finding the job (and quarterback) with the Chiefs to finally get over that hump. And Reid was consistent with the Eagles, making the playoffs in nine of his 14 years. But he was also 0-4 in the NFC Championship Game and 0-1 in the Super Bowl with the Eagles, before the Eagles moved on and won two Super Bowls over the next 12 years. Maybe the 49ers will be in the same sort of conversations with Shanahan if this worst-case scenario comes to fruition. Maybe they won’t. But a deep playoff run with a healthy team without a Super Bowl title won’t be a great look for Shanahan, who already has a perception around him in those types of games.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: Klay Kubiak discusses the 49ers left guard competition and who will play
summary: San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak addressed the media, where he spoke about what’s going on at left guard. Kubiak acknowledged the “very difficult challenge” it takes to prepare for Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, but said the players on the other side of the ball won’t determine which player plays: “I don’t think […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JUNE 03: Carver Willis #74 of the San Francisco 49ers holds a pad during a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on June 3, 2026 in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak addressed the media, where he spoke about what’s going on at left guard. Kubiak acknowledged the “very difficult challenge” it takes to prepare for Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, but said the players on the other side of the ball won’t determine which player plays: “I don’t think so. I think you play who you feel most comfortable with. I think I said this a few weeks ago, though; it’s like, when you look at guard, there’s never any reason why guys can’t rotate as well. I mean, multiple guys can play in the game, and we’ll see how the game goes with who we start and kind of how we want to do the rotation. But you’ve got to get a feel for how the game’s going and how guys are handling stuff. So, nothing’s settled, nothing’s determined right now. It’s not going to be based on experience necessarily. We’re going to go with who we think should start based on who’s had the best camp and kind of where they’re at, and see how the game goes.” Kubiak said he didn’t know if the 49ers would rotate players during the game, saying, “We’re going to have multiple guys up and multiple guys ready to go. So, whether they rotate or not, that’ll be determined as the game goes.” The options include Carver Willis, Connor Colby, and maybe Jarrett Patterson. Realistically, Patterson is Jake Brendel’s backup, and Colby rotates if Willis looks like he’s being overwhelmed. It’s not an easy situation if you’re the 49ers. Whether it’s Willis or Colby, they’re both inexperienced and need to learn on the fly. When you haven’t played, mistakes are inevitable. The team can help Willis out by sliding protections a specific way or putting more on Brendel’s plate, so Willis is the lineman who is free in obvious passing situations. But there’s only so much you can do to hide your left guard. For the most part, he’s going to have to play and hold his own in 1-on-1 situations. Willis and Colby are above-average athletes. Any perceived struggles won’t happen when they’re on the move. Where they might find themselves in trouble his holding up against power or length. We’ll find out in a little more than 48 hours if Willis is up to the task or if the Niners are content with playing musical chairs at left guard once again.

title: ESPN simulation predicts the 49ers will return to the top of the NFC West
summary: Each year, ESPN uses its Football Power Index, which includes several metrics and projections, to simulate and predict outcomes. The FPI for the 49ers entering 2026 is strong, placing them as the fifth-best team ahead of Week 1. Those same projections give the 49ers a 64% chance of making the playoffs and finishing with 10 […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers looks on while coaching his team against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second quarter preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each year, ESPN uses its Football Power Index, which includes several metrics and projections, to simulate and predict outcomes. The FPI for the 49ers entering 2026 is strong, placing them as the fifth-best team ahead of Week 1. Those same projections give the 49ers a 64% chance of making the playoffs and finishing with 10 wins — both good enough for the seventh-highest in the NFL. Seth Walder is the author of these. He used nearly 10,000 simulations. It’s unclear why Walder chose the simulation he did for this exercise, but the one Walder provided had the 49ers tied with the Detroit Lions with an NFL-best 13-4 record. The Niners held the tiebreaker over the Lions, so not only did they defeat the big bad Rams and the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks out for the NFC West title, but Kyle Shanahan’s squad outdid everyone to earn a much-needed bye and a No. 1 seed. Each of those teams had identical records heading into the season into the final stretch of the regular season: Through 12 weeks, the Seahawks, 49ers and Rams were each 9-2 — with only three of those six combined losses coming to teams outside the division! Fast forward to Week 18, with the 49ers and Seahawks entering their finales tied at 12-4 and the Rams one game back at 11-5. But the Rams came out firing in Week 18, blowing out the Seahawks 37-8. The 49ers destroyed the last-place Cardinals 30-3, securing not only the division but also the No. 1 seed in the NFC. Seattle and Los Angeles had to settle for the No. 5 and No. 6 seeds, respectively. So that had the 49ers feeling good entering the playoffs. Was this the year Kyle Shanahan and San Francisco would get over the Super Bowl hump? Here’s how the Wild Card round went: Lions 27, Packers 24 Rams 27, Buccaneers 24 Cowboys 31, Seahawks 19 Jared Goff gets the best of Jordan Love. Matthew Stafford outscores Baker Mayfield, while Dak Prescott tears up the Seahawks defense. That sets up a Divisional Round matchup between Detroit and Dallas, while the Rams travel north to Levi’s Stadium: Rams 24, 49ers 21 Lions 27, Cowboys 20 San Francisco swept the first two, but this one became the Myles Garrett game. The superstar pass rusher delivered 2.5 sacks and deflected a pass that was intercepted. It was just enough, as the Rams prevailed over Brock Purdy and the 49ers 24-21 to advance to the NFC Championship Game. But the superteam couldn’t finish the job. As good as the Rams were, they fell in the NFC title game for a second consecutive season, this time to the Lions. Because although Garrett was great in the divisional round, a different pass rusher was better all year long and in the NFC Championship Game. Aidan Hutchinson , who would be awarded Defensive Player of the Year before the Super Bowl, wreaked havoc on the Rams’ offense. Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown connected for two touchdowns to lead Detroit to a 20-17 victory and another near miss for Los Angeles. Losing to the Rams in another NFC Championship would be heartbreaking for the 49ers, especially if they earned home-field advantage after sweeping Sean McVay during the regular season. My NFC Championship prediction is the Cowboys and the 49ers. Neither gets out of the Divisional Round in this simulation. It’s not far-fetched to think these could be the top four teams in the NFC come January. I think the Seahawks take a step back, while the Eagles can’t get out of their own way. We’ll believe in the NFC South once they give us a reason to. The 49ers, Cowboys, Rams, and Lions have offensive firepower and defensive playmakers. It’ll come down to the battle of attrition. Last year, the injury bug couldn’t stay away from Detroit or San Francisco, while Los Angeles was among the healthiest teams in the NFL. We’ll see which teams are fortunate enough to benefit from injury luck this season.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Which trends will continue or change for the 49ers in 2026?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are preparing to kick off the NFL season Thursday night in Australia against their NFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Rams. The teams split meetings last season, with the 49ers winning in SoFi Stadium and the Rams returning the favor with a convincing win at Levi’s Stadium. While both teams will […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers are preparing to kick off the NFL season Thursday night in Australia against their NFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Rams. The teams split meetings last season, with the 49ers winning in SoFi Stadium and the Rams returning the favor with a convincing win at Levi’s Stadium. While both teams will remain familiar, they won’t be the same in 2025, as both Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay will add new wrinkles to their offenses. With that in mind, let’s look at some statistical and personnel trends that should continue to change for the 2026 season. 49ers rushing success rate Christian McCaffrey was incredible in 2025. With a target rate of 23.5%, the running back was targeted more than CeeDee Lamb, Ladd McConkey, and Michael Pittman. So much of McCaffrey’s production comes from Shanahan’s ability to create space for McCaffrey and mismatches in the passing game. However, on the flip side, the 49ers ranked 16th in the NFL with a 42.4% success rate on rushing plays. Middle of the pack has never been where the 49ers offense sits, but there were multiple reasons for the down season on the ground. McCaffrey, in particular, ranked 37th in the NFL in EPA/rush with his 0.97 average yards before contact, coming in at 46th in the league. On outside zone runs, McCaffrey’s yards-before-contact number falls to 0.63. The 49ers finish 8th in the NFL in EPA/play because of the fifth-highest EPA/pass in the league at 0.12. This number has to go up, and if it does, the offense will be burning bright all season. 21 personnel groupings The 49ers, by far, lead the NFL in 21 personnel with a league-high 393 snaps from 21, which is a 36.32% rate. Only the Baltimore Ravens compete with the 49ers, with a 28.77 EPA out of 21 personnel, second to the 49ers’ 29.99 EPA. This trend is sure to continue while fullback Kyle Juszczyk is on the roster. The 49ers use the veteran fullback to identify coverages and to create lanes as a blocker in the running game. However, the 49ers finished tenth with an -0.02 EPA/rush from 21 personnel. The bump is from the 0.18 EPA/pass, and still the 49ers finished with the highest total EPA from 21 personnel. While the NFL is shifting to lighter backfields, the trend of McCaffrey and Juice on the field isn’t going anywhere. Interception rate Look, this may seem like cherry-picking or taking a simple idea and running with it, but 49ers quarterbacks finished 27th with an interception rate of 2.79%. Funny enough, the Seattle Seahawks had a higher interception rate at 3.12%, but when your defense is dominant and can bail you out, the difference is clear. The 49ers defense will improve from last year, simply because it’s almost impossible to be worse in certain metrics, but turning the football and putting pressure on this defense isn’t the optimal approach. We love when Brock Purdy takes calculated risks, but the biggest improvement needed in his game is limiting interceptions and turnovers overall. You don’t want to curb his playmaking, but living to play another down is definitely a place for Purdy to raise his game.

title: BREAKING: Buccaneers, Mayfield agree to 3-year extension
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers came to terms with QB Baker Mayfield on a 3-year contract extension Monday, solidifying the 31-year-old’s place as the team’s franchise signal caller for this season and beyond. ESPN’s Adam Schefter initially reported on the deal, with Ian Rapoport adding the baseline figures stand at $165 million total — working out […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers throws a pass prior to a preseason NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers came to terms with QB Baker Mayfield on a 3-year contract extension Monday, solidifying the 31-year-old’s place as the team’s franchise signal caller for this season and beyond. ESPN’s Adam Schefter initially reported on the deal, with Ian Rapoport adding the baseline figures stand at $165 million total — working out to about $55 million per year. ESPN sources: two-time Pro-Bowl selection Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers reached agreement today on a three-year contract extension that will prevent the quarterback from becoming a free agent after this season, per me and @RapSheet . Mayfield had broken off talks as camp… pic.twitter.com/twurowrOyz — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 8, 2026 It stands as a stark reversal from the off-season, when several reports asserted that Mayfield’s contingent and the team were far apart on talks. This disagreement came to a head at the beginning of training camp, when the quarterback called initial offers from the team “disrespectful” and made clear that negotiations were closed until after the season, when Mayfield was due to be a free agent. Circumstances clearly changed in the last few weeks, resulting in what is now the richest contract in Buccaneers history for the 9th year veteran. Details on structure have not yet been revealed, but his new $55 million per year average trails only Dak Prescott and Patrick Mahomes now, matching Matthew Stafford, Trevor Lawrence, Jordan Love, Josh Allen, and Joe Burrow. Mayfield was set to play out the final year of a 3-year, $100 million extension, which he built of his 1-year, $4 million prove-it deal back in 2023. Mayfield has, in large, been a good-to-very good passer and leader for Tampa Bay. In 51 starts, Mayfield has amassed 12,237 passing yards, 95 passing touchdowns (top 5 in the NFL), and 37 interceptions to go along with some trademark scrambles that highlight 923 yards rushing and 5 additional scores. He looked off to an extremely hot start in 2025 before injuries and general team dysfunction led to a disappointing overall campaign, but this extension signals that he and the team are confident in a rebound with a refreshed approach. The Buccaneers and Mayfield kick off their 2026 campaign Sunday on the road against the Cincinnati Bengals at 1 p.m.

title: Titans’ 1st impression vs. the Jets will say a lot
summary: Many reporters on the Tennessee Titans beat are calling Sunday’s Week 1 matchup versus the New York Jets a “must-win” opener. That is obviously ridiculous on the surface, but there’s some merit to those claims given the context. No team’s season was ever decided in Week 1, but these Titans are attempting to recapture this […]
full_text: (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Many reporters on the Tennessee Titans beat are calling Sunday’s Week 1 matchup versus the New York Jets a “must-win” opener . That is obviously ridiculous on the surface, but there’s some merit to those claims given the context. No team’s season was ever decided in Week 1, but these Titans are attempting to recapture this fanbase’s trust. The Titans endured consecutive 3-14 seasons in 2024 and 2025. This small-market fanbase hasn’t exactly been forgiving (understandably so). Many late-season games at Nissan Stadium have recently been played in front of meager crowds. The Titans underwent significant changes this offseason, both on and off the field. While general manager Mike Borgonzi continued rebuilding the roster, a rebranding also occurred. The Titans have three new uniforms, a new logo, and are preparing to open a new stadium in 2027. For Titans fans to maintain excitement over all the off-field developments, the on-field product needs to warrant it. The Jets have been considered a laughing stock of the NFL (the Titans, too). If Tennessee loses in Week 1 to the Jets, it wouldn’t be shocking if large portions of this fanbase snickered, said “same ole Titans,” before finding other ways to fill their Sundays. There’s also the revenge element. Head coach Robert Saleh used to coach these Jets. John Franklin-Myers, Jermaine Johnson II, Tony Adams, Solomon Thomas, and Jacob Martin are among those who played for them. Everyone involved wants to prove they’ve moved onto bigger and better things, with Saleh proving he was never the problem. Realistically, the Titans don’t need to qualify for the playoffs to convince this fanbase they’re on the right track. Fielding a competitive squad that doubles their 2024/2025 win total by finishing 6-11 would highlight direction and growth. Beginning the campaign by beating the Jets would be considered a good-faith gesture.

(Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) Well, this is not the start to week one the Tennessee Titans were hoping for. It came out yesterday that LB Cedric Gray suffered a concussion in a UTV accident. The good news here is that the injury wasn’t more serious than it was. The bad news is that Gray is now in concussion protocol. We know that no two concussions are the same. There is a chance that Gray is able to make it through the protocol in time to play on Sunday against the New York Jets, but that seems unlikely. The most likely scenario is that they have to try to win this game without Gray on the field. Gray emerged as a really good player for the Titans last season. He had 164 total tackles in 16 games last season in his second year with the Titans. He’s a big key for the success of the defense in 2026. Hopefully, he won’t be off the field for very long.

title: Who will lead the Titans in receiving in Week 1?
summary: The Tennessee Titans will make their 2026 NFL season debut by hosting the New York Jets at Nissan Stadium in Week 1 this Sunday. There’s so much to learn about these new-look Titans. Head coach Robert Saleh and the team’s new coordinators Brian Daboll and Gus Bradley will officially make their debuts. The most important […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Carnell Tate #14 of the Tennessee Titans looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL preseason game against the Chicago Bears at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans will make their 2026 NFL season debut by hosting the New York Jets at Nissan Stadium in Week 1 this Sunday. There’s so much to learn about these new-look Titans. Head coach Robert Saleh and the team’s new coordinators Brian Daboll and Gus Bradley will officially make their debuts. The most important aspect of the Titans’ 2026 campaign is the development of sophomore quarterback Cam Ward. Coach Daboll is being tasked with overseeing his ascension. The Titans’ new-look passing game will finally be unveiled versus the Jets. This is a deep receiving core in Tennessee. Carnell Tate was drafted at fourth overall to grow alongside Ward. Wan’Dale Robinson was signed in free agency for his ability to be a high-volume, reliable weapon. Calvin Ridley is also back, and Elic Ayomanor had an excellent training camp. The Titans are four-deep at receiver. Who do you think will lead the Titans in receiving in Week 1? It’s an interesting question. Fans would love to see Tate explode after he failed to record a single preseason catch. Robinson should be Ward’s most reliable weapon, possibly leading the Titans in targets. Ridley is a big-play threat who once played in Daboll’s offense at Alabama. Running backs and tight ends should also be heavily involved in the Titans’ passing attack. Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears, Gunnar Helm, and Daniel Bellinger will play notable roles in Daboll’s offense. Ward will be tasked with spreading the ball around to a plethora of players. The Titans should also establish the run via Pollard and Spears. This Titans-Jets rematch is littered with revenge storylines. From Saleh to John Franklin-Myers, Jacob Martin, Jermaine Johnson, Solomon Thomas, and Tony Adams, Tennessee is loaded with former Jets players. Who leads the Titans’ new-look passing attack in receiving is another question.

The predictions have more than the usual number of predictions that the Commanders will win the division, the NFC championship, and even the Super Bowl, and Washington players are heavily represented in predictions of Comeback Player of the Year, Offensive Player of the Year, Defensive Rookie of the Year, and League MVP. There’s nothing wrong with a bit of rooting for the home team — and, who knows? You may be right. I’ll summarize the broad strokes below, but if you want to hold yourself or your Hogs Haven nemesis accountable for his or her preseason optimism or pessimism, bookmark this link where 51 brave souls put their reputations on the line by signing their (user)names to predictions written in blood before the first snap of the 2026 season. The NFC East The Eagles were the most popular pick here, with 43% of the vote, but the Cowboys were surprisingly strong at 35%. It says something that 78% of readers on Hogs Haven picked Dallas or Philly to win the division. I’m not sure what it says, but something, anyway. About 20% of participants stayed true to the burgundy & gold, which is a bit less than I might’ve expected on a site full of passionate fans, but far beyond the national perception of Washington’s chances this year. Most popular picks for division champs in the 7 other divisions: When it comes to the AFC, where passions may not run as high, only 7 teams got more than 20% of the vote for regular season champs across the 8 divisions, and one team in each division got a clear majority of the vote. In the NFC, the Rams are the clear favorite in the West; the Bucs only slightly less so in the South, but the picture in the NFC North is muddled, with the only agreement being that the Vikings won’t be in contention. NFC NFC West – Rams (92%) NFC South – Buccaneers (64%), Saints (21%) NFC North – Lions (48%), Bears (29%), Packers (21%) AFC AFC East – Bills (87%) AFC North – Ravens (67%), Bengals (29%) AFC South – Texans (64%), Jaguars (27%) AFC West – Broncos (52%), Chiefs (31%), Wildcard Teams Voting for the AFC was consistent, with none of the top-3 teams in the wildcard vote showing up as divisional champs. Not surprisingly, the only division where things are a bit non-rational in this prediction exercise is the NFC East. The Eagles, who got the most votes for division champion (but not a majority) got picked as a wildcard team by pretty much everyone who didn’t pick them as division champs. Obviously, Philly can’t be both division champ and a wildcard team, so… If we assign the NFC East championship to the Eagles, then these results would put Washington into the playoffs as a wildcard team If we assume the Eagles get into the playoffs as a wildcard team, then the implication is that the Cowboys would be the division champs and the Commanders would be out of the playoffs. For my projected playoff seedings below (based on % of vote received), I assumed the scenario where the Eagles win the division, the Commanders qualify as a wildcard team, and the Cowboys watch the playoffs from their sofas. NFC Seahawks 73% Eagles 40% Bears 31% Commanders 29% 49ers 29% Lions 27% AFC Patriots 48% Chiefs 48% Chargers 44% Ravens 29% Bengals 29% Broncos 23% Based on these results, playoff seedings would be: Conference Champions There’s a lot of optimism being shown here by about 1 in 5 Hogs Haven readers. The consensus picks of Rams-Bills seem to be in line with national expectations and betting odds. NFC – Rams (60%), Commanders (19%) AFC – Bills (54%), Ravens (17%) Super Bowl Champions Rams 41% Bills 23% Commanders 15% Again, some real die-hard fans of the burgundy & gold are carrying the banner here. Also, I suspect that the Rams getting something like 2:1 odds (or is it 1:2?) of beating Buffalo in February is not far astray from national sentiment. First pick in the 2027 Draft Dolphins 40% Cardinals 25% Jets 14% Browns 8% This list appears to be close to the consensus of the 4 worst teams in the NFL as we approach the start of the season, which probably guarantees that at least one of them will make the playoffs. Awards I’ve listed the most popular pick in each category, except OPOY, where Josh Allen received 1 more vote than Jahmyr Gibbs. There was a clear favorite in every other prediction (though that does not mean a majority, just a clear separation from the #2 vote-getter). Comeback Player of the Year Jayden Daniels Coach of the Year Sean McVay Offensive Rookie of the Year Jeremiyah Love Defensive Rookie of the Year Sonny Styles Offensive Player of the Year Josh Allen Jahmyr Gibbs Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett League MVP Josh Allen Predict the Commanders regular season record 10-7 (21%) 8-9 (14%) 5-12 (14%) 7-10 (12%) 6-11 (10%) 9-8 (10%) These 6 outcomes accounted for 81% of the vote. You can see that, among these predictions, there are a lot more people expecting a losing record than a winning one. Count me among the optimists. I predicted 9-8 with a playoff win. title: Can Washington Commanders survive, thrive with Nick Allegretti at center?
summary: With the season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles less than a week away, the angst about the Commanders’ starting center position has reached obsessional levels.  The level of concern about a single roster position may have even surpassed the anxiety about the offensive tackle situation which gripped the fanbase ahead of the 2024 season. And […]
full_text: With the season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles less than a week away, the angst about the Commanders’ starting center position has reached obsessional levels. The level of concern about a single roster position may have even surpassed the anxiety about the offensive tackle situation which gripped the fanbase ahead of the 2024 season. And just look how that turned out. The makeshift duo of rookie third-round pick Brandon Coleman and fringe starter/reliable backup Andrew Wylie, whom many predicted would get the Commanders rookie quarterback killed, actually held up well enough for Jayden Daniels to have the best rookie debut of any QB in the modern era, leading the Commanders to within one game of the Super Bowl. The truth is nearly every NFL team has a few weak links on the roster, even those that make it to the Super Bowl. Sometimes that is the result of attrition through the season, with backups replacing starters. And in other cases, it is the result of situations like the Commanders found themselves in this offseason, when luck didn’t go their way in free agency or the draft. To illustrate what I mean, and hopefully put the Commanders’ center situation in perspective, I had a look at the starting offensive lines of teams that played in the Super Bowl over the past six NFL seasons. After missing out on Tyler Linderbaum in free agency, and failing to find value at center in the draft until Day 3, the Commanders are set to face the Eagles on opening day with Nick Allegretti snapping to Jayden Daniels. Allegretti is no All-Pro, but is he really bad enough to single-handedly prevent his team from making it to the playoffs? To answer that question, we’ll take a tour of the weakest links along the interior offensive lines of the last 12 Super Bowl teams. But before we do, let’s take a close-up look at the player at the center of attention. The Next Man Up G/C Nick Allegretti, 8 th year, age 30 6’ 4” | 310 lbs | 32.25” arms | RAS: 7.6 | 2026 cap number: $3.84 million 2025 Stats: 16 games | 4 starts | 260 snaps | 1 sack | 2 QB hits | 8 total pressures | 5.7% pressure rate | 45.1 run block grade | 3 penalties Allegretti has been a career backup with occasional stints as a starter, playing his first five seasons with the Chiefs and his last two with the Commanders. In his second season with the Chiefs, he started nine games at left guard, including two playoff games and Super Bowl LV. In 2024, he started all 17 regular season games and three playoff games for the Commanders at left guard. Throughout his career, Allegretti has played predominantly at left guard, but has also started three games at center and four at right guard. The Commanders like Allegretti’s toughness, reliability, intelligence and ability to play all three positions on the interior. Performance-wise, he is a replacement-level player at this point in his career, meaning that he is about what you’d expect from a veteran free agent on an inexpensive contract. Allegretti’s 5.7% pressure rate allowed in pass protection in just four starts in 2025 would have placed him at the 21 st percentile of starting iOL (approximated by the 96 centers and guards with the highest snap counts), if he had maintained that rate for a full season. Median for “starting” iOL was 4.6%. However, that is a very small sample to draw conclusions from blocking metrics, which are subject to considerable game-to-game variability. I would usually like to have at least twice as many games played. The figures from his most recent full season starting might be more representative of his abilities. In 2024 he allowed a pressure rate of 4.99%, which is at the 40 th percentile using last season’s figures. That year he allowed three sacks and one QB hit in 650 true pass blocking snaps. Unless he’s had a dramatic decline at age 30, he is probably somewhere between a below average starter and a bottom 20% starter in pass protection. Allegretti’s run blocking grades peaked at 71.3 in his sophomore season and have held steady in the low 60’s through 2024, before cratering to 45.1 last season. That might indicate a sudden drop off, but is more likely an artifact of having only played four games. His 63.9 run blocking grade from 20 games in 2024 ranked 57 th among the 96 most active iOL (41 st percentile). Unless he really fell off the cliff in 2025, his run blocking is probably a little below average for a staring interior offensive lineman. Overall, Allegretti’s performance in his most recent full season profiles in the below-average starting range. The numbers from 2025 are much worse. But it is dangerous to draw conclusions from a 4 game sample due to game to game variability. Comparable or Worse iOL Who Have Started in Super Bowls Now that we have a handle on the Commanders’ 2026 starting center, let’s see how he stacks up against the weakest links on the interior offensive lines of Super Bowl teams over the past 6 NFL seasons. Super Bowl LIX (2025) – Seattle Seahawks 29, New England Patriots 13 RG Anthony Bradford, Seahawks 6’ 4” | 335 lbs | 33.5” arms | RAS 9.78 | 3 rd year | age 24 2025 Stats: 20 starts | 1,037 snaps | 3 sacks | 5 QB hits | 28 total pressures | 6.1% pressure rate | 55.4 run block grade | 4 penalties I’ll kick this off with the player who inspired this article. Some Seahawks fans believe that their Super Bowl champion right guard is the worst player in football. Bradford started all 20 games at RG for the Seahawks last season and earned a Super Bowl ring in the blowout victory over the Patriots. His performance in the big game was not wonderful, with three QB hurries allowed and a pressure rate of 7.5%. But it was hardly his worst game of the season. Bradford is a physically imposing blocker with freakish athleticism, who has become legendary on the internet for his frequent mental gaffes and lapses of awareness. Let’s take a look at some of his work: TRENDING: #SEAHAWKS GUARD ANTHONY BRADFORD CONTINUES TO GO VIRAL EVERY WEEK. Bradford is one of the worst players in the league. Every week, Bradford figures out a way to get worse — it is truly a spectacle to watch. pic.twitter.com/wtLwm7qNME https://t.co/zXfJRUwqNr — MLFootball (@MLFootball) December 15, 2025 In an otherwise great season for the Seahawks, he was the one player who managed to stand out for the wrong reasons. His 6.1% pressure rate in pass protection ranked 83 rd out of 96 starting iOL in 2025. His numbers were worse than Allegretti’s last season and well below Allegretti’s level in 2024. Bradford’s 2025 run blocking grade ranked 74 th out of 96 iOL (23 rd percentile). The frustrating thing for Seahawks fans is that Bradford is wildly inconsistent. Plays where he is completely lost or whiffs are interspersed with dominant blocking efforts. Overall, his play is worse than Allegretti’s, but not bad enough to keep the Seahawks from taking home the Lombardi. Super Bowl LIX (2024) – Philadelphia Eagles 40, Kansas City Chiefs 22 LG Mike Caliendo, Chiefs 6’4” | 301 lbs | 30.9” arms | RAS 6.91 | 3 rd year | age 27 2024 Stats: 20 games | 6 starts | 410 snaps | 2 sacks | 3 QB hits | 15 total pressures | 6.2% pressure rate | 45.6 run block grade | 1 penalty Caliendo is a backup guard for the Chiefs. He got an opportunity to start 6 games at LG late in the regular season and the playoffs, when Andy Reid moved starting LG Joe Thuney to LT to replace struggling starter Wanya Morris. His numbers in pass protection and run blocking are even worse than Bradford’s and Allegretti’s. Nevertheless, the Chiefs won three regular season games and two playoff games with Caliendo starting at left guard. Super Bowl LVIII (2023) – Kansas City Chiefs 25, San Francisco 49ers 22 LG Nick Allegretti, Chiefs 2023 Stats: 21 games | 3 starts | 253 snaps | 2 sacks | 1 QB hit | 12 total pressures | 7.8% pressure rate | 59.6 run block grade | 1 penalty The weakest link on the Super Bowl LVIII champions’ iOL was none other than the man himself, Nick Allegretti. He was…

full_text: The Washington Commanders have released their first unofficial depth chart of the 2026 regular season. They released their intial (and unofficial) one before the first preseason game, but this is the first one released after the 53-man roster cut. There aren’t many surprises on the document, with some clarity provided at the cornerback spot. Mike Sainristil and Amik Roberson are listed as first-teamers, with Rasul Douglas and Fabian Moreau behind them. There isn’t a slot cornerback position listed, so we’re unsure of who would play inside within the sub packages. Odds seem great that Roberton or Sainristil would move into the slot and Douglas would play on the outside. The Commanders could also use safeties Tyler Owens or Quan Martin in that spot. Also confirming what we already knew, Frankie Luvu is a starting off-the-ball linebacker with rookie Sonny Styles and Leo Chenal’s in reserve. The Commanders depth chart lists three receiver spots — they’ll play a ton with two and multiple tight ends — and Treylon Burks was considered the third starting receiver over Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown. title: NFL Power Rankings: Commanders have lots of questions to answer in Year 3
summary: The Washington Commanders are entering a critical offseason in 2026, and needed an infusion of youth, talent, and some luck as they try to bounce back from a 5-12 season. The second year of Adam Peters’ “recalibration” of the roster started with sky-high expectations after an NFC Championship Game appearance the year before. A Terry […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 10: Head coach Dan Quinn of the Washington Commanders talks to Jayden Daniels #5 against the New York Jets in the first half of the preseason game against at MetLife Stadium on August 10, 2024 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets defeated the Commanders 20-17. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders are entering a critical offseason in 2026, and needed an infusion of youth, talent, and some luck as they try to bounce back from a 5-12 season. The second year of Adam Peters’ “recalibration” of the roster started with sky-high expectations after an NFC Championship Game appearance the year before. A Terry McLaurin hold-in, along with injuries to multiple starters made for a miserable season. Now we’re ready to see what Year 3 brings to Washington. The Commanders used free agency to make massive changes to the defense, along with firing defensive coordinator Joe Whitt Jr, and replacing him with Daronte Jones. That focus on defense continued with their first pick in this year’s draft, Ohio State LB Sonny Styles. Washington also brought in CB Amik Robertson, DL Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, Charles Omenihu, and Tim Settle, along with LB Leo Chenal. Washington also made major changes on the offensive side of the ball. There were reportedly issues with former offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury’s use of personnel/playcalling last season, which was amplified by injuries to major players like Jayden Daniels and Terry McLaurin. David Blough took over the reigns from his former boss, and is making significant changes to the offense, and helping to mold Daniels into a more complete NFL QB. He also got some help in free agency with players like TE Chig Okonkwo and RB Rachaad White. Adam Peters used Washington’s second pick in the draft(3rd round) on WR Antonio Williams. The Laremy Tunsil injury and questions at C and LG have power rankers worried about the health and well-being of Jayden Daniels as he returns from an injury-filled season. Can Nick Allegretti keep the pocket clean for Daniels as he works under center more, or will he be forced to scramble early and often? The Commanders start the season with low expectations and a tough early schedule. Washington ranks as high as #18 with high praise for this year’s free agency and draft classes. The other side of the spectrum has them ranked as low as #31, and some dark times in Washington. Winning the Super Bowl odds : +7,000 To Make the Playoffs: Make +265, Miss -330 Jayden Daniels MVP Odds: +3,000 Jayden Daniels Comeback Player of the Year Odds: +1,000 Washington Commanders Win Total O/U: Over 7.5( +105 ), Under 7.5(-125) High: 18 Low: 31 Average: 23.7 #18 Sports Illustrated (Orr) I see Washington as a possible 10-game winner. Some analysts I respect have this team finishing dead last in the NFC East. It’s all on the table, especially with large-scale changes at the coordinator positions and a ton of new everyday starters. Jayden Daniels’s health remains the biggest x-factor, though. In a David Blough system, we’ll see him even more protected, we’ll see play-action even more weaponized and—possibly—the full extent of his powers unleashed. There’s a reason I nearly arm wrestled my fantasy comanager for the right to draft Terry McLaurin this year. #20 ESPN Milestone to watch: Quarterback Jayden Daniels setting a franchise record for single-season TD passes. The only time a Washington quarterback threw for more than 30 touchdowns was Sonny Jurgensen in 1969 (31). Daniels threw for 25 in his rookie season, and the Commanders have a stronger receiving corps than last season with Terry McLaurin , Stefon Diggs and promising rookie Antonio Williams . Daniels also has looked ultra-sharp in David Blough’s new offense in practices. If Daniels stays healthy — and the offensive line without Laremy Tunsil can protect him — he can top Jurgensen. — John Keim #21 Sporting News (Iyer) The Commanders haven’t had the best offseason with Jayden Daniels and his personnel losses while Dan Quinn is still trying to assemble the right defensive pieces on an older winning team. Their vibes are more last-place, with the Giants being more competitive. NFL Trade Rumors (Woodie) It was a banner first year for QB Jayden Daniels. Not so much last year. As it stands, while the roster is better than it was a year ago, there are still major questions on the offensive line and the defense as a whole. I trust Daniels, as long as he can stay healthy, and Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs should be a great receiver duo. But can the Commanders protect Daniels or run the football? And can the defense stop anyone? The answers to those questions will define Washington’s season. Team Rankings #22 Yahoo Sports (Schwab) No preseason injury was more damaging than the Commanders losing left tackle Laremy Tunsil for all or most of the season. That will affect the entire offense, which didn’t add much in the offseason . This is not how Jayden Daniels wanted to start his third season. Pro Football Focus (Locker) Odds to make playoffs: 28% Odds to win Super Bowl: 1% The Commanders’ pixie dust ran out in 2025, with injuries to Jayden Daniels and a struggling defense culminating in a 5-12 finish. Washington welcomes in two new coordinators on each side of the ball as well as a bevy of fresh faces like Stefon Diggs , Sonny Styles, Leo Chenal and Odafe Oweh . Daniels’ health, his ability to be protected without Laremy Tunsil and the team’s defensive efficacy will define whether or not Dan Quinn’s bunch can return to the postseason. FTN Fantasy (Kelley) 2024 showed the ceiling of the Jayden Daniels experience. 2025 showed the floor. We’ll see what 2026 can offer. #23 The Athletic (Graff/Kendall) Mock’s projected win total: 7.6 The loss of Laremy Tunsil is big, especially for protecting an injury-prone quarterback. And a joint practice against the Ravens went terribly for the Commanders’ O-line and the offense in general. They signed D.J. Humphries and Stefon Diggs in August, but this team will go as far as Jayden Daniels takes it. And after training camp, it doesn’t seem like it’s going very far. Sharp Football Analysis (Summerlin) They added Stefon Diggs , and every snippet about how the Commanders plan to run their offense this season has been promising. The issue is the offensive line might not cooperate with Laremy Tunsil expected to miss most of the season. The Score The Commanders’ offense has weapons, but Jayden Daniels will have a tough time getting the ball to them after losing star left tackle Laremy Tunsil to a major injury in training camp. Unless Washington can figure out how to keep the third-year quarterback upright and healthy, it’ll be another long season. SB Nation But there are questions with each team. Will the Commanders offensive line be as bad as reports out of training camp sound? Windy City Gridiron (Leming) 2026 Question To Answer: Who are the Commanders? The team that went to the NFC Championship Game or the 5-12 group who struggled last season. Jayden Daniels’ health and play style might dictate that answer. Heading into last season, many had Daniels as a strong MVP candidate heading into Year 2. Like Houston, following up a historic rookie year is no easy feat. Their “true self” is probably somewhere in the middle of the last two seasons, but Daniels must stay healthy and show tangible growth in David Blough’s offense. That’s a tough ask for a first-year coordinator with minimal coaching experience. #24 Walter Football The Redskins appeared to improve their defense by drafting Sonny Styles and adding a couple of other pieces, including Odafe Oweh, Leo Chenal, and Amik Robertson. Styles, however, has been brutal in training camp and the preseason. Nevertheless, the important thing is Jayden Daniels’ health. If Daniels can remain on the field for most of 2026, the Redskins will have a good chance of making a playoff run, but that might be a tough task…

title: Future Hogs – Week 1: College football players who could help the Commanders
summary: The first week of the college football season is in the books, so it’s time for Future Hogs. This is a series of articles during the college football season that looks at draft-eligible players that could improve the Washington Commanders. I’ll feature players each week whose play stands out and how they could fit on […]
full_text: ATHENS, GA - SEPTEMBER 05: Georgia Bulldogs offensive lineman Drew Bobo(74) during the college football game between the Tennessee State Tigers and Georgia Bulldogs on September 5, 2026, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by John Adams/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The first week of the college football season is in the books, so it’s time for Future Hogs. This is a series of articles during the college football season that looks at draft-eligible players that could improve the Washington Commanders. I’ll feature players each week whose play stands out and how they could fit on the Commanders’ roster. While opening weekend of the college football season featured lots of players and coaches at new schools, it didn’t feature many ranked-on-ranked matchups. The only one, #9 Ole Miss and #24 Louisville, turned into a shootout where Ole Miss needed a walk-off field goal to get the victory. Louisville was the only team in the AP Top 25 to lose, but Michigan almost carried that distinction. The Wolverines needed a last-second hail mary to beat Western Michigan. Oregon won, but Boise State made it close. LSU punished an unranked Clemson team, leading to the question of whether the program is still among one of the best in the sport. Week 2 will feature two major Big 10-SEC matchups. Michigan will look to improve as they host Oklahoma. The Sooners will go into Ann Arbor after a shutout win over UTEP. The highlight of the week will be Texas visiting the Horseshoe to face Ohio State. Last year’s matchup was a defensive battle that featured inexperienced QBs, but Arch Manning and Julian Sayin now have a season’s worth of starts under their belts. It should be an exciting game that features several NFL prospects. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to comment with players that stood out to you. Lincoln Kienholz | QB | Senior | Louisville Jayden Daniels is the unquestioned starter for the Commanders at QB. With the weapons he has in the passing game, he’ll bounce back from a disappointing, injury-filled sophomore season. The Commanders should consider adding talent at this position as backup Marcus Mariota, who was injured in the preseason, gets older. He’ll also be a free agent at the end of the season. Athan Kaliakmanis is QB3 and may move into the role of QB2 if Mariota doesn’t re-sign. Lincoln Kienholz was a backup QB at Ohio State that transferred to Louisville. He is a talented runner at the position that is still developing as a passer. He missed several easy throws during Louisville’s loss to Ole Miss. What stood out most was that when he needed to be his best in the game, Kienholz stepped up. Kienholz made accurate throws on the move and decisive runs that kept the Cardinals alive. If he can play that way consistently, he’ll have a good chance of getting drafted in 2027. Kienholz would be an interesting developmental prospect behind Jayden Daniels. The 6’2”, 215 pound signal caller went 18 of 29 for 309 yards and two touchdowns through the air and 69 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Louisville QB Lincoln Keinholz with a big time throw generated out of structure. Keinholz is currently > 300.00 total ypg in his first collegiate start.. pic.twitter.com/RO7LW7cUgN — Adam Carter (@impactfbdata) September 7, 2026 Lincoln Keinholz going crazy 😂🔥 pic.twitter.com/iQglSME1oi — Brutus Wayne™ (@BuckeyeBat) September 7, 2026 Kamari Moulton | RB | Senior | Iowa The Commanders look to have a running back by committee this season with Bill Croskey-Merritt getting the majority of carries, Rachaad White and Jeremy McNichols handling third downs, and Kaytron Allen in the role of big back. White and McNichols will be free agents after the season, so running back might need reinforcement again next offseason. Kamari Moulton was prolific in the Hawkeyes’ victory over Northern Illinois. He was over 100 yards by the end of the first quarter. Iowa uses a lot of outside zone runs, and Moulton sticks his foot in the ground and bursts through the line of scrimmage. He can make quick cuts to find open space or avoid defenders. Once in the open field, Moulton can go the distance thanks to his speed. For a back that is 5’9”, 211 pounds, he should be a little better breaking tackles and dealing with contact. Moulton finished the game with 183 yards and two touchdowns on 11 carries. From the 50 🤩 Kamari Moulton took this one to the house for No. 22 @HawkeyeFootball 's second score of the day. Watch on BTN pic.twitter.com/WSvlJYL14h — Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) September 5, 2026 KAMARI MOULTON 37yds FOR HIS 2ND TD (and 132 yds in the 1st qtr) pic.twitter.com/9sSOp2DJHG — Heavens! (@HeavensFX) September 5, 2026 KJ Duff | WR | Junior | Rutgers Rutgers took it on the chin in Week 1, losing to a UMass team that had lost 16 games in a row. Maybe they’re missing Athan Kaliakmanis. Nonetheless, KJ Duff is an NFL talent and their lead receiver. If you’re a person that thinks the Commanders need a big possession receiver with the strength to deal with press coverage, look no further than the 6’6”, 225 pound Duff. At that size, Duff has more agility and fluidity than you might expect. He also has some of the best hands out there. What Duff won’t give you is a lot of speed or yards after the catch. He had nine receptions, 196 yards, and three touchdowns in the Scarlet Knights’ loss to the Minutemen. KJ Duff just showed why he’s one of the best WRs in college football 😳🔥 9 REC, 196 YDS, 3 TD An unreal way to start the season. pic.twitter.com/2GRyPsQBcr — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 4, 2026 Jamari Johnson | TE | Redshirt Junior | Oregon After signing Chig Okonkwo to join John Bates, Ben Sinnott, and Colson Yankoff, tight end should not be at the top of the list of needs for the Commanders. If offensive coordinator David Blough plans to use a lot of 12 personnel, having multiple talented tight ends will help the offense. Jamari Johnson has a chance to be the first tight end drafted in 2027. Similar to his predecessor Kenyon Sadiq, Johnson is an athletic tight end that will make more of an impact as a receiver. His hands are solid, making some impressive catches, and he has some elusiveness and speed after the catch. At 6’5”, 255 pounds, it’d be nice to see him run through more contact. He blocks well and has a lot of experience with it because he played more inline while Sadiq was moved around the formation. Johnson had four catches for 57 yards and a touchdown in a win over Boise State. A Jamari Johnson TD and he celebrates with @theoregonduck 🦆 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/AQxnN3gUKZ — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) September 5, 2026 Drew Bobo | C | Senior | Georgia The Commanders’ center situation can be described many ways. I’ll say that the position is unsettled. Nick Allegretti will be the starter at the position despite relatively little experience at the position in the NFL. Behind him is sixth-rounder Matt Gulbin, a player I was high on leading up to the draft but is entirely unproven. Drew Bobo, son of Georgia offensive coordinator Mike Bobo, should finish the college football season as one of the best center prospects in the country. A foot injury that required surgery ended his season last year, but he looks healthy to start the new season. The fifth-year senior is 6’5”, 305 pounds. Bobo is strong, usually controlling defenders once he gets his hands on them. Bobo also moves well at his size. Georgia uses gap/power concepts in the run game, but Bobo will pull on some of those plays. He also looks good on the few outside zone runs I saw. Bobo can play high which will be taken advantage of more often in the NFL. He helped lead Georgia to 660 total yards in their win over Tennessee State. This OL is doing some impressive blocking man Nate Frazier 2nd TD of the game. pic.twitter.com/SRPnhFkAQn — Top Tier…

full_text: Dec 22, 2024; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) runs the ball against Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun (53) during the third quarter at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Peter Casey-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Washington Commanders are entering Year 3 of the Adam Peters/Dan Quinn/Jayden Daniels era, and they kick it off with a pair of road games against division rivals. The Philadelphia Eagles are up first, and they are big favorites at home to kick off the new season. Both teams will have new offensive coordinators when they meet up at Lincoln Financial Field. David Blough takes over from Kliff Kingsbury in Washington, and Sean Mannion replaces Kevin Patullo. Both first-time coordinators are tasked with installing new, under center offenses and there will be an adjustment period for Jayden Daniels and Jalen Hurts. The defenses are a different story with Daronte Jones taking over the Commanders from Joe Whitt Jr, and Vic Fangio forgoing retirement for another year in Philly. Washington went big on defense in free agency, and also used the No. 7 overall pick on former Ohio State LB Sonny Styles. Will that be enough to turn around a defense that was consistently inconsistent last year? Division games can be unpredictable, but most people are expecting the Eagles to take the season opener in their house. The two teams have vastly different season projections, with the Eagles near the top, and Washington’s prospects severely dimmed after last season fell apart. title: Commanders news: Optimism rises with healthier roster for Philly trip
summary: The Daily Slop – 8 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Albert […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - AUGUST 28: Stefon Diggs #3 of the Washington Commanders walks on the field before the preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 8 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links At long last… Week 1 is upon us 🙌 pic.twitter.com/QZ66mrMfWf — NFL (@NFL) September 7, 2026 Articles Sports Illustrated Albert Breer’s Takeaways: Where Every NFL Team Stands Heading Into the 2026 Season It’s really rare that a veteran coach such as Dan Quinn goes through the sort of on-the-fly wholesale philosophical change that the Commanders did this offseason, and there’s no question it’s just different with more complex schemes coming in with new coordinators David Blough and Daronte Jones. Now the trick will be fitting some of the old standbys into the new way of doing things, and all eyes are going to be on quarterback Jayden Daniels in that regard . Losing Laremy Tunsil in camp—he won’t be back until at least January, and even that may be a longshot)—is a tough blow, and only underlines how his adjustment to Blough’s scheme has to chart the course back to the playoffs. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN NFL team previews 2026: Predictions, rankings, depth charts Commanders Biggest strength: Jayden Daniels. The third-year QB gives the Commanders a chance in every game and, as one AFC executive said, erases a lot of faults. Daniels has grown as a leader and in his comfort level running a new offense. He also has the strongest receiving corps he has played with in Washington this season. He also should have a stronger defense to help, giving him either more chances or better field position. Daniels just needs a line that can be solid. — John Keim This season is a success if … Daniels stays healthy and the defense produces with its addition of speed and athleticism. If all that happens, the Commanders have a chance for a strong rebound season. — Keim One key fantasy nugget: With a healthy Daniels, wide receiver Terry McLaurin is a solid bounce-back candidate this season. He averaged 11.4 points per game in 2025 but will be the WR1 in a Washington offense featuring more West Coast system routes. — Bowen Bold prediction for 2026: New safety Nick Cross will lead all safeties in tackles. Cross recorded an 89th percentile tackle rate (tackles per play) against the run among safeties last year, and 74th percentile against the pass. — Walder To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated 5 Questions That Will Define Commanders vs. Eagles in Week 1 Which Washington Receiver Becomes Philadelphia’s Third Problem? With Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs as players the Eagles will obviously prioritize, that will leave a stack of guys who could get opportunities to step forward. That list includes Antonio Williams, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane, Dyami Brown, and Treylon Burks. Williams’ strong summer likely signals he’ll be someone to watch, although don’t be surprised to see Diggs move around to different spots, including the slot. The most hopeful outcome for Washington: Philadelphia’s secondary depth will be tested as someone outside the top two receivers steps up and makes them regret it. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Hogs Haven Mark Tyler breaks down Commanders defense & why it will be the backbone of the 2026 campaign More than half of the defense has completely turned over. Gone are Von Miller (who was once a great player in this league) and Jacob Martin. They are being replaced by uber-athletic edge rushers in Oweh and Chaisson. Dorance Armstrong, who was a starter last year before being injured, should slot into a rotational role along with rookie Joshua Josephs once he returns from his one-game suspension. The interior has been bolstered by the additions of Tim Settle and Charles Omehihu to go along with Payne and Kinlaw. Both are scheme/technique diverse and can be moved around the front five. Washington’s linebacker corps has been completely revamped. Styles takes over for the aging Bobby Wagner – who was a liability anywhere outside the A and B gaps and in coverage. He offers the ability to impact all three levels of this defense and will share green dot responsibilities with veteran Frankie Luvu. Speaking of Luvu, he came into camp in the best shape of his career and is looking to regain his 2024 form after being played out of position for the majority of 2025. Leo Chenal is the new free-agent addition, and his versatility and toughness against the run and as a situational pass rusher as a walked-up SAM will be a welcome addition to this defense. The Commanders defensive backs have taken on a completely new identity. Safety Nick Cross will be the leader of the secondary. His presence on the defense will force offensive coordinators to monitor his alignment on every play. Jeremy Reaves and Quan Martin (who had a very good training camp), will both see time in Jones’ three-safety looks and Tyler Owens seems to have carved out a role as a “position-less player” who can be deployed at all three levels. Sainristil and Robertson can move between the inside and outside with Douglas and Moreau adding the veteran presences until Trey Amos returns. At kickoff on Sunday afternoon in Philly, there could be up to eight new starters on this 2026 defense. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Three offensive players I’m watching closely in Week 1 against the Eagles TE Chig Okonkwo The former Maryland product is known for creating yards after the catch and has an explosive athletic profile. Built like a wide receiver at 6’3″ and 238 pounds, Okonkwo may not have the precise route-running savvy of Ertz, but he should inject a different kind of vertical stress into the offense. In D.C., he will be playing with the best quarterback of his career. In Tennessee, his ceiling was capped by a revolving door of shaky quarterback play, and now he has a signal-caller with pinpoint accuracy who can lead him up the field. Okonkwo signed a three-year, $30M deal this offseason to bring some serious youth and explosiveness to our tight end room. The Commanders desperately lacked a true seam-buster last year, especially as Ertz battled injuries down the stretch. Enter Okonkwo, who is coming off career highs with 56 receptions for 560 yards. More importantly, the man is an absolute YAC monster: last season, he ranked 7th among all NFL tight ends in Yards After Catch per reception at 6.2 yards, according to Next Gen Stats. We haven’t seen Okonkwo much this offseason due to the team managing his health, but all signs point to a breakout season for the former Titan. Will this come to fruition, or did we all fall for Ashburn Syndrome? I want to see some heavy targets dialed up for Chig right out of the gate in Week 1. In Tennessee, he thrived on manufactured touches—designed bubble screens, motion out of the backfield, and flexing into the slot to isolate linebackers. If the Eagles try to pin their ears back and play aggressive coverage to slow down Terry McLaurin, Okonkwo should find plenty of green grass over the middle for quick, explosive catch-and-run opportunities. Throw in rookie Antonio Williams and tight end Chig Okonkwo, and you’ve got yourself a pretty dynamic unit. If you’ve been paying attention, there are actually several reasons to…

title: Washington Commanders at the Eagles in Week 1 – Inside the Matchup
summary: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer, Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates […]
full_text: Jan 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles safety Brandon Johnson (49) breaks up pass intended for Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks (13) at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer, Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026. From John Portis: Things have changed a lot since June, when Bill-in-Bangkok wrote his preview of this week’s season opener against the defending NFC East champs in Philly. The loss of Laremy Tunsil turned up the heat on the Commanders’ 2026 season before it even started, while the absence of Nick Allegretti for most of training camp put the spotlight on Adam Peters’ decision, back in February, to move on from center Tyler Biadasz. A move to injured reserve with a designation to return for Trey Amos has shaken confidence in a secondary that struggled last season, but the addition of Stefon Diggs has been huge for the outlook of the Commanders’ offense. Sports writers have soured on the Commanders early, even as the coaches and players have reaffirmed their confidence in one another. Frascella’s 2026 NFC East Preseason Predictions: 4. Washington Commanders: 5-12 3. New York Giants: 6-11 2. Philadelphia Eagles: 10-7 1. Dallas Cowboys: 12-5 … what are your predictions? https://t.co/Lcn4kqZChe pic.twitter.com/svDyH7OniR — John Frascella (Football) (@NFLFrascella) September 4, 2026 The Washington Commanders have two new coordinators in David Blough and Daronte Jones. Blough hasn’t unveiled his new offense, but we know to expect the quarterback under center more, plenty of motion, and play-action. Penalties have been a concern discussed by head coach Dan Quinn throughout training camp. Daronte Jones has kept his defense under wraps, but occasional glimpses — like a six-man blitz versus Detroit — show a blitz-heavy scheme with disguised pressures and coverages. New Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is also installing an under center, motion-heavy offense, with a core philosophy of providing clarity for Jalen Hurts before the snap. That offense should be timing- and rhythm-based. The unique alignments and route concepts littered within this Sean Mannion offense is fun to study even this early on. He’s got RBs flexed out, WRs at the wing behind an OT, pony personnel (two RBs), on top of the pre-snap motion (orbit/return) that’s ingrained in his scheme… — Ryan Fowler (@_RyanFowler_) August 13, 2026 Eagles defensive coordinator, Vic Fangio, returns to run his two-high safety system designed to disguise coverages pre-snap behind disciplined front seven execution. There seems to be some thought among Eagles fans that, as a rookie defensive coordinator, Daronte Jones is a nice slow pitch start for Mannion, but Jones already appears to be one of the more competent coaches on Dan Quinn’s staff. The new offensive schemes in Philly and Washington represent significant shifts for the quarterbacks of both teams. Simply huddling the offense on a regular basis will be new for Jayden Daniels. Last season, the average NFL offense huddled about 82 percent of the time. With Daniels on the field, the Commanders huddled just about 32 percent of the time. So far, Jayden Daniels has looked sharp during training camp and practice with the word “surgical” being used a lot, but after taking an ugly three offensive snaps in the 2nd preseason game, Dan Quinn shut Jayden and the rest of the 1st-team offense down for the rest of that game and the final one in Baltimore. There is a lot to project, but with new offensive weapons, Daniels should be effective if the line can give him time to work. Jalen Hurts, on the other hand, has reportedly had a rocky transition so far, throwing numerous interceptions in training camp. Mannion’s offense tasks him with throwing in rhythm as a wide receiver comes out of his breaks, which does not appear to be a completely natural fit for Hurts. Mannion is expected to want to work the middle of the field where Jalen has little experience. If the Commanders can disrupt the timing of the Eagles’ passing attack, there should be an opportunity for the secondary to corral some interceptions. Quarterbacks Throwing Over the Middle since 2023 From the Stats & Scheme newsletter pic.twitter.com/KtTFwaEDag — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) September 4, 2026 Eagles Training Camp Day 16 Takeaways: Jalen Hurts has 13 interceptions in 16 practices this year Hurts had 15 interceptions the last four training camps combined Hurts and offense are turning it over way too much — and if it keeps up in the regular season they both will and… pic.twitter.com/DxqviQ5i5V — Eliot Shorr-Parks (@EliotShorrParks) August 26, 2026 The Commanders have invested heavily in edge talent, adding both Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson in the offseason. If both are healthy, they will lead the pass rushing attack for the Washington. Jones will be counting on the two edges to speed up Hurts’ clock and protect Washington’s secondary. The Eagles return Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis; the pair working against new Commanders starting center Nick Allegretti will be a matchup to watch. Not listed in Hog Haven’s summer preview, which was published in June (and which you can read below), is Philly’s trade acquisition of Dontayvion Wicks. First-round selection Makai Lemon suffered a hamstring injury during OTAs and experienced some setbacks, so it should be Wicks and Smith to start following the trade of A.J. Brown. Washington also added wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who will look to breakout in Washington’s remade offense versus Eagles free agent addition Riq Woolen. Both offensive coordinators prioritize three-down ability in their running backs, so we should see plenty of Saquon Barkley and Commanders’ free agent addition Rachaad White in the receiving game. This is a tough matchup for the Commanders to start their season, with the difficulty level ratcheted up on the road. The team’s best hope is the Eagles’ offense takes longer to gel than Washington’s defense. If the defense can contain the game early and allow Jayden Daniels time to settle in, he could provide enough game-changing plays to give his team the chance to walk away with an upset win in a divisional season opener on the road.
