title: NFL team previews 2026: Predictions, rankings, depth charts
summary: Here's everything you need to know for the 2026 regular season, including how all 32 NFL teams rank and key stats ahead of Week 1.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season kicks off Wednesday with a Super Bowl rematch featuring the reigning champion  Seattle Seahawks hosting the New England Patriots  ( 8:20 p.m. ET, NBC ). Then, on Thursday, the NFL will have its first-ever regular-season game in Australia , where the Super Bowl-favorite  Los Angeles Rams will take on the San Francisco 49ers  ( 8:35 p.m. ET, Netflix ). 

 To welcome back football, we're previewing every single team in the league. Our NFL Nation reporters identified strengths and concerns for all 32 rosters, and then they laid out what would make 2026 a successful season. Analyst Matt Bowen gave a fantasy nugget for each team, analytics writer Seth Walder made 32 bold predictions, and ESPN Research provided QB stats to know.

 Plus, our Football Power Index predicted chances for every team to win its division, make the playoffs and more. The model even suggested best- and worst-case scenarios for all 32 teams, based on the 90th- and 10th-percentile outcomes across thousands of simulations, respectively.

 This is everything you need to know for the start of the season, which will conclude Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, for Super Bowl LXI on ESPN.

 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LV | LAC | LAR | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA 
 SF | TB | TEN | WSH 

 

 

 

 1. Los Angeles Rams 
 Chances to make the playoffs: 84.9% 
 Chances to win division: 50.4% 
 Projected wins: 11.3 
 Strength of schedule: Third hardest 
 2025 record: 12-5

 Biggest strength: The passing game. There are several options to choose from on this star-studded roster, but it's hard not to pick the reigning MVP. Quarterback Matthew Stafford is coming off the best season of his career and will again have one of the best receiver pairs in the NFL: Davante Adams and Puka Nacua . Last season, Adams led the league with 14 receiving touchdowns, and Nacua led the NFL with 129 catches. -- Sarah Barshop 

 Biggest concern: Offensive tackle. The Rams don't have much depth at tackle, which could matter if left tackle Alaric Jackson is suspended. The NFL is conducting its own investigation into an alleged incident of domestic violence by Jackson, who is not facing criminal prosecution because his case was assigned for diversion . Third-round pick Keagen Trost , who was expected to back up Jackson and Warren McClendon Jr ., left the preseason opener with a hamstring injury. Coach Sean McVay said he's hopeful Trost will return to start the season. -- Barshop 

 QB stat to know:  Stafford is coming off a career-high 46 passing touchdowns -- his third season with 40 or more passing scores. Those three seasons are tied for the most by any QB in NFL history along with Aaron Rodgers  and Tom Brady. However, Stafford has seen major regression following each season of 40 passing TDs -- including going from 41 to 20 in 2012 and going from 41 to 10 in 2022. -- ESPN Research 

 Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 14-3 
 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 9-8

 This season is a success if ...  the Rams win the Super Bowl. The Rams took steps to maximize the remaining time that Stafford wants to play, so expectations are sky-high for Los Angeles. -- Barshop 

 One key fantasy nugget: The Rams regularly isolate Adams in scoring position given his ability to win off the release. His 14 touchdown receptions on end zone throws last season were the second most in a season this century (Randy Moss had 16 in 2007). -- Bowen 

 Bold prediction for 2026: Tight end Terrance Ferguson will catch eight touchdown passes. I'm buying the hype here because it just makes too much sense. The Rams need a third pass catcher behind Nacua and Adams, and with a year of experience in the league after being a 2025 second-round pick, Ferguson could emerge as that guy. If either of those two receivers misses time, his ceiling could be even higher. -- Walder 

 
 Full schedule | Roster | Depth chart 
 Read more on the Rams 

 
 

 
 

 

 2. Buffalo Bills 
 Chances to make the playoffs: 84.1% 
 Chances to win division: 67.1% 
 Projected wins: 10.7 
 Strength of schedule: 14th easiest 
 2025 record: 12-5

 Biggest strength: Josh Allen . It's pretty simple. The Bills have an opportunity to win a Super Bowl once again this year, despite a first-time head coach, and that's because of who is playing quarterback. Allen, 30, is going into his ninth NFL season and has a new No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore . Breaking records has become commonplace for the 2024 MVP, and Allen gives the team a chance in every game. -- Alaina Getzenberg 

 Biggest concern: It is a transition year for the new defensive scheme. Coordinator Jim Leonhard has been open about the fact this year's defense will not fully look like his vision for the unit as it transitions from a 4-3 to 3-4 base. There is a mix of new players who fit the scheme specifically and carryovers from the previous regime. How the group comes together will go a long way in determining the unit's success. -- Getzenberg 

 QB stat to know:  Allen's dual-threat ability is unlike anything the NFL has seen. Allen already has 299 passing and rushing TDs combined in his first eight seasons, 40 more than the next-closest player ( Patrick Mahomes , 259). In fact, he already has the most through a player's first nine seasons (next closest: Peyton Manning, 288). -- ESPN Research 

 Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 13-4 
 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 8-9

 This season is a success if ...  the Bills reach the Super Bowl. Unfortunately for new coach Joe Brady, that's the bar. Maximizing Allen's tenure is the priority, and anything comparable to or less than what Sean McDermott accomplished won't make for a fully successful season. -- Getzenberg 

 One key fantasy nugget:  Allen gives fantasy managers a major boost when the Bills have the ball on the doorstep of the end zone. He converted 22 of 28 true goal-line carries (78.6%) over the past three seasons. -- Bowen 

 Bold prediction for 2026: Wide receiver Keon Coleman will record 750 or more receiving yards and at least five touchdowns -- both career highs. Earlier this offseason I thought there was a decent chance he'd be on a different team by now. But Coleman also hasn't been that bad in his first two years, posting a 49 overall score in ESPN's receiver score (just below average) and 1.6 yards per route run. Even though the Bills added Moore, I could see Coleman having a mini breakout in Year 3. -- Walder 

 
 Full schedule | Roster | Depth chart 
 Read more on the Bills 

 
 
 

 

 3. Seattle Seahawks 
 Chances to make the playoffs: 68.0% 
 Chances to win division: 26.3% 
 Projected wins: 10.2 
 Strength of schedule: Sixth hardest 
 2025 record: 14-3

 Biggest strength: The defense remains the strength even though it lost three players -- safety Coby Bryant , cornerback Riq Woolen and outside linebacker Boye Mafe - from the unit that allowed the fewest points in the NFL last season. The Seahawks still have plenty of difference-makers on that side of the ball, and they still have one of the game's brightest defensive minds, coach Mike Macdonald, calling the shots. -- Brady Henderson 

 Biggest concern: It's more of a question mark than a concern, but Sam Darnold and the offense will be relying on a first-time coordinator in Brian Fleury. Macdonald's choice to replace Klint Kubiak, Fleury will be running an offense that's similar to his predecessor's, but he will almost certainly have to endure some growing pains as he calls plays for the first time. -- Henderson 

 QB stat to know:  Darnold has won 14 games in each of the past two seasons, making him one of two quarterbacks in NFL history with consecutive 14-win seasons along with Tom Brady in 2003 and 2004. No quarterback has had three consecutive 14-win seasons. -- ESPN Research

title: Predicting the 2026 NFL playoff field, plus Super Bowl pick
summary: Which teams from last season's playoffs will return -- and which ones will miss out? Who will be the surprises in the bracket? And who will win the Super Bowl?
full_text:
It's postseason projection time. With hours to go before the first game of the 2026 NFL season , I'm picking the 14 teams that will be celebrating after the league plays 272 regular-season games. There's so much football to come and so many unexpected things we'll see along the way, but like anyone else, I want to lay out the playoff field I expect to see in January before the games kick off in mid-September.

 Of course, that would be too easy. If you've read this column over the past couple of years , you'll remember that there's a twist. One of the most common mistakes we make as football fans -- myself included -- is overconfidence in the teams we saw excel last year. We're collectively too inclined to pick teams that made the playoffs a year ago to make it back in the current season. Ask me to pick 2026 playoff teams without any constraints and I'd pick at least nine of the 14 teams that made it in 2025.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 History tells us that's underestimating the chaos and variance that comes with 17-game NFL seasons. The league has been using the 14-team playoff format for only a few years now, but if we go back to 2002 and treat the seventh-best team in each conference as a playoff team, about 56% of teams that make it to the postseason in any given season make it back the following year. That's just under eight teams per campaign.

 Eight teams in, six teams out. There's no guarantee that 2026 will play out like an average season in terms of playoff returnees, but the evidence says our playoff predictions should start there. I'll take things a step further by looking at division champions and teams with losing records in 2025 to tailor the field even closer to what a historic playoff field typically looks like by the end of the regular season. I'll detail how those play out along the way. And at the end, I'll make my Super Bowl pick for the upcoming season.

 

 
 Jump to a section: 
 2025 division champions 
 2025 wild-card berths 
 From out to in 
 Barnwell's Super Bowl pick 

 
 

 Which 2025 division champions will return to the playoffs? 
 Let's start by splitting last season's playoff teams into two groups. Since 2002, just under 60% of teams that won their division in a given year have made it back to the playoffs the following year. That's 4.8 teams per year, which we'll round up to five. So, of the eight division winners from 2025, I have to pick five to return to the playoffs in 2026.

 We can split that even further. About 43% of division winners repeat as champs the following season, with teams such as the Tom Brady-era Patriots and the  Patrick Mahomes -era Chiefs as near-perennial favorites to finish first. If we remove the Patriots and Chiefs from the data set, the rate of repeating divisional winners drops to 36%. That's an average of about three division winners retaining their titles each season.

 

 One of the weirdest things about the 2025 season factors in here. In 2024, six of the eight teams that won their division the prior year retained their crowns, which was just the third time that has happened in the eight-division era. In 2025, everything went in the opposite direction. Just one of the eight reigning champs held on to its division title for another year. The one team that did so was the Philadelphia Eagles , who became the first team to win back-to-back titles in the NFC East in more than two decades. Four 2024 division champs -- the Chiefs, Ravens, Lions and Buccaneers -- missed the postseason outright in 2025.

 History tells us to pick three division winners to repeat as champions, with two more making it back to the postseason as wild cards. I'll then be left with three division winners from 2025 that I'll need to pick to miss the playoffs entirely. I'm sure that won't upset anyone ...

 Running through my options, I'm already beginning to squirm. I'm not sure there are three division winners with good chances of repeating in 2026. I like some of last season's wild-card teams more than the division winners. If this were just "pick eight playoff teams to repeat," I might have five division winners missing the playoffs. This is why I like doing this column in this very particular way -- it forces me to think about choices I don't necessarily love but that might turn out to be more realistic as the season plays out in the months to come.

 
 

 Seattle Seahawks 
 My pick for 2026 : In the playoffs (NFC West champions)

 It feels almost controversial to pick the defending Super Bowl champions to stay atop the NFC West for another year. It's easy to understand why the Rams are favorites to top the Seahawks and return to the top of the division; they added Myles Garrett , Aaron Donald , Trent McDuffie  and Jaylen Watson to their roster this offseason.

 But the Seahawks did beat the Rams twice in three tries last season. They went 14-3, finishing two games ahead of Los Angeles in the race for the NFC West, and led the league in DVOA. Sure, the Seahawks were one of the league's healthier teams, especially on offense, but they also outscored opposing teams by more than 11 points per game and went a sustainable 4-3 in games decided by seven points or less.

 The champs lost several players on defense ( Coby Bryant , Riq Woolen  and Boye Mafe among them), but coach Mike Macdonald has a significant track record of developing both young players and underappreciated veterans into useful contributors on the defensive side of the ball. And virtually everybody of note beyond Super Bowl MVP  Kenneth Walker III is back on offense. It would be a surprise if the Seahawks weren't competing for a division title this season.

 

 
 

 Philadelphia Eagles 
 My pick for 2026 : In the playoffs (NFC East champions)

 If the Eagles were able to overcome what had been a multi-decade run of new champions in the NFC East to finally hold on to their division crown, I'm willing to back Jalen Hurts & Co. to make it three straight in 2026. Things didn't end well for the Eagles in 2025, as they lost four of their final seven games before being bounced out of the playoffs by the 49ers , but you might remember the Eagles going through a similar scenario in 2023. They started 10-1, lost five of their last six games and were then blown out by the Bucs in the wild-card round. Yet Philly won the division the following season -- and also won the Super Bowl.

 The Eagles weren't great on offense, but things really began to crater once they lost star right tackle   Lane Johnson in November. The 36-year-old is back as part of what should be a healthier offensive line. Vic Fangio fielded the youngest defense in the league last season, and that unit could be even more productive after adding Riq Woolen and Jonathan Greenard to the mix during the offseason. Sean Mannion's new under-center offensive scheme creates some uncertainty, but the Eagles have one of the highest floors of any team in the NFL.

 
 

 New England Patriots 
 My pick for 2026 : In the playoffs (AFC East champions)

 I've already written about why I don't expect the Patriots to win 14 games again, which shouldn't be any sort of significant surprise. (It's hard to win 14 games twice in a row!) Even with a bit of a step backward, though, the Patriots could still hold on to their AFC East title with something like an 11-win campaign.

 Their schedule is tougher, but it's still the 11th-easiest slate in the league per ESPN's Football Power Index . They'll probably suffer more injuries after being one of the healthiest teams a year ago, but unless stars such as  Drake Maye , Christian Gonzalez  and A.J. Brown miss significant time, the Patriots should still have plenty of talent. And if the blitz-happy defensive scheme that helped sustain the Patriots as their offense struggled during the AFC playoffs carries over into 2026, the Pats might actually be a better team on a snap-by-snap basis than they were in 2025 -- even if that doesn't produce a similar win-loss…

title: South Africa vs. New Zealand - Kick-off time, team news, how to watch RGR finale in Baltimore
summary: South Africa head into Saturday's fourth Rugby's Greatest Rivalry (RGR) Test against New Zealand in Baltimore 2-1 up, and a win would leave Dave Rennie's side in no doubt about the size of the gap they have to close ahead of next year's World Cup.
full_text:
South Africa head into Saturday's fourth Rugby's Greatest Rivalry (RGR) Test against New Zealand in Baltimore 2-1 up, and a win would leave Dave Rennie's side in no doubt about the size of the gap they have to close ahead of next year's World Cup.

 If the All Blacks manage to force a series draw against the reigning back-to-back world champions in the USA, they will head home feeling they are on solid ground for a challenge next year in Australia.

 Rennie's side started the series with a 33-16 win in the first Test at Ellis Park, but the Springboks fought back with a 33-26 victory at Cape Town's DHL Stadium. The teams returned to Johannesburg for the third Test at FNB Stadium, with South Africa securing the series lead in a 29-24 win.

 

 The third Test was South Africa's most convincing performance despite a relatively tight scoreline in the end due to a late All Blacks try.

 Rassie Erasmus has hailed New Zealand's progress this year, but Rennie will be hoping his side can demonstrate the same resilience when on the back foot that the Springboks have shown in recent years - including this series.

 If they can snatch this series draw, that will not yet be enough to prove that the tables have turned in world rugby, but it will show that the All Blacks are still strong enough to go toe-to-toe even after being on the receiving end of the backlash - or 'Boklash' - after winning the first Test.

 Key details 
 Date: Saturday, September 12 at 5 p.m. EDT (11 p.m. CAT, 9 a.m. on Sunday, September 13 in Mainland New Zealand)

 Venue: M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore, Maryland

 How to watch: The match will air on SuperSport's channels 201 and 211 in South Africa. For fans in New Zealand, Sky Sport holds RGR rights. UK viewers will be able to watch the games on Sky Sports

 

 Match officials 

 Referee: Karl Dickson (RFU)

 Assistant Referee 1: Matthew Carley (RFU)

 Assistant Referee 2: Christophe Ridley (RFU)

 TMO: Andrew Jackson (RFU)

 FPRO: Matteo Liperini (FIR)

 Team news 
 Cheslin Kolbe is set to miss the series decider for the Springboks after breaking his jaw in the third Test, with Damian Willemse returning from his own injury to start at fullback. Morne van den Berg gets the nod at scrumhalf, with Cobus Reinach benched.

 South Africa: 15 Damian Willemse, 14 Kurt-Lee Arendse, 13 Jesse Kriel, 12 Damian de Allende, 11 Ethan Hooker, 10 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, 9 Morne van den Berg, 8 Jasper Wiese, 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit, 6 Siya Kolisi (captain), 5 Ruan Nortje, 4 Eben Etzebeth, 3 Wilco Louw, 2 Malcolm Marx, 1 Ox Nche

 Replacements: 16 Deon Fourie, 17 Gerhard Steenekamp, 18 Thomas du Toit, 19 Lood de Jager, 20 Andre Esterhuizen, 21 Cameron Hanekom, 22 Cobus Reinach, 23 Manie Libbok

 All Blacks: TBC

 Stats 
 The Springboks have won 14 of the 15 Tests in which Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has started as their flyhalf - with the only exception being the defeat to the All Blacks in this series at Ellis Park.

 Feinberg-Mngomezulu has appeared in 8 further games as a substitute, with 6 of those being victories.

 Siya Kolisi picked up his 55th win as Springbok Test captain in the 29-24 win at FNB Stadium, surpassing John Smit to become the most successful Springbok captain of all-time by this metric.

title: Panthers banking on RBs Hubbard, Brooks despite injury histories
summary: Carolina wants to run the ball more, but how will each back -- including AJ Dillon -- handle the workload?
full_text:
Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales wants to run the ball more, especially during the 2026 NFL season . He has made his intentions clear over the past three summers.

 And with offensive coordinator Brad Idzik now calling plays , and 2024 second-round pick Jonathon Brooks returning to the mix , Carolina is hoping for a boost in production and consistency from its running back rotation. After a couple of years of uneven production, the Panthers are counting on a trio of running backs with notable injury histories to get the ball moving: Brooks, Chuba Hubbard and AJ Dillon .

 Brooks, who was sidelined in practice last week because of general soreness, also missed Monday's workout. Canales said last Thursday that he was "very optimistic" about Brooks' availability in Week 1 against the Chicago Bears ( Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, Fox ). However, on Monday, Canales said he remained hopeful on Brooks but wouldn't give an update on his status until Wednesday.

 

 Brooks is expected to share the backfield workload in 2026 with Hubbard, the Panthers' returning starter, and as Rico Dowdle proved last season, having a tandem to ride the hot hand in the backfield is important in any offense.

 "Yeah, we'll definitely roll it out just the way we have been," Canales said last month. "Where you have a lead back for the series, the other guy comes in on third down so they can be in there for the protection, and also we run the ball on third down. So those are good opportunities to just keep a guy into the game, while the other person, whether it's Chuba or [Brooks], we'll make that decision when we get closer.

 "But whoever the lead guy for the base downs is, they'll get the bulk of that rhythm."

 Here's a breakdown of the Panthers' current running back depth chart and the latest news on their health:

 

 Chuba Hubbard | Age: 27 
 2025 stats: 511 rushing yards and a TD on 134 carries (3.8 yards per carry); 223 receiving yards and three TDs on 30 catches (7.4 yards per catch)

 Recent injury history: Hamstring injury (missed entire 2026 preseason); calf injury (missed two games in 2025)

 Hubbard was hampered by the aforementioned calf injury throughout the 2025 season, despite missing only two games. He eventually lost his starting job to Dowdle -- who is now in Pittsburgh -- and finished with a forgettable stat total in the Panthers' push toward a playoff spot. After winning the NFC South title, Hubbard once again became the primary back in the team's wild-card loss to the Los Angeles Rams .

 Hubbard appeared to be on a load management schedule throughout training camp. While he frequently worked with the starting group in practice, the first-team reps were spread out. The veteran playmaker sustained a hamstring injury midway through camp, and he missed the entirety of the preseason game slate. He also missed out on joint practices with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Houston Texans .

 Hubbard returned to practice last week. Prior to the preseason finale, he said he could have played in the final game if it had been a meaningful matchup. But the Panthers rested their starters and took precautions with Hubbard throughout the summer. Resting Hubbard for a big workload appears to be the plan.

 Hubbard, who signed a four-year, $33.2 million contract extension in 2024, has been backed by Canales and general manager Dan Morgan at every turn, and their hope is he can return to the form that warranted his long-term pact in the first place. He ran for 1,195 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2024 before his injury-plagued 2025 campaign.

 

 Jonathon Brooks | Age: 23 
 2025 stats: N/A

 Recent injury history: Tore right ACL in 2023 (at Texas) and in 2024 (he missed entire 2025 season and only played in three games in 2024)

 Brooks made his training camp and preseason debuts this summer. During the previous two offseasons, Brooks was sidelined as he recovered from ACL surgeries on his right knee. The No. 46 overall pick in the 2024 draft initially injured his knee while playing for the Longhorns. But during his rookie season, Brooks returned to the field in Week 12 and played in three games before retearing his right ACL against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 14.

 

 After missing the entire 2025 season, he returned to practices in the spring and has had a steady workload ever since. The Panthers have been patient with Brooks in his recovery, and he had the occasional rest day sprinkled into the workout schedule.

 The Panthers are hoping he can become a home run threat in the offense. He displayed excellent hands as a receiver out of the backfield in training camp. And while his preseason rushing stats (23 yards and a touchdown on eight carries) and pass protection won't wow anyone, Brooks has looked confident while rushing into contact.

 Brooks, if available for Week 1, is likely to be used as a change-of-pace partner for Hubbard -- who is more of a traditional north-south runner -- throughout drives.

 The Panthers aren't likely to have an even workload split right away, but Hubbard and Brooks will share reps in the backfield immediately, depending on the latter's health. If Brooks can make big plays early and prove his durability in the first month of the season, he could become the top back in the rotation soon enough.

 

 AJ Dillon | Age: 28 
 2025 stats: 60 rushing yards on 12 carries (5.0 yards per carry); three catches for 21 yards (7 yards per catch)

 Recent injury history: Neck stingers in 2023 and 2024 (he missed entire 2024 season)

 Dillon entered camp as a long shot after a forgettable one-year stint with the Eagles in 2025. Dillon -- who missed the entire 2024 season with the Green Bay Packers with a neck injury -- played in seven games for the Eagles, and he was a healthy scratch for the other 10 games.

 However, during the Panthers' preseason, Dillon proved his worth as a receiver, runner and special teams asset. Dillon ran 14 times for 46 yards and two touchdowns and caught eight passes for 75 yards. He also played 10 snaps on special teams, as he was used as a wing blocker on the punt team.

 Dillon could be used occasionally on third down as a short-yardage back, especially with the Panthers opposing QB sneaks with quarterback Bryce Young . He could also be used on third down as a blocker and receiver out of the backfield. That said, it's worth noting that Canales, historically, has rarely used his third back on offense when his top two options have been healthy and available.

 
 Practice squad options: Anthony Tyus III , Ahmani Marshall 
 Tyus spent all of last season on the practice squad before returning to Carolina for the offseason program and training camp. He produced 127 rushing yards and a lost fumble on a team-leading 31 carries in the preseason; he also caught all five of his targets for 24 yards and a touchdown.

 Marshall was added to the roster last week. He previously played for the Cleveland Browns , who waived him during the cut-down deadline last month. Marshall appeared in all three preseason games for Cleveland, producing 46 rushing yards, 48 receiving yards and a touchdown catch on 29 total touches. A 2025 undrafted free agent out of Appalachian State, the Winston-Salem native has yet to appear in a regular-season game.

title: NFL execs predict 2026 award winners: MVP, top rookies, more
summary: Who will win MVP? Who will take offensive and defensive rookie of the year? Who is primed for a breakout? We asked execs and scouts for their picks.
full_text:
The march to the ultimate stage -- Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, in SoFi Stadium -- begins Wednesday, when the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks square off at Lumen Field (8:20 p.m. ET, NBC). The Los Angeles Rams are the trendy Super Bowl pick in league circles. But keep in mind this is the era of ultimate parity. At this time last year, the Seahawks and Patriots had 60-1 and 80-1 odds to win the Super Bowl, respectively.

 The journey to a championship will unfold alongside brilliant individual efforts. The hunt for league MVP will be defined by elite quarterback play. Other top awards at the annual NFL Honors will highlight the game's best.

 We asked league executives and scouts to sort out who will hold the hardware when the 2026 season ends. From MVP to rookies and coach of the year, few of the major awards offer a clear consensus at this early stage. The possibilities are endless and enticing.

 
 Jump to: 
 MVP  | OPOY  | DPOY  | OROY  | DROY 
 Comebacks  |  Breakouts  |  Top coach 

 
 

 

 

 MVP: Joe Burrow , Cincinnati Bengals 
 None of the top quarterbacks in their primes is a controversial pick. The top four passers between ages 29 and 30 -- Patrick Mahomes , Josh Allen , Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow -- have been selected in this very exercise as MVP predictions from 2021 through 25. Only Burrow lacks the actual hardware. But he slightly edges the field here, despite a push from Los Angeles' Justin Herbert and reservations about Burrow's durability.

 In his last full season (2024) he threw for 4,918 yards and 43 touchdowns. Health is the primary issue holding him back. "He senses the urgency this year and is talking like it -- I think he's ready to back it up," an AFC executive said. "If he stays healthy. Big if."

 

 The Bengals' offense will evolve this year, featuring more under-center work, which could open up a running game that ranked 29th last year.

 Allen, meanwhile, is looking to join Aaron Rodgers , Jackson and Mahomes as active players with multiple MVPs.

 "I'm done banking on Burrow because of the injuries," an AFC exec said. "I would, if not for health issues. [Matthew] Stafford  won't get it again, Mahomes is coming back from injury, and even though you can't count out Lamar, he's taken a step back. Allen is the safest bet."

 As for Herbert, people inside the league value his work much more highly than some factions of the internet do. "Don't think he got enough credit for everything he did last year when the OL got decimated by injuries," an NFC exec said. "They get healthy and a proven, creative playcaller that can make his life easier and [offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel] hasn't had a QB this gifted."

 Also receiving votes:   Justin Herbert ( Los Angeles Chargers ), Josh Allen ( Buffalo Bills )

 

 
 

 Offensive Player of the Year: Jahmyr Gibbs , Detroit Lions 
 Running backs have won three of the past six OPOY awards, and Gibbs might be next. He has made back-to-back-to-back Pro Bowls despite averaging 225 carries per year as a 1A option alongside David Montgomery . He still managed 39 rushing touchdowns, or one every 17th rushing attempt. And he caught 77 passes for 616 yards last season.

 "He'll rise to the occasion as the lead back; the Lions will be competitive; and they'll probably be in a lot of shootouts, which will help Gibbs' production," a veteran NFL scout said.

 It's worth noting that Detroit entered the week with minimal experience behind Gibbs. Backups Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors have combined for nine NFL rushing attempts. Veteran Isiah Pacheco is on injured reserve.

 Neither Gibbs nor Atlanta's Bijan Robinson has won this award despite the duo jockeying for tailback supremacy. That could change this year.

 Also receiving votes:   Ja'Marr Chase ( Cincinnati Bengals ), Bijan Robinson ( Atlanta Falcons )

 

 
 

 Defensive Player of the Year: Will Anderson Jr ., Houston Texans 
 Anderson can become the fifth edge rusher in the past six years to win this award. Fending off reigning champ Myles Garrett won't be easy, but voters in such exercises often like to predict ascending young players breaking the mold.

 

 Anderson is 25, squarely in his prime, and has improved his sack total in each of his first three seasons, from seven to 11 to 12. Houston has a realistic chance to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl thanks to a vaunted defense led by Anderson.

 "He can have the type of 15-sack season that will define him, especially with Danielle Hunter on the other side," an NFL personnel evaluator said. "You can't double both. He can be the leader of that defense, which is just nasty."

 Also receiving votes:   Myles Garrett ( Los Angeles Rams )

 

 
 

 Offensive Rookie of the Year: Jadarian Price , Seattle Seahawks 
 This was a close race among the top two running backs selected in the 2026 draft (both out of Notre Dame), an ascending player in Cleveland and a QB2 in the AFC West.

 Price, the 32nd overall pick by the reigning champion Seahawks, has impressed head coach Mike Macdonald with his coachability and open-field vision. In fact, some in Seattle feel Price can add a new dimension to the running game, despite new Kansas City Chief Kenneth Walker III's consistent production over the previous four years.

 Price is playing for an elite team as a potential lead option. Seattle plans to use two or three backs as part of each game plan, but Price should be showcased a lot.

 "He's the best they've got, and that offense is dedicated to running the ball," an NFC scout said. " Zach Charbonnet  isn't ready yet."

 Also receiving votes: Jeremiyah Love ( Arizona Cardinals ), KC Concepcion ( Cleveland Browns ), Fernando Mendoza ( Las Vegas Raiders )

 

 
 

 Defensive Rookie of the Year: Caleb Downs , Dallas Cowboys 
 The Cowboys have big plans for Downs, who instantly becomes one of Dallas' most versatile players.

 When I asked head coach Brian Schottenheimer at training camp where Downs is best served on the field, he said "anywhere," then pointed out that he can cover star receiver CeeDee Lamb up the seam.

 The Cowboys will play Downs primarily in the slot, where he can disrupt in the open field. "He will play in the middle of the defense, so he will probably have some ball production and high tackle numbers," an AFC executive said. "And if he helps turn around Dallas' defense, he'll be looked at as a catalyst."

 

 The last defensive back to win DROY was Sauce Gardner in 2022, when he recorded two interceptions and 20 pass deflections. Ball production is a must to win this award.

 Also receiving votes: Rueben Bain Jr. ( Tampa Bay Buccaneers ), Mansoor Delane ( Kansas City Chiefs ), R Mason Thomas (Chiefs), David Bailey ( New York Jets )

 

 
 

 Comeback Player of the Year: Patrick Mahomes , Kansas City Chiefs 
 This one is set up for Mahomes like a well-blocked bubble screen. The three-time Super Bowl MVP has crushed his rehab from a torn ACL and PCL. He's poised to play in Week 1. The offense should be better overall, with a Walker-led running game and a healthier receiving corps.

 And, perhaps for the first time in his career, a hint of doubt hovers over Mahomes and his place in the quarterback pantheon. He has had multiple down years (by his standards) statistically. "He's such an elite competitor and player that I'm counting on him responding," an AFC scout said. "He hears the noise."

 Also receiving votes: Kyler Murray ( Minnesota Vikings ), Aaron Donald ( Los Angeles Rams ), Jayden Daniels ( Washington Commanders )

 

 
 

 Breakout player: Matthew Golden , Green Bay Packers 
 Last year was a roller coaster for Golden, who earned rave reviews in 2025 training camp, then spent the season as a tertiary option. He finished the season with 29 catches for 361 yards on 44 targets. All of those totals ranked outside of the top three among Packers weapons last year.

 

 The departure of Romeo Doubs opens a spot for Golden in the team's three-receiver sets alongside…

title: One thing Deshaun Watson has to improve to remain Browns' starter
summary: Whether the veteran passer can regain dominance over this particular skill will help determine his role in 2026.
full_text:
When Deshaun Watson takes the field as the Cleveland Browns ' starting quarterback during Sunday's Week 1 game (1 p.m. ET, CBS) at the Jacksonville Jaguars , it will likely mark the beginning of his final opportunity to salvage his tenure in Cleveland -- and possibly his NFL career.

 Whether Watson can do so hinges on him recapturing a semblance of his Pro Bowl form with the Houston Texans , a player for which the Browns were willing to trade three first-round picks and give a fully guaranteed $230 million contract in March 2022 after more than two dozen women accused him of sexual assault and inappropriate conduct during massage sessions.

 

 Suspension- and injury-related layoffs have been the story of Watson's time in Cleveland. His latest physical setback: two Achilles surgeries that cost him all of the 2025 season and 22 months between live game action. Watson acknowledged that, at the age of 30 and after multiple significant injuries, his style of play might not resemble that of his peak dual-threat capabilities in Houston.

 However, his accuracy on downfield passing and willingness to push the ball -- once a strength -- is an area of his game that has declined in recent years and will need to improve if he wants to keep his job as QB1.

 When Watson was named to three consecutive Pro Bowls as a member of the Texans, he wasn't just one of the league's premier mobile quarterbacks but a pinpoint passer able to stretch the field.

 In 2018, Watson ranked third among 34 qualifying quarterbacks in completion rate (58.8%) on downfield passes (attempts that traveled at least 10 air yards), according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Watson led the NFL in passing yards in 2020, and he only trailed then-Saints QB Drew Brees in completion rate on downfield pass attempts at 59.9%. Even in Watson's six-game run in his first year in Cleveland after sitting out the 2021 season and serving an 11-game suspension, he completed 53.1% of his downfield passes, which would have ranked sixth.

 

 That mark has declined in recent years. In 2023, Watson completed 39.3% of his downfield attempts, which would have ranked as the worst rate in the league if he qualified. His 33.3% off-target rate on such passes only trailed Panthers QB Bryce Young for the worst in the league. Watson's stat worsened in 2024, as he completed a career-low 37.9% of downfield attempts before his Achilles tear sidelined for the final 10 games of the season.

 Compounding Watson's struggles is an aversion to attempting to push the ball downfield. Watson's average depth of target has dropped significantly, from 9 yards in his final Pro Bowl season in 2020 to a career-low 7.1 in his most recent season in 2024, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Watson threw downfield on a career-low 26.9% of his passes in 2024, his second career season with a rate below 30%, including his 28.8% mark in his 2022 debut season with the Browns.

 The struggles coincide with a right, throwing shoulder injury that Watson originally sustained against the Tennessee Titans in Week 3 of the 2023 season. He ultimately underwent season-ending surgery for a fractured glenoid after a Week 10 road win against the Baltimore Ravens .

 Watson returned for the start of the 2024 season but never looked comfortable before his season-ending Achilles injury in October 2024.

 In his first news conference since rupturing his Achilles, he said in June this was the first time he felt 100% healthy since initially injuring his shoulder against the Titans.

 Despite confidence in his physical state, Watson's passing was inconsistent in training camp, and he struggled to push the ball downfield in the preseason. In two preseason games, he was 1-of-6 for 20 yards and an interception on downfield passes; such attempts made up just 22.2% of his passes in the preseason.

 

 "That's something I've always been pretty good at, especially in the past," Watson said Aug. 19. "But those looks and opportunities got to come up. Whatever coach is calling, I try to execute as much as possible, keep the chains moving. Especially early on, it's hard to really start taking shots when the defense is sitting back on that. Especially with Chicago [first preseason game], they were playing a lot of two-wide shells, so a lot of underneath things were right there. But that's something I definitely want to continue to work on, and when those opportunities come, take advantage of it."

 Explosive plays are a priority in first-year head coach Todd Monken's offense. In a 2023 presentation at The Harbaugh Academy, Monken listed explosive plays as one of six figures that best explain how teams win games.

 After Watson was named the Browns' starting quarterback on Aug. 24 despite struggles in the second preseason game, questions surfaced on how much leeway he would have as QB1. If he's unable to generate the explosive plays Monken desires, Watson's backup, Shedeur Sanders , could provide a more aggressive option.

 Though Sanders struggled as a rookie in 2025, his downfield passing -- and willingness to do so -- have been one of his greatest assets. During his seven starts last season, Sanders completed 15 passes on downfield attempts, tied for 19th most among quarterbacks during that span; his 58 downfield attempts were 17th most. Sanders was even better in this year's preseason, completing 5 of 8 of his downfield attempts for 106 yards with a touchdown and an interception (36.4% of his attempts were downfield passes).

 Adherence to one of Monken's core tenets could define Watson's 2026 season. Watson's first test comes against a Jaguars defense that allowed a 42.8% completion percentage on downfield throws last season, the fifth-lowest rate in the NFL.

 "Everyone's chasing explosives and trying to not to turn it over," Monken said last week. "And that's what you're trying to do. What's the defense trying to do? Turn you over and not allow explosives. That's really the big chess match, is that. The ways that you win.

 "Obviously having explosive players helps that. Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. I'm confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field, otherwise we wouldn't be starting him."

title: Todd Monken, QBs, the Browns and a lifetime in pursuit
summary: At age 60, the first-time head coach brings to Cleveland a gritty resolve, an ability to cut through to QBs and a dream that this will be "my last job."
full_text:
TODD MONKEN'S ENTRY into the coaching ranks seemed predestined, but the same couldn't be said for an ascension to one of the top jobs in the NFL.

 However, after three-plus decades of chasing a dream, a monthlong hiring process and three rounds of days-long interviews, Monken finally got the news of a lifetime from the Cleveland Browns .

 In late January, Browns owner Jimmy Haslam texted Monken to ask if he could join yet another video call meeting. At this point, Monken knew the hiring process was nearing its end, so he asked if he could wear a sweatshirt instead of a suit.

 Haslam obliged, and when the two connected, the owner asked if Monken was wearing Browns paraphernalia.

 

 "I said, 'No, but I can take a crayon here and draw a logo on it like a fifth-grader,'" Monken recalled to NFL Network at the scouting combine in February. "... Even throughout the whole process, I've had other opportunities and to not get one of those jobs, [it's] not that you come to the thought that you'll never get one, but to finally have it come to fruition, again, pretty neat."

 Monken turned 60 on Feb. 5, two days after the Browns introduced him as the franchise's 19th noninterim head coach and 11th since returning to Cleveland in 1999. He had enjoyed a decades-long career in coaching, and had this Browns opening not worked out, he had a job waiting for him as the New York Giants ' offensive coordinator, working with former boss John Harbaugh.

 Now, in what outsiders are already calling a lost season primed to take advantage of a hyped 2027 quarterback draft class, Monken has set his sights on maximizing the QBs he has on the roster and a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity as a first-time NFL head coach, beginning Sunday on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ). People who know Monken best say his passion, intellect and ability to connect with others can cut through for a young Cleveland team in need of a firm culture and new identity after winning just eight games over the past two seasons.

 "I'm not getting any younger, let's be real honest here," Monken said at his introductory news conference. "Although I'll say this, the version you're getting of me now is a hell of a lot better than it would have been 15, 20 years ago."

 
 

 
 COINCIDENTALLY, CLEVELAND'S PRESEASON opener against the Chicago Bears on Aug. 15 brought Monken back to the roots of his almost-40-year rise through the coaching ranks.

 In Wheaton, a suburb about 30 miles west of Chicago, Monken grew up in a football family with a storied history. His father, Bob, was a legendary coach at Lake Park High School in Roselle, Illinois, for 30 years. As the Browns' plane descended into Chicago, Monken could spot the football fields that were named after his father.

 "Todd's from a kind of coaching royalty in Illinois," said Randy Oberembt, Monken's football coach at Knox College (Illinois).

 Monken's dad, along with four uncles who all coached high school football in the area, was inducted into the Illinois Coaches Hall of Fame. The five Monken boys had seven sons, all of whom got into coaching at some level. Monken's coaching generation also includes his cousin Jeff, who is the head football coach at Army. Monken's 25-year-old son, Travis, is an offensive analyst with the Browns.

 "I think as kids, we loved the game because we saw our dads loved the game and put that joy into football," Jeff Monken told ESPN. "There were a lot of us that followed our fathers into that profession. Not every single Monken boy cousin did it, but darn near all of us."

 At its essence, though, Monken's father and his mother, Jo Ellen, a second-grade teacher, were educators. That upbringing served as the foundation for everything Monken has done as a football coach. Joe Ellen died in 2023 and Bob died in 2024.

 "We didn't make a ton of money. We didn't have that," Monken told ESPN. "But what they did for me, helping me, engaged in our lives and then disciplining me, I think that's where you see highly successful people; that is the starting point. That's not the end-all. There's plenty of people that were as lucky as I am, but I'm just saying that gives you a f---ing head start. To me, that's where privilege comes from."

 

 
 DESTINED TO FOLLOW in his forebears' footsteps, Monken began his college career as a quarterback at Western Illinois -- "I realized I could evaluate talent and I wasn't very good" -- but then transferred to the College of DuPage, a junior college, where he played baseball before landing at Division III Knox College.

 "I knew then at that moment I wanted to coach," Monken told ESPN. "I helped my dad out my first year at the junior college, and I knew I wanted to coach. I loved it, loved being part of a team. So I thought if I wanted to coach, I felt like I had to play. I felt like I had to go play, whether I was right or wrong."

 Years before he inherited Cleveland's quarterback quandary and oversaw the competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders , Monken was in the middle of his own at Knox. He was in a quarterback competition with the incumbent, multiyear starter and All-American Bob Monroe. After suffering an injury and spending his first season at Knox as a backup, Monken split playing time with Monroe in his second season; Monroe played the first and third quarters, while Monken played the second and fourth quarters.

 As odd as the dynamic was, it failed to cause friction between the two then and now; they have remained close friends after their playing days. Monroe was even in attendance for Monken's introduction as the Browns' head coach.

 

 The next season, with Monroe graduating, Monken became a full-time starter and was named a 1988 Division III All-American, leading the nation in pass attempts, completions and completion percentage. He was also a two-sport athlete, lettering in baseball, and was inducted into the athletic department's hall of fame.

 "We wanted him to stay with us for another year, and we would've gladly turned the offense over to him in 1989, but he wanted to get into [coaching]," Oberembt told ESPN.

 "And that to me was very telling because he was willing to go up to Grand Valley State, be a [graduate assistant] without really knowing what was going to happen up there. And it turned out that that was one of the great coaching laboratories in college football, if you look at what those guys went on and did. And then the rest of his trips, I think what we learned is he was always willing to take the hard job, and he's a ferocious worker."

 
 MONKEN BEGAN HIS coaching journey at Grand Valley State as a graduate assistant in 1989 -- he worked alongside then-defensive coordinator Brian Kelly -- and then bounced around the country in various assistant roles. This also included a four-year stint from 2007 to 2010 in Jacksonville as the Jaguars' wide receivers coach.

 At his higher-profile stops, a theme in Monken's coaching résumé emerged: He could connect with all types of quarterbacks and produce high-octane offenses. There was Brandon Weeden at Oklahoma State. Monken's lone head-coaching job was at Southern Mississippi, where he inherited a winless program and brought it a conference championship with Nick Mullens by Year 3.

 "The difference with him was he has an extremely high level of confidence," former Oklahoma State coach Mike Gundy told ESPN. "I would go in his office and ask him what he thought about the game this week. And he would say, 'I'll be disappointed if we have to punt one time.' And he was serious. ... And he always had the ability to instill a high level of confidence in the players."

 Similar success for Monken carried into the NFL, when Dirk Koetter tapped him to be the Buccaneers' offensive coordinator. But after a forgettable one-year stint in Cleveland in 2019 -- Monken was the OC for Freddie Kitchens but didn't call plays during a disappointing 6-10 season -- the staff was fired, and Monken…

title: Respectful Lions eager to tangle with Saints in opener
summary: Campbell spent five seasons as an assistant to Sean Payton and credits the former Saints coach as the reason he was hired in Detroit.
full_text:
ALLEN PARK, Mich. -- Dan Campbell began his pre-practice speech on Tuesday morning by highlighting his longtime adoration for the New Orleans Saints organization.

 Campbell expressed his respect for the way they've built the program -- and doesn't want his team overlooking the Week 1 opponent -- as the Detroit Lions prepare to kick off the 2026 season against the Saints on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox).

 "He opened this morning by talking about how not only have they had this mindset there that the defensive football and grind-it-out football is big-time in their mentality," said Scottie Montgomery, Lions associate HC/wide receivers coach. "But, also, the personnel that they have that's been set by players that have been there before and that are there now and they continue that grit."

 Campbell's thoughts and coaching DNA were shaped throughout his time within the Saints organization, which he often references.

 Campbell spent five seasons with the Saints (2016-20) as an assistant head coach/tight ends coach before being hired as head coach of the Lions in 2021.

 He won his only previous game versus the Saints as Lions head coach at New Orleans' Caesars Superdome in 2023.

 In New Orleans, Campbell benefited from the tutelage of former head coach Sean Payton with Mickey Loomis, serving as the executive vice president/general manager, where they captured four NFC South division titles during that span.

 "It means a lot. Had it not been for my time there with that organization, it's a class act and a class organization and being with Sean Payton, obviously, I wouldn't have gotten this opportunity," Campbell said. "So, it means a ton and the environment's got to be right.

 "It's got to be the right conditions and we had the right conditions, and you don't forget those and you try to carry over the things that you feel like are done right that you do right and take them to where you go, and there's a lot of similarities in that regard."

 The Week 1 contest at Ford Field will mark his second time facing the Saints, and Campbell says, "they have got some potency" on this year's roster despite coming off a 6-11 season.

 After starting with a 2-10 record last year, the Saints went 4-1 in their final five games as the defense allowed 17.6 points per game in Weeks 14-18, which was tied for the fifth fewest in the NFL with the Los Angeles Chargers during that span.

 Detroit is also looking to bounce back from a disappointing 2025 season where they finished 9-8 while failing to reach the postseason for the first time since 2022.

 

 The Lions enter 2026 with high expectations, including a 40% chance to win the NFC North, per ESPN Analytics, which is the highest of any team in the division, despite finishing last in the NFC North last season.

 Lions assistant head coach/safeties Jim O'Neil described the team's level of excitement as being extremely high for the opening week, notably after completing "as hard of a camp as I've been around."

 "We got after it, and I feel that everybody got better," O'Neil said.

 For Campbell, it goes without saying that this Saints game means a lot. Although he's respectful of the opponent, he's done everything throughout training camp to make sure "we'll be ready to go" at kickoff.

 Nobody within the organization wants to let him down while going against his former team, either.

 "There is a certain level of heightening of awareness from assistants to make sure we give our head football coach the best opportunity we can and our program and the organization the best chance we have to go win this game," Montgomery said.

title: Expectations for Packers' MarShawn Lloyd with Josh Jacobs out
summary: Lloyd is finally healthy and Josh Jacobs is on the commissioner exempt list, but how much of a workload can Lloyd handle in Week 1?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The first time MarShawn Lloyd touched the ball in the preseason this year, he stumbled -- his description -- just before he cut his run back to the right and regained his balance. Lloyd still managed a 5-yard gain, but on the way back to the huddle, quarterback Jordan Love asked him if he was OK.

 "Jordan kind of noticed that and he was like, you good?" Lloyd recalled. "I'm like, yeah, I'm good."

 After all the injuries, all the practices missed and all the games Lloyd watched in street clothes, who could blame the Green Bay Packers quarterback for wondering?

 "Once I got hit the first time," Lloyd said, "it was fine"

 In the month since that preseason opener in Pittsburgh, Lloyd answered some more questions. Yes, he could make it through an NFL training camp. Yes, he showed some of the same moves that the Packers fell in love with when they picked him in third round of the 2024 NFL draft. No, his confidence has not wavered.

 Yet with Sunday's season opener at the Minnesota Vikings  ( 4:25 p.m. ET, CBS ) just days away, one question lingers: How much can he handle?

 With Josh Jacobs on the commissioner exempt list while the NFL investigates him for violations of the personal conduct policy, Lloyd has become the Packers' de facto RB1. That's a heavy stone to carry for someone who has been healthy enough to play in only one NFL game over the past two seasons combined.

 

 "As ready as he's ever been since he's been here," Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said of Lloyd. "He looks good. He's handling all the physicality, the things that he needs to as a running back. It was good to get him out there and feel that. I think one of the things, particularly the running backs, the ball carriers, receivers, tight ends, when they haven't played a lot, protecting the ball, taking hits -- all those types of things -- you need some of that to get ready. I think he's ready."

 But ready for what, exactly? Five carries? 10? Even more?

 "That's to be determined," coach Matt LaFleur said. "Who knows? I couldn't tell you right now, so we'll see how he's feeling. He's had a really steady camp. I think he did an outstanding job. Obviously his availability has been critical and we'll just see how it goes."

 When the offseason program began in April, all the Packers wanted was to see Lloyd get through OTAs.

 When Lloyd made it through OTAs, they wanted to see Lloyd get through the early portions of training camp.

 When Lloyd handled the first two weeks of practice, they wanted to see Lloyd play in the preseason games.

 The highlight of Lloyd's 28 snaps in the preseason game was an 11-yard touchdown catch on an option route against the Broncos on Aug. 21. In the first two preseason games, Lloyd had 12 touches (10 carries and two catches). While most of the starters sat out of the preseason finale against the Cardinals, the original plan was for Lloyd to play before LaFleur changed his mind.

 "The more I thought about it, I was like, 'Do we?'" LaFleur said. "You know, he's had such a great training camp, and ultimately, I felt like it was best for the team."

 

 The Packers have three running backs on the active roster: Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson . Brooks has been mostly a third-down, pass-protecting back. Johnson just arrived in Green Bay last week after a cut-down day trade with the Steelers. They will probably have to elevate Pierre Strong Jr . from the practice squad for Sunday against the Vikings.

 Lloyd's issues began with hamstring and hip injuries early in his first training camp with the Packers in 2024. He came back in time for Week 2 and had six carries for 15 yards and one catch for 3 yards. To date, that remains his only NFL regular-season or playoff game experience. And even that was done after only 10 snaps because of an ankle injury that landed him on injured reserve two days later. During his rehab from the ankle, he reinjured his hamstring and then underwent emergency surgery to have his appendix removed.

 It only got worse in Year 2. He didn't play a game last season. He started 2025 on injured reserve because of another hamstring injury and just when he came back to practice late in the year, he had another setback and returned to IR.

 In an effort to figure out why this kept happening, Lloyd spent part of this offseason at the Meyer Institute of Sport in California, where it was discovered that a torn ACL in college likely had been causing stress on the rest of his body.

 "Body feels good," Lloyd said at the end of the preseason. "Now it's just like, you just came from camp, so you just gotta rest and recover and just do that on repeat."

 That rest came last weekend in the form of a getaway in Chicago. He went to see Ye (Kanye West). The concert was at Soldier Field, home of the Chicago Bears . It was actually Lloyd's first time in the stadium. Because of his injuries, Lloyd rarely traveled to road games the past two seasons. Same goes for the Vikings' U.S. Bank Stadium.

 "For that to be my first game," he said. "That'll be fun."

title: Travis Hunter, wife give gifts to nurses who helped with birth of their child
summary: The nurses who helped care for the couple's son's while he was in the Wolfson Children's Hospital neonatal ICU left a lasting impression.
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter and his wife, Leanna Lenee, were understandably overwhelmed when their son was born nearly eight weeks premature in August 2025.

 The support they received from multiple nurses while their son spent weeks in the Wolfson Children's Hospital neonatal ICU left a lasting impression on the couple, which is why they surprised those nurses with lunch and scrubs Tuesday.

 "They treated us very well, took care of us, and I saw the work that they did for everybody else," Hunter said. "They took care of us just like they took care of everyone else here. So it was definitely really, really special to come back and give back to them.

 "Being first-time parents, you need all the help you can get going through the experience."

 And while they were thankful for all the nurses who helped, they were especially appreciative of Rebekah Davis. They saved her scrubs for last, and when she came up to get them she got a tearful hug from Leanna.

 

 "Being first-time parents, we prepared for a lot," Leanna said. "We prepared for the nursery and bottles and all that stuff, but something you can't prepare for is your son being born almost eight weeks early and him being in the NICU. And it was really hard for both of us, and we didn't know what to do. It was something unexpected. Rebekah was somebody who was very calming to us. I remember I tried to stay at the hospital every single night, and she was like, 'Go home, please. We got it. We'll take care of him.' And she celebrated with us all the wins, all the little milestones. She kept both of us grounded because it was really scary seeing your child just in all these little tubes and stuff. And she was amazing.

 "All the nurses here were amazing to us. So Wolfson will always hold a special place in our hearts."

 Travis Hunter, who was going through training camp and the beginning of the 2025 NFL season while his son was still in the hospital, tried to get to Wolfson whenever he could. Sometimes that meant coming over at night after a full day of practices and meetings, and he was grateful the hospital was willing to accommodate him.

 "I [didn't] speak a lot when I came in the building, but y'all made me feel comfortable being able to come here and stay," Hunter told the nurses. "Y'all make me feel very special and I really appreciate it."

title: Weighing on the pros and cons of 49ers', Rams' Melbourne travel
summary: Two NFL franchises will travel the globe for a Week 1 matchup. What are the positives and negatives about each team's travel?
full_text:
MELBOURNE, Australia -- Although the Los Angeles Rams will pose as the home team for the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers , it's the Niners who spent the week leading up to the game making themselves at home in Melbourne.

 That's because the teams elected to take completely opposite approaches to the longest road trip for a regular-season game in NFL history. The Niners opted to fly 16 hours and nearly 8,000 miles to Australia last Wednesday night, landing in Melbourne on Friday morning, a little more than a week before the 10:35 a.m. (AEST) kickoff this Thursday.

 The Rams, meanwhile, plan to arrive the day before the game. Both teams will return to California immediately after the game.

 Those disparate approaches have left both teams open to questions on the better approach to the long trips and how it might affect their performances in Week 1.

 The NFL leaves travel plans for games both domestic and international up to the teams, with no mandate on arrival or departure.

 "It's at the team's discretion," Charlotte Offord, general manager of NFL Australia and New Zealand, said. "Everyone has their own method in terms of how they believe they should show up and what's best for the team. Both teams coming in have completely different approaches and that's fine."

 No matter the outcome, it's safe to assume at least some of the postgame analysis will include the travel discrepancy. But will it really matter?

 A pair of medical professionals -- Dr. Cheri Mah, a sleep physician and performance specialist, and Dr. Vonda Wright, an orthopedic sports surgeon -- offered a better understanding of the pros and cons of each approach.

 

 The 49ers' plan 
Upon learning they'd be playing in Australia, the Niners sought information on the best way to execute.

 "I would love to just show up the day before and just play, but I'm not the best when it comes to the science and everything on that stuff," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. "You ask people who've done it a number of times, you ask people who study it, you take all their opinions in ... The recommendation for everybody has been to tell us when to go, and it's made a lot of sense. And I know how our players feel also. I was a little bit on the fence. Science wasn't and our players weren't at all. That helped me get off the fence."

 The Niners flew to Australia late last Wednesday night and arrived early that Friday morning. They had some light walk-throughs and "shake-outs" to get their bodies loose over the weekend before having a normal practice week on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday.

 The pros: According to Mah, who has worked with NFL teams on their sleep methods and spoke at the player health and safety summit in the spring about how to travel smarter, the Niners will at least be able to recover from travel fatigue and jet lag, even if body clocks aren't fully calibrated.

 "I think it's helpful that they've given themselves a cushion to do that because regardless of the jet lag, there's also travel fatigue [from] this 16-hour flight that they're taking," Mah said. "That's a long time on a flight. And being able to recover from the travel fatigue is a separate issue than just how the body clock is adjusted and how that can affect your sleep and daytime functioning.

 "What the Niners are doing I think definitely will be helpful to have those additional days in between." 
 
 

 While the 49ers won't practice at the same time as the scheduled kickoff, those sessions will be pretty close to that window.

 "They will have had three or four days to shift their time a couple hours forward," Wright said. "They will have slept; they will have eaten. Will they be totally acclimated? Nope. But they will have had two or three days to get [a] solid eight [to] 10 hours of sleep in."

 Both Wright and Mah noted that another benefit of early arrival is the chance to get and stay hydrated (the Niners gave each player a specific amount of water to consume on the plane ride based on their size and needs) as well as get sunlight at the proper times of the day.

 The cons: Even with a week in the country, the Niners will not be able to fully reset their body clocks to Australia time due to passing through many time zones. According to Mah and Wright, it takes the body roughly one full day for every time zone crossed.

 On a flight this long over the international date line, there's not enough time for the 49ers to catch up. The Niners will then face the opposite effect in returning to California to begin preparation for Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins .

 San Francisco will have a few extra days off upon returning to the West Coast, but it will still take careful planning to get back on Pacific time before returning to practice.

 "Their reacclimating coming east may be more difficult," Wright said. "Afterward, they may need to have a tight schedule of light and dark and on the way back feed the guys as they would be on the West Coast and taking short naps and just trying to reacclimate them."

 
 The Rams' plan 
Much like they did before playing the Jacksonville Jaguars in London last season, the Rams will be in and out of Australia quickly. In fact, they're likely to spend more time on the round-trip flights than they will on the ground in Melbourne.

 The plan is to arrive in Australia on Thursday, play the game Friday and head home. The plan worked in London in 2025 when they beat the Jaguars 35-7. Head coach Sean McVay acknowledged that it's a bit of a different approach, but he and his staff believe that "staying in rhythm and routine" is of the utmost importance.

 "The thinking in its simplest form is, what do we deem the best for our football players and for them to try to be at their best?" McVay said. "There are different approaches and theories. But I do have a lot of trust in our group and we'll see. Hopefully it works out."

 The pros: The Rams' plan centers on maintaining their current body clock in a way that aligns with the kickoff. While kickoff is in the morning Australia time, that's still within a couple of hours of what would be a normal kickoff for a primetime game on Pacific time.

 According to Mah, the Rams staying accustomed to that body clock also puts them in a window -- 4 to 8 p.m. -- that usually allows for enhanced athletic performance.

 "That's when records are broken and gold medals are won, and it's this unique window where physical performance we know is enhanced," Mah said. "They are likely trying to leverage this window by keeping their body clocks in that prime window. That is obviously a pro of doing so and coming in and trying to then return home quickly." 
 
 

 Another advantage for the Rams is that they should have less trouble readjusting to Pacific time as they begin preparation for Week 2 and beyond.

 The cons: The biggest issue for the Rams is the travel itself. The London plan worked well in part because the Rams traveled directly from Baltimore, turning an 11-hour flight into a seven-hour trip. The flight to Melbourne is more than double that, which can cause increased stress on the body.

 "Every player's going to walk off the plane stiff, every joint's going to be aching, and it's going to take the rehab team a lot of work just to get some fluid back in those joints," Wright said. "But it's not just a tired leg problem. Less than 24 hours after getting off a plane, you've got a whole body timing problem. And both things are happening at once for them.

 "The travel fatigue from the journey itself, cramped up, no sleep. And the dehydration is real on a long flight like that. So, you've got the physical tiredness and then the time zone, the jet lag, which is the mismatch between body clock and local times."

 Mah said the other part of the challenge is the game's early start time. Though their bodies might feel like they're in their usual prime window, it's still an unusual time to begin.
