title: Betting Patriots-Seahawks: Edge to champs in Super Bowl rematch
summary: Odds, game picks, prop plays and advice to help you bet Wednesday night's Patriots-Seahawks opener.
full_text:
It's a Super Bowl rematch to start the season, and despite Seattle 's dominant 29-13 win -- which was even more one-sided than the final score implies -- the Seahawks are only a 3-point favorite at home against the New England Patriots  on Wednesday. The Seahawks' departures in the secondary ( Coby Bryant , Riq Woolen ) have put their defensive back depth under a microscope, and with a litany of preseason injuries entering the contest ( Bud Clark on injured reserve; Nick Emmanwori and Ty Okada expected out), it could be an easier day through the air for the Patriots. The arrival of free agent receiver Romeo Doubs and trade acquisition A.J. Brown certainly help there as well.

 

 It's a new offense in Seattle, as coordinator Klint Kubiak departed to take the Las Vegas Raiders ' head coaching job. Brian Fleury replaces him and figures to run much of the same stuff but without Super Bowl MVP RB Kenneth Walker III , who left in free agency for the Kansas City Chiefs , meaning the Seahawks will need a new go-to player for this rematch. The Patriots are alarmingly thin on pass rushers; Harold Landry remains on PUP, and second-round rookie Edge  Gabe Jacas is still working his way into form after a long offseason absence. Sam Darnold should have time when he needs to drop back.

 

 

 Betting outlook 
 I'm expecting a heavier dose of dropbacks on both sides of the ball. Seattle's offensive approach will remain full of heavy personnel and run action but given the Patriots' weakness at pass rusher and the uncertain state of the Seahawks' running back room, the air should be the preferred method of attack for the Seahawks. Meanwhile, the Patriots have two shiny new pass catchers in Doubs and Brown that they're excited to debut against a Seahawks secondary that's absent Woolen and Bryant (departed in free agency) and likely Emmanwori and Okada (injury). That, along with the expected absence of running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), gives the Patriots a bigger edge in the passing game than they had last go around.

 

 With more passes expected, I lean to the over at 44.5 (-108). But 44 is a key number, and Week 1 has been heavy to the under over the past few years. Unders were 4-12 in the opening week last season and 29-51 over the past five Week 1s. Defenses tend to start the year with catered game plans, given the long runway for planning. Does the familiarity for these two teams change that at all? I'm not sure. I'll look to get a live over if we fall below 44 early in the first quarter, but I don't feel compelled to take anything preflop.

 Notable player props, bets 
 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. 

 

 Total points UNDER 44.5 (-112) 

 Joe Fortenbaugh: Let's start with the Seattle offense, a unit that ranked eighth in scoring last season. That group will be without Super Bowl MVP Walker, backup running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) and offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak (Raiders head coach). That's a sizeable chunk missing from a first-class offense. The defense, while not exactly the same as the unit that ranked first in the NFL in defensive EPA last season, will still prove formidable and has the benefit of the crowd noise at Lumen Field. The key to the handicap, however, is the fact that Week 1 scoring has dipped the past few years, thanks to defenses that have favored an abundance of 2-deep safety looks in order to limit explosive plays. Case in point: Week 1 of the 2021 season saw an average total score of 48 points. In the four years since, the Week 1 average total score has dropped to 42.5 points.

 Rhamondre Stevenson rushing yards UNDER 58.5 (-110) 

 Solak: The Patriots could not run the ball a lick in their Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks. Stevenson had 23 yards on seven carries and Henderson had another 19 on six. Drake Maye ended up being the Pats' leading rusher thanks to his scrambles. Now, Stevenson's total rushing prop has risen given Henderson's dubious status for Wednesday's game (ankle). At 58.5, I'm willing to take the under. I expect a pass-heavy approach for the Patriots, given their new receiver room (Doubs, Brown) and the Seahawks' injuries in the secondary (Emmanwori, Okada).

 

 Eli Raridon anytime TD scorer (11-1, first TD scorer (50-1) 

 Solak: Raridon, the Patriots' third-round rookie tight end, has been a depth chart climber all offseason. Free agent TE Julian Hill , signed to be the blocking running mate to incumbent starter Hunter Henry , was lost for the season with knee injury. That opened the door for Raridon to climb to TE2, and he spent most of the preseason on the bench with the starters while other rookies accumulated snaps. I'll take touchdown odds at longer than 10-1 on a TE2 who figures to get play-action routes in the red zone any day of the week.

 Hunter Henry receiving yards OVER 34.5 (-110) 

 Eric Moody:  Brown and Doubs should draw plenty of targets, but Henry still has Maye's trust and should remain heavily involved. He finished second on the Patriots in targets last season and has ranked 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine seasons. The matchup helps too, as Seattle allowed the fifth-most receptions and fourth-most receiving yards to tight ends last season.

title: Ann Michael Maye dishes on skyrocketing profile with Drake's ascent
summary: One of the organic trickle-down effects of Maye's rapid ascent to stardom is how his wife, Ann Michael, has seen her own profile skyrocket.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will be in the spotlight when the 2026 NFL regular season kicks off Wednesday in a Super Bowl LX rematch with the Seattle Seahawks .

 

 One of the organic trickle-down effects of Maye's rapid ascent to stardom is how his wife, Ann Michael, has seen her own profile skyrocket.

 "It's something I didn't expect and wasn't trying to gain a following," Ann Michael told ESPN in a recent interview. "It's really cool in that it just happened in the most natural way. It's been fun to see the New England community rally around not just Drake but me as well.

 "This whole world I'm in now, social media, this following, is something I didn't know anything about. So it's cool to see, day by day, the different opportunities that come in. I just did a Make-A-Wish and it was one of the coolest experiences I've ever had. It's cool to see what comes knocking on my door. It has brought so many fun and awesome opportunities."

 Another example of Ann Michael's rise: Her robust social media presence has businesses such as Dawn and Cascade building marketing campaigns around her -- a natural fit after her "Bakemas" TikTok series went viral last holiday season.

 So that explains why Ann Michael took part in some media interviews in recent weeks, tying in the "superDISHions" theme with Drake's football superstitions.

 "Game-day cooking for me, I love to make a loaf of sourdough bread in the morning. It makes the house smell so good, especially as it starts to get a little colder -- that's the perfect way to start off the game day," she said.

 "Drake is kind of picky about what he'll eat on game days, but I'm always making little grab-and-go peanut butter energy balls. He loves those -- like the perfect snack, pretty light, not going to make him feel too full before a game."

 Another of Drake's favorites, grilled cheese, wouldn't fit on the game-day menu. Fresh fruit and cookies with red and blue M&M's are a staple for guests, especially after games. And Buffalo chicken dip is another go-to choice for the Mayes, especially on Saturdays when watching college football.

 Ann Michael is often cooking for a larger crowd of family and friends staying at their home, and she said one necessity is having the kitchen clean.

 "Preparation is the biggest thing. I like to prep as many things as I can ahead of time, so when people are here, I can just enjoy their company and have fun," she said. "That's also when an effective and quick cleaning also comes into play, because obviously any time you cook I can do dishes like five times a day. The last thing you want to be doing is spending an hour cleaning your kitchen."

 This is the family's third year in New England, and Ann Michael has come to appreciate the region.

 "I didn't really know what to expect moving from North Carolina. That's where I grew up and went to college, so I was always there. Moving up here has been an adjustment, but it's been so cool to experience the community -- everyone has been so great and welcoming with open arms," she said. "I've tried to explore a lot of the different areas. One of the coolest things I've realized is there are so many states and places all so close together -- you can get so many places within driving distance. I went to New York for 24 hours [last] week, so that was so fun that I could do that."

 They also attend events together when time permits.

 "The sports culture here, having all the professional sports teams -- going to a Red Sox game, a Celtics game, Bruins, things like that has been super fun for us," she said.

 Now, it's all about football season.

 "I'm so excited for football to be back. I can't believe it's starting and feel like time has flown," she said. "After last season, it was such a fun season -- so many cool memories and opportunities. It obviously didn't end the way that we wanted, so I think that makes everybody more excited to get back and hopefully chase that same goal this year."

title: Are the Super Bowl Champion Seahawks built to repeat in 2026?
summary: The Seahawks are not the favorites to win the Super Bowl or their division. What hurdles will they have in 2026?
full_text:
RENTON, Wash. -- Six months after the Seattle Seahawks hoisted the Vince Lombardi Trophy for the second time in franchise history, Richard Sherman was struck by the team's post-Super Bowl vibe. As he chopped it up with Mike Macdonald at the start of an Aug. 10 training camp practice, the retired cornerback wanted to know how the third-year head coach got his players to lock back in.

 "How did you get these guys so -- this is such a hungry-ass team," asked Sherman, who starred for the Super Bowl XLVIII-champion Seahawks and still lives in the Seattle area. "We were still hungry after the first one, but you still felt like this dude got paid, this dude's starting to feel himself, this dude's pissed off he's not getting enough money.

 "You don't feel none of that here. You don't feel nothing here but f---ing grind, work."

 Macdonald answered in typical self-effacing fashion, complete with a contemplative pause.

 "Umm, I don't know," he said. "It's just what we do, you know?"

 "But that's easier said than done," Sherman said.

 Captured by HBO's "Hard Knocks," the 40-second exchange illustrated one of the challenges that Super Bowl winners face, and why the Seahawks are equipped to handle it as they try to become only the ninth repeat champion in NFL history and only the third this century. That quest begins Wednesday ( 8:20 p.m., NBC ), when they open their 2026 season against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field.

 But other roadblocks await. The Seahawks lost four key players in free agency from the team that beat New England in Super Bowl LX , including the game's MVP in running back Kenneth Walker III and cornerback Riq Woolen , whose departure looks more significant now than it did in March. With Klint Kubiak getting poached as well, quarterback Sam Darnold and the offense will be relying on a first-time coordinator in Brian Fleury. Meanwhile, the division-rival Los Angeles Rams loaded up this offseason on their way to becoming betting favorites to win the NFC West and Super Bowl LXI.

 

 Those are more than just champagne problems that the champs will have to navigate. But the feeling inside team headquarters is that, as Macdonald has put it, not "an ounce of complacency" has been evident. 

 "We're more focused than ever," veteran defensive tackle Jarran Reed  said. "A lot of people always try to bring up the Super Bowl and all that, but literally nobody talks about it. We don't bring it up. We just worry about the day that we're in, the present that we're in, and we just attack the day.

 "I think we're more hungry this year, too, which is surprising. We know what we have to do."

 

 'This league is about making hard decisions' 
 When the dust settled on the Seahawks' 29-13 win over the Patriots at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California, general manager John Schneider commemorated the title by adding to his collection of arm tattoos. The new ink on the crease of his right elbow includes the letters LX underneath the Golden Gate Bridge.

 In the same spot on his left elbow are the letters XLVIII underneath the New York City skyline, which is near where the Seahawks claimed their first Lombardi trophy at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, 12 years earlier.

 Schneider is the only GM in NFL history to win two Super Bowls with different head coaches and none of the same players. His 2014 Seahawks came within a yard of repeating as champions after an offseason in which their roster took significantly more hits than the current one just did.

 Schneider has been here before. But he still needed to hear something that his close friend and Tampa Bay Buccaneers counterpart Jason Licht told him over a late-night dinner at this year's NFL combine in Indianapolis. Schneider said Licht reminded him that you can't make emotional decisions while trying to keep a Super Bowl-winning team intact.

 

 A few days later, Seattle said goodbye to Walker as he agreed to a three-year, $43.05 million deal with the Kansas City Chiefs at the start of the free agency negotiating window. Three other key players would follow: outside linebacker Boye Mafe ( three years, $60 million with the Cincinnati Bengals ), safety Coby Bryant ( three years, $40 million with the Chicago Bears ) and Woolen ( one year, $12 million with the Philadelphia Eagles ).

 Taking Licht's reminder to heart wasn't easy. But it was necessary, especially with megadeals coming down the pike for wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba ($42.15 million per season in new money), cornerback Devon Witherspoon ($33 million) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams ($30 million), who all signed extensions this offseason.

 "Obviously we're going to miss those guys, but you've got to keep moving forward," Schneider said on Seattle Sports 710 AM before the Seahawks' first preseason game. "To get all those [other] guys back was a big deal for us. This league is about making hard decisions after every season, and this is no different whether you win a world championship or don't."

 The Seahawks re-signed a pair of starters in wide receiver Rashid Shaheed and cornerback Josh Jobe , as well as every notable backup save for special teamer Dareke Young . With no salary cap casualties -- Seattle has a league-low $2.33 million in dead money charges for 2026, per OverTheCap -- Schneider and vice president of player administration Joey Laine brought back all but six of their 52 players who played at least 100 combined snaps (including special teams) during the regular season and playoffs. By comparison, the 2014 Seahawks lost 13 of the 48 players who met that playing-time threshold the year before.

 "It was more than I anticipated looking back," Schneider said. "That's a credit to the coaches and Joey Laine and our personnel staff in terms of guys wanting to be here and just keeping as many guys as we possibly can."

 Having seen the Seahawks' locker room gradually lose its edge in the later years of the Legion of Boom era, Schneider approached April's draft with an eye for competitors .

 Seattle's eight-man class was headlined by top pick Jadarian Price , whom the Seahawks hope can replicate some of Walker's explosiveness. He'll lead  their backfield while Zach Charbonnet spends at least the first four games on the physically unable to perform list following ACL surgery.

 Second-round safety Bud Clark was supposed to push Ty Okada for Bryant's old starting job, but he's out for the season with a broken ankle. Third-round cornerback Julian Neal missed much of camp with a quad injury that has kept him from factoring in the battle to replace Woolen as CB3, which had looked like perhaps the only potential weak point of a defense that allowed the fewest points in the NFL last season.

 Safety, however, has become another early-season concern, with Okada sidelined with a hamstring injury and Emmanwori taking longer than expected to return from July right ankle surgery .

 

 Between their injury issues and free agent departures, the Seahawks could have their work cut out for them as they try to recapture their defensive dominance of 2025. But with much of the unit entering Year 3 in Macdonald's scheme, familiarity will be an asset.

 "There's a lot of continuity in the players that we have, so it allows a kind of unspoken, at times, understanding of what we're doing and why we're trying to do something," defensive coordinator Aden Durde said. 

 While the Seahawks lost established talent on defense, the rival Rams added it in a big way. Bringing future Hall of Fame defensive tackle Aaron Donald out of retirement capped an offseason in which Los Angeles also acquired All-Pro defensive end Myles Garrett as well as cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson .

 The two teams played three nail-biters last season, with the Seahawks winning the rubber match at home in the NFC Championship Game. But now, DraftKings gives the Rams the best odds to win the NFC West at -105 (ahead of Seattle at +215) and Super…

title: Buccaneers extend Baker Mayfield: Key intel and a grade
summary: Why did Mayfield change his mind about a negotiating deadline, and what does it mean for other QBs?
full_text:
It was a surprise, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers now have their quarterback locked in through the 2029 season after giving Baker Mayfield a three-year, $165 million extension Monday -- the largest contract in the franchise's history.

 The Bucs offered a two-year extension, according to sources, but the two sides could not reach an agreement before Mayfield's mandated training camp deadline. But all of that has changed for the 2018 No. 1 pick.

 Mayfield enters Year 4 in Tampa after first signing a one-year, $4 million deal worth up to $8.5 million in 2023. In 2024, the Bucs gave Mayfield a three-year deal for $100 million in total and $50 million guaranteed.

 Now, they lock their guy up again, but what does this mean for the future? Buccaneers reporter Jenna Laine, national reporter Jeremy Fowler and NFL analyst Ben Solak dish on the happenings surrounding this deal five days before Tampa Bay kicks off its season at the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ).

 

 Mayfield and the Bucs couldn't come to terms during camp. What changed? 

 A deadline. Mayfield wanted to cut off talks at the start of camp, but he never shut down the possibility of the Bucs trying again. In recent days, Tampa offered a deal that gave Mayfield two things he wanted: an agreement longer than two years, which was a sticking point originally, and average pay of $55 million per year, in line with Jacksonville's Trevor Lawrence and Green Bay's Jordan Love . He felt that he had performed well enough to enter that salary tier. Tampa Bay's willingness to put him there helped facilitate a deal. Per sources, after the Bucs' final contract offer of two years and just north of $100 million, the two sides stopped talking. But those talks resumed over the weekend. -- Fowler and Laine 

 What does this mean for Mayfield and the Bucs this season? 
 The Bucs entered training camp with not one but two disgruntled team captains in Mayfield and defensive tackle  Vita Vea . Mayfield practiced, but Vea held in by not practicing (he was also dealing with a back injury) and he requested a trade. Those are not ideal circumstances entering a season for a team trying to get back into the playoffs after missing them for the first time since 2020 last year.

 

 The Bucs re-signed Vea last month , and in locking in Mayfield now, they avoided not only a seasonlong distraction -- although Mayfield has been very good at tuning it out -- but also what is likely a much higher dollar figure in the coming months. You have to consider how much the market will change with several QBs being in line for contracts next year, plus a rising salary cap. Multiple agents told ESPN to expect today's $50 million will be $60 million tomorrow. Mayfield has said he does not need financial incentives to play better. He'll always seek ways to motivate himself. As his high school coach Hank Carter told ESPN, "His grease is always hot."

 This can put to rest some of the concerns GM Jason Licht faced during training camp about a potential decline in the team's culture -- between those two deals not getting done and the departure of Mike Evans and retirement of Lavonte David. Licht responded by saying, "Not at all. ... I feel like the culture is maybe at one of its highest points." This helps reaffirm that. -- Laine 

 What does this mean for C.J. Stroud , Bryce Young and other QBs awaiting new deals? 

 Not much. The overall quarterback market remains relatively unchanged, and Houston is comfortable placing Stroud in the $50 million-and-up club that 13 quarterbacks now occupy. Mayfield has a proven statistical track record; whereas with Stroud, Houston must decide how far it is willing to go to prevent Stroud from playing out his rookie deal, which he seems comfortable doing. Stroud, Young and others know that the market will balloon next offseason, when several stars from the 2024 draft class are eligible for new deals and Lamar Jackson could look for his next contract. -- Fowler 

 How would you grade the Mayfield extension? 

 B:  Mayfield is a playmaker with high peaks (he was producing at top-of-the-league levels for stretches of 2024 and 2025) but low valleys (injuries and overaggressive play create big mistakes). He's obviously a good enough quarterback to extend but now must deliver the high-level, veteran consistency of a Jared Goff or Brock Purdy (both $53 million APY) in order to return value on this deal. This looks like a reasonable, market-rate deal for the Buccaneers. What will be interesting to see is how much guaranteed money is in the final year of the contract, as the Bucs were reportedly pushing for a two-year deal at first before capitulating to the three-year extension. -- Solak
